units.la: PRaclarè Oratorum Princeps, Lector benevole, Historiam dixit vitam magistram. Quemadmodum enim sapiens magistra eis, quibus prafecta est, salutaria, qua sequantur, prascribit precepta & viuendi rationes: ita etiam historia practica, qua hominum actiones enarrat voluntarias, rerum praeteritarum proponens veritatem, docet, quid in rebus politicis sit imitandum, quid contra fugiendum. Eam, qua de Rebus Belgicis est, id quoque praestare, qui negauerit, is se eius non admodum peritum esse ostenderit. Nam siue Imperatores, siue Reges, Principes, Respublica, Magistratus, Belli duces, Chiliarcha, Centuriones, Milites gregarii alii, cuiuscunque tandem sint ordinis ac conditioditionis, eam cum iudicio legerint ac perpende-rint, videbunt, discentque ab ea, quae & ipsis & Reipubl. si sequantur aut vitent, laudi & emolumento futura sint. Reges ac Principes, siue absolutam sibi in subditos, siue non absolutam attribuant potestatem, haud raro parum profici seuitia ac crudelitate, vbi & verae pietati & patriae libertati bellum indicitur. Inferiores Magistratus & Respublicae, agnoscent, quantum possit ad conseruandam patriam concordia, & contra ad eam subuertendam discordia. Belli duces, non facile praelio summam rei esse committendam; nec animos statim esse abiiciendos, etsi vna atque altera expeditione (quod Principi AVRAICO accidit) euentus consiliis minimè respondeat. Ceteri deniq; quos nominaui, alia discent, quae hîc commemorare nihil attinet.
units.tr: The most famous of orators, kind reader, called history the teacher of life. For just as a wise teacher sets out for those in her charge the wholesome precepts and rules of living that they should follow, so practical history, which relates human actions freely undertaken and sets forth the truth of past events, teaches what in public affairs is to be imitated and what is to be avoided. Anyone who denies that the history of the Belgic affairs offers this benefit shows that he is not much acquainted with it. For whether emperors, kings, princes, commonwealths, magistrates, generals, captains of a thousand, centurions, or ordinary soldiers, of whatever rank or condition, read and weigh it carefully, they will see and learn from it what will bring praise and advantage to themselves and to the commonwealth if they follow it or avoid it. Kings and princes, whether they claim an absolute power over their subjects or not, seldom gain anything by savagery and cruelty when they declare war on true piety and on the liberty of the fatherland. Lesser magistrates and commonwealths will recognise how much concord can do to preserve the fatherland, and conversely how much discord can do to overthrow it. Generals will learn that the decision of a matter should not readily be entrusted to a single battle, and that spirits should not be cast down at once, even if one or another campaign (as happened to Prince William of Orange) turns out quite differently from what was planned. The rest whom I have named will learn other lessons, which it is not worth recounting here.

units.la: Quae cum ita habeant, nemo est, qui non intelligat, plurimum ab omnibus omnium Ordinum hominibus iis deberi, qui in Historia rerum Belgicarum nobis fideliter scribenda operam suam collocarunt, quemadmodum etiam huius libelli Auctori. Cum enim animaduerteret, multis tantum ocii ab aliis negociis non superesse, vt integram ab EMA-
units.tr: Since this is so, no one can fail to understand how much all men of every rank owe to those who have devoted their labour to writing for us a faithful history of the Belgic affairs, as also to the author of this little book. For when he perceived that many men, because of their other business, had too little leisure to read through the whole history written by Emanuel van Meteren

units.la: NVELE à METEREN aut aliis conscriptam e-uoluerent historiam ; eam in istam redegit Epito-men, à qua quid tibi expectandum, malo te ex i-psius, qui sequitur, versu, quàm meis verbis co-gnoscere. Vale, & siqua animaduertes inter le-gendum errata Typographica, ea benigne ignosce & corrige.
units.tr: or by others, he condensed it into this Epitome. You will learn what to expect from it better from the verse that follows, I think, than from my own words. Farewell, and if you notice any typographical errors while reading, kindly excuse them and correct them.

units.la: PErlegere ingentes cui non vacat ordine Libros, Historiæ & tumido vela dare Oceano; Sedulus exiguos legat is, relegatque libellos, Securo, tenui, vectus in amne, rate. Forsitan hæc veniet quoque per compendia eodem, Quo mora eum longa vix graue ductet iter. Pinge prius parua, quæ vis loca adire, tabella, Sic regio poterit quæque patere tibi. Corporis exiguam magni prius inspice formam, Singula quo melius membra notare queas. Qui seriem ergo cupit breuiter cognoscere Rerum Belgarum, breuis huic seruiet iste liber.
units.tr: He who has no leisure to read through huge books in order, and to set sail on the swelling ocean of history, but reads and re-reads small little books eagerly, carried in a slender boat on a safe stream, may perhaps reach the same goal by these shortcuts, which a long delay would hardly let him travel by a heavy road. First paint on a small tablet the places you wish to visit; so whatever region lies open to you can be seen. First look at the small form of a great body, so that you may better be able to note each limb. Therefore whoever wishes to know briefly the sequence of Belgian affairs, this little book will serve him briefly.

units.la: Pantaleon Candidus Austriacus, S. B.
units.tr: Pantaleon Candidus of Austria sends good wishes.

units.la: RERVM BELGICA-RVM EPITOME. DOMINI BRABANTIÆ CIRCA TEMPORA CAROLI MAGNI, &c.
units.tr: THE EPITOME OF THE AFFAIRS OF BELGIUM. THE LORDS OF BRABANT AROUND THE TIME OF CHARLEMAGNE, etc.

units.la: PIpinus, Carolomanni filius, Dominus fuit Brabantiæ. Is vxore ducta ex gente Aquitanica, Suevos aliosq; Germaniæ populos bello vicit. Huic filius Grimoaldus successit, cuius consilio Sigisbertus Rex Francorum templa & cœnobia varia extruxit.
units.tr: Pippin, son of Carloman, was Lord of Brabant. Having married a woman of the Aquitanian people, he conquered the Swabians and other peoples of Germany in war. His son Grimoald succeeded him, and by his counsel King Sigebert of the Franks built various temples and monasteries.

units.la: Quo fatis functo Soror Beggacum marito Prouinciæ præfuit.
units.tr: When he died, his sister Begga governed the province together with her husband.

units.la: Nota. Soror Gertrudis inter Diuas est relata.
units.tr: Note: Sister Gertrude has been counted among the saints.

units.la: Matrem in gubernatione excepit filius Pipinus II. cognomento Herstallus,& in gubernatione 29.annos fuit.
units.tr: Her son Pippin II, surnamed Herstal, succeeded his mother in the government, and held it for 29 years.

units.la: Ex Plectrude filios habuit, Dragum, Grimoaldum, Christi fidei martyrem,& Siluium, & filiam Notburgin sanctam, Coloniæ sepultam. Omnium horum liberorum mortem vidit pater.
units.tr: By Plectrude he had sons: Drogo, Grimoald, a martyr of the Christian faith, and Silvius, and a daughter, Notburga, a saint, buried at Cologne. The father lived to see the death of all these children.

units.la: Frisii religionis Christianæ expertes, & passim grassantes,à Pipino, Traiecto capto, vincuntur, & ad fidem Christi conuertuntur, Guilibrardo antistite ad eos misso.
units.tr: The Frisians, ignorant of the Christian religion and raiding everywhere, were conquered by Pippin after he captured Utrecht, and were converted to the faith of Christ, with Willibrord, bishop, sent to them.

units.la: Pipinus ex Alpiade (cuiusdam Nobilis vxore) Carolum MartelMartellum suscepit, Pleétrude vxore adhuc superstite. Hoc coniugium cum S. Lambertus Episcopus Traiectensis reprehendisset, frater Alpiadis eum interfecit, hic vero phthiriasi correptus & punitus interiit.
units.tr: Pippin took Charles Martel as his son by Alpaida, the wife of a certain nobleman, while Plectrude was still alive. When Saint Lambert, bishop of Utrecht, rebuked this marriage, Alpaida's brother killed him; he himself was seized by lice-disease and died punished.

units.la: Carolus Martellus Saxones vicit, Alemanos & Sueuos subegit, Eudonem Visigotorum, Aquitaniae & Vasconiae principem fudit. Hunc vindicaturi Saraceni Burdegalam & Turonem vastarunt. Sed Martellus ad 70. M. Saracenorum occidit. Postremo Frisios subegit.
units.tr: Charles Martel conquered the Saxons, subdued the Alemanni and Swabians, and routed Eudo, prince of the Visigoths, of Aquitaine and Gascony. The Saracens, intending to avenge him, laid waste Bordeaux and Tours. But Martel killed 70,000 Saracens. Finally he subdued the Frisians.

units.la: Hilderico Francorum Rege mortuo, Carolus delatum sibi regnum recusauit: Imperare, inquiens, Regibus, quam Rex esse, malo. Et in locum patris demortui suffecit eius filium Dagobertum. Huic post quadriennium defuncto substituit huius fratrem Lotarium, post Chilperico cognato Regnum permisit, qui id 15. annos tenuit.
units.tr: When Hilderic, King of the Franks, died, Charles refused the kingdom offered to him, saying: "I would rather rule over kings than be king." In place of his dead father he set up his son Dagobert. After four years Dagobert died, and Charles put in his place Dagobert's brother Lothair. Afterwards he gave the kingdom to Chilperic, his cousin, who held it for 15 years.

units.la: Cum Luitbrandus Longobardus Romam obsideret, Gregorius III. Pont. postquam à Leone Imp. nihil opis habuit, Carolum hunc rogauit, vt Luitbrandum ad discessum ab vrbe permoueret, quod is tanquam ab amico summo obtinuit. Hinc Pontificum in Gallos propensio.
units.tr: When Liutprand the Lombard was besieging Rome, Pope Gregory III, having got no help from the Emperor Leo, asked this Charles to persuade Liutprand to withdraw from the city. He obtained this from Liutprand as from a close friend. Hence the Popes' inclination toward the Franks.

units.la: Carolomannus filius Austrasiam & Sueuiam accepit. Pipinus alter filius Burgundiam & Franciam. Sed Carolomanno sponte Monasterium Romae ingresso, Pipinus solus dominatum in omnibus obtinuit. Is Aquitanos & Alemanos deuicit. Hunc Zacharias P. Regem Galliae nuncupauit, qui cum Ecclesiae Romanae vehementer faueret, & Pontifices contra Longobardos tueretur, Christianissimi nomen consecutus est. Pinus contra Aquitanos bellum gessit, & Nauserico Aquitaniae Principi pacem dedit. Sed cum is tumultuari coepisset, Pipinus Carolum filium misit, qui eum compescuit.
units.tr: Carloman, the elder son, received Austrasia and Swabia; the other son, Pippin, received Burgundy and France. But when Carloman voluntarily entered a monastery at Rome, Pippin alone obtained dominion over everything. He conquered the Aquitanians and the Alemanni. Pope Zacharias named him King of the Gauls, and since he greatly favoured the Roman Church and defended the Popes against the Lombards, he won the name of Most Christian. Pippin waged war against the Aquitanians and gave peace to Nauserich, prince of Aquitaine. But when Nauserich began to stir up trouble, Pippin sent his son Charles, who restrained him.

units.la: Pipinus senex mortuus reliquit filios Carolomannum & Carolum Magnum, sed illo mortuo, hic solus Imperium obtinuit.
units.tr: Pippin died as an old man, leaving sons Carloman and Charles the Great; but when Carloman died, Charles alone held the empire.

units.la: Carolus Magnus iure belli Regno Galliae adiecit Aquitaniam niam, Vasconiam, Pyreneos montes, Italiam totam, Saxoni-am, Pannoniam, Daciam, Istriam, Liburniam, Dalmaciam, Sa-racenos in angulum Hispaniæ compulit. Vicit & Desiderium Longobardorum Regem Papæ hostem. Hadrianus Papa Carolum Romæ egregiis decretis ornatum dimisit.
units.tr: Charles the Great, by right of war, added to the kingdom of the Gauls Aquitaine, Gascony, the Pyrenees, all of Italy, Saxony, Pannonia, Dacia, Istria, Liburnia and Dalmatia; he drove the Saracens into a corner of Spain. He also defeated Desiderius, King of the Lombards, the enemy of the Pope. Pope Hadrian sent Charles away from Rome, adorned with excellent decrees.

units.la: Carolus Saxones rebelles domuit.
units.tr: Charles subdued the rebellious Saxons.

units.la: Vicit & Bauarum & Hunnos.
units.tr: He also conquered the Bavarians and the Huns.

units.la: Carolus à Leone Papa Romæ Imperator proclamatur.
units.tr: Charles was proclaimed Emperor at Rome by Pope Leo.

units.la: Carolus Scholam Parisiorum fundauit.
units.tr: Charles founded the school of Paris.

units.la: Ex Hildegarde habuit Ludouicum, Pipinum & Carolum. Ex Faftrada filias Theodoretam & Hiltrudem.
units.tr: By Hildegard he had Louis, Pippin and Charles. By Fastrada he had daughters, Theodrada and Hiltrud.

units.la: Ludouicus Pius filius Caroli M. dominium earum terrarum suscepit.
units.tr: Louis the Pious, son of Charles the Great, took over the rule of those lands.

units.la: Genealogiam Caroli M. vide in Epitome Regum Galliæ.
units.tr: See the genealogy of Charles the Great in the Epitome of the Kings of Gaul.

units.la: Quæ post Ludovici Pii Principatum gesta sunt, vsque ad tempora Godefridi Barbati, Ducis, qui Brabantiam, terram ab Arduennæ Principibus occupatam, primus recuperauit, ea haudquaquam incorruptis rerum gestarum monumentis tradita, nec affirmare nec refellere certum est. Ad Godefridum igitur Ducem pergemus.
units.tr: As for the events after the rule of Louis the Pious, up to the time of Godfrey Barbatus, Duke, who first recovered Brabant from the Princes of the Ardennes who had occupied it, it is not certain either to affirm or to refute them, since they have been handed down in records of events that are by no means intact. So we shall proceed to Duke Godfrey.

units.la: Godefridus Barbatus post Brabantiam armis recuperatam bellum indixit Arnouto, Principi Grunbergano, sed ab eo victus est. Barbati nomen accepit, quod patri promisisset, se non ante positurum barbam, quam recuperasset prouincias ademptas, Lotharingiam & Brabantiam. Valde commendatur à pietate propter constituta a b eo monasteria, tum à comitate & labore. Afflingini sepultus.
units.tr: Godfrey Barbatus, after recovering Brabant by arms, declared war on Arnold, Prince of Grunberg, but was defeated by him. He received the name Barbatus (the Bearded) because he had promised his father that he would not shave his beard until he had recovered the provinces taken from him, Lorraine and Brabant. He was highly commended for piety on account of the monasteries he founded, and also for courtesy and industry. He was buried at Affligem.

units.la: Godefridus II. filius bellum contra Henricum Lymburgæ Ducem, qui Lotharingiam vastabat, gessit, & Trudonis oppidum oppugnauit, occupauit, & magistratus nouos imposuit. Auxilio Aquensium Grunbergam rursus inuasit, sed irrito successu. Non multum supra triennium præfuit. Louanii sepultus.
units.tr: Godfrey II, his son, waged war against Henry, Duke of Limburg, who was ravaging Lorraine; he attacked and took the town of Tongeren and imposed new magistrates. With the help of the men of Aachen he again invaded Grunberg, but without success. He ruled for not much more than three years. He was buried at Leuven.

units.la: Godefridus. III. filius. Infans in aciem contra Grunberganos ganos delatus, vt Brabantini alacrius pugnarent. Idem olim fecerunt Macedones cum Illyricis dimicaturi.
units.tr: Godfrey III, son, was carried as an infant into the battle line against the men of Grunberg, so that the Brabanters would fight more eagerly. The Macedonians once did the same when about to fight the Illyrians.

units.la: Ex Margaretha Henrici Lymbergani filia suscepit Henricum, & Albertum Episcopum Leodiensem, & Aleydam, reginam Angliae.
units.tr: By Margaret, daughter of Henry of Limburg, he had Henry, Albert (bishop of Liège), and Aleyda, Queen of England.

units.la: Fames & terræmotus circa ea tempora.
units.tr: Famine and earthquakes occurred around this time.

units.la: Godefridus præfuit 43. annos, Louanii sepultus.
units.tr: Godfrey ruled for 43 years and was buried at Leuven.

units.la: Henricus I. filius gubernauit 48. annos, declaratus est Dux Principum, qui contra Turcam profecti sunt. A reditu cepit Florentium Comitem Hollandiae, & Otonem Geldricum.
units.tr: Henry I, son, governed for 48 years; he was declared leader of the princes who set out against the Turk. On his return he took Florent, Count of Holland, and Otto of Guelders.

units.la: Obsedit, cepit & vastauit Leodium, magna cæde patrata: sed Episcopus Leod. vindictam meditans, duo millia Brabantinorum occidit.
units.tr: He besieged, took and ravaged Liège, with great slaughter. But the bishop of Liège, meditating vengeance, killed two thousand Brabanters.

units.la: Anno M.CC.XIV. Oto IV. Imp. Traiecti duxit Mariam filiam Henrici huius, & huius auxilio bellum cum Rege Franc. gessit, sed magno prælio facto dissipati sunt.
units.tr: In the year 1214, the Emperor Otto IV married Mary, daughter of this Henry, at Utrecht, and with her father's help waged war against the King of the Franks; but after a great battle they were scattered.

units.la: Henricus II. magnanimus, filius illius, regnauit 22. annos.
units.tr: Henry II, the magnanimous, his son, reigned for 22 years.

units.la: Ex Philippi Imp. filia suscepit filium & filias 4. Ex Sophia pientissima fœmina habuit filium Henricum III.
units.tr: By the daughter of Emperor Philip he had a son and four daughters. By Sophia, a most pious woman, he had a son, Henry III.

units.la: Coloniam frustra obsedit.
units.tr: He besieged Cologne in vain.

units.la: Albertus Magnus & Thomas Aquinas ea tempestate vixerunt.
units.tr: Albert the Great and Thomas Aquinas lived in that age.

units.la: Innocentius IV. P. hunc Henricum contra Fridericum II. Imperatorem creari voluit, sed Henricus hanc dignitatem recusauit.
units.tr: Pope Innocent IV wanted this Henry to be elected against the Emperor Frederick II, but Henry refused this dignity.

units.la: Henricus III. filius, pacis cultor rexit 13. annos, genuit Henricum ad gubernationem non idoneum, & Iohannem, & Godefridum, & Mariam Regi Galliae nuptam.
units.tr: Henry III, son, a lover of peace, ruled for 13 years. He begot Henry, who was unfit for government, and John, and Godfrey, and Mary, who was married to the King of France.

units.la: Iohannes I. filius, ex Guidonis Flandriae Comitis filia suscepit Iohannem.
units.tr: John I, son, had a son, John, by the daughter of Guy, Count of Flanders.

units.la: Gessit bellum ob Geldriam & Limburgum.
units.tr: He waged war over Guelders and Limburg.

units.la: Episcopum Colonienfem magno prælio vicit & cepit. Arcem Worenk, ex qua mercatores Colonienses & Iuliacenses infestabantur, diruit.
units.tr: He defeated and captured the bishop of Cologne in a great battle. He destroyed the fortress of Worringen, from which the merchants of Cologne and Jülich were being harassed.

units.la: Iohannes sororem in Gallia à Petro Brosemo falso delatam asseruit, & calumniatorem hunc laqueo suspendit.
units.tr: John vindicated his sister, who had been falsely accused in France by Pierre Brosse, and hanged this slanderer on the gallows.

units.la: Anno M.CC.LXXXIII. moritur Aloys mater Iohannis I. Louanii sepulta pientissima foemina.
units.tr: In 1283 Aleyda, the mother of John I, died, a most pious woman, buried at Leuven.

units.la: Margaretham filiam matrimonio iunxit Henrico iuniori Lucembergensi Duci, qui postea factus est Imperator.
units.tr: He married his daughter Margaret to Henry the Younger, Duke of Luxembourg, who afterwards became Emperor.

units.la: Iohannes in nuptiis Regis Angliae in hastiludio laesus obiit, sepultus Bruxellis apud Minoritas.
units.tr: John was injured in a joust at the wedding of the King of England and died; he was buried at Brussels among the Minorites.

units.la: Iohannes II. filius gubernauit 19. annos.
units.tr: John II, son, governed for 19 years.

units.la: Philippus IV. Rex Franc. Flandriam occupat, Guidone eius terrae Principe cum duobus filiis capto, propterea quod Guido Princeps Flandriae filiam suam, quam Rex ex baptismo susceperat, filio Regis Angliae nuptui dare voluerat. Sed cladem accipit, dum Flandri Gallorum equos fustibus caedunt, & maxima nobilitas Gallorum caeditur.
units.tr: Philip IV, King of the Franks, occupied Flanders, capturing Count Guy, prince of that land, together with two sons, because Guy, Prince of Flanders, had wished to give his daughter, whom the King had received at baptism, in marriage to the son of the King of England. But the French suffered a disaster, while the Flemings beat the French horses with clubs, and the greatest nobility of the French was slaughtered.

units.la: Redit Philippus, & Insulas obsidet, sed fit transactio, Guido dimittitur.
units.tr: Philip returned and besieged the islands, but a settlement was reached and Guy was released.

units.la: Henricus Lucemberg. Imp. libertatem vendendi salis & piscium ad Antuerpienses transtulit. Hinc motus ciuiles inter Mechlinenses & Bruxellenses.
units.tr: Henry of Luxembourg, Emperor, granted the Antwerpers the liberty of selling salt and fish. Hence civil disturbances arose between the men of Mechlin and of Brussels.

units.la: Iohannes III. filius praefuit 43. annos, iustus & modestus Princeps, propter bella patris & aui contractum est aes alienum, quod mercatores, ne rapinis creditorum vexarentur, exoluerunt.
units.tr: John III, son, ruled for 43 years, a just and modest prince. Because of his father's and grandfather's wars, debt had been incurred, which the merchants paid off, so that they would not be harassed by the plundering of creditors.

units.la: Anno M.CCC.XV. propter 10. Mensium pluuias maxima fames orta, sequuta miserabilis pestis, conspectus Cometa.
units.tr: In 1315, because of ten months of rain, a great famine arose, followed by a wretched plague; a comet was seen.

units.la: Iohannes obsedit & cepit Sitterium, propterea quod Haynutus Falkenburgensis Traiectenses infestauit.
units.tr: John besieged and took Zierikzee, because Hainault of Falkenburg was harassing the people of Utrecht.

units.la: Vixit tunc Iohannes Mandeuil, Anglus, qui fere totum orbem terrarum peragrauit.
units.tr: At that time lived John Mandeville, an Englishman, who travelled over almost the whole world.

units.la: Mechliniae incendium.
units.tr: Fire at Mechlin.

units.la: Filii Iohannis III. omnes sine liberis discesserunt. Filia Iohanna hanna nupsit Wenceslao, Iohannis Bohemiæ Regis filio, Caroli IV. Imp. fratri.
units.tr: All the sons of John III departed this life without children. His daughter Joanna married Wenceslas, son of John, King of Bohemia, brother of the Emperor Charles IV.

units.la: Wenceslaus gener Iohannis III. succedit in Brabantia.
units.tr: Wenceslaus, son-in-law of John III, succeeds in Brabant.

units.la: Cum mercatores Brabantini iter per terram Iuliacensem facerent, & spoliarentur, ibi Wenceslaus contra Wilhelmum Iuliacensem pugnauit, & ab illo captus est. Sed Wilhelmus Iuliacensis Caroli IV. Imper. fratris eius minis coactus eum liberum dimisit.
units.tr: When Brabantine merchants were travelling through the land of Jülich and were being robbed, Wenceslaus fought there against William of Jülich and was taken captive by him. But William of Jülich, compelled by the threats of his brother Charles IV, the Emperor, released him freely.

units.la: Wenceslaus, vt & cæteros proceres captiuos redimeret, exactiones instituit, inde motus ciuilis apud Louanienses ortus, qui ægrè sopitus est.
units.tr: Wenceslaus, in order to ransom the other captive nobles too, imposed levies. From this a civil disturbance arose among the people of Louvain, which was with difficulty quelled.

units.la: Wenceslaus obit Lucemburgi.
units.tr: Wenceslaus dies at Luxembourg.

units.la: Iohanna vidua post obitum Wenceslai mariti Brabantiam gubernauit, & Geldrum vicit, obiit anno 1406.
units.tr: After the death of her husband Wenceslaus, the widow Joanna governed Brabant and conquered Guelders. She died in 1406.

units.la: Successit in Brabantiæ Principatu Antonius, Philippi Audacis Valesii Burgundiæ Ducis secundo genitus filius.
units.tr: Antony, the second son of Philip the Bold of Valois, Duke of Burgundy, succeeded to the principality of Brabant.

units.la: Nota: Obseruandum hic est, quomodo deinceps Germaniæ inferioris regiones, antea diuersis Principibus parentes, quatuor Francorum Dominorum Burgundiæ Ducum auspiciis tandem sint connexæ, & in vnum Principatum redactæ. Qui fuerunt (post Ludouicum Flandriæ Comitem) Philippus Audax Antonius, Philippus Bonus, & Carolus Pugnax.
units.tr: Note: Here it should be observed how the regions of Lower Germany, formerly ruled by various princes, were at last joined together under the auspices of four Dukes of Burgundy, French lords, and brought into a single principality. They were (after Louis, Count of Flanders) Philip the Bold, Antony, Philip the Good, and Charles the Bold.

units.la: Nam Iohannæ filiæ Iohannis III. Brabantii, Wenceslai viduæ, soror fuit Margaretha, quæ nupsit Ludouico Flandriæ Comiti, suscepit filiam Margaretham.
units.tr: For Margaret, the sister of Joanna, daughter of John III of Brabant and widow of Wenceslaus, was married to Louis, Count of Flanders, and bore a daughter, Margaret.

units.la: Hanc anno M. CCC. LXIX. duxit in vxorem Philippus Audax Valesius, Burgundiæ Dux, (qui fuit filius Iohannis Audacis Regis Galliæ) & ex ea suscepit Iohannem Intrepidum, qui in Burgundiæ ducatum successit, & Antonium, qui in Brabantiæ ducatum ratione Iohannæ magnæ materteræ suæ sufficitur. Huius Iohannis Intrepidi filius Philippus Bonus, deinde, Antonio & filiis Iohannæ & Philippo Ducibus Brabantiæ sine liberis demortuis Brabantiam Burgundiæ adiunxit, cui successit Carolus Pugnax, sicut in hac tabula videre est.
units.tr: In 1369 Philip the Bold of Valois, Duke of Burgundy (who was son of King John of France), took her as his wife, and by her had John the Fearless, who succeeded to the duchy of Burgundy, and Antony, who in right of his great-aunt Joanna was appointed Duke of Brabant. The son of this John the Fearless, Philip the Good, afterwards annexed Brabant to Burgundy, after Antony and the sons of Joanna and Philip, Dukes of Brabant, had died without children. Charles the Bold succeeded him, as can be seen in this table.

units.la: Iohannes III.
units.tr: John III.

units.la: 1. Iohanna vxor Wenceslai Bohem.
units.tr: 1. Joanna, wife of Wenceslaus of Bohemia.

units.la: 2. Margaretha vxor Ludouici Comitis Flandriae. Margaretha vxor Philippi Valesii Audacis, Ducis Burgund. filii Iohannis Regis Galliae.
units.tr: 2. Margaret, wife of Louis, Count of Flanders. Margaret, wife of Philip the Bold of Valois, Duke of Burgundy, son of King John of France.

units.la: 1. Iohannes Intrepidus.
units.tr: 1. John the Fearless.

units.la: 2. Antonius, Dux Brabantiae.
units.tr: 2. Antony, Duke of Brabant.

units.la: 3. Philippus Neuers Dux Brabantiae. Philip-bonus.
units.tr: 3. Philip, Duke of Brabant. Philip the Good.

units.la: 1. Iohannes, Duces Brabantiae.
units.tr: 1. John, Dukes of Brabant.

units.la: 2. Philippus. Carolus Pugnax. Maria vxor Maximiliani Imperatoris. Philippus I. Rex Hispan. Carolus V. Imp. Rex Hisp. Philippus II. Rex Hispan. Philippus III. Rex Hispan. SVCCESSORES Brabantiae. Iohannes III. Wenceslaus. Iohanna vidua. Antonius Burgun. Iohannes. Philippus. Philip-bonus. Carolus pugnax. Maximilianus Imp. &c. Ludouicus Mulauus fuit filius Ludouici Niuernensis. Comes Flandriæ decimus septimus, Niuercii Rhetelii dominus Salınarum & Mechliniæ, paterna, Comes inferioris Burgundiæ & Artesiæ materna hæreditate.
units.tr: 2. Philip. Charles the Bold. Mary, wife of Emperor Maximilian. Philip I, King of Spain. Charles V, Emperor and King of Spain. Philip II, King of Spain. Philip III, King of Spain. SUCCESSORS in Brabant: John III. Wenceslaus. Joanna, widow. Antony of Burgundy. John. Philip. Philip the Good. Charles the Bold. Maximilian, Emperor, etc. Louis of Male was the son of Louis of Nevers, seventeenth Count of Flanders, lord of Nevers, Rethel, Salins and Mechelen, holding by paternal inheritance, and Count of Lower Burgundy and Artois by maternal inheritance.

units.la: Philippus audax eius gener, filius Iohannis Valesii audacis Regis Galliæ, cognomen audacis accepit, quod patri in prælio apud Pictones Anno M. CCC. LVI. assiduus manserit comes, cum capto captus & in Angliam simul adductus.
units.tr: Philip the Bold, his son-in-law, son of John of Valois, King of France, received the nickname "the Bold" because at the battle of Poitiers in 1356 he remained constantly at his father's side as companion, and was captured along with him and led together with him into England.

units.la: Iohannes Valesius intrepidus, filius Philippi natu maximus, duxit Margaretham Alberti Bauari Comitis Hannoniæ, Hollandiæ, Zelandiæ, & domini Frisiæ filiam, & omnium paternorum & maternorum dominiorum solus hæres est.
units.tr: John the Fearless of Valois, the eldest son of Philip, married Margaret, daughter of Albert of Bavaria, Count of Hainault, Holland and Zeeland and lord of Friesland, and is the sole heir of all the paternal and maternal dominions.

units.la: Anno M. CCC. XCVI. à patre in Hungariam cum multis Belgis & Gallis in subsidium Sigismundi Imp. contra Turcam missus, & à Baiasete captus ducentis millibus Coronatorum redemptus domum rediit. Patris partes acerrimè defendit in dissidiis contra Ducem Aurelianum, Galliæ Regis fratrem, administrationis Regni causa Rege Carolo sexto certis temporum spaciis furore correpto.
units.tr: In 1396 he was sent by his father into Hungary with many Belgians and French to aid Sigismund, the Emperor, against the Turks. Captured by Bayezid, he was ransomed for two hundred thousand crowns and returned home. He defended his father's cause most fiercely in the disputes against the Duke of Orléans, brother of the King of France, over the administration of the kingdom, since King Charles VI was at certain periods seized by madness.

units.la: Iohannes anno M.CCCC. VII. Ducem Aurelianum Parisiis noctu interfici curat. Hinc horrida bella, Aureliani prolibus confæderatorum potentia fretis cædem patris vlcisci conantibus.
units.tr: In 1407 John had the Duke of Orléans killed by night at Paris. Hence came dreadful wars, as the sons of Orléans, relying on the power of their allies, tried to avenge their father's slaying.

units.la: Anno M.CCCC. XVIII. Parisienses Burgundo addicti, accersito Lutetiam Burgundico præsidio, centum viginti nobiles, & quatuor millia plebeiorum ex Aurelianis interemerunt, corporibus Burgundicis crucibus incisis.
units.tr: In 1418 the Parisians, devoted to Burgundy, summoned a Burgundian garrison to Lutetia and slew a hundred and twenty nobles and four thousand commoners of the Orléans party, with crosses cut into the bodies of the Burgundians.

units.la: Interim Angli totam fere Normanniam in potestatem suam redigunt, quibus dum Galli vnanimes resistere satagunt, Delphinus Carolus & Aureliani fictam pacem cum Burgundo ineunt, qua iureiurando confirmata, locus colloquutioni constituitur Montleri oppido supra Lutetiam super ponte: Ibi in consalutatione Iohannes Burgundus cæditur anno M. CCCC.XIX. ætatis 48. Hinc bellum inter Gallos & Burgundos gundos sedecim annos durauit, & Angli prope vniuersam Galliam occuparunt, donec à Philippo bono filio compositum est.
units.tr: Meanwhile the English brought almost all of Normandy under their power. While the French strove to resist them with one accord, Dauphin Charles and the Duke of Orléans made a feigned peace with Burgundy. When this was confirmed by oath, a place for a conference was fixed at the town of Montereau, above Paris, on the bridge. There, at the greeting, John of Burgundy was cut down in 1419, in his forty-eighth year. Hence the war between the French and the Burgundians lasted sixteen years, and the English occupied nearly the whole of France, until it was settled by Philip the Good, his son.

units.la: Iohannes aliquando 30. Millia Leodiensium occidit.
units.tr: John once killed 30,000 men of Liège.

units.la: Antonius, secundus Philippi Audacis filius Dux Brabantiæ factus est ex dispositione, patris Philippi Valesii.
units.tr: Antony, the second son of Philip the Bold, was made Duke of Brabant by the arrangement of his father, Philip of Valois.

units.la: Antonius hic terras à facinorosis hominibus purgauit. Apud Leodienses maximus motus fuit propter electionem Episcoporum.
units.tr: This Antony cleared the lands of criminals. Among the people of Liège there was a very great disturbance over the election of bishops.

units.la: Antonius, auxiliaturus Gallo, in pugna contra Anglos occiditur. Bruxellis sepultus, Princeps industrius. Strenuus, reliquit filios Iohannem & Philippum, Brabantiæ successores.
units.tr: Antony, about to aid the Frenchman, was killed in battle against the English. Buried at Brussels, an industrious and vigorous prince, he left sons John and Philip, successors in Brabant.

units.la: Iohannes quartus Antonio patri in Brabantia & reliquis ditionibus successit. Vxorem duxit Iacobam Wilhelmi à Beyern Comitis Hannoniæ & Hollandiæ filiam. Iacoba hæc, quod non permitteretur ei suo arbitratu viuere, & quod sibi familiares adimerentur, in Angliam discessit, & ibi Gloucestria nupsit, qui Caletum veniens Hannoniam nomine vxoris occupat. Sed Iohannes Hollandiam (ne & eam is occuparet) per fratrem Philippum protexit, & ab Hollandis, Frisiis & Zelandis honorifice susceptus est. Iacoba hæc causa multorum bellorum fuit.
units.tr: John IV succeeded his father Antony in Brabant and the other dominions. He married Jacoba, daughter of William of Bavaria, Count of Hainault and Holland. This Jacoba, because she was not allowed to live as she pleased and her household attendants were taken away from her, went off to England, and there married Gloucester. He, coming to Calais, seized Hainault in his wife's name. But John protected Holland, lest Gloucester seize that too, through his brother Philip, and was honourably received by the Hollanders, Frisians and Zeelanders. This Jacoba was the cause of many wars.

units.la: Anno M.CCCCXXI. multi pagi in Hollandia ruptis aggeribus vndis absorpti & summersi sunt.
units.tr: In 1421 many villages in Holland were swallowed up and submerged by the waves after the dikes were broken.

units.la: Iacoba iudicio Romæ à Gloucestria separata est, neque tamen Iohannes eam recepit.
units.tr: Jacoba was separated from Gloucester by a judgement at Rome, yet John did not take her back.

units.la: Anno M.CCCCXXV. fundatum est Gymnasium Louaniense. Iohannes obit Anno M. CCCC.XXVI. Princeps laudatus.
units.tr: In 1425 the university of Louvain was founded. John died in 1426, a praised prince.

units.la: Philippus frater Iohannis successit, tantum triennium praefuit, & duceturus Iolentam, Ludouici Siciliæ Regis filiam, moritur. Maximi terræ motus extitere. In Cathalonia viginti vrbes euersæ.
units.tr: Philip, John's brother, succeeded him and held office for only three years. About to marry Isabella, daughter of Louis, King of Sicily, he died. Very great earthquakes occurred. In Catalonia twenty towns were overthrown.

units.la: Filiis Antonii siue hæredibus defunctis, peruenit Brabantia ad Philippum Valesium Bonum, Iohannis intrepidi patrui Philippi filium.
units.tr: With the sons of Antony, or their heirs, dead, Brabant passed to Philip of Valois the Good, son of Philip, uncle of John the Fearless.

units.la: Philippus Valesius Bonus, cum anno M.CCCC.XIX. successisset patri in Ducatu Burgundiæ, patruelibus quoque in Ducatu Brabantiæ anno M.CCCC.XXX. succedit. Fuit Princeps benignus, cordatus, & inde cognominatus Bonus. Vltioni mortis paternæ animum statim intendit.
units.tr: Philip of Valois the Good, having succeeded his father in the duchy of Burgundy in 1419, also succeeded his cousins in the duchy of Brabant in 1430. He was a kindly and judicious prince, and so was surnamed the Good. He at once set his mind on avenging his father's death.

units.la: In Galliam profectus Regem adit, bellum inter Gallum & Anglum dirimit, ea lege, vt Henricus V. Angliæ Rex, Catharina Caroli VI. Galliæ Regis filia in vxorem ducta, ei in Regno succederet, Carolo Delphino (prædictæ cædis causa) excluso & exhæredato. Hoc matrimonio natus Henricus VI. Angliæ Rex, qui, patre Henrico & auo materno Carolo mortuis, puerili ætate Rex Angliæ & Galliæ coronatur. Bellum itaque Angli, Burgundi & Galli in Delphinum gerunt, qui post patris sui mortem titulum Caroli septimi Gallorum Regis sibi assumpsit. Verum postea dissidio & intestino bello in Anglia, gubernaculi atque tituli Regni gratia inter familias Loucestriam & Eboracensem, nominibus albæ & rubræ rosæ distinctas, exorto, Anglis paulatim possessiones in Galliis ademptæ, Philippus quoque ab Anglis alienior factus, eâ (inter plures alias) maxime causa, quod Angliæ gubernator Dux Gloucestrinus patruus Regis vxorem duxisset Iacobam filiam atque hæredem Hannoniæ, Hollandiæ, Zeladiæ & Frisiæ, cui tetra erat discordia cum marito suo superstite Iohanne, (Philippi Burgundi fratris Antonii filio Iacoba quoque auunculi sui filia) quem diuortii quadam specie reliquerat, nuptias causata incestas, quod amitimi essent.
units.tr: Going into France, he approached the King and settled the war between the Frenchman and the Englishman, on the condition that Henry V, King of England, having married Catherine, daughter of Charles VI, King of France, should succeed to the kingdom, Charles the Dauphin being excluded and disinherited because of the aforesaid murder. Born of this marriage was Henry VI, King of England, who, on the death of his father Henry and his maternal grandfather Charles, was crowned King of England and France while still a boy. So the English, Burgundians and French waged war on the Dauphin, who after his father's death assumed for himself the title of Charles VII, King of the French. But afterwards a dissension and civil war broke out in England over the government and the title of the kingdom, between the houses of Lancaster and York, named after the white and red roses. The English gradually lost their possessions in France, and Philip too became more estranged from the English, chiefly (among many other reasons) because the English governor, the Duke of Gloucester, uncle of the King, had married Jacoba, daughter and heiress of Hainault, Holland, Zeeland and Friesland. He had left her in a bitter discord with her living husband John (son of Antony, and so Philip's nephew; Jacoba too was his daughter of an uncle), under a kind of divorce, alleging an incestuous marriage, because they were related within the forbidden degrees.

units.la: Gloucestrius armata manu in Hollandiam, postea in Zelandiam vxoris suæ ditiones possessurus irrumpit, sed frustra, ægerrime id ferente Philippo, quod Hannonia, Hollandia, Zelandia & Frisia ad eum, mortua sine prole Iacoba, deuenire deberent. His aliisque de causis Philippus consultò se ad reconciliationem cum Delphino (tunc Rege) induci non est grauatus. tus. Rex enim Papæ & Cardinalium, Dei vindicta propósita, Ducem impellentium, intercessione, indesinenter quibusuis conditionibus Duci reconciliare studebat.
units.tr: Gloucester, with an armed force, burst into Holland and afterwards into Zeeland, intending to take possession of his wife's dominions, but in vain. Philip took it very badly that Hainault, Holland, Zeeland and Friesland ought to come to him, Jacoba having died without issue. For these and other reasons Philip did not hesitate to be deliberately drawn into reconciliation with the Dauphin, who was then King. For the King, through the intercession of the Pope and the cardinals, who urged the Duke, setting before him the vengeance of God, unceasingly strove to be reconciled with the Duke on any terms whatever.

units.la: Pax itaque post 13. annorum bellum Atrebaci compositā anno M.CCCC.XXXV. summo Philippi commodo & honore, qui hinc multas regiones & ditiones, vltionem quoque & insignem satisfactionem, de patris nece assecutus est.
units.tr: Thus, after the thirteen-year war was ended by the peace concluded at Arras in 1435, Philip gained great advantage and honour, since from it he obtained many regions and lordships, and also vengeance and a notable satisfaction for his father's murder.

units.la: Huius tam candidæ pacificationis, aliarumque egregiarum virtutum ergo, Philippus cognomento bonus dictus, maximè autem quod Ducem Aurelianum (cuius pater ab huius patre trucidatus, vnde capitale odium primo ortum) 25. annos à prælio Aziucurtio in Anglia carceri mancipatum ducentis millibus coronatis redemerit; sororem præterea suam Mariam vxorem ei dederit, quibus beneficiis inimicitias ob cædem factam prorsus extinxit.
units.tr: For the sake of this so candid pacification and his other outstanding virtues, Philip was surnamed "the Good." This was chiefly because he ransomed Duke Orléans for two hundred thousand crowns. The duke's father had been butchered by Philip's father, which was where the deadly hatred first arose, and the duke had been held in prison in England for 25 years since the battle of Azincourt. Philip also gave his sister Mary to him as his wife. By these kindnesses he completely extinguished the enmity caused by the killing.

units.la: Philippus Bonus primo Dux Burgundiæ, Comes Flandriæ, inferioris Burgundiæ, Antesiæ, Palatinus sacri Imperii, Marckgrafius, Salinarum & Mechliniæ Dominus, multis ditionibus postea auctus fuit.
units.tr: Philip the Good was first Duke of Burgundy, Count of Flanders, of Lower Burgundy and of Artois, Palatine of the Holy Roman Empire, Margrave, and Lord of Salins and Mechelen. He was afterwards enlarged by many further lordships.

units.la: Morte enim Theodori Comitis Namurcensis Comitatum Namurcensem Anno M.CCCC.XXIX. præterea cognati sui Philippi Ducis Brabantiæ absque liberis defuncti, Ducatus Lotharingiæ, Brabantiæ, Limburgi insuper Iacobæ suæ consanguineæ sine prole mortuæ, Comitatum Hannoniæ, Hollandiæ, Zelandiæ & Frisiæ ditionem nactus est. Postremo quoque Ducatu Lucemburgensi potitus est anno M.CCCC.XLIII. Elisabetha enim Dux Lucemburgi vidua Antonii Brabantiæ Ducis Philippi patrui, cum subditos suos sibi minus obedientes ægrè ferret, Philippo tanquam tutori possessionem suam transtulit, certa pensione annua sibi reseruata.
units.tr: On the death of Count Theodore of Namur, he obtained the County of Namur in 1429. Then, when his cousin Philip, Duke of Brabant, died without children, he gained the Duchies of Lorraine, Brabant and Limburg. Further, on the death without issue of his cousin Jacqueline, he gained the County of Hainault and the lordship of Holland, Zeeland and Friesland. Lastly he took possession of the Duchy of Luxembourg in 1443. Elizabeth, Duchess of Luxembourg and widow of Anthony, Duke of Brabant, Philip's uncle, was unhappy that her subjects were less obedient to her, so she transferred her possession to Philip as guardian, reserving a fixed annual pension for herself.

units.la: Bella varia gessit earum regionum causa. Gandauenses & Leodienses domuit. Ordinem aurei Velleris, tempore, quo Isabellam vxorem duxit, Anno M.CCCC.XXX. Burgis instituit. Statuit pręterea regimen aulicum certis officiis, quod
units.tr: He waged various wars for the sake of these regions. He subdued the people of Ghent and of Liège. In 1430, at the time when he married Isabella, he founded the Order of the Golden Fleece at Bruges. He also set up a court government with fixed offices, which

units.la: C Hispanica & Austriaca familia in hunc vsque diem seruat.
units.tr: the Spanish and Austrian house keeps to this day.

units.la: Anno M. CCCC. XXXVII. Philippus Caletum Anglorum obsidet, sed rursum discedit. Burgenses rebellarunt, qui ad extremum impetrarunt veniam, sic vt 18. viri nudis pedibus incedere sint coacti.
units.tr: In 1437 Philip besieged Calais, held by the English, but again withdrew. The men of Bruges rebelled, and at last obtained pardon, though eighteen of them were forced to walk barefoot.

units.la: Fuit Philippus vrbanus, magnificus, sumptuosus, splendidus corporis ornatu, supellectili, conuiuiis & sumptibus, bellicosus, hosti (Mahometi etiam Turcarum Imperatori) formidabilis. Eius consuetudinis studiosi Angli, Galli, Pontifices, Imperatores, Reges, Duces, aliique Principes. Et quanquam munificentissimus, sumptuosissimus atque bellicosissimus (cum 48. annos continuos bella gesserit, arduaque superauerit) acerbis tamen exactionibus subditos suos non grauauit, florentibus summopere omni rerum abundantia regionibus.
units.tr: Philip was urbane, magnificent, sumptuous and splendid in his personal dress, his household furnishings, his banquets and his expenses. He was warlike and formidable to his enemies, even to Mahomet, the Turkish emperor. Englishmen, Frenchmen, Popes, Emperors, Kings, Dukes and other princes were keen to imitate his habits. He was most generous, most lavish and most warlike: he waged wars for 48 years without a break and overcame hard difficulties. Yet he did not burden his subjects with harsh exactions, and his lands flourished greatly in every kind of abundance.

units.la: Reliquit legitimum haeredem filium vnicum, Carolum; nothos autem quatuordecim, quos ad summos honores prouexit.
units.tr: He left one legitimate heir, his son Charles, but fourteen illegitimate sons, whom he raised to the highest honours.

units.la: Anno M. CCCC. LXIV. Pius II. Papa Principes Europae ad bellum contra Turcas gerendum incitauit. Philippus se & militem parauit, sed propter senium ipse non abiuit, sed Antonium filium nothum misit, qui cum in Galliam veniisset, vidit literas quasi a patre scriptas, quibus mandabatur, vt occideretur. Ideo is non processit amplius. Literae ex non a patre, sed a Consiliariis quibusdam scriptae putabantur.
units.tr: In 1464 Pope Pius II urged the princes of Europe to wage war against the Turks. Philip prepared himself and his soldiers, but because of his old age he did not go himself. Instead he sent his illegitimate son Anthony, who, when he came into France, saw a letter apparently written by his father, ordering that he be killed. Therefore he went no further. The letter was thought to have been written not by the father but by certain counsellors.

units.la: Philippus Dauentrienses obsedit, quod obstitissent, ne Dauid Philippi filius eligeretur in Episcopum Traiectensem.
units.tr: Philip besieged Deventer, because the people there had opposed David, Philip's son, being elected Bishop of Utrecht.

units.la: Philippus obiit Brugis anno M.CCCC.LXVII. aetatis 72. regni Burgundiae anno XLVIII. Brabantiae XXXVII. Omnium honorum, statuum & dignitatum affluentissimus, vtpote cui, recusanti tamen, etiam sacrum Romanum Imperium offeretur. Gemmarum & vasorum pretiosorum singularis amator.
units.tr: Philip died at Bruges in 1467, aged 72, in the 48th year of his reign in Burgundy and the 37th in Brabant. He was the most abundantly endowed with honours, estates and dignities of all men, and although he refused it, the Holy Roman Empire was offered to him. He was a singular lover of gems and precious vessels.

units.la: Carolus Pugnax filius succedit Philippo bono anno M. CCCC.LXVII. aetatis 34. natus est Digii Burgundiae anno M.
units.tr: His son Charles the Bold succeeded Philip the Good in 1467. He was aged 34, and was born at Dijon in Burgundy in

units.la: CCCC.XXXIV. Didicit Latinas literas, imbutus etiā Musicis. Doctorum Mecoenas fuit, preces canonicas ipsemet legit. Cæsteynius quidam patrisConsiliarius Carolo infensus cogitauit eum veneno necare, quod resciens Carolus permissu patris eum supplicio affici curauit, ac per id odiumConsiliariorum in se concitauit, & sic pater ei valde infestus est redditus, quem tamen Antonius nothus patri rursus reconciliauit.
units.tr: 1434. He learned Latin letters and was also trained in music. He was a patron of learned men, and he himself read the canonical prayers. A certain Cæsteynius, a counsellor of his father, who was hostile to Charles, planned to kill him with poison. Charles discovered this and, with his father's permission, had the man executed. By this he stirred up the hatred of the counsellors against himself, and his father became very hostile to him. Anthony, his illegitimate brother, nevertheless reconciled him to their father again.

units.la: Prima expeditio Caroli fuit in Ludouicum Regem Galliæ, quem ad montem Henrici magno prælio vicit. In Gallia reddidit quæ occuparat.
units.tr: Charles's first campaign was against Louis, King of France, whom he defeated in a great battle at Mont-l'Héry. In France he gave back what he had seized.

units.la: Vxor Isabella in eius absentia mortua est, sepulta Antuerpiæ, fæmina in pauperes benefica.
units.tr: His wife Isabella died in his absence and was buried at Antwerp. She was a woman generous to the poor.

units.la: Dionatenses ad Mosam ope Leodiorum Brabantiam & Hannoniam vastant, contemptim de Philippo patre Caroli loquentes, sed Carolus eos bello inuasit, & vrbem deleuit.
units.tr: The men of Dinant, with the help of the people of Liège, laid waste Brabant and Hainault along the Meuse, speaking contemptuously of Philip, Charles's father. But Charles attacked them in war and destroyed their town.

units.la: Philippus pater moritur Anno M.CCCC.LXVII.
units.tr: Philip the father died in 1467.

units.la: Ad primum ingressum Caroli impunitas concessa est plus octingentis maleficis, qui cum Principe Gandauum sunt ingressi. Immigratio eximia pompa facta est.
units.tr: At Charles's first entry, impunity was granted to more than eight hundred criminals, who entered Ghent with the Prince. The entry was made with remarkable pomp.

units.la: Gandauii tumultus exortus est. Ciues enim sua priuilegia repetiuerunt, quæ pater ipsis ademerat, id quod Carolus in civitate existens ex metu promisit: verum à discessu recusauit. Gandauenses postea veniam petunt & obtinent.
units.tr: A tumult broke out at Ghent. The citizens demanded back the privileges which his father had taken from them. Charles, while in the city, promised this out of fear, but on leaving he refused to keep his word. Afterwards the men of Ghent asked for pardon and obtained it.

units.la: Mechlinienses domum profecti euerterunt, sed coacti sunt eandem reficere, ob idque multa ciuibus priuilegia adempta sunt.
units.tr: The people of Mechelen went to the house and tore it down, but they were forced to rebuild it. Because of this, many privileges were taken from the citizens.

units.la: Carolus Leodienses bello aggreditur, & eos veniam petere cogit.
units.tr: Charles attacked the people of Liège in war and forced them to ask for pardon.

units.la: Nuptiæ Caroli cum Margaretha sorore Eduardi Quarti Anglorum Regis Brugis supra modum splendidè celebratæ sunt. In fidem recipit Hollandos.
units.tr: The marriage of Charles and Margaret, sister of Edward IV, King of the English, was celebrated at Bruges with extraordinary splendour. He took the Hollanders under his protection.

units.la: Anno M.CCCC.LXVIII. Leodienses rebellarūt. Vrbs fuit amplissima, 3 z. templis parochialibus magnifica, eam obsidet Carolus, auxilio Ludouici Regis Galliæ, quam captam diripuit. ripuit. Supplices vna manu exertum gladium, altera facem ardentem, gestare coacti. Gallus cum Carolo ingressus pectore non rectam, sed Andreae crucem habuit, innuens omnem belli gloriam ad Carolum pertinere.
units.tr: In 1468 the people of Liège rebelled. The city was very large and magnificent, with many parish churches. Charles besieged it with the help of Louis, King of France, and after taking it he plundered it. The suppliants were forced to carry a drawn sword in one hand and a burning torch in the other. The Frenchman who entered with Charles wore on his breast not a straight cross but St Andrew's cross, signalling that all the glory of the war belonged to Charles.

units.la: Aquenses iuuerant Leodios commeatu. Et eos igitur Carolus adgredi parauit. Sed cum ei claues obuiam tulissent, & solutis 80. M. floren. veniam impetrarunt. Profugi Leodium remigrare & vrbem restaurare permittuntur.
units.tr: The people of Aachen had supplied the Liégeois with provisions. Charles therefore prepared to attack them. But when they came to meet him bearing the keys, and paid 80,000 florins, they obtained pardon. The exiles were allowed to return to Liège and restore the city.

units.la: Frisii imperium Caroli auersantur.
units.tr: The Frisians resisted Charles's rule.

units.la: Eduardus Rex Angliae socer Caroli a Nobilibus pulsus, hinc ante Catesium maxima caedes.
units.tr: Edward, King of England, Charles's father-in-law, was driven out by the nobles. Hence there was a great slaughter before Calais.

units.la: Anno M.CCCC.LXXII. Cometa conspectus.
units.tr: In 1472 a comet was seen.

units.la: Caroli opera dimissus est ann. M.CCCC.LXXIII. Antonius Geldriae Princeps, quem filius Adolphus septennium captiuum tenuerat & Adolphum custodiae tradit, anno 1473. Quod quidam sic referunt.
units.tr: Anthony, Prince of Guelders, was released in 1473 through the efforts of Charles. His son Adolf had held him captive for seven years, and Charles handed Adolf over to custody in 1473. Some report this as follows.

units.la: Haereditariis suis regionibus a patre relictis, Ducatum Geldriae, & comitatum Zutphaniae a Duce Arnoldo Egmondano nonaginta duob. coronatorum millibus emptos adiunxit, seruante Arnoldo annuam pensionem ad vitam. Quam quidem venditionem Arnoldus moriens testamento suo ratam esse voluit, Carolo duce herede instituto, exhaeredato autem filio suo Adolpho, ob summam eius in patrem contumaciam & rebellionem: toto enim sexennio patrem miserrime captiuum detinuerat.
units.tr: To the hereditary lands left to him by his father, Charles added the Duchy of Guelders and the County of Zutphen, which he had bought from Duke Arnold of Egmond for 92,000 crowns, Arnold keeping an annual pension for life. Arnold, when dying, wished this sale to be confirmed by his will, with Duke Charles named as heir and his son Adolf disinherited, on account of Adolf's great disobedience and rebellion against his father. For Adolf had kept his father most miserably captive for six years.

units.la: Hinc Carolus Dux, mortuo Adolpho, octoginta insuper mille florenis empta actione a Geraldo Iuliacensi Duce, filiis Wilhelmo & Adolpho consentientibus, atque Imperatore Friderico tertio concedente, Anno 1473. Geldriae possessionem nactus est, Adolpho in carcere Cornaci coniecto, qui post Caroli mortem ereptus, & Dux militiae contra Gallos factus in obsidione Cornatensi occubuit, relicto vnico filio Carolo, qui postea Bethimae cum Comite Engelberto Nassouio a Gallis captus, tandem ab iis in Geldriam mittitur, bellumq; contra Maximilianum Cæsarem, & Philippum Hispaniæ Regem, & Carolum V. Cæsarem gerit, vsque ad annum 1536. cum, dirempta omni controuersia, Carolum Cæsarem secundo heredem post suam mortem instituit, mortuus sine liberis Anno 1538.
units.tr: Hence Duke Charles, after Adolf's death, obtained possession of Guelders in 1473. He had additionally bought the claim for 80,000 florins from Gerard, Duke of Jülich, with the consent of Gerard's sons William and Adolf, and with the permission of Emperor Frederick III. Adolf had been thrown into prison at Cornaco. After Charles's death he was freed and made commander of the army against the French, and he died in the siege of Cornaco. He left a single son, Charles, who was later captured by the French at Béthune together with Count Engelbert of Nassau, and was finally sent back by them to Guelders. He waged war against Maximilian Caesar, Philip King of Spain, and Charles V Caesar, until 1536. Then, with all controversy settled, he named Charles Caesar his second heir after his death. He died without children in 1538.

units.la: Carolus Adolphi, qui Geldria cessit, filios semper honorificè sustentauit.
units.tr: Charles always honourably supported the sons of Adolf, who had yielded Guelders.

units.la: Carolus monet Geldros, vt sibi pareant, mox, cum exercitu Geldriam inuadit & subiugat. Carolus etiam Zutphaniæ solemnibus ceremoniis initiatur.
units.tr: Charles warned the people of Guelders to obey him. Soon with an army he invaded Guelders and subdued it. Charles was also initiated into the lordship of Zutphen with solemn ceremonies.

units.la: Eo anno æstas calidissima fuit.
units.tr: That year the summer was very hot.

units.la: Eo Anno Fridericus III. Imp. & Carolus Treuiris conuenerunt, & collocuti sunt. Carolus Fridericum splendidissimo conuiuio excepit.
units.tr: In that year Emperor Frederick III and Charles met at Trier and held talks. Charles entertained Frederick with a most splendid banquet.

units.la: Carolus Mechliniæ celebre Parlamentum instituit.
units.tr: Charles founded the famous Parliament at Mechlin.

units.la: Carolus patris & matris Isabellæ corpora Brugis in Burgundiam deportari curat, & Digii in Carthusiensium monasterio sepeliri.
units.tr: Charles had the bodies of his father and mother, Isabella, brought from Bruges to Burgundy and buried at Dijon in the Carthusian monastery.

units.la: Rupertus Bauarus Episcopus Coloniensis apud Carolum cognatum questus, quod circumiectę ciuitates obstarent, quo minus annuos suos prouentus ex iis locis colligere posset. Carolus igitur bellum in Colonienses parans Nouesium grauiter obsidet. Maxima in vrbe fames.
units.tr: Rupert of Bavaria, Archbishop of Cologne, complained to his cousin Charles that the neighbouring cities stood in the way of his collecting the annual revenues from those places. Charles therefore prepared war against the Cologners and laid siege to Neuss in earnest. Within the city there was the greatest famine.

units.la: Aduenit Fridericus Imp. cum exercitu, vt Carolum ab obsidione absterreret. Sed ille nihil territus in obsidione persecutus est, & per velitationes milites Cæsaris vicit. Postea opera Legati Papæ transactio facta est.
units.tr: Emperor Frederick arrived with an army to frighten Charles away from the siege. But Charles, not at all alarmed, pressed on with the siege, and by skirmishes he defeated the Emperor's soldiers. Afterwards, through the efforts of the Pope's legate, a settlement was made.

units.la: Ludouicus XI. Rex Galliæ in Arthesia & Picardia grassatur, obsessurus & Atrebacum: sed Carolus misso eo exercitu eum cohibet.
units.tr: Louis XI, King of France, ravaged Artois and Picardy, intending to besiege Arras as well. But Charles sent an army there and checked him.

units.la: Eduardus magnum exercitum cum Carolo coniungit, vt Gallum inuadant: Verum Gallus Legatione missa pacem petit, & inducias nouennales obtinet. Eduardus ad sua redit.
units.tr: Edward joined a great army with Charles in order to attack the Frenchman. But the Frenchman sent an embassy, sought peace, and obtained a truce of nine years. Edward returned home.

units.la: Carolus ob fœdera sibi non seruata, in Lotharingia, Renato in Galliam fugiente multa occupat & Nantium obsidet, & demum deditione capit, & sic totam Lotharingiam in obsequium reducit. Fuit haec ultima eius victoria. Vulgò creditum est, omni fauore Numinis destitutum eum postea nunquam feliciter pugnasse cum hoste, quod eodem tempore multò grauissimis exactionibus Clerum exoneraßet. Quanquam expedit nonnunquam (scribit Barlandus) quosdam ad frugalitatem vocare, sed satis iustæ ad id faciendum rationes acceßerint.
units.tr: Because the treaties made with him had not been kept, Charles seized much in Lorraine, while René fled into France, and he besieged Nancy, and at last took it by surrender; and so he brought all Lorraine back into obedience. This was his last victory. It was commonly believed that, deprived of the favour of heaven, he never afterwards fought successfully with the enemy, because at the same time he had burdened the clergy with very heavy exactions. Yet (Barlandus writes) it is sometimes expedient to call certain people to frugality, though there were reasons sufficiently just for doing so.

units.la: Subactis Lotharingis transtulit bellum in Heluetios, quod hi populi non multò antea Sabaudiam (vbi præerat neptis eius) tumultuose ingressi multa damna dederunt. Itaque primum sunt missi ab Heluetiis Legati, quos Princeps Carolus vix auditos iussit confestim abscedere, atque ipse eodem tempore sequutus in vrbe Gransouia, quam nonnulli dicunt ab eo tum expugnatam, plures Heluetios in crucem sustulit. Hinc Heluetii Carolum bello adorti sunt, in quo Carolus fusus & fugatus est, pridie Iohannis Baptistæ. Scribunt quidam hic periisse opes Caroli.
units.tr: Having subdued Lorraine, he turned the war against the Swiss, because these peoples, not long before, had entered Savoy tumultuously (where his niece was ruling) and caused much damage. Accordingly, first, envoys were sent by the Swiss, whom Prince Charles, having scarcely heard them, ordered to depart at once; and he himself, following at the same time, in the town of Grandson, which some say was then taken by him, put many Swiss to the cross. Thereupon the Swiss attacked Charles in war, in which Charles was routed and put to flight, the day before the feast of John the Baptist. Some write that here the resources of Charles perished.

units.la: Carolus vindictæ cupidissimus & irrequietissimus, exercitu altero comparato, contra Heluetios iterum infeliciter pugnat & fugit. Hic nobilitas eius periit.
units.tr: Charles, most eager for revenge and never at rest, having raised a second army, again fought unsuccessfully against the Swiss and fled. Here his nobility perished.

units.la: Sic Lotharingus animum recipiens Nanceam & terras suas recuperat. Carolus igitur collecto milite Nanceam obsidet, & euocatus ad pugnam in ea succumbit, in hoc prælio vitam suam amisit Anno 1477, pridie Epiphaniorum. Post diem tertium in fossa congelata nudo & glacie rigido corpore inuentus est. Huc autem calamitatis præcipue deuenit, proditione perfidi comitis Itali Campobassum, qui eo infidelitatis à Rege Ludouico inductus erat. Carolus .n. ministeria extraneorum potiora quàm suorum subditorum hac imprimis de causa habebat, quod operâ communitatis Flandriæ patri in obsidione Caletana, & auo in Hannouia apud Veromanduos minus feliciter successisset. Ea, quam dixi clade, Carolus ille magnanimus, totius Chri- stiani orbis, dum viueret, potentissimus, & bellicosissimus Princeps interemptus est, à paupere & tenui Heluetiorum plebe, & Duce Lotharingiæ, viginti annorum iuuene. Ille inquam Carolus, qui se alterum Alexandrum aut Carolum Magnum suis heroicis factis euasurum sperabat, hoc modo succubuit, cum regnasset annos decem, Anno ætatis suæ 44. relicta vnâ filia Maria hærede.
units.tr: Thus the Lorrainer took courage again and recovered Nancy and his lands. Charles, therefore, gathering soldiers, besieged Nancy, and, called out to battle there, he succumbed; in this battle he lost his life in the year 1477, the day before Epiphany. Three days later he was found in a frozen ditch, his naked body stiff with ice. The chief cause of this calamity was the treachery of the faithless Count Campobasso, an Italian, who had been induced to this disloyalty by King Louis. For Charles held foreigners in higher esteem than his own subjects, chiefly for this reason: that under the auspices of the Flemish commonalty his father had met with less success at the siege of Calais, and his grandfather in Hainaut among the Veromandui. By the disaster I have described, that magnanimous Charles, while he lived the most powerful and most warlike prince of the whole Christian world, was slain, by the poor and humble common people of the Swiss, and by the Duke of Lorraine, a young man of twenty years. That Charles, I say, who hoped to surpass by his heroic deeds another Alexander or Charlemagne, was thus overcome, after he had reigned ten years, in the forty-fourth year of his age, leaving one daughter, Mary, as heir.

units.la: Annus mortis Caroli continetur hoc versu, nempe. 1477.
units.tr: The year of Charles's death is contained in this verse, namely 1477.

units.la: En CeCIDIt beLLo BVrgVnDVs CaroLVs, eheV.
units.tr: Lo, Charles the Burgundian fell in war, alas!

units.la: Erat Carolus mediocris staturæ, robustus, firmus ossium compagibus, carnosus, facie nonnihil oblongâ, fronte ampla, oculis fuscis, intuitu acri & virili, naso longo, ac inferius crassiore, mento quoque longiusculo, colore pallidiore fermecinericio, coma, barba & superciliis fuscis. Paucos sua ætate pares habuit, fame, siti, frigore, calore & laboribus feredis: non mulierosus, verum castus, temperans & bellicosus: rigidus in pauperum oppressores, iustitiæ obseruantissimus.
units.tr: Charles was of middling stature, sturdy, firm in the joints of his bones, fleshy, with a somewhat long face, a broad forehead, dark eyes, a keen and manly gaze, a long nose, thicker towards the bottom, a rather long chin too, a rather pale, almost ash-coloured complexion, and dark hair, beard and eyebrows. In his age he had few equals in enduring hunger, thirst, cold, heat and toil. He was not given to women, but chaste, temperate and warlike; harsh towards oppressors of the poor, and most observant of justice.

units.la: Hactenus paucis commemorauimus, quibus modis hæ germaniæ inferiores regiones, à quatuor nobilissimis & potentissimis Principibus, sub vno Principe tanquam capite, Ducatui Burgundico, varie annexæ, & titulo Burgundicæ domus simul insignitæ sint: quæ vltimi Ducis Caroli Pugnacis morte vnicæ suæ filiæ hæredi obuenit: fere autem pessumiuit: ademit enim ei Rex Galliæ Ducatum & comitatum Burgundiæ, Vicecomitatum Auxoniæ, dominia Salmorum & Noreslii, comitatus Masconnensem, Charloisium, & Auxerrensem, Picardiam, Ponthiacum, Ballouisium & ciuitates ad fluuium Sonuam sitas, &c. Præterea Atrebacum, Tornacum, & pleraque alia loca: quod hæc omnia tanquam bona feudalia à Galliarum Rege profecta, fœminæ possidere non possent, huiusmodi causas prætexente Gallo. Neque difficile ei fuit has possessiones invadere. Nam virorum nobilium auctoritate præstantium & militarium, maxima pars postremis bellis & præliis cæsa aut capta pta erat, quosdam quoque, ne quid adferrent detrimenti, inescabat, vt Antonium & Balduinum, Burgundos, nothos, bello strenuos. Prouinciarum praeterea gubernatores atque administratores praetextu nuptiarum filii sui Delphini, cum Maria Caroli filia, in suas partes callide pertrahebat: arte quoque & dolo tumultus atque seditiones in Flandria (Flandris foedus & connubium cum Gallo recusantibus) concitare satagans. His, vt dixi, modis Burgundiae Ducatus a Germania inferiore separatus, terminique Belgici contracti atque depressi, donec auxilio familiae Austriacae (nupta Archiduci Maximiliano haerede Maria) partim recuperati sunt, instauratique.
units.tr: Thus far we have briefly recounted the means by which these Lower Germanic regions were variously joined, under one prince as head, to the Burgundian Duchy by four most noble and powerful princes, and were at the same time marked with the title of the house of Burgundy; these fell to his only daughter and heir upon the death of the last duke, Charles the Bold, and yet were nearly ruined. For the King of France took from her the Duchy and County of Burgundy, the Viscounty of Autun, the lordships of Salins and Noyers, the County of Mâcon, Charolais and Auxerre, Picardy, Ponthieu, Bailleul, and the cities on the river Somme, and so on. Besides, Arras, Tournai and many other places: the Frenchman pretending that, since all these were feudal possessions proceeding from the King of France, a woman could not hold them. Nor was it difficult for him to invade these possessions. For the greater part of the noblemen of authority and military distinction had been slain or captured in the recent wars and battles; some of them too he enticed, lest they should do any harm, as Antoine and Baudouin, Burgundian bastards, valiant in war. Moreover, he cunningly drew into his own party the governors and administrators of the provinces, under the pretext of the marriage of his son the Dauphin with Mary, Charles's daughter; he also strove by craft and deceit to stir up tumults and seditions in Flanders, where the Flemings refused alliance and marriage with the Frenchman. By these means, as I have said, the Duchy of Burgundy was separated from Lower Germany, and the Belgic borders were narrowed and pressed down, until they were partly recovered and restored by the help of the Austrian family (Mary having been married to the Archduke Maximilian, the heir).

units.la: Maria Valesia, Caroli Pugnacis vnica filia, haeres Burgundiae, & inferioris Germaniae, nupta Maximiliano Austriaco Friderici tertii Imp. filio, Gandaui 18. Augusti Anno 1477. Fuit Maximilianus Princeps imprimis clarus, strenuus & ingeniosus, vigesimo aetatis suae anno.
units.tr: Mary of Valois, the only daughter of Charles the Bold, heir of Burgundy and of Lower Germany, was married at Ghent on 18 August in the year 1477 to Maximilian of Austria, son of Emperor Frederick III. Maximilian was a prince especially distinguished, valiant and gifted, in the twentieth year of his age.

units.la: Maria vxore ducta, statim Gallo, ne plura inuaderet, restitit, multa oppida, aliaque loca recuperauit. Victor praeterea Gallos secundo admodum praelio Guinegathensi non procul a Therouana superauit, summa potissime Flandrorum militum hastatorum strenuitate. Ordinem aurei Velleris (Burgundicae familiae claritatem atque amplitudinem) restituit Anno 1478.
units.tr: Having taken Mary as wife, he at once resisted the Frenchman, lest he should invade further, and recovered many towns and other places. Moreover, as victor, he defeated the French in a second battle, very much a success, at Guinegate, not far from Thérouanne, chiefly by the great courage of the Flemish spearmen. In 1478 he restored the Order of the Golden Fleece, the glory and greatness of the Burgundian house.

units.la: Quinto coniugii anno Maria equo, quo vehebatur, decidens, grauiter laesa, obiit mortem, relicto filio Philippo, anno 1478 nato, & filia Margaretha.
units.tr: In the fifth year of their marriage Mary, falling from the horse on which she was riding, was grievously injured and died, leaving a son Philip, born in 1478, and a daughter Margaret.

units.la: Mox post eius mortem generalis pax inita cum Gallo, decreto connubio Margarethae cum Delphino Franciae. Verum Delphinus tamen postea, Margaretha nondum nubili ad patrem remissa, vxorem duxit filiam & haeredem Britanniae, quam Maximilianus coniugem accipere statuerat.
units.tr: Soon after her death a general peace was made with France, with a marriage between Margaret and the Dauphin of France having been decreed. But afterwards the Dauphin, Margaret not yet being of marriageable age and having been sent back to her father, took as his wife the daughter and heir of Brittany, whom Maximilian had resolved to take as his wife.

units.la: Post Mariae Ducis obitum dissidia, seditiones & bella in inferiori Germania, maxime autem in Flandria, inter Maximilianum & Prouincias oriuntur, quae, quod nostri aeui turbis & tumultib. absimilia non sint, paucis hic referre non inutile puto.
units.tr: After the death of Duke Mary, quarrels, seditions and wars arose in Lower Germany, but especially in Flanders, between Maximilian and the Provinces. Since these are not unlike the disturbances and tumults of our own age, I think it not unhelpful to report them briefly here.

units.la: Dissidii prima causa fuit administratio regionum, & tutela Philippi pueri Archiducis Maximiliani filii, quem pater cum omnibus suis ditionibus pro suo imperio regere volebat, quod subditi Statuum consilium aliquatenus minore annis Philippo permisere. Hinc post multas turbas atque seditiones sequentium articulorum reus accusatur Maximilianus.
units.tr: The first cause of the dispute was the administration of the regions and the guardianship of Philip, the boy son of Archduke Maximilian, whom the father wished to rule with all his dominions as his own empire; the subjects, however, allowed the Council of the Estates to have some say, since Philip was under age. Hence, after many disturbances and seditions, Maximilian is accused of the following articles.

units.la: Quod à suis diuulgatum esset, eum in animum induxisse, Brabantiam, Hannoniam, Hollandiam, Zelandiam, & Frisiam ab aliis Prouinciis abalienare, veroque haeredi suo filio adimere tanquam feudalia bona Imperii, in quae foeminae non succedunt, Caroli Ducis postremi morte ad Fridericum Imp. suum patrem iure deuoluta.
units.tr: It was made known by his own people that he had resolved to detach Brabant, Hainaut, Holland, Zeeland and Friesland from the other Provinces, and to take them from his true heir, his son, as feudal possessions of the Empire, into which women do not succeed, by right devolved on Frederick the Emperor, his father, on the death of the last Duke Charles.

units.la: Haec autem verissima esse, liquido comprobat ipsa postulatio Louanii deputatis siue designatis quatuor primariarum Ciuitatum propositta, quae certam pecuniae summam a Brabantis, Hannoniis, Hollandis & Zelandis exigebat: hos vero designatos super his aliisque rebus Mechliniae consultantes capi, & Vilvvordam auehi iubet; quod pacem cum Gallo fecissent, & certum foedus inter Brabantos & Flandros meditarentur, tandemque consilio & instinctu extraneorum quorundam Consiliariorum auaritia ardentium, fere omnes, vt caeteris metum incuteret, capite truncari, aut in exilium agi mandat, infelicem eorum casum, praecipue autem Nicolai Huetfeldii, pluribus summopere dolentibus atque miserantibus.
units.tr: That these things are most true is clearly proved by the very demand put forward by the four chief cities to the deputies or designated men at Louvain, which exacted a certain sum of money from the Brabanters, Hainaulters, Hollanders and Zeelanders; and he ordered these designated men, who were consulting at Mechlin about these and other matters, to be seized and carried off to Vilvoorde, because they had made peace with the Frenchman and were planning a sure alliance between the Brabanters and the Flemings; and at last, on the advice and instigation of certain foreign councillors burning with greed, he ordered almost all of them to be beheaded or sent into exile, to strike fear into the others, their unhappy fate being lamented and pitied by many, especially that of Nicolas Huetfeldt.

units.la: Quod Cimelia & pretiosissima quaeque Burgundicae domus, quae plurima erant, dissiparet & alienaret, dominia quoq; oppignoraret.
units.tr: He squandered and alienated the treasures and the most precious possessions of the house of Burgundy, of which there were very many, and he also pawned the lordships.

units.la: Praeterea sibi ius proprietatis & dominii in regiones arrogaret, se titulo Ducis, Comitis & Domini decoraret, earumq; insignia arma gestaret, suo quoque nomine aes cudi & signari, nulla filii tutelae facta mentione, procuraret.
units.tr: Besides this, he claimed for himself the right of ownership and dominion over the regions, adorned himself with the titles of Duke, Count and Lord, bore their arms as insignia, and had money struck and stamped in his own name, without any mention of his son's guardianship.

units.la: Extraneis & alienis munia siue officia detulisset, eaque pretio & mercede locasset.
units.tr: He gave offices and duties to foreigners and outsiders, and let them out for payment and hire.

units.la: Prouincias bello vexaret, praetextu subditos, & rebelles puniendi, niendi : cum tamen ei subditi non essent, nec rebelles proinde dicendi : huius quoque controuersiæ & litis causa Curiam Regis Franciæ, tanquam supremi iudicis, appellare debuisse.
units.tr: He laid waste the provinces with war, under the pretext of punishing subjects and rebels, although they were not his subjects and could not properly be called rebels. In this dispute and lawsuit he ought to have appealed to the Court of the King of France as supreme judge.

units.la: Hi pluresque articuli totius dissidii, unde seditiones & bella orta, præcipuæ causæ fuerunt.
units.tr: These and other articles of the whole quarrel were the chief causes of the uprisings and wars.

units.la: Maximilianus Deuderomondam, postea Oudenardam, & alia loca capit: depopulantur deuastantque sui superiores Germani milites regionem Wasianam, prædamque Antuerpiæ (ciuitate hac Maximiliani partes tenente) vendunt: bello quoque nauali certat: Bierulietum obsidet, sed in Zelandiam statim fugere coactus. Gandenses, Comes Romondus, Rauenstcinius, iique nobiles viri Burgundicæ familiæ, cognatione & affinitate iuncti, auxiliaribus aliis regionibus, non tantum terra, sed & mari acriter infestant. Slusianis omnia diripientibus. Vlissinganisque die ipso Pentecostes spoliantibus & vastantibus. Gualtero Dombergio in templi adytis occiso.
units.tr: Maximilian took Deinze, afterwards Oudenaarde, and other places. His German soldiers, under their commanders, laid waste and ravaged the district of Waas and sold the plunder at Antwerp, which city held Maximilian's side. He also fought a naval battle and besieged Biervliet, but was at once forced to flee into Zeeland. The Ghent men, Count Romondus, Ravenstein, and those noble men of the Burgundian family, bound by kinship and marriage, with other auxiliaries, attacked fiercely not only by land but also by sea. The people of Sluis plundered everything, and on the very day of Pentecost they despoiled and devastated Vlissingen, Walter Domberg being killed in the sanctuary of the church.

units.la: Franciscus Bredenrodius vir nobilis acre bellum in Hollandos & Zelandos intendit: Westcapella, Zirckzeum aliaque loca capta. Ex Hollandia & Zelandia Antuerpiam nauigare sine valida conductorum manu periculosissimum. Saftingæ arx, plurimaque alia propugnacula extincta.
units.tr: Francis Bredenrode, a noble man, waged fierce war against the Hollanders and Zeelanders: Westkapelle, Zierikzee and other places were taken. To sail from Holland and Zeeland to Antwerp without a strong force of hired men was most dangerous. The fortress of Safting and very many other defences were destroyed.

units.la: Tandem decisione facta, Archidux puer Philippus Gandauidetentus in patris tanquam tutoris & curatoris potestatem traditur, eâ inter alias conditione, ne absque Statuum consilio aliquid ageretur. Verum pacta non diu seruata: Maximilianus enim interea Romanorum Rex creatus, ex superiore Germania in Flandriam rediens, Cassantium, inde Slusam venit, suis hic grassari, & in Flandricum populum sæuire incipientibus, non sine magna grauiorum facinorum suspicione, postea vi armata Brugas intrat. Hic rursus pax, Friderico Imp. patre suo præsente, constituta.
units.tr: At last, a settlement having been made, the young Archduke Philip, who had been held at Ghent, was handed over into the power of his father as tutor and guardian, on the condition, among others, that nothing should be done without the advice of the States. But the agreement was not kept for long: for Maximilian, meanwhile elected King of the Romans, returning from upper Germany into Flanders, came to Kassel, and from there to Sluis. Here, when his men began to run riot and rage against the Flemish people, he, not without great suspicion of more serious crimes, afterwards entered Bruges by armed force. Here peace was again established, with his father Emperor Frederick present.

units.la: Sed cū initio anni M.CCCC.LXXXVIII.
