Antuerpia Brugas, satellitū multitudine stipatus, militib. præterea plurib. circumcirca dispositis, rediisset, Brugenses violentia veriti, hospitiū ei arcemCraneburgicam designant, vbi eum magnifice pro sua amplitudine excipiunt, non finecuftodibus tamen: ministros eius omnes grauiter fuípectos aut captos detinent, aut à Domino separant, imprimis Cancellarium Burgundiæ Abbatem diui Bertiui, Dominos Polheimii, Comitem Philippum Naffouium, Dominum Dugellium & Matthiam Payartum, duorum postremorum, & Petri Lanckhafii fui thefaurarii, aliorumque quorundam ceruicibus tandem incifis.
units.tr: But when, at the beginning of the year 1488, Maximilian returned from Antwerp to Bruges, surrounded by a crowd of bodyguards and with many soldiers stationed all around, the men of Bruges, fearing violence, assigned to him as lodging the castle of Craneburg, where they received him magnificently, in keeping with his rank, yet not without guards. They held all his ministers, who were gravely suspected, either captured or separated from their lord; above all, they finally had the heads cut off the Chancellor of Burgundy, the Abbot of Saint Bertin, the lords of Polheim, Count Philip of Nassau, Lord Dugelle and Matthias Payart, the last two, and Peter Lanckhals, his treasurer, and some others.

units.la: Tum vero conuocato Statuum generalium & consanguineorum Burgundicorum consilio, pax noua 16. Maii anno 1488. decernitur; Pontifice Romano dirum anathema Flandris minante.
units.tr: Then, indeed, after a council of the General States and the Burgundian kinsmen had been summoned, a new peace was decreed on 16 May in the year 1488, the Roman Pontiff threatening the Flemings with dreadful anathema.

units.la: Huius postremæ pacis conditionibus Maximilianus Romanorum Rex omni custodia liberatus, obsidibus datis, consanguineis Burgundicis, imprimis Duce Piuio, Domino Rauensteinio consanguineo Burgundico, mandat atque permittit, vt & bellum contra fegerat, nisi pacificationis articulos omnes exacte obseruet. Fridericus autem Imp. nuncio de filii sui captiuitate accepto, cum exercitu potenti è Germania aduenit, Ducibus Saxoniæ, Bauariæ, Brunsuigii, Margrauiis Brandeburgensi & Badensi, Landgrauio Hesso & aliis comitatus, pacem ratam habere recusat, Gandauum quadraginta diesobsidet: hic Margrauius Brandeburgensis arcubalistæ telo ictus. Postremo cernens Imp. se suo exercitu nihil aut parum exequi, & filium liberum & incustoditum à Flandris dimissum, obsidionem soluit, agrisque depopulatis in superiorem Germaniam cum Maximiliano reuertitur, relicto ibi Alberto Duce Saxoniæ vicario exercitus præfecto, qui plurimis Anglis militibus sibi assóciatis longo tempore bellum contra inferioris Germaniæ regiones gessit, & Slusam obsidet: Neoportum quoque à Cordeo, ibidem vulnerato, militum non exiguâ copiâ cinctum: Gandenses Dixundam ex improuiso capiunt. In Brabantia Buscoducensis ciuitas neutri parti addicta: Louanium, Bruxella, Thenæ Rauensteinio, consanguineis Burgundicis dicis & Flandris : Antuerpia verò, Mechlinia & Lira Alberto Saxoniæ Duci operam præstant: Infestissimis animis vndique grauissima damna inimicæ parti inferuntur. Præsidia Bruxellensia Vilvvordam vi capiunt, diripiunt & exurunt. Saxo violenter occupat Louanium, Arschottum igne delet. Thenæ & alia loca destructa, peste & dira lue aliisque malis vbique locorum grassantibus, sæua & deformis toti regioni facies, donec prouectioris ætatis Archidux Philippus circiter annum M. CCCC. XCII. turbis sedatis, & pace constituta vbique, Princeps inauguratur, & rerum habenas accipit.Friderico autem Philippi auo mortuo,pater Maximilianus factus Imperator tor Anno M. CCCC. XCIV.has regiones consilio & opera plurimum iuuit. Erat enim vir strenuus & ingenio pollens, dilatandis Imperii finibus, si vires & facultates suffecissent, imprimis idoneus.
units.tr: Under the terms of this last peace, Maximilian, King of the Romans, was freed from all custody, after hostages were given; he commanded and permitted, through his Burgundian kinsmen, above all Duke Pius and Lord Ravenstein, a Burgundian kinsman, that war should be waged against him too, unless he observed all the articles of the pacification exactly. Emperor Frederick, however, having received word of his son's captivity, came from Germany with a powerful army, accompanied by the Dukes of Saxony, Bavaria and Brunswick, the Margraves of Brandenburg and Baden, the Landgrave of Hesse and others, and refused to ratify the peace; he besieged Ghent for forty days. Here the Margrave of Brandenburg was struck by a crossbow bolt. At last, seeing that the Emperor was achieving little or nothing with his army, and that his son had been released by the Flemings and was no longer guarded, he lifted the siege, and after laying waste the fields he returned with Maximilian to upper Germany, leaving behind as vicar and commander of the army Duke Albert of Saxony, who, with many English soldiers joined to him, waged war for a long time against the regions of lower Germany and besieged Sluis. He also besieged Nieuwpoort, where Cordes was wounded there, and surrounded it with no small number of soldiers. The Ghent men took Dixmude by surprise. In Brabant the city of Bois-le-Duc, attached to neither side, [...]; Leuven, Brussels, and Tienen gave their support to Ravenstein, the Burgundian kinsmen and the Flemings; but Antwerp, Mechelen and Lier lent their help to Duke Albert of Saxony. With the bitterest hatred, the most grievous losses were inflicted on the hostile party from every side. The garrison of Brussels took Vilvoorde by force, plundered it and set it on fire. Saxon troops violently seized Leuven and destroyed Aarschot by fire. Tienen and other places were laid waste, and with plague and deadly pestilence and other evils raging everywhere, the face of the whole region was savage and hideous, until, around the year 1492, when the Archduke Philip had come of age, the disturbances were calmed and peace was established everywhere, and he was inaugurated as Prince and took up the reins of government. Then, after the death of Philip's grandfather Frederick, his father Maximilian, made Emperor in the year 1494, greatly helped these regions by his counsel and labour. For he was a vigorous man of great ability, and especially well suited to extending the boundaries of the Empire, had his strength and resources sufficed.

units.la: PHILIPPVS ARCHIDVX AVSTRIÆ.
units.tr: PHILIP, ARCHDUKE OF AUSTRIA.

units.la: Anno M.CCCC.XCII.inauguratur, & rerū habenas accipit. Vxorem duxit Liræ Ioannam Hispanam anno M.CCCC. XCVI.
units.tr: In the year 1492 he was inaugurated and took up the reins of government. In 1496 he married Joanna of Spain at Lierre.

units.la: Philippi soror Margaretha Austriaca, Anno M. CCCC. XCVII. in Hispanias vecta, nupsit Ioanni Castiliæ, vnico Principi Ioannæ Hispaniæ, Philippi vxoris fratri, cui filium peperit. Patre autem & nato eodem anno mortuis, diuersa Hispaniarum regna Philippi Austriæ Ducis vxori, Iohannis natu maximæ filiæ, hæreditate obuenerunt.
units.tr: Philip's sister Margaret of Austria was carried to Spain in 1497 and married John of Castile, the only son of Joanna of Spain, Philip's wife's brother, to whom she bore a son. Both father and son died in the same year, and the different kingdoms of Spain passed by inheritance to Philip, Archduke of Austria, husband of Joanna, John's eldest sister.

units.la: Hac matre geniti Gandaui Anno 1500. 24. Febr. Carolus postea Imperator eius nominis Quintus, Ferdinandus & 4. filiæ, Leonora Emanuelí Regi Portugalliæ primo, postea Francisco Regi Galliæ nupta; Catharina, Iohanni Regi Portugalliæ; Isabella Christiano Regi Daniæ, Suediæ & Noruegiæ. Maria Ludouico Regi Hungariæ.
units.tr: Born of this mother at Ghent on 24 February 1500 were Charles, afterwards Emperor Charles V, and Ferdinand, and four daughters: Eleanor, first married to Emmanuel, king of Portugal, and later to Francis, king of France; Catherine, to John, king of Portugal; Isabella, to Christian, king of Denmark, Sweden and Norway; and Mary, to Louis, king of Hungary.

units.la: Philippus Austriacus, iam Hispaniarum rex, per Franciam HispaHispanias petit, ibique variorum Regnorum coronis redimitur. Inde per Italiam rediens sororem prædictā Margaretham, iam Ducis Sabaudiæ vxorem, in Germania autem patrem Maximilianum inuisit.
units.tr: Philip of Austria, now king of Spain, travelled through France to Spain, where he was crowned with the crowns of several kingdoms. Returning through Italy, he visited his sister Margaret, now wife of the Duke of Savoy, and in Germany he visited his father Maximilian.

units.la: Philippi tempore Anno M.D.X. tanta fuit annonæ vilitas in Zelandia, vt octaua pars mensuræ tritici, anser saginatus, libra Butyri, poculum vini Pictauiensis simul emerentur sex stuferis, non multo amplius quàm quarta parte Francici coronati tunc æstimatis.
units.tr: In Philip's time, in 1510, provisions were so cheap in Zeeland that an eighth part of a measure of wheat, a fattened goose, a pound of butter and a jug of Poitou wine could all be bought together for six stuivers, not much more than a quarter of the French crown was then valued at.

units.la: Anno M. D. V. Philippus Hispaniæ Rex, Gubernatore Belgii D. Wilhelmo Croyo (domino Cheuresi & Arschoti) constituto, Hispanias cum vxore repetens, & pelagi tempestatibus actus, in Anglia magnificentissimè à sorore sua eiusque marito excipitur. In Hispanias reuersus moritur anno 1506. ætatis 28.
units.tr: In 1505 Philip, king of Spain, with Lord Wilhelm de Croÿ (lord of Chièvres and Aarschot) appointed governor of Belgium, was returning to Spain with his wife when he was driven by storms at sea. In England he was received most magnificently by his sister and her husband. Returning to Spain, he died in 1506 at the age of 28.

units.la: Fuit Philippus Princeps bonus, probus, pacis amans, voluptuosus, ciuilis, libertatis studiosus. Bellum memorabile nullum gessit præterquam in Geldros. Carolum Geldriæ Ducem pacem secum facere coëgit: Carolus autem post Philippi à Belgio discessum eam violat, valido exercitu Brabantiam invadens, Tournhautum in Campania depopulatur: postea Leodiensi adiutus milite Diesthenium frustra occupare tentat, comite Nassouio resistente. Halenum verò igne delet, & Thenas vi superat.
units.tr: Philip was a good prince, upright, a lover of peace, fond of pleasure, courteous and zealous for liberty. He waged no memorable war except against the Gelderlanders. He forced Charles, Duke of Guelders, to make peace with him; but after Philip left Belgium, Charles broke the peace, invading Brabant with a strong army and plundering Tournhout in the Campine. Afterwards, aided by soldiers from Liège, he tried in vain to seize Diest, Count Nassau resisting him. He destroyed Halen by fire and by force overcame Tienen.

units.la: MARGARETHA AVSTRIACA GVBERNATRIX BELGII.
units.tr: MARGARETHA OF AUSTRIA, GOVERNESS OF THE NETHERLANDS.

units.la: Margaretha Austriaca secundò vidua & Sabaudiæ dotaria, posthæc Belgii gubernatrix decernitur, quæ consilio & opera sui patris Maximiliani Cæsaris sapienter & placide satis pupilli Caroli Archiducis terras defendit & rexit.
units.tr: Margaret of Austria, a widow for the second time and holding the dower of Savoy, was afterwards appointed governess of the Netherlands. With the counsel and help of her father, the Emperor Maximilian, she defended and governed the lands of her ward, the Archduke Charles, wisely and with considerable calm.

units.la: Anno M. D. XIII. Henricus Angliæ Rex per Caletum in Flandriam venit, Galliam bello opprimere parauit. Huic Cæsar far Maximilianus & Belgarum nobilitas socia arma iungunt, atque primo grandem cladem Gallis inferunt. Postea Anglus Teronauum & Tornacum vrbes capit: verum cum post septennium Gallo Tornacum reddidisset, Comes Henricus Nassouius Caroli Austriaci nomine idem strenue expugnauit.
units.tr: In the year 1513 Henry, King of England, came through Calais into Flanders, intending to crush France by war. The Emperor Maximilian and the nobility of the Netherlands joined arms with him against her, and at first they inflicted a great defeat on the French. Afterwards the Englishman took the towns of Thérouanne and Tournai; but when, seven years later, he had handed Tournai back to the French, Count Henry of Nassau, acting in the name of Charles of Austria, stormed it vigorously.

units.la: CAROLVS ARCHIDVX AVSTRIÆ INAVGVRATVR.
units.tr: CHARLES, ARCHDUKE OF AUSTRIA, IS INAUGURATED.

units.la: Anno M.D.XV. Carolus Archidux Gandaui à Wilhelmo Croyo Domino Chamesii & Arschoti probè educatus, & ab Adriano Florensio Pædagogo, postea Cardinale & Pontifice eius nominis 6. optimè institutus, in Brabantia & aliis suis hæreditariis Regionibus inauguratur, Anno 15. ætatis, Christi 1515.
units.tr: In 1515 Charles, Archduke, was brought up well at Ghent by Wilhelm de Croÿ, lord of Chièvres and Aerschot, and was thoroughly instructed by Adrian of Florence, his tutor, who was later Cardinal and Pope of that name, the sixth. In his fifteenth year, in the year of Christ 1515, he was inaugurated in Brabant and his other hereditary regions.

units.la: Anno M.D.XIX. Cæsar Maximilianus Caroli auus moritur, qui, vt potuit, imperiale sceptrum nepoti præparauit. Carolus enim, eo defuncto, absens (erat tum in Hispaniis) Francoforti Romanorum Rex & Imperator eius nominis Quintus eligitur.
units.tr: In 1519 the Emperor Maximilian, Charles's grandfather, died, having prepared the imperial sceptre for his grandson as far as he could. For Charles, who was absent at the time (he was then in Spain), was elected King of the Romans and Emperor at Frankfurt after Maximilian's death, and took the name Charles V.

units.la: Carolus anno M.D. XX. in Germaniam inferiorem reuersus Aquisgrani Romanorum Rex, postea Bononiæ Romanus Imperator à Clemente Pontifice coronatur.
units.tr: In 1520 Charles returned to Lower Germany, was crowned King of the Romans at Aachen, and later was crowned Roman Emperor at Bologna by Pope Clement.

units.la: Anno M.D.XXI. celebrat Comitia Wormatiæ. Hic Martinus Lutherus damnatur & proscribitur, Carolo V. prolixissimum programma contra Lutherum publicante. Nota, De valore numismatum eorum temporum vide Meteranum. Carolus Imperator vxorem duxit Isabellam, Emanuelis Portugalliæ Regis filiam, hæc ei peperit Valedolitii in Hispania Anno M. D.XXVII. 21. Maii filium Philippum: duas insuper filias, quarum vna Maria nupta Maximiliano Ferdinandi filio, postea Imperatori; altera Iohanna, Principi Portugalliæ; genuit hæc Sebastianum Portugalliæ Regem, in Barbaria anno 1574. cæsum, 4. Augusti.
units.tr: In 1521 the Diet was held at Worms. Here Martin Luther was condemned and outlawed, Charles V publishing a very lengthy proclamation against Luther. Note: for the value of the coinage of those times, see Meteranus. The Emperor Charles married Isabella, daughter of Emmanuel, King of Portugal; she bore him at Valladolid in Spain, on 21 May 1527, a son, Philip, and two daughters besides: one of them, Mary, married Maximilian, son of Ferdinand, later Emperor; the other, Joanna, married the Prince of Portugal, and she bore Sebastian, King of Portugal, who was slain in Barbary on 4 August in the year 1574.

units.la: Anno M. D. XXIX. Pax Cameracensis inter Carolum & Gallum. Carolus Cæsar Austriæ suæ à Turca subtimens, & Franciscus Gallus suarum rerum acerbitate commotus, cogitabant utrinque de pace ineunda. Locus conuentui dictus Cameracum, ciuitas libera, neutralis. Adsunt igitur Margaretha Maximiliani Imp. filia, & Aloysia Allobrox Regia mater, quæ eadem Franciæ rebus præerat, Caroli soror, cum utriusq; partis viris delectis primariis. Adsunt & ex variis locis & Regnis Legati. Ibi diu multumque rebus pensitatis, tandem pax constituta est. Sic ut Gallus penderet pro redemptione obsidum duodecies centena millia scutatorum, de quibus sextans cederet Angliæ Regi. Rex redderet quicquid iurisdictionis Mediolanensis & Regni Neopolitani præoccupasset. Quod Burgundos seu Æduos attineret, iustitium ut esset. Leonora Caroli soror nuberet Regi.
units.tr: In 1529 the Peace of Cambrai was made between Charles and the French king. Charles the Emperor, fearing for his Austrian lands because of the Turk, and Francis, King of France, moved by the bitterness of his own affairs, both began thinking of making peace. The place appointed for the meeting was Cambrai, a free and neutral city. There came, therefore, Margaret, daughter of the Emperor Maximilian, and Louise of Savoy, the king's mother, who was in charge of French affairs, and Charles's aunt, together with the chief men chosen from each side. Envoys also came from various places and kingdoms. There, after the matter had been weighed for a long time and in much detail, peace was finally agreed on, on these terms: that the French king should pay, for the ransom of the hostages, twelve million crowns, of which a sixth part would go to the King of England. The king was to restore whatever jurisdiction he had seized over Milan and the Kingdom of Naples. As for the Burgundians, or Ædui, there was to be a truce. Leonora, Charles's sister, was to marry the king.

units.la: Anglicana lues exorta, Turca Viennam obsidet. Laboratum apud Teutonas supernates, bello, peste, fame, culpa collata in mutationem religionis, quæ in illud temporis incidit.
units.tr: A plague broke out in England; the Turk besieged Vienna. Among the Germans of the upper regions there was suffering from war, plague, and famine, and the guilt was laid on the change of religion that came about in that time.

units.la: Anno M. D. XXX. In Belgio maritimo horrendæ inundationes.
units.tr: In 1530 there were terrible floods in maritime Belgium.

units.la: Anno M. D. XXXI. Carolus Bruxellam venit, & Margaretha demortuæ in gubernatricem Belgii surrogat Mariam Ludouici Vngariæ Regis relictam viduam.
units.tr: In 1531 Charles came to Brussels, and in place of Margaret, who had died, he appointed as governess of the Netherlands Mary, widow of Louis, King of Hungary.

units.la: MARIA GVBERNATRIX BELGII.
units.tr: MARIA, GOVERNESS OF BELGIUM.

units.la: Anno M.D.XXXII. Turca iterum Austriam inuadit.
units.tr: In the year 1532 the Turk again invades Austria.

units.la: Gallus & Anglus contra Cæsarem absentem consultant.
units.tr: The Frenchman and the Englishman take counsel against the Emperor, who is absent.

units.la: Anno M. D.XXXII. Anglus Arrogouiam repudiat.
units.tr: In 1532 the Englishman repudiates Aragon.

units.la: Anglus se Principem Ecclesiæ Anglicanæ nuncupat.
units.tr: The Englishman styles himself Prince of the Church of England.

units.la: Anno M. D. XXXVII. Cæsariani in Belgio Gallis longè superiores, in Italia vicissim succumbebant hosti.
units.tr: In 1537 the Imperialists in Belgium were far superior to the French, while in Italy they in turn were worsted by the enemy.

units.la: Anno M. D. XXXVIII. Anglus tumbam S. Thomae euertit.
units.tr: In 1538 the Englishman overthrew the tomb of St Thomas.

units.la: M.D.XXXIX. mortua in partu Isabella Caroli V. vxor.
units.tr: In 1539 Isabella, wife of Charles V, died in childbirth.

units.la: Carolus Imperator Burgundicae domui ciuitatem & terras Traiecti vlterioris & Transfiliulaniam perfectè annexuit, resignatione Henrici Bauari Traiectensis Episcopi, qui regionem ab aduersarii Ducis Geldriae iniuriis diutius tueri non poterat.
units.tr: The Emperor Charles fully annexed to the Burgundian house the city and lands of Utrecht and Overijssel, on the resignation of Henry of Bavaria, Bishop of Utrecht, who could no longer defend the region for long against the injuries of the enemy, the Duke of Guelders.

units.la: Postea quoque pacto & morte postremi Caroli Egmondani, Geldriaabsolutè Germaniae inferiori accessit anno 1538.
units.tr: Afterwards too, by treaty and by the death of the last Charles of Egmont, Guelders came entirely under Lower Germany, in 1538.

units.la: Status praeterea & dominia Groningae, ante ditioni Traiectinae & Geldrensi subiecta, sponte atque propto animo tandem se Carolo Imperatori dediderunt, anno 1536. Qui non tantum praedictas has ditiones, verum etiam Cameracensem ciuitatem & Cambresianam terram Germaniae huic inferiori iunxit. Cum autem Geldria & Traiectum vlterius feuda imperii semper sint habita, Carolus Imperator hac imprimis de causa Anno 1548. die 16. Iunii in comitiis Augustanis non tantum Geldriam & Traiectum, verum etiam inferiores omnes regiones sub vno circulo, nempe Burgundico, inferiorum regionum in ordinem coegit, & hac ratione imperio deuinxit, vnde iis priuilegio concessum, defensione, libertate, & iure vti, non aliter atque reliqua Imperii membra, tantum contribuendo, quantum duo Principes Electores, contra Turcam autem quantum tres: ita tamen vt propria sua priuilegia obseruantes imperii determinationibus aut constitutionibus non obligentur.
units.tr: Moreover, the states and lordships of Groningen, formerly subject to Utrecht and Guelders, at last surrendered themselves of their own accord and with good will to Emperor Charles, in 1536. He joined not only these aforementioned territories but also the city of Cambrai and the land of Cambrésis to this Lower Germany. Since, however, Guelders and Utrecht had always been held as fiefs of the Empire, Emperor Charles, chiefly for this reason, on 16 June 1548 at the Diet of Augsburg, brought not only Guelders and Utrecht but all the lower regions into one order under one circle, namely the Burgundian, and by this means bound them to the Empire. Hence it was granted to them to enjoy the privileges, defence, liberty and right of the Empire, no otherwise than the remaining members of the Empire: contributing only as much as two Electoral Princes, but against the Turk as much as three. Yet they are not bound by the decisions or constitutions of the Empire, so long as they observe their own privileges.

units.la: PHILIPPVS REX HISPANIAE BELGII DOMINVS.
units.tr: PHILIP, KING OF SPAIN, LORD OF BELGIUM.

units.la: Philippus Austriacus Hispaniarum rex huius nominis secundus, Caroli V. Imperatoris vnicus filius haereditarius, Germaniae inferioris Dominus.
units.tr: Philip of Austria, King of the Spains, the second of that name, the only hereditary son of the Emperor Charles V, Lord of Lower Germany.

units.la: Adhuc iuuenis duxit Mariam Iohannis Portugalliae Regis filiam, filia, quæ prima Philippi vxor ei genuit ann. M. D. XLV. 9. Iulii filium Carolum, statim autem à partu puerpera vitam obiit, summa Ducissæ Albanæ aliarumque primariarum fœminarum (quibus pueri puerperæque cura commissa fuit) negligentia, vt tunc fama erat. Puerpera enim inconsulte & temere melonem comederat, interea dum hæ indulgentias promerendi gratia aberant, spectatum horrendi supplicii Lutheranorum sacræ inquisitionis sententia damnatorum spectaculum.
units.tr: While still a young man he married Mary, daughter of John, King of Portugal, who as Philip's first wife bore him a son, Charles, on 9 July 1545; but she died immediately after giving birth. This was, as was then the talk, through the carelessness of the Duchess of Alba and the other leading ladies to whom the care of the boy and the mother had been entrusted: the woman in childbed had recklessly and thoughtlessly eaten a melon, while these ladies were away seeking to earn indulgences by watching the dreadful execution of Lutherans condemned by the sentence of the Holy Inquisition.

units.la: Anno M.D.XLVI. tanta fuit apud Belgas frumenti caritas, vt Amsterdami siliginis vehes Antuerpiensi mensura 37½. Viertheil siue quartanos continens venderetur 68. aureis. Anno autem secundo post, nempe M. D. XLVIII, tanta facta vilitas, vt eodem 68. aureorum pretio simul emerentur, & vehes tritici, vehes siliginis, vehes hordei, vehes auenæ, quarta pars vasis butyri, trecentæ lardi libræ, trecentæ casei Hollandici libræ, centum casei manualis libræ, thorax vnus, par calceorum, pileus, pera, ouis bene saginata, vas Gedanæ cereuisiæ, vas Roftothimæ cereuisiæ, supererantque emendo vino sex Stuferi. Hoc modo Deus Opt.Max. sua omnipotentia caritatem vilitatemque annonæ inferre valet;
units.tr: In the year 1546 there was such a dearth of grain among the Belgians that at Amsterdam a wagonload of rye, measuring 37½ Antwerp viertels, or quartans, was sold for 68 gold pieces. In the second year after that, namely 1548, there was such a glut that for the same price of 68 gold pieces one could buy at once a wagonload of wheat, a wagonload of rye, a wagonload of barley, a wagonload of oats, a quarter of a barrel of butter, three hundred pounds of bacon, three hundred pounds of Dutch cheese, a hundred pounds of hand cheese, one breastplate, a pair of shoes, a cap, a pouch, a well-fed egg, a barrel of Danzig beer, a barrel of Rostock beer, and there was still enough left to buy six stoups of wine. In this way almighty God, by His omnipotence, is able to bring about both the dearness and the cheapness of food;

units.la: Anno M. D. XLVIII. mittit Carolus Imperator Maximilianum ex fratre Ferdinando nepotem in Hispanias, eumque, filia sua Margaretha vxore ducta, Regnorum gubernatorem constituit: Philippum vero filium 21. annos natum in Belgium ex Hispaniis vocat, qui Andrea Doria itineris duce quinquaginta triremibus, totidemque navibus in Italiam appellens honorificè Genuæ excipitur. 25. Nouembr. Inde Mediolani variis arcubus triumphalibus & theatris sumptuose exstructis decoratur: post Tridenti Mauritius Saxoniæ Dux sacri Imperii Elector ei aduentum summopere gratulatus rogat, apud patrem pro capto Landtgrauio Hassiæ intercedat, quod se facturum recipit. Hinc per Germaniam superiorem in inferiorem descendit. Carolus autem pater ducem Arc-
units.tr: In 1548 the Emperor Charles sent Maximilian, his nephew by his brother Ferdinand, to Spain, and having married him to his daughter Margaret, appointed him governor of the kingdoms. He summoned Philip, then twenty-one years old, from Spain into Belgium. Philip, with fifty galleys and as many ships under Andrea Doria as his escort, put in at Italy, where he was received with honour at Genoa on 25 November. From there he was adorned at Milan with various triumphal arches and sumptuously built stages. Afterwards at Trent Maurice, Duke of Saxony and Elector of the holy Empire, warmly congratulated him on his arrival and asked him to intercede with his father for the captured Landgrave of Hesse; this he promised to do. Thence he descended through Upper Germany into Lower Germany. His father Charles, meanwhile, had sent the Duke of Arschot with the most splendid troops of public horsemen to meet his son as far as Upper Germany, to escort him with the highest honour and ceremony.

units.la: E fchotanum cùm publicorum equitum turmis instructissimis obuiam in superiorem vsque Germaniam miserat filium, summo honore & officio deducendi gratia. Itaque Bruxellæ, Calendis Aprilis Anno M.D.XLIX. ætatis suæ 22. magnifice recipitur, patreatque amitis, Helionora & Maria, hic ipsius adventum coram gratulantibus.
units.tr: So at Brussels, on the Kalends of April 1549, in the twenty-second year of his age, he was received with great pomp, and his aunts Eleanor and Mary greeted his arrival there in the presence of the rejoicing crowd.

units.la: Tota hæc æstas gratulationibus & publicis lætitiis transacta. Brugii in Hannoniis amita Maria gubernatrix honorificentissime & liberalissime eum tractauit. Hinc ab Imperatore aut Gubernatrice in Brabantiam, Flandriam, & alias vicinas regiones deductus, vbique futurus Princeps inauguratur, priuilegiaque præcipue ciuitatibus Brabantiæ primariis p lætum introitum iureiurando confirmat. Autuerpiam autem io. Sept. regie introducitur ab 879. Ciuibus & incolis equitibus purpura holoserica vestitis, hos pedisequis 416. pretiosò ornatu comitantibus. Horum equitum plurima pars, Magistratus & publicorum Ciuitatum munitorum administratores, reliqui diuersarum nationum mercatores erat. Fuere præter hos 4000. pedites vno eodemque insigni militari habitu induti. Ciuitas insuper, mercatorum vero nationes quinque arcus triumphales & theatra 26800. florenorum sumptu erexere. Impendit adhuc Ciuitas ducenta sexaginta florenorum millia. Magnificum, splendidum & imprimis lætum hunc triumphum graphicè descripsit Cornelius Grapheus, Ciuitatis Antuerpiensis Secretarius. Itineris quoque totius historiam Hispaniæ Christophorus Stella literis mandauit.
units.tr: The whole of this summer was spent in congratulations and public rejoicings. At Bruges in Hainault his aunt Mary, the regent, entertained him most honourably and generously. From there, led by the Emperor or the regent into Brabant, Flanders and the other neighbouring regions, he was inaugurated everywhere as the future prince, and he confirmed by oath the privileges, above all of the chief cities of Brabant, on his joyful entry. At Antwerp, on 10 September, he was received royally by 879 citizens and residents mounted and dressed in purple silk, who were accompanied by 416 attendants in precious ornament. Most of these horsemen were magistrates and administrators of the public and fortified cities; the rest were merchants of various nations. Besides these there were 4000 foot soldiers, all dressed in one and the same distinctive military garb. The city, and the five nations of merchants, erected triumphal arches and stages at a cost of 26,800 florins. The city spent a further 260,000 florins. Cornelius Grapheus, secretary of the city of Antwerp, described this magnificent, splendid and above all joyful triumph in pictures. Christopher Stella committed the whole history of the journey through Spain to writing.

units.la: Postquam Philippus totius Belgii futurus Dominus, iam inaugeratus, regionum priuilegia iureiurando sanxisset, cum Cæsare patre in Germaniam superiorem ad comitia Augustana proficiscitur, quem pater Principibus Electoribus hic insinuare & commendare, spe postea potiundi Romani imperii, voluit. Sed cum Ferdinandus Caroli frater, cui multa soboles, quarum Maximilianus vnus Germanis Principibus præcipuè gratus erat, in suum incommodum hoc vergere sentiret, sta-tim tim ex Germania in Italiam, hinc in Hispanias proficiscitur.
units.tr: After Philip, now inaugurated and about to be lord of the whole of Belgium, had confirmed the privileges of the regions by oath, he set out with his father the Emperor for Upper Germany, for the Diet of Augsburg. His father wished to introduce and recommend him to the Electoral Princes there, in hope that he might afterwards obtain the Roman empire. But when Ferdinand, Charles's brother, who had many children, of whom Maximilian alone was especially dear to the German princes, perceived that this would turn to his own disadvantage, he at once set out from Germany into Italy and thence into Spain.

units.la: Galliarum Rex Anno M. D. LII, capit Metas, Poulinum & Verdunium. Mari quoque classem nauium Belgicarum mercibus variis & pretiosis ex Hispaniis emissarum: idque summa dexteritate & versutia: Galli enim nauibus suis bellicis Regionem Scotię vehere simulantes, petunt à Belgis, vt omnia tormenta sua in Reginæ gratiam & honorem eiacularentur, quod dum absque suspicione faciunt, statim inermes bombardis exoneratis à Gallis facile capiuntur. Hinc bellum septennè contra Gallos redintegratur, causa controuersiarum tam in Italia, quam in Germania præcipuè nata. Ex Belgio in Champaniam ab Imperatore missus Martinus Rossemius, omnem Regionem depopulatur, & Asthenum capit.
units.tr: In 1552 the King of France took Metz, Toul and Verdun. He also took by sea a fleet of Belgian ships laden with various and costly wares sent out from Spain; he did this with the greatest skill and cunning. For the French, pretending with their warships to be conveying the Scottish realm, asked the Belgians to fire off all their artillery in honour and favour of the Queen; while they did this without suspicion, the unarmed men, their guns having been discharged, were easily captured by the French. Thence the seven-year war against the French was renewed, its causes having arisen chiefly from disputes both in Italy and in Germany. From Belgium Martin Rossem was sent into Champagne by the Emperor; he laid waste the whole region and took Attigny.

units.la: Anno M.D.LII. Carolus Metim obsidet, sed propter frigus & luem coactus est recedere.
units.tr: In 1552 Charles besieged Metz, but was forced to withdraw on account of the cold and the plague.

units.la: Anno M.D.LIII. occupatur Terouana, capitur Montmorcius Connestablii filius; inuaditur Æsdinum, caeduntur multi celebres viri. Gallus occupat Marieburgum.
units.tr: In 1553 Thérouanne was occupied; Montmorency's son, the son of the Constable, was captured; Hesdin was invaded, and many famous men were slain. The Frenchman occupied Marienburg.

units.la: Anno M.D.LIII. moritur Eduardus Angliæ Rex, Henrici VIII. filius, iuuenis pius, doctus: habuit duas sorores, Mariam, matre Catharina Caroli V. matertera, & Elisabetham, fœminâ Anglica, Thomæ Bullei Comitis Weilshyrae filia. Henricus voluit Ianam Greyam suam neptem Euangelicæ doctrinæ dedi-tam sibi succedere. Maria vero à plerisque electa Ianam illam cum proximis cognatis supplicio miserabili & indigno affecit, & Papismum introduxit, auctore Cardinale Polo. Versatur & Elisabetha soror in periculo propter religionem.
units.tr: In 1553 Edward, King of England, son of Henry VIII, died, a pious and learned young man. He had two sisters: Mary, whose mother Catherine was the aunt of Charles V on her mother's side, and Elizabeth, the daughter of Thomas Boleyn, Earl of Wiltshire. Henry had wished his granddaughter Jane Grey, who had been given over to the evangelical doctrine, to succeed him. But Mary, chosen by most, subjected that Jane, with her closest relatives, to a wretched and undeserved execution, and, under the influence of Cardinal Pole, introduced Popery. Elizabeth, her sister, was also in danger on account of religion.

units.la: M.D.LIV. Philippus celebrat nuptias cum Maria Regina Angliæ die Iacobi.
units.tr: In 1554 Philip celebrated his marriage with Mary, Queen of England, on the feast of St James.

units.la: Exoritur seditio Antuerpiæ.
units.tr: A sedition broke out at Antwerp.

units.la: Angliæ Regina conatur pacem condere inter Cæsarem & Gallum.
units.tr: The Queen of England tried to make peace between the Emperor and the French king.

units.la: M. D. LV. Philippus ex Anglia in Galliam contendit. Carolus V. Belgii regiones filio Philippo, certis solemnitatibus committit. Nota, quæ fuerint quorumlibet orationes.
units.tr: In 1555 Philip set out from England to France. The Emperor Charles handed over the regions of Belgium to his son Philip with certain solemnities. Note what speeches were made by each of them.

units.la: Carolus Imperator commemorat, se nouem expeditiones seu profectiones in Germaniam fecisse, sex in Hispanias, septem in Italiam, decem in Belgium, quatuor in Gallias, belli & pacis tempore, duas in Angliam, duasque expeditiones in Africam, quæ omnes 40. sunt numero. In quibus octies mare mediterraneum transnauigauit & ter oceanum.
units.tr: The Emperor Charles records that he had made nine expeditions or journeys into Germany, six into Spain, seven into Italy, ten into Belgium, four into France, in times of both war and peace, two into England, and two expeditions into Africa, which are forty in all. In these he crossed the Mediterranean eight times and the Ocean three times.

units.la: Carolo sermone finienti lachrymæ per ora fluunt, maxima multitudinis parte ad collachrymandum commota, respondet Philippus. Tum Iacobus Masius nomine Statuum.
units.tr: As Charles finished his speech, tears ran down his face, and most of the crowd was moved to weep with him; Philip replied. Then Jacob Masius spoke on behalf of the States.

units.la: Reliquum Actum vide in Meterano.
units.tr: See the rest of the action in Meteranus.

units.la: Bruxellis tunc septem capita regali corona redimita cernebat, nempe ipsum Imperatorem, eiusque filium Philippum, Maximilianum, Eleonoram Galliæ, Mariam Hungariæ, & Mariam Bohemiæ Reginam, quibus accessit septimus Muteasses rex Tuneti, præter multos inferiores Principes, videlicet Duces Sabaudiæ, Lotharingiæ & Daniæ, cum aliis.
units.tr: At Brussels one then saw seven heads crowned with the royal diadem: the Emperor himself, his son Philip, Maximilian, Eleanor of France, Mary of Hungary, and Mary, Queen of Bohemia. To these was added a seventh, Muteasses, King of Tunis, besides many lesser princes, namely the Dukes of Savoy, Lorraine and Denmark, with others.

units.la: Sub finem Augusti acerrimum prælium nauale commissum est inter Gallos & Hollandos, sic ut consertis nauibus inuicem tanquam terra dimicarint per sex horas, donec igni exorto 6. Gallorum, & 6. Hollandorum naues consumptæ sint. Gallorum circiter mille, Hollandorum ad 300. periisse putatur. Hollandorum strenua pugna cumprimis celebrata laudibus, quod tantum onerarias & parum instructas, altas tamen; Galli autem præsidiarias & bellicas multo plures, militumque numero potentiores haberent naues.
units.tr: Near the end of August a most fierce naval battle was fought between the French and the Dutch. The ships were locked together and fought as if on land for six hours, until a fire broke out and six French and six Dutch ships were burned. About a thousand Frenchmen and about 300 Dutchmen are thought to have perished. The Dutch resolute fighting was especially praised, since they had only merchant ships, few guns and poorly equipped, though high-sided; the French, on the other hand, had many more warships and guard ships and were stronger in the number of soldiers.

units.la: Anno M. D. LVI. Paulus IV. P. fauens Gallo Columenses Cæsarianos infestat. Hià Duce Albano Prorege Neapolitano opem petunt, mittit & Gallus Guisium in Italiam. Sed postquam Quintinum captum est, illud bellum est compositum.
units.tr: In the year 1556 Pope Paul IV, favouring the French, harassed the Imperialist Colonnesi. They sought help from the Duke of Alba, viceroy of Naples, and the French also sent Guise into Italy. But after Saint-Quentin was taken, that war was brought to an end.

units.la: Carolus Cæsar in Zelandia scribit fratri Ferdinando, se omni officio defunctum Romani Imperii sceptra ei committere. Cuius negotii cõficiendi causa delegit Wilhelmum Nassouium souium Orangiæ Principem, cum Doctore Georgio Sigismundo Seldio Vicecancellario, & Wolffgango Hallero Secretario. Sed traditio illa solemnis tandem in Comitiis Anni 1558. 24. Februarii Francoforti facta est. Carolus imperio defunctus cum vtraque sorore, Eleonora Regina & dotaria Galliæ atque Portugalliæ, & Maria Hungariæ Regina, Belgii gubernatrice, in Hispaniam soluunt. Carolus in Hispania in Monasterio Ordinis D. Hieronymi octo à Placenza milliaribus adhuc duos annos precibus & Deo vacans vixit.
units.tr: Charles Caesar wrote from Zeeland to his brother Ferdinand that, having discharged every duty, he was committing to him the sceptres of the Roman Empire. To carry out this business he chose William of Nassau, Prince of Orange, with Doctor Georg Sigismund Seld, vice-chancellor, and Wolfgang Haller, secretary. But the solemn handover was at last made at the Diet of Frankfurt on 24 February 1558. Charles, having resigned the empire, sailed to Spain with both his sisters, Eleanor, Queen of France and dowager of Portugal, and Mary of Hungary, governor of Belgium. In Spain, in a monastery of the Order of St Jerome eight miles from Plasencia, Charles lived for two more years, devoted to prayer and to God.

units.la: Rex Philippus post patris discessum Emanuelem Philibertum Sabaudiæ Ducem, suæ matris sorore filia Portugalliæ natum, Belgii gubernatorem constituit.
units.tr: After the father's departure, King Philip appointed Emmanuel Philibert, Duke of Savoy, born of his mother's sister, the daughter of Portugal, as governor of Belgium.

units.la: Status Belgici Italico & Gallico grauati bello, nouennalem exactionem Regi consentiunt.
units.tr: The States of Belgium, burdened by the Italian and French war, agreed to a nine-year levy for the King.

units.la: Regina Galliæ duas filiolas peperit, quarum vni, ob continentes præteritorum annorum victorias, superbum nomen Victoriæ fortunati parentes dederunt, altera Ioanna est nominata, quæ ambæ vitam arcto temporis puncto concluserunt, sicuti breuissimum etiam fuit victoriarum Gallicarum curriculum.
units.tr: The Queen of France bore two little daughters. To one of them, because of the continuous victories of the past years, the fortunate parents gave the proud name Victoria; the other was called Joan. Both ended their lives in a very brief span of time, just as the course of French victories was very short.

units.la: M. D. LVI. Ingens Cometa conspectus in Martio. Conspiratio contra Reginam Angliæ.
units.tr: 1556. A huge comet was seen in March. A conspiracy against the Queen of England.

units.la: L. D. LVII. In Anglia bellum contra Gallum proclamatur. In Belgio partes vtrinque induciis spretis altera alteram circumuenire student. Amiralius Galliæ, Picardiæ gubernator, Duecum capere tentat, sed elusus Lentium oppidum diripit.
units.tr: 1557. In England war against France is proclaimed. In Belgium both sides, having scorned the truces, strive to outwit each other. The Admiral of France, governor of Picardy, tries to seize Dunkirk, but being foiled he plunders the town of Lens.

units.la: Burgundi (Philippi Regis duces) castra ad Guisiam, quasi oppidum obsessuri, metantur. Sed collectis copiis omnibus Quintini fanum cingunt. Erat in vrbe Telignius, post intromissus Amiralius Caspar Colignius, Com. Castilionæi. Interea Gallus Montmorencium Connestablium cum valida manu eo mittit. Conantur per lacum scaphis subsidia obsessis adferre; sed pauci in vrbem peruenerunt, Andelotus tamen cum
units.tr: The Burgundians (the Dukes of King Philip) pitch camp near Guise, as if about to besiege the town. But, with all their forces gathered, they surround the shrine of St Quentin. There was in the town Telligny; afterwards Admiral Gaspard de Coligny, Count of Châtillon, was admitted. Meanwhile the French King sends Montmorency the Constable there with a strong force. They try to bring help to the besieged by boats across the lake, but few reached the town; yet Andelot, with

units.la: 500. 500. matutino tempore oppidum ingreditur.
units.tr: 500, 500, enters the town at morning time.

units.la: Burgundi rati, Gallorum exercitum post introductum militem recessurum esse, Egmondano auctore Gallos insequuntur. Commissum prælium. Cæsi Galli memorabili clade, capto Connestablio & innumeris Proceribus, & præcipua nobilitate Gallorum interfecta. Postea Quintinum expugnatur, & Hanum capitur. Admiralius in captiuitate incumbens lectionibus librorum sacrorum, ad agnitionem Euangelicæ doctrinę deducitur.
units.tr: The Burgundians, thinking the French army would withdraw once the soldiers had been admitted, pursued the French at the urging of Egmont. Battle was joined. The French were cut down in a memorable disaster, the Constable was taken, and countless lords and the chief French nobility were slain. Afterwards Saint-Quentin was stormed and Han was captured. The Admiral, while in captivity, devoted himself to reading the holy books and was led to acknowledge the Evangelical doctrine.

units.la: Fit pax inter Pontificem & Philippum Regem.
units.tr: Peace is made between the Pope and King Philip.

units.la: Henricus Rex trepidauit quidem, sed cum sese recollegisset, collecto milite, quasi alio cogitaret, subito Caletum obsidione cingit, idque omni vi oppugnans capit, simul & Gyneum occupat. Angli per tempestatem obsessis opem ferre nequiuerunt, id quod Mariam Reginam ita torsit, vt mœror non leuis causa mortis fuerit, quæ eodem anno in Nouembri sequuta est.
units.tr: King Henry was indeed alarmed, but when he had recovered himself and gathered soldiers, as if he were thinking of some other place, he suddenly surrounded Calais with a siege, took it by assault with all his force, and at the same time occupied Guînes. The English, because of a storm, could not bring help to the besieged. This so tormented Queen Mary that grief was no small cause of her death, which followed in November of that year.

units.la: M. D. LVIII. Delphinus ducit Mariam Stuartam Scotiæ Reginam, vnicam Iacobi V. postremi Regis filiam. Nuptiæ Parisiis anno 1558. celebratur. Quo tempore generosa Lotharingiæ Ducissa, Christierni Regis Daniæ ex Caroli V. sorore filia, primo de pace vtrinque inter Reges agere coepit.
units.tr: 1558. The Dauphin married Mary Stuart, Queen of Scots, the only daughter of James V, the last king. The wedding was celebrated at Paris in 1558. At that time the noble Duchess of Lorraine, daughter of Christian, King of Denmark, by a daughter of Charles V's sister, first began to negotiate peace between the kings on both sides.

units.la: Gallus Theodonis villam ad Molam obsidet & capit. In obsidione plurimi Galli cæsi, & Marschalcus Petrus Strozius, cui cum Duce Guisio (manu eius humero innitente) colloquenti pectus sclopeto traiectum est.
units.tr: The French besieged and took the village of Thionville at Mola. In the siege many Frenchmen were slain, and Marshal Pierre Strozzi, while conversing with Duke Guise (whose hand rested on his shoulder), had his chest pierced by a musket ball.

units.la: Galli Duce Termeo ex Caleto Flandriam infestant, quibus Comes Egmondanus opponitur, & Gallos ad Greuelingam acie vincit & fundit. Cæsi ibi supra mille. Termeus & alii capti.
units.tr: The French, under Thermes, attacked Flanders from Calais; Count Egmont was set against them, and he defeated them in battle at Gravelines and routed them. More than a thousand were slain there; Thermes and others were taken.

units.la: Angliæ Regina classem adornat.
units.tr: The Queen of England prepares a fleet.

units.la: Duorum Regum exercitus instructissimi circa Darlenum consistunt, neque tamen generali prælio periclitari audent, hinc tandem ad pacem animum intendunt. Conuenere igitur Cerecampii vtriusque partis magnates.
units.tr: The armies of the two kings, most fully equipped, stood near Dourlens, yet dared not risk a general battle; so at last they turned their minds to peace. Accordingly the magnates of both parties met at Cateau-Cambrésis.

units.la: Maria Regina Angliæ moritur, succedit soror Elisabetha annos nata 25. sub qua Anglia à fide Papæ discessit, & quia sub Maria religionis causa exules fuerunt, tunc in Angliam redierunt.
units.tr: Queen Mary of England died, and her sister Elizabeth succeeded her, aged 25. Under her England withdrew from the faith of the Pope. And because under Mary they had been exiles for religion, they now returned to England.

units.la: In Februario Eleonora, in Octobri Maria sorores Caroli V. moriuntur. Carolus V. moritur 21. Septembris, confessus se animæ salutem ab vnius Domini nostri IESV CHRISTI meritis expectare reformatorum professione & sententia.
units.tr: In February Eleanor, and in October Mary, sisters of Charles V, died. Charles V died on 21 September, confessing that he expected the salvation of his soul from the merits of our one Lord Jesus Christ, in the profession and judgement of the Reformed.

units.la: Mortui etiam sunt Christianus & Christiernus Daniæ Reges. Christiernus Daniæ, Suetiæ & Norwegiæ Rex fuit, & propter tyrannidem à subditis reiectus est, electis aliis. Tandem anno 1552. à Carolo V. cuius sororem Isabellam vxorem habuit, adiutus regnum recuperare voluit. Sed captus & 22. annos in carcere detentus erat. Ex vxore hac suscepit filium, qui in Belgio diem obiit, & filiam Christiernam Lotharingiæ Ducissam, quæ anno 1585. Hispanum & Gallum Reges reconciliauit. Eius filius Lothar. Dux anno M. D. LIX. duxit vxorem Claudiam filiarum Galli alteram.
units.tr: The Kings of Denmark, Christian and Christiern, also died. Christiern was King of Denmark, Sweden and Norway, and because of his tyranny he was rejected by his subjects, others being chosen. Finally, in 1552, aided by Charles V, whose sister Isabella he had as his wife, he wished to recover the kingdom. But he was captured and kept in prison for 22 years. By this wife he had a son, who died in Belgium, and a daughter, Christierna, Duchess of Lorraine, who in 1585 reconciled the Kings of Spain and France. Her son, Duke of Lorraine, in 1559 married Claude, the other daughter of the King of France.

units.la: Propter mortem Mariæ Angliæ dilatata est tractatio pacis, quæ tandem multis arbitris composita est.
units.tr: Because of the death of Mary of England the treaty of peace was delayed; it was at last concluded with many arbitrators.

units.la: Elisabethæ Angliæ restituitur Caletum.
units.tr: Calais is restored to Elizabeth of England.

units.la: Inter conditiones etiam hæ fuerunt, vt litibus controuersiisque veteribus vtrinque prorsus seclusis; vtpote de Galli protenso imperio in Flandriam; de regno Neapoli, Ducatu Mediolanensi, & de prætensis Philippi possessionibus Burgundiæ Prouinciæ, & aliis. Hispanus Quintini fanum, Hanum & Castellatum Gallo, Gallus Theodonis villam Mariæburgum, Iuosum, Damullierium &c. Hispano restituat &c.
units.tr: Among the conditions were also these: that old quarrels and disputes on both sides should be utterly set aside, namely the French claim to empire in Flanders, the kingdom of Naples, the duchy of Milan, the alleged possessions of Philip in the province of Burgundy, and others. The Spaniard was to restore to the Frenchman the shrine of St Quentin, Han and Catelet; the Frenchman was to restore to the Spaniard the village of Thionville, Marienburg, Yvoy, Damvillers, etc.

units.la: Hispanus ducat filiam Galli Isabellam, Sabaudus sororem Galli Margaretham &c.
units.tr: The Spaniard was to marry the French King's daughter Isabella, and the Savoyard the French King's sister Margaret, etc.

units.la: Reliqua capita vide alibi.
units.tr: The remaining articles see elsewhere.

units.la: Instituta gaudia publica.
units.tr: Public joys are instituted.

units.la: Albanus nomine Philippi sponsalitias solemnitates celebrat, Sabaudus ipsemet coram suam ducit.
units.tr: Alba celebrates the betrothal solemnities in the name of Philip; the Savoyard himself takes his bride in person.

units.la: HenricusRex alacrem & fortissimum se præbens contra de-hortationes Reginæ & aliorum etiam, tertio die, & extremo, Montgomerium ad certamen equestre prouocans, læditur in dextro oculo, & post 10. dies moritur.
units.tr: King Henry, showing himself eager and most brave against the dissuasions of the Queen and of others too, on the third day, and the last, challenged Montgomery to an equestrian contest. He was wounded in the right eye and died ten days later.

units.la: Ex filiabus Isabella Hispano nupta est, altera Lotharingiæ Ducissa, tertia Nauarræ Regina facta est. Filii Franciscus, Carolus & Henricus in Regno sibi successerunt. Quartus anno 1582. Brabantiæ Dux inauguratus est.
units.tr: Of the daughters, Isabella was married to the Spaniard, another became Duchess of Lorraine, and the third became Queen of Navarre. The sons Francis, Charles and Henry succeeded to the kingdom. The fourth was inaugurated Duke of Brabant in 1582.

units.la: Paulus IV. P. moritur, Iesuitarum fundator. Et quia is populum bellis & exactionibus grauauit, ideo eius morte lætabatur.
units.tr: Pope Paul IV died, the founder of the Jesuits. And because he had burdened the people with wars and levies, they rejoiced at his death.

units.la: Philippus Belgio in Hispaniam discessurus constituit Belgii Gubernatricem Margaretham, Ducissam Parmæ, suam sororem. Instituit etiam consilium Status, & consilium secretum. Membra huius consilii vide in ipsa historia.
units.tr: Philip, about to depart from Belgium for Spain, appointed as governor of Belgium Margaret, Duchess of Parma, his sister. He also instituted a council of State and a secret council. The members of this council are to be seen in the history itself.

units.la: MARGARETHA GVBERNATRIX BELGII AB ANNO M.D.LIX. VSQVE AD ANNVM 1567.
units.tr: Margaret, Governess of the Netherlands, from the year 1559 to the year 1567

units.la: Philippus secundo aurei Velleris ordinem Gandaui celebrat.
units.tr: Philip celebrates the order of the Golden Fleece at Ghent for the second time.

units.la: Belgarum Status Regi supplicem libellum exhibent, vt militem Hispanum & extraneum extra Regnum dimittat. Quod Rex quidem perpendens, Priuilegiorum rationem promittit, sed eorundem abitus in sesquiennium protrahitur, in id nempe tempus, quo ob perditam in Barbaria Gerbiam militi eo loci opus erat.
units.tr: The States of the Netherlands present a humble petition to the King, asking that he dismiss the Spanish soldiers and foreigners from the kingdom. The King, weighing the matter, promises to respect the privileges, but the departure of the soldiers is delayed for a year and a half, namely until the time when, because Gerbes had been lost in Barbary, soldiers were needed there.

units.la: Quod autem Belgii Status tam acriter instarent, dimittendosque Hispanos postularent, his præcipue mouebantur rationibus. Quod multi Aulici Regi Philippo addictissimi, summæque apud eum auctoritatis, in Belgio permanentes, effundissent, se offensos vindictam expectare, quod in postremis contributionibus & nouennali exactione eis pecuniæ tractandæ adempta esset potestas; cum Status, aulicorum auaritiæ tiæ frena iniicientes, suis hanc colligendi, & stipendiariis Regionis militibus satisfaciendi, prouinciam tradidissent. Quod quidem factum isti euidetem inobedientiæ speciem interpretabantur, vtpote Principi leges statuere volentium, neque publicarum pecuniarum dispensationem ei credentium.
units.tr: The reasons why the States of the Netherlands pressed so hard and demanded that the Spaniards be sent away were these in particular. Many courtiers, most devoted to King Philip and of great authority with him, who remained in the Netherlands, had been offended, and they expected vengeance, because in the last contributions and the nine-year levy the power of handling money had been taken from them. The States, putting a check on the greed of the courtiers, had handed over this task to their own officials, to collect the money and to pay the soldiers who were paid by the country. This action those courtiers took as a plain sign of disobedience, since they regarded the States as wanting to make laws for the prince and as not entrusting to him the disbursement of public money.

units.la: His se iunxerunt & alii quidam, tam indigenæ, quàm alienigenæ, auctoritatem atque gubernacula in primis aucupantes, ac propositum opinionemque Regis, Ducis Albani, Inquisitorum Hispanorum & aliorum promouere studentes. Horum praecipuus erat scopus, Lutheranos & haereticos, neque ex Belgio, neque ex Hispania quidem posse profligari, nisi Rex plena absolutaque obedientia, potestate, & iurisdictione in Regionibus suis inferioribus potiatur, atque Inquisitionem Hispano more instituat: alias enim actum esse de regionibus: Istud autem peregrinorum militum praesidiis moliri consultissimum esse.
units.tr: Certain others joined them, both natives and foreigners, who were chiefly hunting for authority and the helm of government, and who were striving to advance the purpose and opinion of the King, of the Duke of Alva, of the Spanish Inquisitors and of others. The chief aim of these men was that the Lutherans and heretics could be put down neither in the Netherlands nor indeed in Spain, unless the King obtained full and absolute obedience, power and jurisdiction in his lower provinces, and set up the Inquisition in the Spanish manner; otherwise, they said, it would be all over with the countries. And they held that it was most advisable to bring this about by means of the garrisons of foreign soldiers.

units.la: Haec artes prouidis circumspectisque aliquot è Statuum numero viris satis notæ, eos tam instanter abitum Hispanorum persequi coegerunt.
units.tr: These schemes, known well enough to some of the wise and circumspect men from the number of the States, compelled them to pursue so urgently the departure of the Spaniards.

units.la: Rex in Hispaniam nauigat.
units.tr: The King sails to Spain.

units.la: Rex Siuiliæ seuerissime in Euangelicos animaduertit, postea 28. Nobiles primarios exuri mandat.
units.tr: The King of Sicily punished the Evangelicals most severely; afterwards he ordered twenty-eight of the leading nobles to be burnt.

units.la: M. D. LX. Adducitur Isabella sponsa. Celebrantur nuptiæ inenarrabili sumptu & pompa.
units.tr: 1560. Isabella is brought to be married. The wedding is celebrated with unspeakable expense and pomp.

units.la: Omnia Hispaniarum Regna Carolo, Philippi filio, tanquam futuro Regi, iusiurandum præstant.
units.tr: All the kingdoms of Spain take the oath to Charles, son of Philip, as the future King.

units.la: Sub Francisco Rege Galliæ orta sunt odia Nobilium contra Guisios, quasi Regis iuuenis auctoritate pro suo libitu abuterentur, & tanquam à Carolo Magno descendentes, ad Regnum adspirarent.
units.tr: Under King Francis of France, hatreds arose among the nobles against the Guises, on the ground that they abused the authority of the young King as they pleased, and that, descended from Charlemagne, they aspired to the kingdom.

units.la: Secuta seditio Ambosæ, occisus Reginaudius, & reliqui Nobiles capite plexi. Habitum colloquium Poissiacenum de religione.
units.tr: Then followed the uprising at Amboise, Renaudie was killed, and the remaining nobles were beheaded. The colloquy of Poissy on religion was held.

units.la: M. D. LXI. Edictum Ianuarii de pace religionis in Gallia, vt reforreformatæ Ecclesiæ suas conciones extra ciuitates haberent. Sed id per Guisianos breui post infringitur. Concio Vassiæ congregata disturbatur, fugatur, cædITur.
units.tr: 1561. The January Edict on the peace of religion in France was issued, so that the reformed Church might hold its sermons outside the cities. But soon afterwards this was violated by the Guisians. The sermon gathered at Vassy was disturbed, put to flight and struck down.

units.la: Sub vidua Francisci Galli Scota, Scotia à Gallico milite turbatur, Papismo restaurato. Verum Scoti Anglorum auxilio Gallos premunt, & reformatam religionem introducunt.
units.tr: Under the widow of Francis, the Scottish Queen, Scotland was troubled by French soldiers, and Popery was restored. But the Scots, with the help of the English, pressed the French and introduced the reformed religion.

units.la: Galli Heblenouum obsidēt. Angli peste absumpti vrbem dedunt, & in Angliam reuersi luem in eam inferunt, vt Leodini autumnali tempore 23. M. hominum sint extincta.
units.tr: The French besieged Havre. The English, carried off by plague, surrendered the town, and on returning to England they brought the pestilence into it, so that in the autumn season at Leuven 23,000 people were killed.

units.la: Nota ea, quæ in Meterano extant de Collegiis Sagittariorum. Item de Gildis seu exercitiis Rhetoricis Belgarum, &c.
units.tr: Note what is found in Meteren about the guilds of archers, and likewise about the guilds or rhetorical societies of the Belgians, etc.

units.la: Addendum hic aliquid est de Priuilegiis Belgarum. Regiones quidem aliæ paucioribus, aliæ gaudent fruunturque pluribus Priuilegiis. Imprimis autem Brabantia & ditiones vltra Mosam, vt Limburgum, Valkenburgum, Dalhemium, inter alia multa lætum introitum, additiones, chartas, & Bullam aureaam obseruant, quibus præcipua hæc continentur priuilegia.
units.tr: Something should be added here about the privileges of the Belgians. Some regions enjoy fewer privileges, others more. Above all, Brabant and the lands beyond the Meuse, such as Limburg, Valkenburg and Dalhem, observe, among many other things, the joyful entry, the additions, the charters and the Golden Bull, in which the chief privileges are contained, namely these.

units.la: Brabantiæ Ducem suis subditis bonum & fidelem dominum futurum.
units.tr: That the Duke of Brabant will be a good and faithful lord to his subjects.

units.la: Nihil vi aut violentia in eos attentaturum, aut attentari vllo modo permissurum.
units.tr: That he will attempt nothing against them by force or violence, nor permit anything of the kind to be attempted in any way.

units.la: Extra iudicium cum eis nequaquam acturum, aut eos etiam agere toleraturum. Verum omnia iure iudicioque facturum, secundum Ciuitatum & tribunalium leges ac iura, quibus Reo palam & coram Iudicibus se per suos Aduocatos tueri conceditur.
units.tr: That he will by no means proceed against them outside the courts of justice, nor allow them to be proceeded against in that way. But that he will do everything by law and judicial process, according to the laws and rights of the cities and tribunals, by which the accused is permitted to defend himself openly and before the judges through his advocates.

units.la: Statum Ecclesiasticum neque promoturum, neque auctu-rum. Præterea regionis Statum non immutaturum citra Nobilium & Ciuitatum consensum.
units.tr: That he will neither promote nor increase the ecclesiastical estate. Moreover, that he will not alter the state of the region without the consent of the nobles and cities.

units.la: Officiis publicis nullos nisi Brabantos, eosque legitimo thoro natos præfecturum certis quibusdam, iisdemque parui momenti officiis exceptis.
units.tr: That he will appoint to public offices none but Brabanters, and those born in lawful wedlock, with the exception of certain offices of little importance.

units.la: Officiorum administratores & præfectos fidei obsequiique iusiurandum Duci regioni præstituros. Ducem nullum bellum suscepturum, nullum pignus apprehensurum, aut tale quid permissurum absque Ciuitatum & regionum consensu.
units.tr: That the administrators and officers of offices will take an oath of loyalty and obedience to the Duke of the region. That the Duke will undertake no war, seize no pledge, nor permit any such thing, without the consent of the cities and regions.

units.la: Militem nullum extraneum in regiones citra Statuum consensum adducturum aut habiturum.
units.tr: That he will bring in or keep no foreign soldier in the regions without the consent of the States.

units.la: Contentum quoque futurum suis redditibus & tributis legitimis, ordinariisque, neque novas vllas exactiones, nisi certas ob causas, Statibusque Regionum approbantibus impositurum.
units.tr: That he will also be content with his own revenues and his lawful and ordinary taxes, and will impose no new exactions, except for certain causes and with the approval of the States of the regions.

units.la: Non conuocaturum Statuum conuentum extra Brabantiae limites. Status praeterea ipsos nullo modo, vt extra Brabantiam aliquid constituant aut concludant, teneri.
units.tr: That he will not summon an assembly of the States outside the limits of Brabant. Moreover, the States are in no way bound to decide or conclude anything outside Brabant.

units.la: Nummum cudere sine Statuum consilio, voluntate & consensu ei non licere. &c.
units.tr: That it is not lawful for him to coin money without the counsel, will and consent of the States, etc.

units.la: Si autem Dux Brabantiae in priuilegia aut legum Prouinciaium chartas delinquat vel peccet, suoue iussu aut permissu contra fiat, vasallos subditosque ab omni fide & obedientia absolutos atque liberos esse, (nisi desistat, restauret, renuntietque) ex ipsis priuilegiis typo impressis manifesto liquet.
units.tr: If, however, the Duke of Brabant offends or transgresses against the privileges or the charters of the laws of the provinces, or if anything is done contrary to them by his command or permission, then the vassals and subjects are absolved from all faith and obedience and are free (unless he desists, makes amends and renounces it). This is plain from the privileges themselves, printed in type.

units.la: Habent & aliae Belgarum Prouinciae similia priuilegia, ita vt ipse Princeps, non quod vult, sed quod priuilegia, quae ante inaugurationem vbiq; iuramento confirmare tenetur, exigunt, facere debeat. Imo Belgas priuilegiorum vigore suis Principibus imperium omne abrogasse atque sequestrasse, Chronici libri liquido diuersis exemplis demonstrant.
units.tr: The other provinces of the Belgians also have similar privileges, so that the prince himself must do, not what he wishes, but what the privileges demand, which he is bound to confirm by oath everywhere before his inauguration. Indeed, the chronicles clearly show by various examples that the Belgians, by virtue of their privileges, have abrogated and set aside all rule over their princes.

units.la: His autem Belgarum Prouinciarum priuilegiis non obstantibus, anno 1521, Luthero in Germania superiore exurgente, Carolus V. Imp. summo zelo Catholicae Romanae Ecclesiae religionis obseruandae, atque Lutheranae doctrinae a Belgarum ditionibus auertendae, mandata edictaque dura & dira contra omnes generaliter sectas edidit, ac quouis fere anno renouauit. Vt autem Status Regionum ad istius negotii consilium non conuocati, populusque Belgicus haec omnia facilius rata haberet, fuere huiusmodi edicta praecipue enormibus schismaticorum corum & hæreticorum (vtpote hominum absq; regula & lege viuentium, Imperii Magistratusque auctoritatem omnem aspernantium, prorsusque abolere molientium) facinoribus fundata: doctrina ipsa veteres hæreses omnes permixte comprehendente, vt ex iisdem placitis satis liquido adhuc constat.
units.tr: Yet, notwithstanding these privileges of the Belgian provinces, in 1521, when Luther had risen up in Upper Germany, the Emperor Charles V, with the greatest zeal for observing the Catholic and Roman religion and for keeping Lutheran doctrine away from the Belgian lands, issued harsh and dreadful mandates and edicts against all sects in general, and renewed them almost every year. But so that the States of the regions, who had not been summoned to the council on this business, and the Belgian people might more readily accept all these measures, such edicts were founded chiefly on the monstrous crimes of those schismatics and heretics (men living without rule or law, who scorn all authority of the Empire and magistrates and strive to overthrow them altogether), and on a doctrine that mixed together all the ancient heresies, as is still sufficiently clear from the same decrees.

units.la: Hac arte factum, vt prædicta placita atque decreta à regionibus quidem admissa, non tamen à Statibus confirmata fuerint. Idque eo magis, quod Pontifex Romanus & ordo Ecclesiasticus ea, tanquam ad obedientiam S. Matris Romanæ Ecclesiæ imprimis spectantia, stricte obseruari feruide instarent atque vrgerent, neque querelæ vllæ generales, sed particulares quædam tantum super his initio auditæ.
units.tr: By this device it came about that the aforesaid decrees and edicts were indeed admitted by the regions, but were not confirmed by the States. And this the more so because the Roman Pontiff and the ecclesiastical order urged and pressed that these be strictly observed, as bearing above all on obedience to the holy Mother, the Roman Church; and at first no general complaints were heard about them, only some particular ones.

units.la: Editorum placitorumque huiusmodi vigore atque rigore, nemini doctrinam, libros aut à Luthero, Wiclefo, Zwinglio, Melanchthone, aliisue similib. edita, qualicunque lingua habere, emere, dare, gerere, legere, conferre aut disputando tractare licitum erat. Interdictum præterea, inter se conferre aut disputare de sacra scriptura, aliisque eam prælegere. (exceptis Theologiæ Doctoribus, cæterisque admissis & approbatis) Ad hæc vetitum, ne quis sciens conscíusue suspectos domo aut hospitio recipiat, eis alimentum, pecuniam, amictum suppediDet, sed eosdem statim deferat, (poena capitis bonorumque amissione constituta) viris gladio plectendis, mulieribus autem viuis terra obruendis, defodiendisq;, dummodo errorem hæresimque abnegantes, ad Romanam religionem se recipiant: alioquin obstinatis exurendis, atque vt de bonis suis testamento, donatione, aut alio modo disponant inhabilibus reddendis. Decretorum itaque prædictorum vi, imperante Carolo V. in Belgio capite truncata, submersa, suspensa, defossa, exusta, aliisque mortis generibus extincta, vltra quinquaginta, vt quidam scribunt, hominum millia: primo plurimis (ob leues admodum causas, nempe carnium esum certis diebus vetitum, seruatos aut lectos libellos, damnata tamen doctrina iisdem údem contenta) Sacerdotibus quoque & Monachis, ob ductas fornicationis vitandæ causa vxores, vita priuatis, vt multis ea de re scriptis libris liquet.
units.tr: By the force and rigour of the edicts and decrees of this kind, no one was permitted to have, buy, give, carry, read, compare or discuss in disputation any books or doctrine published by Luther, Wycliffe, Zwingli, Melanchthon or other similar writers, in whatever language. It was further forbidden to confer or dispute among themselves about Holy Scripture, or to read it aloud to others (except for the doctors of theology and others admitted and approved). Besides this, it was forbidden for anyone knowingly or consciously to receive suspected persons into his house or inn, or to supply them with food, money or clothing, but he must at once hand them over, under penalty of death and loss of goods: men were to be punished by the sword, women to be buried alive and interred, provided that they renounced their error and heresy and returned to the Roman religion; otherwise the obstinate were to be burnt, and they were to be rendered incapable of disposing of their goods by will, gift or any other means. Accordingly, by force of the aforesaid decrees, under the rule of Charles V, more than fifty thousand people, as some write, were put to death in the Netherlands: beheaded, drowned, hanged, buried alive, burnt, or killed by other kinds of death. At first very many were destroyed for very slight causes, namely for eating meat on forbidden days, for keeping or reading little books, the doctrine of which was condemned although the books themselves contained it, and also priests and monks who had taken wives in order to avoid fornication, and who were deprived of life, as many books written on this matter make clear.

units.la: Quum autem hac persecutione parum proficeretur, tandem ab Imperatore, consilio quorundam, Hispanica inquisitio, in Hispaniam contra Mauros siue Saracenos & Iudæos Granatenses subiugatos inuecta, proponitur. Perspectum enim habebant ipsa experientia edocti, plurimos, (qui se in fidei negotio modeste cauteque gererent nouerant, ita vt eos in statuta edictaque peccasse testibus probari non posset) neque capite, aut bonis multare, aut adhibitis tormentis quæstionem habere, fas iuraque patriæ permitterent, sine Inquisitione obrui, opprimique non posse. Proinde Prouinciam, onus atque potestatem in homines inquirendi, & vnumquemque de sua & aliorum, quos nosset, fide examinandi, Ecclesiasticis dare decernunt.
units.tr: When, however, this persecution achieved little, at last, on the advice of certain men, the Spanish Inquisition was proposed to the Emperor. It had been brought into Spain against the Moors or Saracens and the Jews of Granada after their subjection. For those who had learned from experience had clearly seen that many people, who were known to conduct themselves modestly and cautiously in matters of faith, so that they could not be proved by witnesses to have broken the statutes and edicts, could not be crushed without an Inquisition, since the laws and customs of the country did not permit them to be punished with death or loss of property, or to be examined under torture. Therefore they decreed that the office, burden and power of inquiring into men, and of examining each person's faith and that of others he knew, be given to the ecclesiastics.

units.la: Hic agendi inquirendique modus Belgis, spirituali iurisdictioni huius rei causa nequaquam subiectis, nimium rigidus, durus, atque libertati patriæ, priuilegiisque aduersari visus, maxime quod Lutheranorum protestantium, aut reformatorum (vt tunc appellabantur) numerus in Belgio supra modum accreuisset, cum ab omnibus quoquo versum vicinis Christiani piique haberentur, & quod huiusmodi decretorum edictorumque executione Belgæ vicinarum adiacentiumque regionum, quibus cum (magno suo lucro) commercia agebant, hostes persecutoresque reputarentur.
units.tr: This method of proceeding and inquiring seemed far too harsh and severe to the Belgians, who were by no means subject to spiritual jurisdiction in this matter, and contrary to the liberty and privileges of the country. This was especially so because the number of Lutheran Protestants, or Reformed (as they were then called), had increased in Belgium beyond measure, while on every side they were regarded as Christian and pious by all their neighbours. Moreover, the Belgians, through the execution of such decrees and edicts, were regarded as enemies and persecutors by the neighbouring regions with which they carried on trade to their great profit.

units.la: Proinde Carolo V. Anno 1550. formam quandam Inquisitionis introducere volente, regio tota, præcipue Brabantia, strenue intercedit, contradicitque: imprimis vero Antuerpienses extraneorum mercatorum discessum veriti, quouis modo resistunt, summa Gubernatricis Mariæ Hungariæ Reginæ ope, quæ mero patriæ amore Augustam Vindelicorum (vbi Comitia tunc habita) ad fratrem Imperatorem profecta, coram ingenueque statum & situm Belgicarum declarans regionum, gionum, ab eo placitorum edictorumque mitigationem, & Inquisitionis abrogationem impetrat. Quod quidem egregium clementis Reginæ factum adeo ægre & inique Inquisitores Hispani tulerunt, vt ex Hispania apud Imperatorem fratrem hæreseos accusata fuerit; cum tamen hac opera Regiones suo Principi ita deuinxerit, vt nullum onus, nullam exactionem, necessitate vrgete, Carolo recusauerint: imo filio suo Regi Philippo, (tametsi forma quædam inquisitionis in Flandria, aliisque locis adhuc obseruata fuerit) bellis contra Gallos (Belgii causa nequaquam susceptis) quadraginta millones (vt vocant) florenorum intra nouem annos suppeditauerint. Pace vero iam composita, cum Belgicæ regiones pro maximis suis in Principem meritis se mitius regendas, gubernandasque sperarent, certo tandem compererunt, Doctorem Sonnium Anno 1558. Romam profectum, à Paulo IV. P. Bullas datas 19. Martii 1559. & postea à Pio IV. P. 1560. 8. Martii Regis Philippi nomine Belgicas ditiones ornandi decorandique gratia obtinuisse, auctoritate attributa tres Archiepiscopatus instituendi, quod hæ Provinciæ imprimis diuites, potentes & populosæ essent, quodque veteres Episcopatus longius & latius se extenderent, quam vt Episcopi debitam suarum ouium rationem, coramque habere possent, decretumque, hos Archiepiscopos & Episcopos possessionibus, redditibus & obuentionib. præcipuarum Abbatiarum vtifrui debere. Quæ quidem omnia perac-ta, executionique fuere destinata, ipsis veteribus Episcopis & Abbatibus insciis atque inconsultis, nulla quoque ad Status, Regiones aut Ciuitates rogatione ea de relata.
units.tr: Therefore, when Charles V wished to introduce a certain form of Inquisition in 1550, the whole region, especially Brabant, vigorously interceded and objected. Above all the Antwerpers, fearing the departure of foreign merchants, resisted in every way, with the great help of Queen Mary of Hungary, the Governess. Out of pure love of country she went to Augsburg of the Vindelici, where the Diet was then being held, to her brother the Emperor. There she set out in person and frankly the state and condition of the Belgian regions, and obtained from him a mitigation of the edicts and decrees that had been passed and the abrogation of the Inquisition. This noble deed of the gracious Queen so bitterly and unjustly angered the Spanish Inquisitors that they accused her of heresy to her brother the Emperor from Spain. Yet by this effort she bound the regions so closely to their Prince that, although pressed by necessity, they refused Charles no burden or exaction. Indeed, they supplied his son King Philip with forty million florins (as they are called) within nine years for wars against the French, wars by no means undertaken on behalf of Belgium, although some form of inquisition was still observed in Flanders and other places. But when peace had now been concluded, and the Belgian regions hoped to be governed more gently on account of their great merits towards the Prince, they at last learned for certain that Doctor Sonnius had gone to Rome in 1558. From Pope Paul IV he obtained bulls dated 19 March 1559, and afterwards from Pius IV, on 8 March 1560, in the name of King Philip, for the adorning and beautifying of the Belgian dominions. By this authority three archbishoprics were to be established, because these provinces were especially rich, powerful and populous, and because the old bishoprics extended too far and wide for the bishops to give due account of their sheep and oversee them. There was also a decree that these archbishops and bishops should enjoy the possessions, revenues and income of the principal abbeys. All these things were carried out and set in motion without the knowledge or consultation of the old bishops and abbots, and no request on this matter was made to the estates, regions or cities.

units.la: Noui Archiepiscopatus nominatæ vrbes Mechlinia, Cameracum, & Vltraiectum, quarum duæ antea Episcopatus nunc Archiepiscopatus factæ. Mechlinia autem in ipso Brabantiæ meditullio sita, omnium suprema atque metropolitana. Noui Episcopatus Brabantiæ, Antuerpia & Buscumducis, Flandriæ Gandauum, Brugæ & Hypiæ Artesia, tanum Omari, Namurcensis regionis Namurcum, Hollandiæ Harlemum, Zelandiæ diæ Midelburgum, Frisiæ Louarda & Groninga, Geldriæ Ruremunda, Transisulanæ regionis Dauentria, &c.
units.tr: The new archbishoprics are the cities named Mechlin, Cambrai and Utrecht, of which two had previously been bishoprics and were now made archbishoprics. Mechlin, situated in the very middle of Brabant, is the highest and metropolitan of all. The new bishoprics are: in Brabant, Antwerp and Bois-le-Duc; in Flanders, Ghent, Bruges and Ypres; in Artois, Saint-Omer; in the region of Namur, Namur; in Holland, Haarlem; in Zeeland, Middelburg; in Friesland, Leeuwarden and Groningen; in Guelders, Roermond; in the region of Overijssel, Deventer, etc.

units.la: Granuellanus designatus Archiepiscopus Mechlinienſis primarius, qui & Cardinalis fuit. Hæc vbi post Regis discessum Belgarum populus manifeste resciscit, continuo vndique reclamatur, obmurmuraturque, &c.
units.tr: Granvelle, designated chief Archbishop of Mechlin, who was also a Cardinal. When the people of Belgium clearly learned this after the King's departure, they at once protested from every side and murmured against it, etc.

units.la: Episcopi Leodienſis, Cameracenſis & Traiectensis de iurisdictionum limitumque suorum diminutione graauem querelam interponunt, & quod sua iura dominiaque nouis Episcopis traderentur.
units.tr: The bishops of Liège, Cambrai and Utrecht lodge a grave complaint about the diminution of their jurisdictions and boundaries, and that their rights and domains were handed over to the new bishops.

units.la: Abbatiæ quædam, quorum Abbates mortui erant anno 1561. Curiam instanter de eligedis nouis Abbatibus vrgent. Et nihil obtinentes, cum Nobilibus Metropolitanisque Brabantiæ ciuitatibus, tres patriæ Status representantibus Consociatis, acrius insistunt, quibus Gubernatrix, hæc non in sua potestate, verum à Rege postulanda esse, respondet. Mittunt igitur ad Regem, & sua iura declarant: Sed anno 1562. postulata negantur.
units.tr: Certain abbeys, whose abbots had died in 1561, urgently pressed the court to elect new abbots.
