Gaining nothing, they joined with the nobles and the metropolitan cities of Brabant, and with the three estates representing the country, and pressed the matter more sharply. The Governess replied that this was not within her power but must be requested from the King. They therefore sent to the King and declared their rights, but in 1562 their demands were refused.

units.la: Abbatiæ nequaquam contentæ, sociatis Brabantiæ Statibus à Gubernatrice postulant 5. Maii, causam iudicio agi, sed etiam hoc eis nequaquam conceditur.
units.tr: The abbeys, by no means content, together with the allied estates of Brabant, asked the Governess on 5 May that the matter be decided by a court of law, but this too was not granted to them.

units.la: Antuerpienses imprimis nouum Episcopum Sonnium recusant. Nam ab Inquisitione Hispanica sibi metuebant.
units.tr: The Antwerpers above all refused the new bishop Sonnius, for they feared the Spanish Inquisition.

units.la: Mittunt etiam Legatos ad Regem, qui viua voce respondet, eos nulla Inquisitione molestandos, & postquam Legatos per annum detinuisset, anno 1563. in Augusto spem multam proponit, id temporis certas ob causas Antuerpiensis Episcopi introitum prorogandi differendique.
units.tr: They also sent envoys to the King, who replied by word of mouth that they should not be troubled by any Inquisition. After keeping the envoys for a year, in August 1563 he held out much hope, while for certain reasons of that time he postponed and deferred the entry of the Bishop of Antwerp.

units.la: Interim proceres aurei Velleris Florentium Montignium ad Regem mittunt, & is etiam parvo cum fructu redit.
units.tr: Meanwhile the nobles of the Order of the Golden Fleece sent Florent de Montigny to the King, and he too returned with little result.

units.la: Summum sæpe periculum extitit in exequendis supplicis reformatorum, populo contra carnifices tumultuante.
units.tr: The greatest danger often arose in carrying out the supplications against the Reformed, when the people rose in tumult against the executioners.

units.la: M. D. LXIII. attentatur Concilii Tridentini apud Belgas observatio.
units.tr: In 1563 an attempt was made to enforce the observance of the Council of Trent among the Belgians.

units.la: Pertransiit Belgium Elephas iuuenis, sed magnæ molis, Maximiliano Regi Rom. permare missus, qui fe coram Dominis & Dominabus ciuiliter incuruare nouerat.
units.tr: A young elephant, though of great bulk, passed through Belgium, sent by sea to Maximilian, King of the Romans. It had learned to bow politely before the lords and ladies.

units.la: Hyems vsque Epiphaniæ diem peracris.
units.tr: The winter was very harsh until the day of Epiphany.

units.la: M. D. LXIV. obiit diem Ferdinandus Imp. die Iacobi. Odium & discordia inter proceres Belgii & Cardinalem elate arroganterque fe fe gerentem.
units.tr: In 1564 the Emperor Ferdinand died on St James's day. There was hatred and discord between the nobles of Belgium and the Cardinal, who conducted himself haughtily and arrogantly.

units.la: Cardinalis quidem discedit in Burgundiam, sed orta est dissensio Statuum Belgii, quam Cardinaliftæ, vt vocabantur, pariebant.
units.tr: The Cardinal indeed departed for Burgundy, but a dissension arose among the Estates of Belgium, which the so-called Cardinalists stirred up.

units.la: Status Brabantiæ mittunt Egmondanum ad Regem, qui ei regionum statum coram exponat, nouorumque Episcoporum abolitionem, Inquisitionis abrogationem, edictorumque mitigationem impetret, vt imminentia mala quàm plurima auertantur. Et licet ei spes facta sit, quasi Rex sit assensurus, tamen nihil solidi est secutum. Et licet placitorum quædam mitigatio conclusa à quibusdam est: tamen à maleuolis quibusdam Regi consilium datum est, vt Belgium summa sævitia tractet, Inquisitionem Hispanicam inuehat. Quod si se exagitata rebellem præstet, occasiones satis multas facile occursuras, ob quas absolutio iuramenti, Prouinciis à sua Maiestate præstiti, Romani Præsulis authoritate facile impetrari posset. Hac ratione ei facile licitumque esse, Hispanos & extraneos introducere, regiones subiugare, domare, imo pro recens deuictis, debellatrisque (nequaquam patrimonialibus) habere, eas in regnum commutare, & tali regno necessarias leges constituere, Belgarum proceres aliquot capite plectere, vt reliquis timor metusque iniiciatur. Hinc est quod Rex Gubernatrici postea suum edictum perfecte absolutum transmisit. Inde posteriores turbæ ortæ.
units.tr: The estates of Brabant sent Egmont to the King, to set out the state of the regions before him and to obtain the abolition of the new bishops, the abrogation of the Inquisition, and the mitigation of the edicts, so that very many impending evils might be averted. Although he was given hope, as if the King would agree, nothing solid followed. Although some mitigation of the decrees was agreed upon by certain people, yet some ill-disposed men gave the King counsel that he should treat Belgium with the greatest severity and introduce the Spanish Inquisition. If the harassed people showed themselves rebellious, there would soon be ample occasions, for which absolution from the oath sworn to the Provinces by His Majesty could easily be obtained by the authority of the Roman Pontiff. By this plan it would be easy and lawful for him to introduce Spaniards and foreigners, to subdue and tame the regions, and indeed to hold them as newly conquered and won by war (by no means as his patrimony), to turn them into a kingdom and to establish laws needed for such a kingdom, and to put some of the Belgian nobles to death, so that fear and dread might be struck into the rest. Hence the King later sent the Governess his edict, fully absolved. Thence arose the later disturbances.

units.la: Antuerpiæ eduntur crudelia supplicia aduersus Religiosos, vno etiam ex ministris Ecclesiæ reformatæ, Christophoro Smitho, crudeliter interfecto, rem ita grauiter populo indignante, vt ad periculosum motum prope eruperit. Transactio inter Anglos & Belgas, quo ad mercimoniorum commutationem.
units.tr: In Antwerp cruel punishments were inflicted on the Religious, and one of the ministers of the Reformed Church, Christopher Smith, was cruelly killed. The people took this so gravely amiss that it nearly broke into a dangerous uprising. An agreement between the English and the Belgians concerning the exchange of merchandise.

units.la: M. D. LXV. Melita obsidetur a Turca, Sed Christiano milite succurrente, Turca obsidionem soluit.
units.tr: In 1565 Malta was besieged by the Turk, but with Christian soldiers coming to its aid, the Turk lifted the siege.

units.la: M. D. LXVI. Turca Sigetum in Vngaria oppugnat, Soliman no Turcarum Imp. in castris defuncto, cui Selimus fil. in Imp. succedit.
units.tr: In 1566 the Turk attacked Szigetvár in Hungary. Suleiman, Emperor of the Turks, died in the camp, and his son Selim succeeded him as emperor.

units.la: Alexander Farnesius Parmensis, filius Gubernatricis, celebrat nuptias Bruxellis cum Maria, Eduardi Iohannis Regis Portugalliæ filii filia.
units.tr: Alexander Farnese of Parma, son of the Governess, celebrated his wedding at Brussels with Maria, daughter of Eduard, son of King John of Portugal.

units.la: Inquisitio Hispanica Venetiis & Mediolani recusatur.
units.tr: The Spanish Inquisition was refused at Venice and at Milan.

units.la: M.D.LXV. Rex igitur Hispaniar. Philippus, vt doctrinam Euangelii ex Belgio eliminaret, per Gubernatricem Margaretham mandauit, vt edicta Caroli patris renouaretur, vt Concilii Tridentini executio effectui mandaretur, & vt Inquisitio Hispanica introduceretur. Et ne in his expediendis Magistratus & præsides remissiores existant, & vt noui Episcopi negotium promoueant, seuere præcepit: Id enim ad prohibendas hæreses vnice necessarium, & ad obtinendam pacem in Belgio vehementer vtile futurum. Idque mense Decembri.
units.tr: In 1565, therefore, Philip, King of Spain, so that he might eliminate the doctrine of the Gospel from Belgium, ordered through the Governess Margaret that the edicts of his father Charles be renewed, that the execution of the Council of Trent be carried into effect, and that the Spanish Inquisition be introduced. And lest the magistrates and presidents be too lax in carrying these out, and so that the new bishops might advance the business, he sternly commanded it. For this was uniquely necessary for suppressing heresies and would greatly help to secure peace in Belgium. This was in December.

units.la: M.D.LXVI. de his mandatis conquerûtur Ciuitates Brabantiæ apud Consilium Brabantiæ, quod essent contra iuramenta vtrinque præstita. Consilium & Curia respondet, his mandatis nihil noui postulari, sed ea tantum talia esse, quæ etiam superioribus annis proposita fuissent. Populus videns sibi proceres aduersari, magis irritatur. Hinc libelli famosi, & scriptura inuectiua passim spargi, ipsique Gubernatrici obgeri.
units.tr: In 1566 the cities of Brabant complained to the Council of Brabant about these mandates, arguing that they were contrary to the oaths sworn on both sides. The Council and the Court replied that no new demands were being made by these mandates, which were of the same kind as those already issued in earlier years. The people, seeing that the nobles opposed them, were further roused to anger. Hence defamatory pamphlets and abusive writings were scattered everywhere and thrown in the face of the Governess herself.

units.la: Facta quidem promissio de moderatione edictorum, sed sine effectu. Ideo cum mandatum & institutum hoc Nobilibus quibusdam Euangelicis intempestiuum & graue esse videretur, compositoin ter se fœdere intercesserunt. Asserunt enim, edicta & molitiones illas Priuilegiis Belgiæ aduersari. Inquisitionem illam Hispanicam cum diuinis & humanis legibus pugnare, & summam tyrannidem stabilire, & ad libidinem ambitiosobitioforum & auarorum quorundam magnatum explenda m, & in fraudem & oppressionem suorum Priuilegiorum, & ad extremam pernitiem earum Prouinciarum comparatam esse. Adimi per eam ius & neruum Magistratui, & ea collocari in manus Inquisitorum illorum, vt cum aliquis Hispanus, aut Sacrificulus, aut Monachus alicui infensus est, & se vindicare cogitat, aut opibus alicuius inhiat, mox illum de hæresi accusandi, condemnandi & de vita depellendi ansam capiat.
units.tr: A promise was indeed made to moderate the edicts, but it had no effect. Therefore, since this mandate and its institution seemed to some Evangelical nobles untimely and burdensome, they entered into a compact among themselves. They asserted that the edicts and these measures were contrary to the privileges of Belgium; that the Spanish Inquisition clashed with divine and human laws and established the most extreme tyranny; that it had been devised to satisfy the ambition and greed of certain powerful and avaricious magnates, and to the fraud and oppression of their privileges and the utter ruin of those provinces. Through it, they said, the right and strength of the magistrate were taken away and placed in the hands of those Inquisitors, so that whenever some Spaniard, or some priest or monk, was hostile to someone, or planned revenge, or coveted someone's wealth, he would straightway have a pretext for accusing that man of heresy, condemning him and removing him from life.

units.la: Hanc itaque Inquisitionem Hispanicam & antea deprecati sunt, & iterum 5. Aprilis anni 1566. Bruxellis Nobiles numero circiter 400. præeunte Comite Brederodio Lucenbergio Bergense, & Ludouico Nassouio, & Wilhelmo Auraico, libellum supplicem Gubernatrici offerunt, & vt mitigatio edictorum fiat obtestantur. Ea iam esse tempora & rerum statum, vt sine turba & magnis motibus sævitia illa supplicíorum exerceri amplius non possit.
units.tr: Therefore they had already protested against this Spanish Inquisition, and again, on 5 April 1566, at Brussels, about four hundred nobles, led by Count Brederode of Lucenburg, Ludwig of Nassau and William of Orange, offered a written petition to the Governess and earnestly begged that the edicts be softened. They said that the times and the state of affairs were such that the savagery of those executions could no longer be carried out without tumult and great upheaval.

units.la: Gubernatrix sequente die benigne respondet, se petitionem illam ad Regem missuram, edictum mitigaturam, & à Rege bonum responsum, id quod optet & speret, impetraturam esse. Interim in Religione Catholica nihil mutent.
units.tr: On the following day the Governess replied graciously: she would send that petition to the King, would soften the edict, and hoped and wished that she would obtain a favourable answer from the King. Meanwhile they were not to change anything in the Catholic religion.

units.la: Confœderati porro iterum instant, petentes vt fideles hæc eorum admonitiones ponderentur, ne, si inde turbæ existant, sibi id deinceps imputetur.
units.tr: The confederates, moreover, pressed again, asking that these warnings of theirs be weighed by the faithful, so that, if disturbances arose from them, it might not be imputed to them in future.

units.la: Ad extremum ab Assouilio & quodam Secretario fit promissio de suspensione Inquisitionis, & sic fœderati discedunt.
units.tr: At last Assonleville and a certain secretary made a promise to suspend the Inquisition, and so the confederates departed.

units.la: Confœderati illi dicti sunt Geusii, id est, mendici, ea occasione: Cum enim illi Nobiles ibi apparerent, & quidam ex iis tenuioris fortunæ essent, & ne Gubernatrix sibi ab iis timeret, Dominus Barlemont Gelufios seu Geusios & mendicos illos appellauit.
units.tr: Those confederates were called Geuzen, that is, beggars, on this occasion: when those nobles appeared there, and some of them were of rather modest fortune, and so that the Governess might not fear them, Lord Barlemont called the Geuzen, or beggars, by that name.

units.la: Idilli intelligentes vestes ex vili panno sibi compararunt, & nummos formarunt, in quibus ex vno latere effigies Regis, ex altero geminæ manus mutuo implicatæ, saccus item mendicabuli effiēta fuerunt cum hac inscriptione :.
units.tr: They, understanding this, bought coarse cloth for clothing and struck coins, on one side of which was the effigy of the King, and on the other two hands clasped together; likewise a beggar's wallet was depicted, with this inscription:

units.la: FIDELES REGI VSQVE AD BESACE, id est, vsque ad Peram.
units.tr: FAITHFUL TO THE KING UNTO THE BESACE, that is, unto the wallet.

units.la: Gubernatrix misit Margrafium Bergensem & Baronem Montignium ad Regem. Sed responsum diu dilatum est, & Bergensis in Hispania, Deus novit, quâ mortem obiuit: Montignius vero post aliquod tempus, & antequam noua sponsa, quæ pro eo intercessura erat, adueniret, supplicio affectus est, nec eos Papisticæ religionis professio atque obseruatio (Bergensis enim infantes rebaptisari in sua ditione mandauerat) ab exitio immunes reddidere.
units.tr: The Governess sent the Margrave of Bergen and Baron Montigny to the King. But the answer was long delayed, and the Count of Bergen died in Spain, God knows how; Montigny, moreover, after some time, and before the new bride who was to intercede for him arrived, was executed. Nor did their profession and observance of the Papist religion (for Bergen had ordered infants to be rebaptized in his territory) make them immune from destruction.

units.la: Nonnullis igitur locis, quamuis Parmensis imperio minime parearetur, nihilominus tamen istarum literarum denunciatione, populus ex grauissimæ lanienæ metu recreatus, meliorique adeo spe vtens, modeste se continebat. Ecclesiæque magis ac magis amplificabantur, è Nobilibus plerique adiungebantur, fereque sperabatur, è Regis auctoritate, Ordinumque sententia, rebus prudentius consideratis tutiorem fore propediem statum.
units.tr: Therefore in some places, although they did not obey the Parmese government, nevertheless, with the announcement of these letters, the people, relieved of their fear of most grievous slaughter and enjoying a better hope, restrained themselves modestly. The churches were increasingly enlarged, and most of the nobles joined them; and it was almost hoped that, by the King's authority and the judgment of the Estates, with affairs more prudently considered, the state would soon be safer.

units.la: Pontificii contra pertimescebant periculosam ruinam sub rebus hoc aditu esse substratam. Itaque frequentes ad Parmensem adesse, demonstrare, quanto periculo se totamque adeo obiiciat regionem. Eccur non animaduertat istorum hominum voluntatem, quæ quam sit exitiosa, satis superque constet ex eo, quod ausi fuerint, ipsa nescia, fœdus inire, & ex ipsorum quidem audacissimis petitionibus, qui nimirum ordinum Comitia cum Regia auctoritate impudenter coniungant. &c. Sunt igitur illi auctores, vt Ordinum conuentus ipsa agat, id est, eos, qui futuri sint ad istas res idonei, vocet, nec quisquam, nisi suo Imperio delectus, possit illi cœtui interesse.
units.tr: The Papists, on the other hand, feared that a dangerous ruin had been laid as a foundation by this path of events. Therefore they often came to the Parmese and showed him how great a danger he was exposing himself and the whole region to. Why did he not notice the will of those men, and how deadly it is? It was clear enough from the fact that they had dared, without the knowledge of the government itself, to enter into a league, and from the most audacious petitions of these men, who shamelessly join the assembly of the Estates with royal authority, and so on. They therefore advised that the Governor should himself convene a meeting of the Estates, that is, summon those who would be suitable for these matters; and that no one should be able to attend that assembly unless chosen by his own command.

units.la: Parmensis igitur illorum consilio vtens, Ordines particulares cogit, ibi haud dictæ, vt liberis Comitiorum conuentibus mos est, à singulis sententiæ, sed quasi longarum consultationum summa proposita est formula, quam
units.tr: The Parmese, therefore, following their advice, convened the particular Estates; there, not in the manner of free assemblies of the Estates, where each gives his opinion, but as though it were the sum of long deliberations, a formula was put forward, which

units.la: **Editorum moderationem vocabant, & Regis quidem nomine, iussique, illam suis suffragiis approbare, atque iureiurando confirmare.
units.tr: they called the moderation of the edicts, and in the King's name, and by his command, they were to approve it with their votes and confirm it by oath.

units.la: Moderationis vero illius haec erat sententia, vt in eos omnes, qui religion.nouam sequantur, seuere animaduertatur. Supplicii ratio paululum commutata, patibulis nimirum ignium vice substitutis. Bonorum tamen proscriptiones atque exilia aduersus nouae, quam vocabant, doctrinae studiosos, eodem plane modo sanciebantur, quo superioribus Regiis Edictis.
units.tr: The substance of that so-called moderation was this: that all who followed the new religion should be severely punished. The manner of execution was changed a little, the gallows being substituted for fires. Nevertheless, confiscations of property and exile were decreed against those devoted to what they called the new doctrine, in exactly the same way as under the earlier royal edicts.

units.la: Peruagato Edictii istius rumore, exulceratur renouaturque vix dum obductum vulnus, populusque suas querelas de integro repetit, maximarum calamitatum aditum perspiciens.
units.tr: When the rumour of this edict spread, the wound, scarcely closed, was reopened and renewed, and the people, perceiving the approach of the greatest calamities, once more repeated their complaints.

units.la: Crescebat tamen numerus Religiosorum, qui priuatim suas conciones audiebant. Deinde vero cum dolebant, Euangelii doctrinam ideo male audire, quod clam exerceretur, & esset spes, fore, vt maxima populi pars, si publice religio coleretur, ad nouum illud spectaculum conuolaret, conciones publicas habendas esse statuerunt. Ad extremos igitur Flandriae fines, vbi praefectus erat Com. Egmondanus, primum caeperunt fideles publice coetus agitare, verbi Dei audiendi causa, tum continuo Antuerpiae, inde in caeteris Prouinciis creberrima exempla consecuta sunt, sub finem mensis Iulii. Conueniebant primo extra vrbes inermes, at dum intelligunt sibi necti periculum, passimque vident, Inquisitorum operas circumuolitare, palamque caedes illi minitarentur, pars enses ferre primum, tum validiora arma cum agros peteret.
units.tr: Nevertheless the number of the religious who heard their sermons privately grew. Then, since they grieved that the doctrine of the Gospel was ill regarded because it was practised in secret, and there was hope that, if religion were practised publicly, the greatest part of the people would flock to that new spectacle, they resolved that public sermons should be held. Thus, at the far borders of Flanders, where Count Egmont was governor, the faithful first began to hold public assemblies to hear the word of God; then immediately at Antwerp, and afterwards in the other provinces, very frequent examples followed, toward the end of July. At first they gathered outside the cities, unarmed; but when they understood that danger was being prepared for them, and saw everywhere the agents of the Inquisitors flitting about, and the priests threatening them openly with slaughter, some began to carry swords, and then stronger weapons, when they went into the fields.

units.la: Hoc fuit publicarum in Belgicis Ecclesiis concionum initium, quae multis hominum millibus frequentabantur.
units.tr: This was the beginning of public sermons in the Churches of Belgium, which were attended by many thousands of people.

units.la: Accusati super his responderunt, se in publicum prodiisse, non vt Edictis Regiis illuderent, quibus omnem obedientiam reuerentiamque deberent, & vellent reddere; At non se posse amplius pati intolerabiles importunorum hominum insanias atque vecordias, quae publicam conscientiarum pacem tam nefarie interturbarent, & violatis etiam antiquis vrbium priuilegiis,
units.tr: Those accused of these things replied that they had come out into public not to mock the royal edicts, to which they owed and wished to render all obedience and reverence; but that they could no longer endure the intolerable madness and frenzy of unscrupulous men, who so wickedly disturbed the public peace of consciences, and who, violating also the ancient privileges of the cities,

units.la: uilegiis, uflegiis, omnem fidem, societatemque generis humani improbe pessundarent. Coactos ergo se ad istam necessitatem descendisse, cum alioqui malint publico Regiæ Maiestatis decreto publicarum etiam rerum ordinem gubernari.
units.tr: wickedly overturned all faith and the fellowship of the human race. They said they had therefore been forced into this necessity, although otherwise they would prefer that public affairs too be governed by the public decree of His Royal Majesty.

units.la: Concionibus ad aliquot septimanas pacate agitatis, ecce repentina oboritur in Pontificias imagines tempestas. Primum illæ ad extremos Flandriæ fines profligari coeptæ, inde tempestas illa variis vniuersæ regionis in locis eo impetu emanat, quasi supremi Magistratus disertis mandatis attemperaretur ea idolorum, & paucorum, ad prima quidem initia hominum opera, strange, ea magistratus, Pontificiorumque etiam audacissimorum consternatione, vt fidem res prope superet. Magistratus ita fere erat perterritus, vt, quamuis Pontificiam religio omnino sequeretur, & pauci essent, qui illâ idolorum deiectionem actitarent, ipsi tamen & illud permiserint, & re adiuuerint. Gandaui celeberrimo oppido vnus & alter Prætoris cōsternati permissu & nutu omnium templorum statuas & ritualia ornamenta profligarunt. Lieri Flandriæ oppido idem actitatum, Antuerpiæ latitabat. Magistratus publicæ domus parietibus circumclusus, dum per templa custodiarum etiam nutu discurreretur, atque vbique deiicerentur idola. Rem prudentiores ita agi dolebant: illud tamen omnium sententia & vox sonabat. Si populi, ratione haud certe vtentis, improuidus & temerarius zelus excusari non debet, ecquis vero non perspicit singulare Dei aduersus idola, horribilem humani generis luem, iudicium, quibus occæcatus mundus summam Dei Maiestatem tot tantisque modis iam pridem violasset, dum Principum Maiestates Antichristi lenæ tam solicite opponuntur?
units.tr: While sermons had been conducted peacefully for some weeks, behold, a sudden storm arose against the Papist images. First these were begun to be destroyed at the far borders of Flanders; then that storm broke out in various places throughout the whole region with such violence, as if the supreme magistrates had ordered this destruction of idols by explicit commands; and yet it was at first the work of a few men, with such dismay of the magistrates, and even of the most audacious Papists, that the thing almost exceeds belief. The magistrates were so terrified that, although the Papist religion wholly prevailed, and only a few were carrying out this overthrow of idols, they nevertheless permitted it and even helped it along. At Ghent, a very famous town, one or two of the dismayed city officers, with the permission and nod of all, destroyed the statues and ritual ornaments of all the churches. At Lier, a town of Flanders, the same was done; at Antwerp the magistrate hid himself within the walls of the public house, while the guards ran about the churches at a nod, and idols were thrown down everywhere. The more prudent men lamented that the matter was being conducted in this way; yet the opinion and voice of all was this: if the imprudent and rash zeal of a people, not certainly using reason, cannot be excused, who does not nevertheless see in it the singular judgment of God against idols, that horrible plague of the human race, by which the world, blinded, had for so long violated the supreme majesty of God in so many and great ways, while the majesties of princes are so anxiously set against the pimp of Antichrist?

units.la: Occasio stragis idolorum talis fuit: Antuerpiæ circumferebant Sacriculi de more Festi die 18. Augusti imaginem sanctæ Mariæ, & mature in suum locum reposuerunt. Ibi pueri nebulones in templo illo sub vesperam nugas egerunt, & dicteria in statuam illam iecerunt, & alicui vetulæ, quæ cereos vendere ibi solebat, illuserunt, illa vicissim puluerem in eos proiecit. Sic tumultus est ortus, quem officiarii adcurrentes sedauerunt. Sed sequente vespere proterui illi iuuenes redierunt, & impetu facto conclauia & capsulas effregerunt, statuas inuaserunt, deiecerunt, contriuerunt, eamque vim ea nocte in omnibus templis Antuerp. exercuerunt mirabili prorsus successu.
units.tr: The occasion for the destruction of the images was as follows. At Antwerp, on 18 August, as is customary on the feast day, the sacristans carried an image of the Blessed Virgin Mary in procession and promptly returned it to its place. Then some mischievous boys in that church, in the evening, played their pranks, hurled insults at the statue, and mocked an old woman who customarily sold candles there. She in turn threw dust at them. A disturbance arose, which the officers hurrying up calmed. But on the following evening those bold youths came back, and with a sudden attack they broke open the cupboards and chests, assaulted the statues, threw them down and smashed them, and that night they carried out this violence in all the churches of Antwerp with remarkable success.

units.la: Parmensis interistos motus anxia, ne res ad maiores turbas efferretur, putauit necessarium esse, populum mitioris conditionis pollicitatione sedare, remque per confoederatos Nobiles ref. Relig. tentandam, quorum opera motus illi reprimerentur. Illis ergo ad se Bruxellam vocatis, postulat, vtident operam, ne populi tumultus inualescant. At sub Regis Regiorum queAdministrorum praesidio & tutela reuerenter & pacate degant. Liberas fore conciones, quibuscunque locis hactenus fuerint, &c.
units.tr: Parma, anxious lest these disturbances should grow into greater troubles, judged it necessary to calm the people with a promise of milder treatment, and to attempt the matter through the confederate nobles of the Reformed religion, by whose efforts those movements might be suppressed. Having summoned them to Brussels, he asked them to do their best that the tumults of the people should not gain strength, and to live peacefully and respectfully under the protection and guardianship of the King's officials. Sermons would be free in whatever places they had been held hitherto, and so on.

units.la: Fit itaque solemnis vtrinque stipulatio, atque iureiurando confirmatur, adhibita etiam Procerum fide, sigilloque Regio solemne conditur diploma. Singulis Prouin. Praefectis mandatur, haec pacta publice ac solemniter promulgarent, eque illorum praescripto agerent. Edicto inhibetur, ne quae pro Religione iniuriae verbo factoue fiant, qui fecerit, puniatur. Parmensem declarare, omnes vtriusque Religionis homines in Regia tutela ac manu esse. Prouinciar. Praefecti nonnullis in locis ex Rescripti illius formula suos regunt, loca exercendae religionis designant, templa aedificari permittunt, vtrosque homines in suo praesidio esse iubent, id fit ante mensem Augustum.
units.tr: A solemn agreement was therefore made on both sides and confirmed by oath, with the good faith of the nobles also engaged, and a royal seal gave the formal document its authority. The provincial governors were ordered to proclaim these terms publicly and solemnly, and to act in accordance with what was prescribed. An edict forbade any injury, by word or deed, on account of religion, and whoever did it was to be punished. Parma declared that all men of both religions were under the King's protection and hand. In several places the provincial governors, following the form of that rescript, governed their people, designated places for the exercise of religion, permitted churches to be built, and ordered men of both kinds to be under their protection. This was done before the month of August.

units.la: Ad tumultum, qui Antuerpiae exortus est, sedandum missus est Princeps Vranien sis, qui nomine Regis Gubernator eorum locorum fuit, is certis transactionibus pacem ibi restituit, & Inquisitio Hispanica sublata est, & vtriusque Religionis homines in tutelam Magistratus recepti, & concessae conciones, sed ab inermibus adeundae.
units.tr: To quell the tumult that had broken out at Antwerp, the Prince of Orange was sent, who held the office of governor of those places in the King's name. By certain agreements he restored peace there; the Spanish Inquisition was abolished; men of both religions were received under the protection of the magistrate; and sermons were permitted, but only to be attended unarmed.

units.la: Pluribus rebus vltro citroque ab vtraque parte controuersis, sis, tractatis & constitutis, emergit rumor, Ducem Ericum Brunsuicensem colligere militem contra Geusios. Multi igi-tur Protestantium moliuntur fugam, maxima pars eorūdem, vt optima speret, monetur. Rex Gubernatrici scribit, vt Auraicum & cæteros primates magnificis præconiis ob merita eorum erga Regem lactet & retineat. Idem & Rex ipse scriptis ad Auraicum literis fecit. Verum Auraicus blanditiis his fi-dem noluit habere, & Egmondanum ne sideret commonuit, alias ipsum fore Pontem, super quo Hispani in Belgium sint transituri, eumque deinde, vbi eo satis visi fuerint, sint demolituri.
units.tr: Many matters were disputed, discussed and settled back and forth by both sides, when a rumour spread that Duke Eric of Brunswick was raising soldiers against the Geuzen. Therefore many Protestants began to plan flight, and the greater part of them were advised to hope for the best. The King wrote to the Governess that she should flatter and keep Orange and the other leading men with splendid praises for their services to the King. The King himself also wrote to Orange in a letter. But Orange would not put faith in these flatteries, and he warned Egmont not to trust them, otherwise he himself would be the bridge over which the Spaniards would cross into Belgium, and afterwards, once they had been seen there enough, they would tear it down.

units.la: Interea in Hispania deliberatum conclusumque est, vt vis ad sopiendos motus Belgicos adhiberetur, & vt ei rei praeterito Carolo Regis filio praeferretur Dux Albanus. Rex etiam Gubernatrici scribit, vt mandata ante publicata vim obtineant & effectui mandentur.
units.tr: Meanwhile in Spain it was decided and resolved that force should be used to quell the Belgian movements, and that for this task Duke Alva should be preferred to Don Carlos, the King's son. The King also wrote to the Governess that the orders previously published should have force and be carried into effect.

units.la: Confœderati, cum has minas & iram Regis intelligunt, tre- pidant, aliqui de zelo religionis remittunt, cæteri, sese paran-tes, aliquot Ciuitates occupant. Ex quibus præcipua & munitissima fuit Valentia in Hannonia.
units.tr: When the confederates understood these threats and the King's anger, they were alarmed; some gave up their zeal for religion, while the rest, preparing themselves, seized several cities. Among these the chief and most strongly fortified was Valenciennes in Hainault.

units.la: Gubernatrix eo præsidium collocare voluit, quod Ciues recipere noluerunt. Ideo pro contumacibus declarati, & iussu Gubernatricis per Norcarmium obsessi sunt in Decembri.
units.tr: The Governess wished to place a garrison there, which the citizens refused to admit. Therefore they were declared rebellious, and by the Governess's order they were besieged by Noircarmes in December.

units.la: Dornicenses vrbi subsidio venturi, caesi sunt. Valentiarum vrbs sequenti Martio dedita est certis conditionibus, quibus tamen victor non stetit. Nam is concionatores & primates vr-bis strangulari iussit. Sic reliquæ vrbes perculsæ, præsidia Gu- bernatricis receperunt.
units.tr: The men of Tournai, coming to help the city, were cut down. The city of Valenciennes surrendered in the following March on certain conditions, which the victor nevertheless did not keep. For he ordered the preachers and the chief men of the city to be strangled. Thus the other cities, struck with terror, received the Governess's garrisons.

units.la: Antuerpiæ Principis Orengiani auctoritate non erat istarum turbarum ea intemperies, quæ aliis in locis fere euagabatur. At male sani homines otii nimium pertæsi, & ipsi aliud genus, pugnas instituunt, & q. non satis turbulentorū ingeniorū Antuerpiæ esset, accersiuerunt cum Ecclesiæ ref. hominib. digladiaturos Matthæum Illyricum, Flaccium, Spangenbergiū, & alios, obiecta de Caena Domini infelici controuersia, disputationibus exagitanda, & quidem a capite de omnipraesentia Corporis Christi ducto disputationis initio. Omnia ad pugnam apparantur, dum perturbatior in dies magis ac magis rumor stipendiarios illos Doctores, e longinquis regionibus eo deductos, nouo quodam Augustanae Confessionis commento promulgato, cogit suis rebus prouidere atque mature vasis collectis emigrare, turpi profecto intempestiuaque pugnandi cupiditate ad hoc tempus ridicule demonstrata.
units.tr: At Antwerp, under the authority of the Prince of Orange, that unrestrained frenzy which spread almost everywhere in other places of these disturbances did not occur. But men of unsound mind, weary of idleness, began another kind of fighting. And as if there were not enough turbulent spirits at Antwerp, they summoned Matthias Flacius Illyricus, Spangenberg and others to wrangle with the men of the Reformed Church over the unhappy controversy about the Lord's Supper, to be pursued in disputations, and indeed beginning the disputation from the point concerning the omnipresence of Christ's body. Everything was prepared for battle, while a rumour, growing more disturbing day by day, that those hired teachers, brought there from distant regions, had published some new contrivance of the Confession of Augsburg, compelled them to look to their own affairs and to pack up their goods and leave quickly. This showed, to be sure, a shameful and untimely eagerness for fighting, which has been ridiculously exposed up to the present time.

units.la: M.D.LXVII. Antuerpienses Principibus Consilii supplices ad Regem exhibent, in quibus libertatem Religionis petunt; simul amplissimum Regi honorarium deferunt. Pro Euangelicis etiam Brederodus, cui Bruxella interdicta erat, intercedit. Supplicationes illae Gubernatrici oblatae, ab eadem repudiatae sunt, praetendente, quod isti Regi leges ex insolentia praescribere velint, quando, ut conciones publicae haberentur, nunquam eis antea esset permissum, quando rebelles illi exist-ant, & contra Regem se confoederarint.
units.tr: In 1567 the men of Antwerp presented humble petitions to the King through the members of the Council, in which they asked for freedom of religion; at the same time they offered the King a very generous gift. Brederode, to whom Brussels had been forbidden, also interceded on behalf of the Evangelicals. These petitions, offered to the Governess, were rejected by her, on the pretext that these men wished to prescribe laws to the King out of insolence, since public sermons had never been permitted to them before, and since those men were rebels who had banded together against the King.

units.la: Megano, Mansfeldio, Arenbergio, & Erico Brunsuicense militem pro Gubernatrice colligente, foederati idem faciunt. Brederodus circa Vianam, Thelosius circa Antuerpiam.
units.tr: Meghen, Mansfeld, Aremberg and Eric of Brunswick were raising soldiers for the Governess, and the confederates did the same. Brederode acted near Vianen, Tholouse near Antwerp.

units.la: Antonius Bambergius, militiae Dux Buscumducis in Februario ingressus est. Verum cum Reformatorum res parum succederet, in Aprili rursum discedit.
units.tr: Antonius Bamberg, a military commander, entered Bois-le-Duc in February. But since the affairs of the Reformed went poorly, in April he withdrew again.

units.la: Comes de Megen in Buscoducis & Viana Protestantes obruit; & omnes Euangelici pro rebellibus declarantur.
units.tr: The Count of Meghen overwhelmed the Protestants at Bois-le-Duc and Vianen, and all Evangelicals were declared rebels.

units.la: Qua de re Euangelici Belgio excedunt, qui possunt, & Egmondanus in Artois & Flandria, & Auraicus Antuerpiae concliones intermitti fecerunt.
units.tr: Because of this, the Evangelicals who could leave Belgium did so, and Egmont in Artois and Flanders, and Orange at Antwerp, caused the sermons to be discontinued.

units.la: Tholusius Flissingam inuadere tentat, sed frustra. Is deinde militem suum duxit in Osterwil, prope Antuerpiam, sed is ibi per Gubernatricis exercitum fusus est; ipse in horreo combustus, capto catalogo confoederatorum singulorum. Mox intra Antuerpiam maximus tumultus ortus est, quem Auraicus sedauit. dauit, certis articulis propositis & receptis, mense Martio,
units.tr: Tholouse tried to attack Flushing, but in vain. He then led his soldiers to Oosterweel, near Antwerp, but there he was routed by the Governess's army; he himself was burned in a barn, and a list of all the individual confederates was seized. Soon a very great tumult arose within Antwerp, which Orange calmed, with certain articles proposed and accepted in March.

units.la: Brederodus à Gubernatrice pro seditioso damnatur, is Nobilibus confœderatis valedicere iussis cum familia & supellectile Embdam, & inde in Germaniam superiorem proficiscitur, vbi è vita migrat. Vidua eius ex familia de Moers, postea Friderico Electori Palatino nupsit.
units.tr: Brederode was condemned by the Governess as a seditious man. Ordered to bid farewell to the confederate nobles, he set off with his household and furniture for Emden, and from there for Upper Germany, where he died. His widow, of the family of Moers, afterwards married Frederick, Elector Palatine.

units.la: Quinque millia foederatorum exauctorata Monasterium Egmondani depraedantur, maxima eorum pars in Cliuiam veniunt.
units.tr: Five thousand discharged confederates plundered the monastery of Egmont, and the greater part of them came into Cleves.

units.la: Praecipui quidam belli Duces, Nobilesque inter Frisiam & Hollandiam nauigantes perfidia nautae, nauigio in arenam acto, à Molardo oppugnatur, capiuntur, incarcerantur & interficiuntur. Sic multa millia hominum vere Geusii, exules & mendici facta sunt. Innumeri vero etiam mortales miserrime interfecti passim occubuerunt.
units.tr: Certain leading commanders and nobles, sailing between Friesland and Holland, were attacked by Mollard, through the treachery of a sailor, after their ship had been driven onto a sandbank; they were captured, imprisoned and killed. Thus many thousands of men, truly Geuzen, were made exiles and beggars. Innumerable mortals also perished most wretchedly, lying dead everywhere.

units.la: Wilhelmus Auraicus, & multi alii Antuerpia discedunt, in Germaniam sese recipientes.
units.tr: William of Orange and many others left Antwerp, retiring into Germany.

units.la: Gubernatrix cum maximo exercitu Antuerpiam venit, & seueras ibi leges condit. Persecutio Euangelicorum incrudescit, Missa viget, infantes iterato baptizantur.
units.tr: The Governess came to Antwerp with a very great army and enacted harsh laws there. The persecution of the Evangelicals grew fiercer, the Mass flourished, and infants were baptized again.

units.la: Albanus ex Hispania cum exercitu Genoam venit, mense Maio, & miles ex Neapoli & Sicilia Mediolanum vocatus, cum Albano per Sabaudiam & Lotharingiam in Belgium appulit, mense Septembri.
units.tr: Alva came from Spain with an army to Genoa in May, and soldiers summoned from Naples and Sicily to Milan, together with Alva, landed in Belgium through Savoy and Lorraine in September.

units.la: ALBANVS GVBERNATOR BELGII.
units.tr: Alva, Governor of the Low Countries.

units.la: Margaretha gubernatrix, cum Albanus sua Imperia literis Regiis confirmata ostenderet, & typis impressas vulgaret, veniaä Rege fratre petita, Aprilianno M.D.LXVIII. ex Belgio in Italiam ad maritum abiit.
units.tr: Margaret the governess, when Alva showed his commissions confirmed by royal letters and was publishing them in print, asked leave of her brother the King and left Belgium for Italy, to her husband, in April 1568.

units.la: Nota. Albanus Belgiam pacatam inuenit, inquietam & turbatam post septennium abiens relinquit.
units.tr: Note. Alva found Belgium at peace, and he leaves it, after seven years, restless and disturbed.

units.la: H
units.tr: H

units.la: Ingressus omnia loca praesidiis firmat, Inquisitioni parere omnes seuere mandat. Senatum sanguinis dictum instituit, passim in Ciuitatibus Senatores mutat. Publicat quidem condonationem delictorum, verum fraudulèter: redeuntes enim cepit & supplicio affecit. Gandauensibus, Egmondano, qui eorum Praeses erat, frustra intercedente, claues adimit.
units.tr: On entering, he secures all places with garrisons and orders everyone severely to obey the Inquisition. He set up what was called the Council of Blood, and everywhere in the cities he replaced the senators. He did indeed publish a pardon for offences, but fraudulently: for he seized and executed those who returned. Egmont, who was their president, interceded in vain, and Alva took the keys away from the people of Ghent.

units.la: Infantes, qui in ref. Ecclesiis fuissent baptisati, denuo baptisari, mulieres, quarum mariti hac de causa exularent, nouis maritis inuitae copulari, atque Albani imperio multae ita militibus suis nubunt.
units.tr: Infants who had been baptised in the Reformed churches were baptised again. Women whose husbands were in exile for this reason were married, against their will, to new husbands, and by Alva's command many were so given to his soldiers.

units.la: Hispanus miles in vrbibus, non secus ac expugnatis, furiose debacchari.
units.tr: The Spanish soldiers ran riot furiously in the towns, as if they had been taken by storm.

units.la: Generales Status Bruxellis congregantur, audituri, quas functiones Albanus cuique esset commissurus: ibi Egmondanus, & Comes de Horn in Palatium vocati, certis custodiis sunt mandati & constricti.
units.tr: The General States assembled at Brussels to hear what duties Alva would assign to each. There Egmont and the Count of Horn were summoned to the palace, placed under certain guards and bound.

units.la: Prope Antuerpiam Consul eorum, Strale, captus est. Hinc iterum ingens trepidatio & fuga Belgarum in omnes se terras effundentium existit. Hinc horrenda & infinita cum plebeiorum, tum Nobilium ab incarceratione supplicia & excarnificationes exercentur.
units.tr: Near Antwerp their consul, Straelen, was captured. Hence there was again great panic, and the Belgians fled, scattering into all lands. Hence horrible and endless tortures and executions, both of commoners and of nobles, were carried out on the imprisoned.

units.la: Albanus curauit fortissimum Castrum aedificari prope Antuerpiam. Hinc allusum: Ite in Castellum, quod contra vos est. Imperatae ad id excitandum graues a Ciuibus exactiones.
units.tr: Alva had a very strong citadel built near Antwerp, whence the saying: Go to the castle that stands against you. Heavy exactions were imposed on the citizens to pay for it.

units.la: Albanus militem auxilio mittit Regi Galliarum contra Condaeum & reliquos.
units.tr: Alva sends soldiers to help the King of France against Condé and the others.

units.la: M.D. LXVIII. Wilhelmus Auraicus, vt qui se caput reformatorum seditiosorum, qui Brederodo auctor fuerit muniendi Ciuitatem Viandam contra Regem, qui Antuerpiensibus suaserit colligere militem, ab Albano citatur. Citatur & Antonius Hochstratensis, vt de iis iudicetur & supplicium sumatur.
units.tr: In 1568 William of Orange, as the man regarded as head of the seditious reformers, who had advised Brederode to fortify the town of Vianen against the King, and who had urged the Antwerpers to raise soldiers, was summoned by Alva. Anthony of Hochstraten was also summoned, so that they might be judged and punished.

units.la: Auraicus respondet, non se, sed auctores Inquisitionis Hispanicae causam motuum & turbarum fuisse, se fidelissimum Regi perpetuo extitisse, nec se, qui aurei Velleris membrum sit, huius iudicis legibus teneri. Albanus igitur bona ipsius in fiscum redigit, & filium eius Philippum ex Academia Louaniensi, contra Priuilegia, auulsit, & in Hispaniam misit.
units.tr: Orange replied that he was not the cause of the movements and disturbances, but the authors of the Spanish Inquisition were; that he had always been most faithful to the King; and that he, being a member of the Order of the Golden Fleece, was not bound by the laws of this judge. Alva therefore confiscated his goods for the treasury, and, against their privileges, tore his son Philip away from the University of Louvain and sent him to Spain.

units.la: Auraicus opera Ludouici fratris exercitum ad Mosam duxit, & Peles eius agnatus accepto à Protestantibus Gallis milite, exusta porta Ruremundi ad Dulem pergit, vbi ab Albano cum suis fusus est.
units.tr: Through the efforts of his brother Louis, Orange led an army to the Meuse. His kinsman Pelles, having received soldiers from the French Protestants, burned the gate of Roermond and made for the Dommel, where he was routed by Alva and his men.

units.la: Albanus innumeros ad supplicia rapit.
units.tr: Alva drags countless people off to punishment.

units.la: Ludouicus Nassouius in Frisia se confortauit. Albanus contra eum misit Arebergensem cum Italis, qui 15. vexillis amissis, casus est, & ibi in Monasterio Heiligenlohe tumulatus, cecidit & Adolphus Nassouius frater, & in Wette sepultus.
units.tr: Louis of Nassau fortified himself in Friesland. Alva sent against him Arenberg with the Italians, who, after losing fifteen standards, fell. Adolf of Nassau, the brother, also fell there and was buried at Wedde, and he was laid in the tomb at the monastery of Heiligerlee.

units.la: Ludouicus obsidet Groningam, cui Caesar rogatu Albani praecipit discessum ex Belgio. Veniente Albano Ludouicus abit versus Embden, & deprehensus ab Albano, cum miles stipendia petens, pugnare nollet, prope Groningam fusus & fugatus est, amissis Comite Hochstratense & aliis, 22. Iulii.
units.tr: Louis besieged Groningen. The Emperor, at Alva's request, ordered him to leave the Low Countries. When Alva approached, Louis withdrew towards Emden, but was caught by Alva when his soldiers, demanding their pay, refused to fight; near Groningen he was routed and put to flight, losing Count Hoogstraten and others, on 22 July.

units.la: Albanus, cum multi citati non venirent, in Iunio 18. Nobiles, & aliquos Magnates supplicio afficit. Accusantur & Egmondanus, & Hornensis criminis laesae Maiestatis Regiae, & Bruxellis decollantur.
units.tr: Alva, since many who had been summoned did not come, executed eighteen nobles and some magnates in June. Egmont and Horn were accused of treason against the royal majesty and were beheaded at Brussels.

units.la: Egmondanus inconcusso & irreuocabili Decreto, sibi commoriendum esse dum no obscure videret, ad Maiestatem Reg. literas Gallico idiomate perscriptas hora secunda sub auroram exarauit, quibus veniam ab eius Maiestate petiit, eique coniugem & liberos suos commendauit.
units.tr: Egmont, seeing clearly that by an unshaken and irrevocable decree he too was to die, wrote, at the second hour before dawn, letters in French to His Royal Majesty, in which he asked pardon from His Majesty and commended to him his wife and children.

units.la: Strenuam profecto non semel, praesertim in Anglia anno 54. ad Greuelingam, Anno 57. ad S. Quintinum, Anno 58. & in Francia anno 59. atque alibi bonus Comes ille Egmondanus Regi suo nauauerat operam, &c. Vidi tum, (scribit ille Papista) Comitem illum mortem aequo tulisse animo, atque audiui, non solum Belgas, sed etiam Hispanos milites, (aderant enim in supplicio illius & Hornensis ad 22. Hispanorum militum vexilla praesentia) omnes, imo ipsum Ducem Albanum, lachrymis obitum illius prosecutum fuisse.
units.tr: That good Count Egmont had served his king with vigour, and not only once: in England in 1554 at Gravelines, in 1557 at St Quentin, in 1558 and in France in 1559, and elsewhere. The Papist writes: I saw then that the Count bore his death with equanimity, and I heard that not only the Belgians but also the Spanish soldiers (for the standards of twenty-two Spanish companies were present at his and Horn's execution), indeed the Duke of Alva himself, followed his death with tears.

units.la: Statim post obitum Nobilium, Comitumque, non procul à Louanio sanguinis guttæ ingenti copia sunt repertæ.
units.tr: Immediately after the death of the nobles and counts, not far from Louvain, drops of blood were found in great abundance.

units.la: Auraicus publicatis causis suscepti belli cum exercitu contra Albanum proficiscitur, & superato Mosa ad Stokum venit. Sed cum multis velitationibus ab Albano distineretur, recessit, & Argentoratum abiens ibi militibus stipendia soluit, ope Alberti Mansfeldii, & deinde in Gallicum bellum profectus est.
units.tr: Orange, having published the reasons for the war he had undertaken, set out against Alva with an army, and having crossed the Meuse came to Stockem. But, being detained by many skirmishes with Alva, he withdrew; going to Strasbourg, he paid his soldiers there with the help of Albert of Mansfeld, and then set out for the war in France.

units.la: Elector Palat. pecuniam Hispan. retinet.
units.tr: The Elector Palatine kept back the Spanish money.

units.la: De morte Caroli, Hispaniæ Regis filii, rumor increscebat. Huius mirabilis mortis multæ causæ ferebantur. At constantior Inquisitorum fraudem nonnulla fraudulenter suspicantium, patris iram aduersus filium exacuisse, ut suis torqueis pater legitimum & unicum sibimet & Hispaniæ adimeret. Ad aliquod illinc tempus nunciatur mors Elisabethæ, Hispaniarum Regis Philippi vxoris, Caroli Galliarum Regis sororis.
units.tr: Rumour grew of the death of Carlos, son of the King of Spain. Many causes of this remarkable death were reported. But the more consistent Inquisitors, suspecting that some of it was fraud, held that the father's anger against his son had been sharpened, so that by his own cruelty the father might take from himself and from Spain the legitimate and only son. For some time after this came the announcement of the death of Elisabeth, wife of Philip, King of Spain, and sister of Charles, King of France.

units.la: M. D. LXIX. Albanus nouos illos Episcopos confirmat, quorum in Leuarde Frisiæ primus fuit Cunerus Petri.
units.tr: In 1569 Alva confirmed those new bishops, of whom the first at Leeuwarden in Friesland was Cunerus Petri.

units.la: Albanus magnam crudelitatem exercet.
units.tr: Alva exercises great cruelty.

units.la: Albano controuersia intercedit cum Regina Angliæ, quæ ei pecuniam interceperat, & quod is ei naues mercatorum detinuisset.
units.tr: A dispute arose between Alva and the Queen of England, who had seized his money, and because he had detained the merchants' ships.

units.la: Papa excommunicat Reginam Angliæ, hinc multi Papismum defenderunt, sed ab aliis oppressi sunt.
units.tr: The Pope excommunicated the Queen of England. Hence many defended Popery, but they were overpowered by others.

units.la: Spella latrunculator suspensus.
units.tr: Spella, a brigand, was hanged.

units.la: M.D. LXX. Albanus publicat Pardonna, sed nemo promissis fidem habet propter eam, quam prius exercuerat, tyrannidem.
units.tr: In 1570 Alva published a pardon, but no one trusted the promises, because of the tyranny he had practised before.

units.la: Anna filia Cæsaris Maximiliani, Philippi Regis Hispaniæ sponsa, per Belgium in Hispaniam ducitur.
units.tr: Anne, daughter of Emperor Maximilian and betrothed to Philip, King of Spain, was led through Belgium into Spain.

units.la: Maximæ inundationes in Belgio, cum Antuerpiensium incomparabili damno.
units.tr: Very great floods in Belgium, with incomparable loss to the Antwerpers.

units.la: M. D. LXXI. Albanus exigit decimum nummum, quam exactionem maximus tumultus secutus est. Bruxellenses primi fuerunt, qui Priuilegia sua cum periculo venditarunt. Commoti etiam sunt Brabantii, Flandri, Zelandi, Hollandi. &c.
units.tr: In 1571 Alva demanded the tenth penny, and this exaction was followed by the greatest tumult. The people of Brussels were the first who sold their privileges at the risk of their lives. The Brabanters, Flemings, Zeelanders, Hollanders and others were also stirred.

units.la: Exules etiam de promouenda libertate cogitarunt, ideoque Dominus de Lune, Dominus de Marchia, cum in Anglia esset, & naues adornasset, ad Bruel Hollandiæ vrbem accessit, & cum vnam portam igni incendi curasset, ipse per alteram in vrbem irrupit, & eam in potestatem suam redegit mense Aprili. Mox ibi & in tota Insula omnes imagines templis eiectæ sunt.
units.tr: The exiles too thought about advancing liberty. So Lord de Lumey and Lord de la Marck, who was in England and had fitted out ships, came to Brielle, a town of Holland. Having set one gate on fire, he himself broke into the town through the other and brought it under his power in April. Soon afterwards, there and throughout the whole island, all images were thrown out of the churches.

units.la: Albanus statim mittit Comitem Bossum cum exercitu navali, qui tamen nihil contra Geusios profecit, & altu Roterodamum ingressus custodes portarum & multos cives occidit.
units.tr: Alva immediately sent Count Bossu with a naval force, who nevertheless achieved nothing against the Sea Beggars. Sailing up, he entered Rotterdam, and there he killed the gate-guards and many citizens.

units.la: Albanus timens defectionem vrbium, præsidium collocat in Mittelburg Zelandiæ, & misso Architecto Pacioto, Sabaudo ibidem ædificari voluit Castrum Antuerpiano simile. Die Paschatis orta est rixa inter cives & metatores, qui hospitia militibus distribuunt, vnde tumultus, populo e templo erumpente, ortus est, multi cæsi, & Paciotus captus, & postea laqueo suffocatus est, Albano multum pro eo intercedente, vt qui arcis Antuerp. structuram disposuerat, & sic miles vrbe pulsus est, & vrbs pro Auraico seruata.
units.tr: Alva, fearing the defection of the towns, placed a garrison at Middelburg in Zeeland, and, having sent for the architect Paciotto, a Savoyard, he wanted a citadel like the one at Antwerp built there. On Easter day a quarrel arose between citizens and the quartermasters who assign lodgings to the soldiers. From this a tumult arose as the people burst out of the church; many were slain and Paciotto was captured, and afterwards strangled with a noose, although Alva interceded strongly for him, since he had planned the building of the Antwerp citadel. So the soldiers were driven out of the town, and the town was kept for Orange.

units.la: 24. Maii Ludouicus Nassouius Montem Hannoniæ hoc astu occupat. Vespere præcedente venerunt in hospitium eius vrbis quidam, præferentes speciem mercatorum, qui hospitem interrogant, quam tempestiue portæ solerent aperiri, & edocti quod hora quarta, & data portitoribus pecunia etiam maturius illæ paterent: hanc occasionem arripientes, occisis custodibus, Ludouicum cum 40. equitibus immiserunt, qui in omnibus angulis vrbis dispositi continuo clamant datum iri libertatem Ciuibus ope Auraici contra Albanum, & prospicientes ex fenestris sclopetis petiuerunt, postea 500. equites introducti vrbem sibi vendicarunt.
units.tr: On 24 May Louis of Nassau occupied Mons in Hainault by this trick. On the evening before, some men came to the lodging of a certain townsman, posing as merchants, and asked their host how early the gates were usually opened. Told at the fourth hour, and that with money given to the gatekeepers they would be opened even earlier, they seized this opportunity: after killing the guards they let in Louis with forty horsemen, who, posted at every corner of the town, kept crying out that liberty would be granted to the citizens by Orange's help against Alva. Looking out from the windows, they fired with muskets. Afterwards 500 horsemen were brought in and took the town for themselves.

units.la: Eodem tempore Dominus de Noue etiam occupat Valentiam pro Auraico, sed Hispanis eo aduentantibus, eandem deserunt. Fliessingenses frustra adoriuntur Mittelburgenses, iidem etiam plurimas naues construunt, quibus Hispanos, commeatum & alimonia Mittelburgensibus interclusuros, arcent. Colligunt & militem, qui terra Albano resistant, & occupant Eichenlohe, & Arenburg.
units.tr: At the same time Lord de Noue also seized Valenciennes for Orange, but when the Spanish approached, he abandoned it. The men of Flushing vainly attacked the men of Middelburg, and they also built many ships with which they tried to keep the Spanish from cutting off supplies and provisions from Middelburg. They also gathered soldiers to resist Alva on land, and they occupied Eichenlohe and Arenburg.

units.la: Serraes Capitaneus Fliessingensium multos quidem pagos & vrbem tentat, sed nullibi succedit. Obsidet & Goes, sed eam capere non potest. Nam Capitaneus Albani militem per longissimum tractum, quem illuuies aquarum obsidebat, versus Goes (cum obsessis aliter subuenire non possiet) per quinque horas pedibus transire fecit, & sic Goes defendit. Serraes, re non ex voto Fliessingensium gesta, pro proditore habetur, quam notam ille duello, si quis congredi vellet, abstergere paratus erat, id quod tamen amici eum, ne faceret, prohibuerunt.
units.tr: Serraes, captain of the Flushingers, attacked many villages and the town, but succeeded nowhere. He also laid siege to Goes, but could not take it. For Alva's captain had his soldiers march for five hours on foot along a very long stretch of road, which the filthy floodwaters covered, towards Goes (since he could not otherwise come to the aid of the besieged), and so Goes was defended. Serraes, because the outcome did not match the wishes of the Flushingers, was held to be a traitor. He was ready to wipe away this stain in a duel, if anyone wished to fight him, but his friends forbade him to do so.

units.la: M.D.LXXII. cum ad Enkhusianos venisset, quidam Capitaneus Albani & milites egressi nauibus vim intentarent Ciuibus, Ciues metuentes exactiones decimi nummi milites Ciuitate exegerunt, & à Comite de Lune praesidia petiuerunt. Idem fecerunt Ciues in Alkmar, Horn, Edam, Medenblik, & pleraeque aliae Ciuitates Bruilo proximae.
units.tr: In the year 1572, when Alva came to Enkhuizen, a certain captain and soldiers went out from the ships and threatened violence against the townsmen. The townsmen, fearing the exactions of the tenth penny, drove the soldiers out of the town and sought a garrison from the Count de Lune. The citizens of Alkmaar, Hoorn, Edam, Medemblik, and most of the other towns near Brielle did the same.

units.la: Schonhofen Ciuitas obsidione à Comite de Marchia facta ad subiectionem adacta est. Ambsterdamum nulla vi capi, aut in ordinem redigi potuit.
units.tr: The town of Schoonhoven, after being besieged by the Count de la Marck, was brought to submission. Amsterdam could not be taken by force or brought into order.

units.la: Hunc successum videns Comes Bergensis, & ipse vrbes Dotecum, Duisberg, Zutphen, & in Geldria Herdevvik, Terelberg, Hattum, & alibi Oldenziel & Goer sub potestatem Auraici redegit. Perrexit etiam, & Campen ad deditionem adegit. Similiter & Haffel, Schvvolle, & Steinwik accepit. Alii etiam extorres Nobiles, Duce Iusto de Schvvabeburg, Ciuitates Schenk, Bolsvvare, & Franiken occupant. Groningenses vero à Dn. Billy praesidia petunt, qui aduentans Dokum exurit, & alios ad Stoueren caedit.
units.tr: Seeing this success, the Count of Bergen himself brought under the power of Orange the towns of Doesburg, Duisburg, Zutphen, and in Gelderland Harderwijk, Terlet, Hattem, and elsewhere Oldenzaal and Gorssel. He also went on and forced Kampen to surrender. He likewise took Harderwijk, Zwolle, and Steenwijk. Other exiled nobles, with Duke Justus of Schwabeburg, occupied the towns of Schenkenschans, Bolsward, and Franeker. But the men of Groningen asked Lord Billy for a garrison, and when he arrived he burned Dokkum and cut down others at Stoeren.

units.la: His praeceptis, Albanus indignabundus filium Don Friderieum cum mittit, qui Montem Hannoniæ, & in ea Ludouicum Nas-souium obsideat, dumque Ciues messem conuehunt, multę velitationes fiunt.
units.tr: After these events, the indignant Alva sent his son Don Frederick, who besieged Mons in Hainault, and Ludovicus Nassovius in it. While the citizens were carrying in the harvest, many skirmishes took place.

units.la: Dominus de Salins in subsidium Bergæ septem millia mili-tum erat adducturus, quem Ludou. Nassouius monet, vt cum exercitu ad fratrem Vranienfem se conferat, nec Bergam adeat, ne inopiam in vrbe augeat. Verū Dominus de Salins ex fastu, & ne videatur timidus, improuide pergit, sed incidit in Ducem Belli, & in Hispanos, ibi maximam cladem accipit, eius Capitaneis, Renti & Reingraphio cæsis, Salins & Iunis capti. Sic de tot militibus vix centum in Bergam peruenerunt.
units.tr: Lord de Salins was going to bring seven thousand soldiers to the relief of Bergen, and Ludovicus Nassovius advised him to join his brother of Orange with his army, and not to go to Bergen, lest he increase the shortage of supplies in the town. But Lord de Salins, out of pride, and so as not to seem timid, rashly pressed on, and fell in with the Duke of Alva's general and the Spanish, and there he suffered a very great defeat. His captains Rennes and Rheingrave were slain, and Salins and Hunnes were taken. So of so many soldiers, scarcely a hundred reached Bergen.

units.la: Albanus Abbatiam Espinui occupat, & Bergam grauissime oppugnat, verum hactenus nihil efficit.
units.tr: Alva occupied the abbey of Espinoy and attacked Bergen very fiercely, but so far achieved nothing.

units.la: Auraicus instructo exercitu feliciter rem gerebat, occupatis etiam nobilioribus vrbibus, sub ipsum Parisinarum laniena-rum tempus.
units.tr: Orange, with his army drawn up, was doing well, having also taken the more important towns, at about the time of the Paris massacre of the Huguenots.

units.la: Occupata Mechlinia, & Louanio ad ingentem pecuniæ vim dependendam compulso, Aldenardo etiam capta, Montium omnibus copiis contendebat, vt Ludouico fratri, vbiq; ab Albano arctissima obsidione circumsesse, opem auxiliumque ferret.
units.tr: Mechlin having been occupied, and Louvain forced to pay a huge sum of money, and Oudenaarde also taken, he hurried with all his forces to Mons, to bring aid and assistance to his brother Ludovicus, who was closely besieged everywhere by Alva.

units.la: Magna celeritate ad Albani castra Auraicus accesserat, & magnum quidem detrimentum Albano importaturus videbatur, quum vndiquaque hostibus circumuallaretur, suo tamen pedite importuna stipendii petitione militiam detrectabundo, necquicquam discedit. Cedentibus struit insidias Albanus, quingenti instructi tormentarii, cum equitum turma ad illum persequendum immissi, Castra illius adoriuntur, excubisque obtruncatis, in Auraici Castris alios mactant, alios vulnerant.
units.tr: Orange had come to Alva's camp with great speed, and seemed about to inflict a great loss on Alva, since he was surrounded on all sides by enemies. Yet, since his infantry, who were refusing service and demanding unreasonable pay, were troublesome, he withdrew to no effect. As they withdrew, Alva laid a trap: five hundred armed gunners, together with a troop of horsemen, were sent out to pursue him. They attacked his camp, killed the sentries, and in Orange's camp slew some and wounded others.

units.la: Quum & furorem lanienarum Gallicarum horribilis nuntius maximam perturbationem Ludouico sociisque attulisset, & auxilii Auraici spes amissa esset, vehementiusque indies
units.tr: When the horrible news of the Parisian butchery of the French had brought great alarm to Ludovicus and his allies, and the hope of Orange's help was lost, and Alva pressed harder day by day,

units.la: I AlbaAlbanus vrgeret, hoste depulso, cepit Ludouicus agere de deditione cum Albano, pactisque conditionibus mille quingenti, tributa armorum, equorum, caeterque supellectilis comportandae facultate Montio discedunt, praestito iureiurando, se intra annum armaaduersus Philippum Regem minime gesturos. Ita vulneratus Ludouicus in Germaniam domum discessit, dedita in Albani potestatem opportunisima vrbe.
units.tr: with the enemy driven off, Ludovicus began to negotiate a surrender with Alva. On agreed terms, fifteen hundred men were allowed to leave Mons with the right to carry away their arms, horses, and other baggage, after swearing an oath that they would not take up arms against King Philip for a year. So the wounded Ludovicus went home to Germany, and the most advantageous town was given into Alva's power.

units.la: Tum Auraicus in Brabantiam cedit, aditaque Mechlinia, quum oppidanorum animos, & rerum Gallicarum infelici successu, & recenti nuntio Montii expugnati consternatos videret, Albanique partes haud dubie sequuturos, silentio mouet, vrbemque vacuam relinquit, eam occupat Albanus, & diripit, ingentemque praedam abigit.
units.tr: Then Orange withdrew into Brabant, and having come to Mechlin, when he saw that the minds of the townsmen were dismayed by the unhappy outcome of French affairs and the recent news of the fall of Mons, and that they would undoubtedly follow Alva's side, he quietly moved away and left the town empty. Alva occupied it, plundered it, and carried off enormous booty.

units.la: Licet omnis clerus Albanis honoris ergo obuiam ibat, tamen miles omnem truculentiam & turpitudinem in quemlibet sexum exercuit 1. Octobris.
units.tr: Although all the clergy went out to meet the Spaniards as a sign of honour, the soldiers nevertheless practised every cruelty and outrage against people of every sex, on 1 October.

units.la: Annus notatur hoc versu:
units.tr: The year is marked by this verse:

units.la: SICCIne VICtA IaCes MeChLInIa VIrgo sVperba?
units.tr: Thus, conquered, will you lie, proud virgin Mechlin?

units.la: Albanus etiam Dieftam, Teremundam, Ruremundam, Aldenardum recipit. Inde Zurphania per vim ab Albano occupata, cum atrociter in Ciues saeuiisset, tantus in eos, qui Auraici partes sequuti erant, incidit pauor, vt, quasi iam debellatum esset, milite non iam opus esset, Albanus plerosque e suis Germanis equitibus ab se dimiserit. Traiecti itaque quotidie ad Albanum veniunt, Ciuitates culpam deprecaturae Auraici partibus abdicatis.
units.tr: Alva also received Diest, Thorn, Roermond, and Oudenaarde. Then Zutphen was taken by force by Alva, and after he had raged cruelly against the citizens, such great terror fell upon those who had followed Orange's side that, as if the war were already finished and soldiers no longer needed, Alva dismissed most of his German horsemen. So people came every day from across the Meuse to Alva, to beg pardon for their towns, renouncing the side of Orange.

units.la: Cedunt ex captis a se passim vrbibus Comes Bergensis, & Schemburgius.
units.tr: The Count of Bergen and Schenck also gave up the towns they had captured everywhere.

units.la: Nardam Hollandiae oppidum, quod ab Auraici praesidiario tenebatur, obsidet Albanus, & dedunt se oppidani certis conditionibus: violata tamen fide, Hispanus in praesidiarium & oppidanum impotenter saeuit. Rem indignatus Methynaeus Dux (qui cum potestate ex Hispania in Belgium venerat, & Albano videbatur successurus) & cum Friderico Albani filio grauigrauiter iratus, Bosseducum se recipit, & illic tamdiu commoratus est, donec à Rege reuocaretur, dissensionum illarum inter primarios Belgii Duces admonito.
units.tr: Alva besieged Naarden, a town in Holland which was held by Orange's garrison, and the townsmen surrendered on certain conditions; but, faith having been broken, the Spanish raged without restraint against the garrison and the townsmen. The Duke of Medina, who had come from Spain into the Netherlands with authority and was thought to be going to succeed Alva, was indignant at this matter, and being very angry with Alva's son Frederick, he withdrew to Bois-le-Duc, and stayed there until he was recalled by the King, having been warned about those quarrels among the chief leaders of the Netherlands.

units.la: Nardensium calamitas cæteras Hollandiæ Ciuitates ad constantiam concitauit, ne se eiederent, quem infensiorem amicum quam hostem essent experturæ.
units.tr: The calamity of the men of Naarden stirred the other towns of Holland to steadfastness, so that they would not give themselves up, since they would find an enemy more hostile than a foe, as a friend.

units.la: Parati ergo Harlemenses (est Harlemum Hollandiæ oppidum copiosum) se dedere Albano. Quum Nardensis calamitatis immanitatem audiunt, consilio mutato, Orengiani præsidiarium recipiunt: & mortem potius oppetendam statuunt, quā vltro se in Albani dedant potestatem. Orengiani præsidiarius oppidum nō satis per se munitū summa diligentia munit.
units.tr: So the men of Haarlem (Haarlem is a rich town of Holland), who had been ready to surrender to Alva, when they heard of the savagery of the calamity at Naarden, changed their plan, received the garrison of Orange, and resolved rather to meet death than to hand themselves over voluntarily into Alva's power. Orange's garrison fortified the town, which was not strong enough in itself, with the greatest care.

units.la: In Orengiani societate & amicitia perstant pleraque Hollandiæ vrbes, Leyda, Roterodamum, Dordanum, Haga Comitis, Gucuza, Ganda, Delphi, Brielum &c. Ambsterodamum metropolis firmo Albani præsidio munita erat. Vniuersa vero Zelandia, Middelburgo excepta, Orengiani partes fere sequebatur.
units.tr: Most of the towns of Holland remained in alliance and friendship with Orange: Leiden, Rotterdam, Dordrecht, The Hague, Gouda, Gouda, Delft, Brielle, etc. Amsterdam, the metropolis, was protected by a strong Spanish garrison. Indeed, the whole of Zeeland, except Middelburg, mostly followed Orange's side.

units.la: Fridericus Albani filius Sparedam vrbem, cui Harlemenses subsidium miserant, super glacie indurata expugnat, & Harlemum obsidet copioso exercitu, & furiose oppugnat. Oppidani incredibili strenuitate se defendebant, munitionibus ipsis tanta solertia in vrbe dispositis, vt in vrbis sinum receptus aliquando Hispanus, magna & clade & infamia cogeretur regredi. Itaque ab vtrisque summa & animorum & virium ope decertabatur.
units.tr: Frederick, Alva's son, took the town of Spaarndam, to which the men of Haarlem had sent help, by storm over the hardened ice, and besieged Haarlem with a large army, and attacked it furiously. The townsmen defended themselves with incredible vigour, the defences having been arranged in the town with such skill that the Spaniard, once admitted into the town's bay, was at one point forced to retreat with great loss and disgrace. So both sides fought with the utmost force of spirit and strength.

units.la: Saeuiebat tum periniqua hyems, quæ Hispanis magnam rei gerendæ opportunitatem præbebat, paludibus, quib. ea regio late intexta est, gelu concretis. Gelu tamen fiducia illis male cesit. Sublicium pontem in aquam continuo gelu constipatum extruxerant Hispani, qua in vrbem facerent impetum. Oppidani eos ita vrgent, vt regredi coacti, per pontem illum confertim confluerent, ponsque tanto onere subrutus concideret, eaque mole gelu diduceretur. Itaque magna Hispanorum multitudo in aquam submersa, alii maiorem, alii minorem numerum referunt, sexcentos constantior fama, Pontificii diminuto numero ducentos scribunt.
units.tr: A most severe winter was raging then, which gave the Spanish a great opportunity to act, the marshes, by which that region is widely interlaced, being frozen. Yet the frost turned out badly for them in their hope. The Spanish had built a pile bridge over the water, which was constantly being bound together by the frost, from which they were to make their attack upon the town. The townsmen pressed them so hard that, forced to retreat, they crowded together on that bridge, and the bridge, weighed down by so great a burden, collapsed, and by that mass the ice was broken apart. So a great multitude of Spaniards was drowned in the water. Some report a larger number, others a smaller; the more reliable report says six hundred, while the Papists, reducing the number, write two hundred.

units.la: Immissus ab Orengiano miles, auxilii Harlemensibus ferendi instituto, ab Albano de insperato interceptus, magna clade caeditur, ereptum equitum signum unum, peditum septem, ita septingenti dicuntur interfecti ad eum locum. Nec quicquam tamen obsistente Hispano, auxilium immittit Orengianus obsessis.
units.tr: A force sent by Orange, intending to bring help to the men of Haarlem, was unexpectedly intercepted by Alva and cut down with great slaughter; one standard of horse and seven of foot were seized, so that seven hundred are said to have been killed in that place. Yet, with no Spanish resistance, Orange sent aid to the besieged.

units.la: Sub id tempus in agro Ambsterdamensi dicitur natus vitulus gemino, & capite & dorso, iteratisque pedibus, octo nimirum, & ad paucas horas superuixisse.
units.tr: About that time, in the territory of Amsterdam, a calf is said to have been born with two heads and two backs, and eight legs in all, and to have survived for a few hours.

units.la: Tunc conspecta nova illa Stella, de qua vide Epigramma in Epitome Gallica:
units.tr: At that time the new star was seen, concerning which see the epigram in the French Epitome:

units.la: M. D. LXXIII. In expugnando Harlemo Hispani, defendendo Orengiani ad omnem strenuitatem elaborabant. Dissipato per bellica fulmina muro ita succurrunt oppidani praesidiarii, ut fossa mirabili industria intra urbem opportune circumacta, penetralia urbis ipsis etiam moenibus firmiora conspicerentur.
units.tr: 1573. While the Spanish were storming Haarlem, the Orangists defended it with every effort. When the wall had been shattered by cannon-fire, the garrison and townspeople met the danger so well that a ditch, skilfully dug in a circle inside the city at the right place, made the inner parts of the town appear stronger even than its walls.

units.la: Dum urbs illa obsidetur, & utrique summis viribus contendunt, multa varie interea eveniunt.
units.tr: While that city was being besieged, and both sides strained with all their strength, many things happened in various ways.

units.la: Vigesimo septimo Ianuarii intercipitur a Flielsingensibus classis Hispanica, clade accepta tamen elabitur.
units.tr: On 27 January the Spanish fleet was intercepted by the people of Vlissingen, but it escaped, though it suffered losses.

units.la: Orengianus interea omnibus modis conatur Harlemensibus, annonae penuria laborantibus, succurrere, & opportuna e vicinis & sociis urbibus enauigatione Leyda, Delphis, & frigidissimae hyemis beneficio, via per glaciem munita, efficit, ut oppidanis annona inueheretur.
units.tr: Meanwhile Orange tried by every means to relieve the people of Haarlem, who were suffering from a shortage of food. By shipping supplies from the neighbouring allied towns of Leiden and Delft, and by taking advantage of the very harsh winter, he made a road over the ice, so that food could be brought into the town.

units.la: Ad initium Martii Hispanorum supplementum, quinque nimirum signa in castra veniunt. A Flielsingensibus ad Terneusam aduersus Albani classem prospere pugnatur.
units.tr: At the beginning of March the Spanish reinforcements arrived in the camp, five standards in all. Near Terneuzen the people of Vlissingen fought successfully against Alva's fleet.

units.la: Orengiano (vt varia est belli alea, vel potius multiplex Dei exerciexercituum prouidentia) nauibus auxilium Harlemensibus importare conanti, Boflensis Hollandiæ Reg. præfectus superior aliquot naues capit; continuo noua clades Orengiano subsecuta Amsterdamensium opera.
units.tr: When Orange, as the fortune of war varies, or rather through the manifold providence of God, the Lord of hosts, tried to bring help to Haarlem by ship, the governor of Holland at Bosch, the Spanish commander, captured several ships; immediately a new disaster followed for Orange, through the work of the Amsterdammers.

units.la: Subidem etiam tempus Germani equites, qui Albano merebant, peditea ssumpto tormentario, in agro Leydensi depopulabundi excurrunt, & ingentem prædam abigunt.
units.tr: About the same time the German cavalry, who were serving Alva, together with infantry and a band of artillerymen, made a raid through the territory of Leiden, plundering and driving off a huge booty.

units.la: Post paucos aliquot dies in Regios illarum victoriarum succesibus exultantes, dum Festum Paschatis celebrant, Harlemenses irruunt, & multos obtruncant, multos vulnerant, eodemque rei successu postridie in Albani Castra erumpunt, & nonnullis interfectis, Castris vero perturbatis, in vrbem recipiunt. At quum sub eiusdem diei vesperam in Germanica Castra noctis silentio irrupissent, tunc vero tantam Germanos, recentibus certaminibus nondum recreatos, incidit consternatio, vt relictis Castris fœdam fugam facerent, & palantium hostium Harlemenses ingentem ederent stragem. Oppidani tamen, re ita confecta, quum de reliquo exercitu tentando minime cogitassent, nec tantis copiis sibi pares futuri viderentur, in vrbem redeunt.
