units.tr: A few days later, while the royalists were rejoicing in their successes of those victories and were celebrating Easter, the people of Haarlem rushed out, cut down many of them and wounded many more. With the same success the next day they burst out into Alva's camp, and after killing some and throwing the camp into confusion, they withdrew into the town. But when, towards evening of the same day, they broke into the German camp in the silence of the night, such dismay fell upon the Germans, who had not yet recovered from the recent fighting, that they abandoned the camp and made a shameful flight, and the Haarlemers inflicted a huge slaughter on the scattered enemy. The townspeople, however, once this was done, did not think at all of attacking the rest of the army, and they did not seem likely to be equal to such forces, so they returned into the town.

units.la: Regii, Boflensis Comitis auspiciis, & Orengiani, (quod id ad rem Harlemensium magnum haberet momentum) certatim conanturalii aliis mari esse superiores, vnde vario marte leuibus præliis dimicabatur. Itaque Amsterodamensi commercio (quo in Albani castra commeatus importabatur) impediendo aggerem occupare moliuntur Orengiani. Egressi Amsterodamenses cum Orengianis dimicabant, quum, ecce exrustica-nis fossoribus turma numerosior apparet, Orengiani, adesse Hispanos suspicati, consternantur: ita præ metu nauibus octo in hostium potestatem proditis, confertim ab Amsterodamensibus illorum complurimi obtruncantur: alii fœdam fugam faciunt.
units.tr: The royalists, under the leadership of the Count of Bossu, and Orange, (since this had great importance for the cause of Haarlem), tried eagerly to gain mastery of the sea, from which came a varied fortune in minor skirmishes. Thus Orange's men set out to seize the dyke, in order to hinder the trade of Amsterdam (by which supplies were brought into Alva's camp). The Amsterdammers went out and fought with the Orangists, when suddenly a larger troop of country diggers came into view. The Orangists, suspecting that Spaniards were approaching, were dismayed; so, in their fear, eight ships were handed over to the enemy, and many of them were quickly cut down by the Amsterdammers. The others made a shameful flight.

units.la: Tunc alius quoque Orengiani conatus auxilii Harlemensibus ferendi irritus excidit, Boflensi oram illam maritimam classe Hispanica tutante.
units.tr: Then another attempt by Orange to bring help to Haarlem also came to nothing, since the Spanish fleet was guarding that coast.

units.la: Quum vero Albanus, & delectu Germanor. & Burgundiorum, & ex praesidiorum etiam Belgicorum veteranis habito, in demortuorum locum nova supplementa suffecisset; tum vero obsidione arctius procurata, quum Orengianus constantius succurreret, inter illas moras ingens ingruit in Harlemenses fames. Est enim urbs & per se copiosa, & milite etiam praesidiario tum abundabat.
units.tr: When Alva, having raised new levies of Germans and Burgundians, and also drawn veterans from the Belgian garrisons, had replaced the dead with fresh reinforcements, then, with the siege pressed more tightly, while Orange kept coming to help more and more steadily, in the midst of these delays a terrible famine fell upon the people of Haarlem. The city, indeed, was well stocked in itself, and at that time it was also well supplied with garrison soldiers.

units.la: Orengianus de Harlemo liberanda unice satagens, quantum potest militis ex Hollandia & Zelandia colligit, consilio perrumpendi in urbem, ad auxilium obsessis ferendum. Copiis iis praerat Orengiani nomine Wilhelmus Bronshorstius, Baro Battembergicus. Ad Albani Castra accedunt, Germanorumque excubiis primo impetu obtruncatis, reliquo exercitui infesti instant, quum collectis viribus ita se defendunt Albanici, ut non modo Orengianos repulerint, sed ingenti etiam clade fuderint. Ad mille enim quingenti dicuntur caesi, ablata quatuordecim signa, decem tormenta bellica maiora, trecenti currus, ipse Battembergicus interfectus.
units.tr: Orange, intent solely on freeing Haarlem, gathered as many soldiers as he could from Holland and Zeeland, with the plan of breaking through into the town to bring help to the besieged. Wilhelm Bronckhorst, Baron of Battenburg, commanded these troops in Orange's name. They came up to Alva's camp, and having cut down the German sentries at the first assault, they pressed hard on the rest of the army. But the Alvists, gathering their forces, defended themselves so well that they not only drove back the Orangists but also routed them with a great slaughter. It is said that about fifteen hundred were killed, fourteen standards were taken, ten large cannon, three hundred wagons, and Battenburg himself was killed.

units.la: Ita Albanus late victor Harlemensem oppugnationem vehementius urget.
units.tr: Thus Alva, widely victorious, pressed the siege of Haarlem more vigorously.

units.la: Harlemenses octo mensium obsidione, & longa fame ad summas angustias adducti deditionem faciunt iniquissimis conditionibus: Ut victoris arbitrio & voluntati se permitterent. Ut miles a praeda abstineret, imperata sunt ab Albano bis centena & quadraginta aureorum millia. In oppidanos crudelissime ab Hispanis saevitur per omnes lethi formas. Sexcentos praesidiarios laqueo suffocari Albanus iubet: trecentos seminudos ex urbe eductos in aquam praecipitat, infami certe spectaculo, & barbara crudelitate detestabili, quum in lenitate & misericordia victoriae sit pars maxima. Tolerabilius in primis initiis ira excanduisset, militarem granditatem rancor, carnificis foedo etiam accedente ministerio, sane deturpat, Id fuit ad vndecimum Iulii.
units.tr: The people of Haarlem, brought to the utmost distress by an eight months' siege and long famine, surrendered on the most unfair terms: that they should put themselves at the will and pleasure of the victor; that the soldiers should abstain from plunder; and Alva demanded two hundred and forty thousand gold pieces. The Spaniards raged most cruelly against the townspeople in every form of death. Alva ordered six hundred of the garrison to be strangled with a noose; three hundred, half-naked, were led out of the city and thrown into the water, a truly infamous spectacle and a detestable barbarity, since the greater part of victory lies in clemency and mercy. At first the anger might have been tolerable, but the arrogance of the soldiers, and the rancour of the executioner, with his foul ministry added, certainly disgraced the military. This happened on 11 July.

units.la: Post Harlemum captam Oregianus occupat Alcmariam, Hollandiæ vrbem, diuisis ciuium studiis & partibus: quum iam ab Albanicorum factione, porta vna occupata, equitum peditumque turmæ ab Albano immissæ ad vrbem appropinquarent. Exturbatis tamen Albanicis, vrbe potitur Orengianus.
units.tr: After Haarlem was taken, Orange occupied Alkmaar, a town in Holland, where the citizens' sympathies and parties were divided; for already the Alvist faction had seized one gate, and troops of cavalry and infantry sent by Alva were approaching the town. Nevertheless, the Alvists were driven out, and Orange took possession of the town.

units.la: Hispani perguntad Alcmar. Auraicus præsidium mittit, & Hispani primo reiiciuntur. Vrbs sibi de necessariis rebus prospicit.
units.tr: The Spanish then attacked Alkmaar. Orange sent a garrison, and the Spanish were at first repulsed. The town provided for itself the necessary supplies.

units.la: Hispani vrbem cum 30. M. hominum arctissime obsidènt. Iohannes Arenz minister Ecclesiæ ægrotus Deum in agone cum suis deuote orat, vt vrbi tanquam hospitio fidelium parcat.
units.tr: The Spanish closely besieged the town with 30,000 men. Johannes Arentsz, minister of the congregation, sick, prayed devoutly to God with his people in his last agony, that He would spare the town as a refuge of the faithful.

units.la: Sonoy gubernator Nort Hollandiæ, vt & Status generales, scribunt vrbi, se auxilium missuros.
units.tr: Sonoy, governor of North Holland, as well as the States-General, wrote to the town that they would send help.

units.la: Muri pars labitur, sed reparatur.
units.tr: A part of the wall collapsed, but it was repaired.

units.la: Hispani crebros, & graues impetus faciunt, sed repelluntur.
units.tr: The Spanish made frequent and severe assaults, but they were repulsed.

units.la: Post magnas vtrinque exantlatas molestias, & labores, Hispani obsidionem soluunt, Octobr.
units.tr: After great hardships and labours had been endured on both sides, the Spanish lifted the siege, in October.

units.la: Princeps Auraicus castrum Raineken prope Mittelburg deditione capit.
units.tr: Prince Orange captured the castle of Rammekens near Middelburg by surrender.

units.la: Milites Auraici sub ductu Domini Poyrt mane in Gertrudenberg irrepentes, custodes caedunt. Capitaneus eius loci Drak per fenestram fugit, relicta pecunia in mensa, quam militibus suis soluere parabat.
units.tr: Orange's soldiers, under the leadership of Lord Poyet, crept into Gertruidenberg in the morning and cut down the guards. The captain of that place, Drak, fled through a window, leaving behind on the table the money with which he was preparing to pay his soldiers.

units.la: Albanus armada instructa, in cuius maxima nave, Inquisitio dicta, Dominus de Bossu vehebatur, Nort Hollandos ad Enkenhausen debellare satagit: Verum & Bossu capitur, & reliquæ naues partim fractæ, partim fugatæ sunt. Inquisitio illa nauis Hornum illata spectaculo hominibus fuit.
units.tr: Alva, having equipped a fleet, in whose largest ship, called the Inquisition, Lord de Bossu was carried, tried to subdue North Holland at Enkhuizen. But Bossu was captured, and the other ships were partly wrecked, partly put to flight. That ship, the Inquisition, was brought to Hoorn and was a spectacle to the people.

units.la: Albanus Leyden obsidet.
units.tr: Alva besieges Leiden.

units.la: Interim cum Rex Hispaniæ resciuisset, quod totum Belgium propter importunitatem Albani ad turbam & seditionem commotum esset, revocato illo, Dominum Louys de Requesens, Medina cæli dictum, in Gubernatorem Belgii misit, qui in Novembri appulit. Sed antea à Geusiis parte navium, & magna vi pecuniæ exutus & spoliatus.
units.tr: Meanwhile, when the King of Spain had learned that the whole of Belgium had been stirred up to tumult and sedition because of Alva's arrogance, he recalled him and sent Don Luis de Requesens, called Medina cæli, as governor of Belgium, who arrived in November. But before that he had been stripped and robbed by the Sea Beggars of part of his fleet and of a great sum of money.

units.la: Albanus Ambsterdami, cum vespere promisisset, se mane creditoribus mercatoribus, & aliis satisfacturum esse, tempestiuius, quam illi, surgens abiit Bruxellam, & inde cum opibus in Hispaniam in Decembri profectus est, postquam Belgium multis modis afflixisset & oppressisset, & valde turbatum reliquisset, quemadmodum sequens Belgarum ad Regem Hispaniarum scriptum declarat.
units.tr: Alva, at Amsterdam, having promised in the evening that in the morning he would satisfy his creditors, merchants and others, rose earlier than they did and departed for Brussels, and from there set off for Spain in December with his wealth, after he had afflicted and oppressed the Netherlands in many ways and left it deeply disturbed, as the following letter of the Belgians to the King of Spain makes clear.

units.la: EPISTOLA SIVE LIBELLVS SVPPLEX ad Philippum II. Hispaniæ Regem, nomine Principis Aurai-ci, Ordinum Hollandiæ atque Zelandiæ, & reliquorum totius Belgii fidelium subditorum, qui Ducis Albani atq; Hispanorum tyrannide misere opprimebantur,
units.tr: LETTER OR succinct petition to Philip II, King of Spain, in the name of the Prince of Orange, of the Orders of Holland and Zeeland, and of the other faithful subjects of all Belgium, who were wretchedly oppressed by the tyranny of the Duke of Alva and the Spaniards

units.la: Continens veram originem motuum Belgicorum, remediaq; iis sedandis necessaria.
units.tr: Containing the true origin of the Belgian troubles and the remedies necessary to calm them.

units.la: QVotiescunque fidelissimi, afflictissimique Regiæ Maiestatis tuæ clientes Belgæ de innata tibi singulari quadam benignitate secum cogitarunt, paternam tuam beneuolentiam, qua hæreditarias hasce Prouincias tuas, earumque incolas, iam inde ab illo tempore, quo primum earum dominium gubernationemque à Deo Opt. Max. accepisti, perpetuo & constanter es prosequutus, penitius cum animis suis reuoluentes: toties firma quadam atq; indubitata fiducia erecti certissime sibi persuaserunt, te partim quotidianis ipsorum querelis atque lamentis, partim quorundam Christiani orbis Principum, quos nostri commiseratio tetigit, testificationi tantum tribu-turum,vt miserabilem& calamitosam ipsorum oppressionem, in quam illos inaudita intolerabilisque violentia atque impi-issimum Ducis Albani imperium præcipitauit, semel benigne cognosceres.Sperarunt etiam hæreditariarum Regionum tuarum (quarum tot ac tam præclara in rebus difficilimis erga te tuosque maiores extant officia & merita) luctuosissimam vastitatem, & lamentabilem ruinam, ex inaudita belluinaque Ducis Albani ferocia, immanique tyrannide inuectam, aliquam in animo tuo commiserationis scintillam excitaturam. Neque enim dubitabant,quin te male habiturum esset, quod Albanus, tuendæ religionis Romanæ, & tui nominis prætextu, eo erumperet, vt omnia Prouinciarum iura ac priuilegia abs te, tuisque Maioribus sancita, solemniqueiuramento confirmata, rescinderet ac proculcaret: subditorum tuorum capita ac fortunas oppugnaret, totamque Regionem deuastaret, non se-cus ac li apertum se ac iuratum Maiestatis tuæ subditorumque tuorum hostem declarasset.
units.tr: Whenever your most faithful and most afflicted clients in Belgium have considered, with that singular kindness which is innate in you, your paternal goodwill, by which you have constantly and unfailingly cherished these hereditary provinces of yours and their inhabitants from that time on, when you first received their lordship and government from God Most Good and Most Great, they have turned it over in their minds with deep reflection. Each time, they were raised up by a firm and unshaken confidence, and they were most certainly persuaded that you would at least grant the testimony of their daily complaints and laments, and of certain princes of the Christian world whom our plight had moved, so that you would once graciously take notice of their wretched and calamitous oppression, into which the unheard-of and intolerable violence and the most impious rule of the Duke of Alva have plunged them. They also hoped that the mournful devastation and lamentable ruin of your hereditary realms (which have offered so many and such distinguished services and merits to you and your ancestors in very difficult circumstances) brought on by the unheard-of, beastly ferocity and monstrous tyranny of the Duke of Alva, would kindle some spark of pity in your mind. For they did not doubt that you would be deeply troubled that Alva, under the pretext of defending the Roman religion and your name, had broken out to annul and trample underfoot all the rights and privileges of the provinces, sanctioned by you and your ancestors and confirmed by solemn oath; that he was attacking the lives and fortunes of your subjects and laying waste the whole region, just as if he had openly declared himself, under oath, an enemy of your Majesty and of your subjects.

units.la: Quam ob causam incredibili quodam desiderio hactenus hoc expectarunt, vt M. T. horum pertæsa, opportunis commodisque remediis conseruationi harum Prouinciarum, assertionique suorum subditorum misere oppressorum consule-ret,ponens sibi ob oculos officii Regii rationem. Qui cum ab omnipotenteDeo, Rege omnium Rege, vicarius, iustitiæ suæ administrator, & pastor ac pater populi sis constitutus, ab omni iniuria ac vi eum protegere,& tueri debes:reuocans etiam in memoriam innumera fidelissimaque officia, quæ Belgæ cum in Maiores tuos,tum in teipsum summâ beneuolentiâ fidelitateque contulerunt. Cæterum, quum nunc, idque non sine extremo quodam animi dolore, satis animaduertant,omnes suas petitiones inanes hactenus infrugiferasque fuisse: nihil etiam aliorum Principum relatu testificationeque profectum esse, nihilque solatii ex iis ad se peruenisse: ( quum tamen ipsi opti-mè sibi conscii sint, nullam tibi iustam atque idoneam causam fuisse, ob quam subtracta omni benevolentia ac clementia à inifere oppressis clientibus tuis te auerteres atque alienares) facile intelligunt, haec omnia ex priuatorum quorundam hominum malis artibus,& sinistra narratione prouenire, qui nulla Regiæ vtilitatis ac commodi, sed sola priuatarum cupiditatum ratione habita, in hoc vnum vires suas omnes contulerunt, vt prouincias hasce summo Maiestatis tuæ odio grauarent.
units.tr: For this reason they have hitherto awaited, with incredible longing, that Your Majesty, wearied of these things, would take thought, by timely and suitable remedies, for the preservation of these provinces and for the vindication of your subjects wretchedly oppressed, keeping before your eyes the reason of your royal office. Since you have been appointed by almighty God, King of all kings, as his vicar, administrator of his justice, and shepherd and father of the people, you ought to protect and defend them from every wrong and violence. They also call to mind the countless and most faithful services which the Belgians have rendered, both to your ancestors and to yourself, with the greatest goodwill and loyalty. But now, and not without extreme grief of mind, they clearly perceive that all their petitions have hitherto been vain and fruitless, and that nothing has been achieved by the report and testimony of other princes, and no comfort has come to them from these. Yet they are themselves most conscious that there was no just and proper cause for you to withdraw all goodwill and clemency from your most wretchedly oppressed clients and to turn yourself away from them and estrange yourself. They readily understand that all this arises from the wicked arts and perverse reports of certain private men, who, having no regard for the advantage and interest of the King but only for their private desires, have directed all their strength to this one end: to burden these provinces with Your Majesty's great hatred.

units.la: Quod quidem à multo tempore satis aperte tentarunt, non solum omni studio impedientes, ne humiles nostræ preces, fideles explicationes ad aures tuas peruenirent: verum etiam eas ipsas atque omnia, quæ in hisce prouinciis euenerunt, in deteriorem partem interpretantes, salsissimeque deferentes; nimirum, vt hac ratione Belgicorum ordinum concordiâ diuulsâ, & perturbatione rerum inducta, Prouincias sub tuo nomine vi opprimere, atque ita subditorum tuorum fortunis ac vita libidinem suam explere, & affectus cupiditatesque suas exsatiare possent.
units.tr: Indeed, they have attempted this quite openly for a long time, not only by every effort preventing our humble prayers and faithful explanations from reaching your ears, but also by interpreting in the worst light both these very things and everything that has happened in these provinces, and reporting them most perversely. Clearly, by this method, the harmony of the Belgian orders was to be torn apart and confusion of affairs brought about, so that they might oppress the provinces by force under your name, and thus satisfy their lust with the fortunes and lives of your subjects, and sate their passions and desires.

units.la: Hoc est, clementissime Rex, quod clientes tui summo iure sibi persuaserunt, nullum atrocius aut luctuosius calamitatis atque miseriæ genus ipsis accidere vnquam potuisse, quam quod re ipsa experiantur, aditu mipsum, facultatemque conquerendi apud legitimum ac natiuum Dominum, quem sibi pro tutissimo refugio in extremis suis calamitatibus acceperant, inimicorum atque æmulorum iniquitate, ita eis præclusum fuisse, vt id ipsum, quod brutis animantibus concedi solet, vt mala ac miserias suas eiulatu testentur, variis pessimisque artibus, & immani quadam crudelitate ipsis interdictum ac plane ereptum fuerit.
units.tr: This, most merciful King, is what your clients have most rightly persuaded themselves: that no more atrocious or mournful kind of calamity and misery could ever have befallen them than what they are actually experiencing, namely that, through the injustice of enemies and rivals, access to, and the opportunity of complaining before their lawful and native lord, whom they had accepted as their safest refuge in their extreme calamities, has been so closed to them that what is customarily granted even to brute animals, namely to bear witness to their evils and miseries by lamentation, has been forbidden to them and utterly snatched away by various wicked arts and a kind of monstrous cruelty.

units.la: Qua de causa quum multo tempore ita affecti fuerint, plane secum statuerint, vt tolerantia adhibita optatissimum illum diem expectarent, quo Maiestas tua semel oculos atque aures accommodatura esset, ad ea audienda, atque introspicienda, quorum aspectum, & auditum maleuoli odio atque inuidia flauidia flagrantes hactenus impedierunt: Tamen quum iam ad extremum videant ac sentiant, oppressionem legum ac libertatis de die in diem grauiorem intolerabilioremque fieri ;neque solum ad priuatum ipsorum detrimentum atque perniciem, verum etiam ad harum prouinciarum, quae tibi parent, (quae quidem olim summa prosperitate floruerunt,)ruinam euersionemq; spectare:nulla ratione committere possunt, quin pro ea fidelitate, quam ad vltimum vsque vitae spiritum tibi,& patriae probare deliderant, nouo rursum scripto Maiestati tuae testentur atq; declarent,nihil ipsos impensius optare, quam in integra perpetuaque Maiestatis tuae obedientia durare, obnixe orantes vt originem ipsam calamitatis harum Prouinciarum, & quib. auctoribus, quibusque modis inuecta fuerit, cognoscere velit, vt pro innata sibi benignitate veri Regis officio fungens iustitiam defendat, & ditiones suas ab huiusmodi vi oppressioneque tueatur. Primum hoc à Maiestate tua, quata possunt animi submissione, petunt, in memoriam reuocare secumq; expendere velit, Belgicas ditiones,quum olim in diuersorum dominorum fide ac clientela fuissent, postmodum matrimonialibus contractib. mutuisque stipulationibus, ac tandem iure legitimae successionis & pacti Burgundicae familiae tanquam capiti accessisse. Deinde etiam intercedentibus matrimoniis cum illustrissima familia Austriaca,ac tandem cum potentissimo Hispaniarum Regno sociatas fuisse. Iistamen semper expressis conditionibus & contractibus, vt in iisdem ditionibus,singulisque prouinciis speciatim, sua cuiusque Reipub. administranda ratio, iuraq; & immunitates ab omni memoria per manus traditae sartae tectae manerent, ita vt nulli vnquam harum Prouinciarum, nulli etiam Regno ius aut dominium in aliam prouinciam competere posset, ad eius iura, immunitates ac priuilegia vlla ratione infringeda: quin potius communi concordia & aequali gradu vno aliquo Principe seu capite vteretur,vt multi liberi vno patre,vt huiusmodi concordia coueni-entiaq; intercedete dignitas ipsorum, Principis, & prouinciarum salus
units.tr: For this reason, since they have been so affected for a long time, they have fully resolved to await, with patience, that most longed-for day on which Your Majesty would at last turn your eyes and ears to hear and look into those things whose sight and hearing ill-wishers, burning with hatred and envy, have hitherto prevented. Yet now, since they see and feel at last that the oppression of laws and liberty grows heavier and more intolerable from day to day, and that it aims not only at the private loss and ruin of themselves, but also at the ruin and overthrow of these provinces, which obey you (provinces which once flourished with the greatest prosperity), they cannot in any way refrain from testifying and declaring again in a new writing to Your Majesty, in return for that fidelity which they wish to prove to you and to the fatherland until their last breath, that they desire nothing more earnestly than to remain in complete and perpetual obedience to Your Majesty. They earnestly beg that you may wish to learn the origin of the calamity of these provinces, and by whose authors and by what methods it was brought about, so that, performing the office of a true king from your natural kindness, you may defend justice and protect your dominions from such violence and oppression. First of all, they ask Your Majesty, with all the submissiveness of mind they can muster, that you would be pleased to recall to memory and consider that the Belgian dominions, once in the faith and clientship of various lords, afterwards came, by marriage contracts, mutual stipulations, and at last by right of lawful succession and by agreement, to the Burgundian house as its head. Then, through marriages intervening with the most illustrious Austrian house, and at last with the most powerful kingdom of Spain, they were joined to it. Yet they were always joined under expressed conditions and contracts, so that in these dominions, and in each province in particular, the administration of each commonwealth, and its rights and immunities handed down from memory by hand, would remain whole and intact, so that no right or lordship over another province could ever belong to any one of these provinces, or to the kingdom, to infringe in any way their rights, immunities, and privileges. Rather, they would enjoy one prince or head in common concord and equal standing, just as many children have one father; and the dignity of these provinces and of their prince, and the welfare of the provinces, would be preserved by such concord and agreement.

units.la: Et obnixe rogamus, vt originem harum calamitatum cognoscas, iustitiam defendas, &c.
units.tr: And we earnestly ask that you know the origin of these calamities, defend justice, and so on.

units.la: I.Cumha Prouinciae in diuersorum dominorum clientela fuissent, tandem Burgundica familia accessisse, & tandem Austriaca domui & Hispan. Regno sociatas fuisse, ita tamen vt singulis sua iura & immunitates sarta tectaque manerent. salus ac prosperitas aduersus exterorum infultus, atque extremam vim propugnari ac defendi posset. Quin & Princeps ipse harum ditionum, vt paternam animi propensionem ac beneuolentiam in singulas ex æquo Prouincias declaret,quum imperium adit, eiqueinauguratur, folemniiureiurando fe obstringit, promittens vnicuique Prouinciæ sigillatim, se ita præfuturum ac gubernaturum,vt singulis sua iura, immunitates ac priuilegia sarta tecta tueatur, neque permissurum, vt illa aliqua ex parte infringantur vel imminuantur, neque vt vna Prouincia in alteram vllum imperium habere possit, tantum abest, vt omnes simul exteri cuiuspiam imperio gubernationique subiiciantur. Hisce conditionibus acceptatur declaraturque Dominus harum ditionum, accipiens hoc pacto à subditis iuramentum fidelitatis atque obedientiæ.
units.tr: I. Although the provinces had once been in the clientship of various lords, at last they came to the Burgundian house, and finally were joined to the Austrian house and the Spanish kingdom, yet in such a way that the rights and immunities of each remained whole and intact, so that their safety and prosperity could be protected and defended against the assaults of foreigners and extreme violence. Moreover, the Prince himself of these dominions, in order to declare his paternal disposition and goodwill equally towards each province, when he enters upon his rule and is inaugurated, binds himself by a solemn oath, promising to each province separately that he will so preside over and govern it that he will protect its rights, immunities, and privileges whole and intact, and will not permit any of them to be infringed or diminished in any part, nor that one province should have any lordship over another; much less that all of them together should be made subject to the rule and government of any foreigner. On these conditions the lord of these dominions is accepted and declared, receiving in this way an oath of fidelity and obedience from the subjects.

units.la: Qua quidem de re superuacaneum est, longiorem orationem instituere, quum proculdubio Maiestas tua satis meminerit, quo pacto g.m. Carolus V. Imperator maiorum suorum vestigiis insistens, optimeque intelligens, iuramentum illud inaugurationis, cuius modo mentionem fecimus, vnicum esse firmissimumque fundamentum, cui tam potentia & auctoritas Principis, quam fidelitas & obedientia subditorum innitItur, curauit, vt M. T. ipso viuo, atque adeo præsente, eodem iuramento præstito acceptaretur, & inauguratio tua (quam Felicem aduentum vocant) in omnibus Prouinciis, atque ab omnibus iuramento confirmaretur. Primum tanquam futuro, & quidem vnico Cæsaris hæredi. Deinde discedente Imperatore, quum M. T. plenum absolutumque imperium & administrationem harum ditionum adiret, idem iuramentum denuo in Comitiis omnium totius Belgii Ordinum recitatum arctiusque constabilitum est; adeo vt ab omni memoria constet, hasce ditiones priuatis vniuscuiusque Prouinciæ legibus, immunitatibus atque Priuilegiis semper administratas fuisse.
units.tr: There is no need for a long speech on this matter, since Your Majesty will surely remember how the late Emperor Charles V, following the example of his ancestors and understanding very well that the oath of inauguration just mentioned is the one most firm foundation on which both the power and authority of a Prince and the fidelity and obedience of subjects rest, took care that Your Majesty should be accepted, with the same oath sworn, while he was still alive and present, and that your inauguration (which they call the Joyous Entry) should be confirmed by oath in all the Provinces and by everyone. This was first done for you as the future and indeed the sole heir of the Emperor. Then, when the Emperor departed and Your Majesty took up full and absolute rule and administration of these lands, the same oath was recited again in the assembly of the Estates of all Belgium and was more firmly established. So it is plain from all memory that these lands have always been governed under the private laws, immunities and privileges of each Province.

units.la: Quam quidem administrandi rationem tanta obedientia, obseruantia & fides in Principem est subsecuta, tantus Prouinciarum ciarum inter se amor, tantaque concordia, vt (diuina opitulante Clementia) ditiones prosperrimo felicissimoque rerum statu hactenus floruerint, earumque Principes in summo honoris ac dignitatis fastigio constituti hostibus suis admirationi, terrorique fuerint.
units.tr: Such a manner of government was followed by such obedience, observance and loyalty towards the Prince, and such mutual love and harmony among the Provinces, that these lands (with divine mercy helping) have hitherto flourished in a most prosperous and happy condition, and their Princes, placed at the highest peak of honour and dignity, have been a source of wonder and terror to their enemies.

units.la: Et quidem, ne ex veteribus historiis exempla repetamus, quae quamplurima huc adferri possent, haec ipsa subditorum tuorum fidelitas satis in omnibus bellis à Cæs. Maiest. fuit declarata. Atq; vt bona tranquillitas & protectio harum ditionum maximæ semper illi curæ fuit, ita etiam Maiestas tua meminisse potest, quam accurate, quamq; ardenter & amice sub discessum suum hasce Prouincias præ reliquis omnibus tibi commendarit atque tradiderit. Quin etiam M. T. quum inaugurationem suam difficilimis bellis, grauissimisque oneribus expræteritis bellis inuoluta esset, reipsa comperit, quam acres & parati fuerint subditi tui cuiusuis ordinis pro sua quisq; facultate & viribus, ad vitas & fortunas suas pro tua salute ac dignitate exponendas. Qua in re Prouincia tota ita officio suo satisfecit, vt Maiestas tua deuictis hostibus suis, summo honore & gloria apud omnes Principes parta, finem omnibus bellis atque discordiis, quibus per tot annos maiores tui, ditionesq; vexatæ fuerant, imposuerit.
units.tr: Indeed, not to cite examples from ancient histories, of which very many could be brought forward, the loyalty of your subjects was sufficiently shown in all the wars of His Imperial Majesty. And just as the good peace and protection of these lands was always his chief concern, so Your Majesty can remember how carefully, fervently and affectionately he commended and handed these Provinces over to you above all others when he departed. Moreover, when your inauguration was entangled in very difficult wars and the very heavy burdens of the wars that had gone before, Your Majesty actually found out how keen and ready your subjects of every rank were, each according to his means and strength, to risk their lives and fortunes for your safety and dignity. In this matter the whole Province so fulfilled its duty that Your Majesty, with your enemies defeated and highest honour and glory won among all princes, put an end to all the wars and discords by which your ancestors and these lands had been harassed for so many years.

units.la: Nunc si Maiestati tuæ placuerit, (quod quidem miseri fideles-que subditi tui humilibus precibus abs te contendunt) diligenter inuestigare atque expendere, quisnam fuerit fons atq; origo immutationis ex illa præclara tranquillitate prosperitateque in hanc adeo miserabilem perturbationem & calamitatem rerum, qua nunc temporis ditiones tuæ opprimuntur, deprehendet proculdubio, eam non aliunde oriri, quam ex scelera-tissimo odio atq; inuidia, quam quidam M. T. intimi conceperunt, quaq; adhuc concitantur aduersus opulentiam prosperitatemq;, qua Deus O. M. ditiones subditosq; tuos ornârat.
units.tr: Now, if it pleases Your Majesty (which your wretched and faithful subjects humbly beg of you) to investigate and weigh carefully the source and origin of the change from that splendid tranquillity and prosperity to this miserable disturbance and calamity by which your lands are now oppressed, you will surely discover that it arises from nothing other than the most wicked hatred and envy which certain intimate counsellors of Your Majesty have conceived, and which is still being stirred up against the wealth and prosperity with which God, most good and great, has adorned your lands and subjects.

units.la: Quod quidem odium atq; inuidia cum insatiabili quadam auaritia, aliisq; prauis cupiditatib. flagraret, ita eos in omne genus
units.tr: This hatred and envy, burning with a certain insatiable greed and other wicked desires, drove them so headlong into every kind of

units.la: nus confidentiæ crudelitatisque præcipites egit, vt prorsus obliti omnis beneuolentiæ, studii atque officii, quod hisce ditionibus(à quibus summis honoribus ac beneficiis erant affecti)debebant, perniciosissimum horum ciuilium motuum incendium non absque summo Maiestatis tuæ publicæq; harum Prouinciarum vtilitatis detrimento, omnibus artibus & machinationibus adhibitis excitarunt, nimirum, vt ea ratione ad summum dignitatis gradum, de quo non solum ordines harum Prouinciarum, verum etiam Maiestatem tuam deturbare conantur, facilius peruenire possent.
units.tr: recklessness and cruelty that, utterly forgetting all the goodwill, zeal and duty which they owed to these lands (by which they had been honoured with the highest offices and benefits), they stirred up, by every art and contrivance, this most pernicious fire of civil disturbances, not without great harm to Your Majesty and to the public welfare of these Provinces. They did so in order that by this means they could more easily climb to the highest rank of dignity, from which they are trying to thrust down not only the Estates of these Provinces but also Your Majesty.

units.la: Quum vero facile intelligerent, se hoc nulla ratione consecuturos, saluo iure ac Priuilegiis harum Prouinciarum, quæ teterrimis illorum conatibus ex diametro, quod aiunt, repugnabant, quumque animaduerterent, quam diligentem ac fidelem operam Prouinciæ in suo quæque ordine vocationeq; nauarent, quamq; sancte iuxta formulam iuramenti abs se præstiti priuilegia sua propugnarent ac tuerentur, neque vlla ratione infringi ea labefactariq; sinerent, in hoc vnum velis & remis, vt dicitur, incubuerunt, vt omnes gubernatorü atq; ordinum in hisce ditionib. actiones, quæ ad defensione conseruationemq; eorundé Priuilegiorum pertinebant, ita ad Maiest. tuam deferrent atq; interpretarentur, q. ii ipsi defectione aliquam rebellionemq; aduersus Maiestatem tuam molirentur.
units.tr: But when they clearly understood that they could in no way achieve this while the rights and privileges of these Provinces stood safe (privileges which, as they say, were utterly opposed to their foul attempts), and when they saw how diligently and faithfully the Provinces, each in its own rank and calling, were doing their work, and how holily, according to the formula of the oath they had sworn, they defended and protected their privileges, and would not allow them to be infringed or weakened in any way, they set themselves to one thing with all sails and oars, as the saying goes: to report to Your Majesty, and interpret in the worst light, every action of the governors and Estates in these lands which pertained to the defence and preservation of those privileges, as if they were themselves plotting some defection and rebellion against Your Majesty.

units.la: Inter quos quum præcipui essent quidam Ecclesiastici nominis, omni studio, omnibusque rationibus elaborarunt, vt prætextu religionis cum aliis exteris etiam iis Ecclesiasticis, factionem aliquam inirent, atque ita paulatim secretis machinationibus, fraudulentisque artibus hasce ditiones in Maiestatis tuæ odium pertraherent, vt ita ipsi & suæ factionis homines (qui profecto non Maiestati tuæ, sed exteris Principibus & Prouinciis in Italia & alibi, ac præcipue Romano Pontifici iureiurando obstricti erant) ius & dominium in has ditiones inuadere, eosque, prout sibi commodius visum esset, propagare possent. Posteaquam enim senserunt Ecclesiastici in finitimis Regionibus, atque adeo per vniuersum Christianum orbem, ingentes crassissimosque abusus & errores, qui longinquitate temporis, & nimia inscitia, negligentia, auaritiaque Sacerdotum irrepserat, nunc tandem prodi ac detegi, quumque iam pii omnes ab iis abhorrere coepissent (q; ii, quorum illa vnica cura esse debebat, populū verbo DEI pascere, sanaq; doctrina, & puris moribus imbuere, & cultum DEI ad exemplum Prophetarum & Apostolorum promouere, deserto officio suo non solum aduersus euidens DEI praeceptum, verum etiam aduersus Pontificū decreta, contraq; omnes veterum Conciliorum, atq; adeo contra omnes Principum ac Prouinciarū sanctiones sese in saecularis, vt vocant, ac ciuilis iuris administrationem, quinimo in bellica & politica Prouinciarū negotia supra omnes infimae ac supremae iurisdictionis dominos ingererent, eaq; suo arbitratu gubernarent;) idcirco ipsi summa quadā animi acerbitate salsissimas calumnias excogitarunt, multisq; delationib. & fictis criminationib. fideles subditos tam tuae Maiestat. q; aliorum Regum ac Principum, apud suos Praefectos & Reges onerarunt, malitiosis falsissimisq; calumniis seditionis, rebellionisq; accusantes, quib. artibus omnia Imperia atq; Prouincias atrocibus dissidiis atq; discordiis, imo v. flagrantissimorum bellorum incendiis miscuerunt, subditosque in dominos, & dominos in subditos concitarunt. Ad summam, perturbato rerum omnium ordine ac statu, deforme atq; horribile quoddam chaos inuexerunt, parum solliciti, in quos ea calamitas esset redundatura, modo ipsi, quae sibi propositū habebāt, promouere possent, reliquis omnib. subImp. suū ac potestatem redactis.
units.tr: Among these men, since certain persons of ecclesiastical name were the chief ones, they laboured with every zeal and by every means, under the pretext of religion, to form a faction with other foreigners, even ecclesiastical ones; and so, gradually, by secret schemes and fraudulent arts, to draw these lands into hatred of Your Majesty, so that they themselves and the men of their faction (who were bound by oath not to Your Majesty but to foreign princes and provinces in Italy and elsewhere, and above all to the Roman Pontiff) might be able to invade the right and dominion over these lands and extend it as seemed more convenient to them. For when the ecclesiastics in neighbouring regions, and indeed throughout the whole Christian world, had perceived that huge and gross abuses and errors had crept in through the long passage of time and the excessive ignorance, negligence and greed of the priests, and that these were now at last being brought to light and exposed, and when already all pious people had begun to shrink from them (those whose sole care should have been to feed the people with the Word of God, to imbue them with sound doctrine and pure morals, and to promote the worship of God after the example of the Prophets and Apostles, but who, deserting this duty, not only against the plain command of God but also against the decrees of the Pontiffs, against all the councils of the ancients, and indeed against all the sanctions of princes and provinces, thrust themselves into the administration of so-called secular or civil law, and even into the military and political affairs of the Provinces, above all the lords of lower and higher jurisdiction, and governed them at their own pleasure), therefore they devised, with a certain fierce bitterness of spirit, the most bitter calumnies. By many accusations and fabricated charges they burdened faithful subjects of Your Majesty and of other kings and princes before their own prefects and kings, accusing them with malicious and utterly false slanders of sedition and rebellion. By these arts they mixed all empires and provinces with savage dissensions and discords, indeed with the blazing fires of the most fierce wars, and stirred up subjects against their lords and lords against their subjects. In short, having thrown the order and state of all things into confusion, they introduced a certain foul and horrible chaos, being little concerned on whom that calamity would fall, provided they themselves could advance what they had proposed, with all the others reduced beneath their own power.

units.la: Hoc etiam consilio Inquisitionem (quae aduersus Iudaeos primum Christianique nominis abiuratores institVta fuit) in has Regiones vi inuehere conati sunt, vt eius ope ac subsidio omnia prouincialia iura, priuilegia & consuetudines, atque adeo omnes contractus iuramento confirmatos, & pacta funditus euerterent atque delerent: eaque ratione plenam absolutam lutamque potestatem, & imperium in omnes fideles tuæ Maiestatis subditos exercerent, qui nihil aliud quam iuramenti, quo se tibi obstrinxerant, fidelem obseruationem tuebantur, atque vrgebant, omnem aliam exterorum dominorum, tam Ecclesiasticorum quàm laicorum introductionem recusantes: quippe qui nihil aliud sibi propositum haberent, quam eos falsis hæreseos rebellionisque criminationibus opprimere, vt eo facilius id quod statuerant consequerentur.
units.tr: With this same aim they tried by force to bring into these regions the Inquisition (which was first set up against the Jews and against apostates from the Christian name), so that by its help and support they might utterly overthrow and destroy all provincial laws, privileges and customs, and indeed all contracts and agreements confirmed by oath. In this way they would exercise full, absolute and unlimited power and dominion over all the faithful subjects of Your Majesty, who were defending and insisting on nothing but the faithful observance of the oath by which they had bound themselves to you, and who refused the introduction of any other foreign lords, whether ecclesiastical or lay. For those men had no other aim than to crush them with false charges of heresy and rebellion, so that they might more easily achieve what they had resolved.

units.la: Eodem etiam Consilio, nouos suos Episcopos, quorum institutio manifeste omnibus iuribus prouincialibus, priuilegiisque iureiurando confirmatis repugnat, & magnam Regiæ Maiestatis auctoritatisque tuæ imminutionem secum trahit, vi inuexerunt: neque iis quidem ob ipsorum probitatem aut eruditionem ad id electis (nam plerunque indoctissimos ineptissimosque homines delegerunt) sed hoc vnum sibi proponentes, vt fideles administros atque auxiliatores haberent, qui ipsorum ferocitati atque libidini obsecundare, crudeliaque eorum consilia absque vllo cuiuspiam metu exequi possent.
units.tr: By the same design they forcibly introduced their new bishops, whose appointment manifestly contradicts all provincial laws and privileges confirmed by oath, and carries with it a great diminution of Your Royal Majesty's authority. Nor were these men chosen for their uprightness or learning (for they generally picked the most unlearned and unfit men), but with this one aim: that they might have loyal agents and helpers who could humour their ferocity and lust, and carry out their cruel plans without fear of anyone.

units.la: Quum vero scelerata illorum consilia, eorumque futuri euentus magis ac magis quotidie innotescerent, & in publicum erumperent, cœperunt optimates, & prouinciarum gubernatores, ipsæque adeo ciuitates continuis petitionibus, & testificationibus, aliisq; rationibus Maiestati tuæ significare, quanto pere dignitas, & iurisdictio Maiestatis tuæ hoc pacto imminueretur, atque ab ipsis inquisitoribus, & Episcopis proculcaretur, qui maxima ex parte exteri ac peregrini, omnesque exteris dominis iuramento obstricti, atq; adeo (vt ipsimet profitentur) à tua iurisdictione liberi exemptiq; essent. Hoc etiam tibi euidentissimis rationibus comprobarunt, & ob oculos posuerunt, huiuscemodi innouationes nulla plane ratione inuehi posse, quin tota Regio in perpetuam quandam vastitatem, extremamque perniciem adduceretur, quum facile intelligi posset, omnem illum religionis prætextum nihil aliud fuisse, quam laruam, cuius speciè Maiestati tuæ imponerent: atque ita, omnes qui apertos ipsorum abusus & vitia dicto vel facto oppugnarent ac damnarent, aut à manifestis ipsorum erroribus (quos ne ipsi quidem celare poterât) desciscerent, è medio tollerent. Quorum quidem tantus erat hisce ditionibus numerus, adeoque in singulos dies crescebat, vt, si Maiestas tua illorum instigantium consiliis ac suasionibus acquiescens in instituta seueritate perstitisset, te ad extremum Regem absque populo, & præfectum subditis destitutum reddituri fuerint, quemadmodum manifeste satis constare potest ex innumerabili multitudine eorum, qui in hisce ditionibus prætextu religionis ferro, igni, aqua miserabiliter extincti sunt: vt eos præteream, qui exilii causa solum verterunt, qui secum omne genus opificiorum artificiorumque mechanicorum in alias Regiones transtulerunt, cum incredibili earundem Prouinciarum ac Maiestatis tuæ detrimento.
units.tr: When the wicked designs of these men and the consequences that would follow from them became more and more evident every day and broke out into the open, the nobles, the governors of the provinces, and even the cities themselves began to inform Your Majesty, through constant petitions, sworn testimonies, and other means, how greatly the dignity and jurisdiction of Your Majesty were diminished by this arrangement, and how they were trampled underfoot by the inquisitors and bishops themselves. Most of these men were foreigners and strangers, all bound by oath to foreign lords, and, as they themselves profess, free and exempt from Your Majesty's jurisdiction. They also demonstrated to you, by the most evident reasons, and set before your eyes, that such innovations could not be introduced by any means without bringing the whole region to a lasting desolation and extreme ruin. For it could easily be understood that all this pretext of religion was nothing but a mask, under whose appearance they imposed upon Your Majesty. Thus they would remove from the scene everyone who openly opposed and condemned their abuses and vices, by word or deed, or who separated from their manifest errors, which they themselves could not even conceal. The number of these men in these provinces was so great, and grew from day to day, that if Your Majesty had persisted in the severity you had decreed, yielding to the urgings and persuasions of these instigators, you would in the end have been made a king without a people, and a ruler deprived of subjects. This is clear enough from the countless multitude of those who in these provinces have been wretchedly put to death by sword, fire, and water on the pretext of religion. I say nothing of those who left the country in exile, and who carried with them every kind of craft and mechanical trade into other lands, to the incredible loss of these provinces and of Your Majesty.

units.la: Hæ porro causæ Maiestatem tuam tandem moverunt, vt aequabilitate quadam moderationeque Edictorum rebus afflictis consuleres, expresse declarando, te eius animi non esse, vt Inquisitio in hisce Regionibus stabiliretur. Quod ipsum etiam à Ducissa Parmensi, & Prouinciarum gubernatoribus, Maiestatis tuæ nomine, ciuitatibus & communioni, solenni iuramento intercedente, conditum promissumque fuit, & in omnibus Ciuitatibus, expresso mandato supremi Præfecti promulgatum publicatumque fuit.
units.tr: These considerations at last moved Your Majesty to provide for the afflicted state of affairs by a certain even and moderate manner of edicts, expressly declaring that it was not your intention that the Inquisition should be established in these regions. This same promise was also made and sworn, under solemn oath, by the Duchess of Parma and the governors of the provinces in Your Majesty's name, to the cities and the community, and by express command of the supreme governor it was proclaimed and published in all the cities.

units.la: Caeterum haud multo post tempore hoc ipsum rescissum fuit, per eos quos ante diximus, qui hoc Maiestati tuæ depinxisse ac persuasisse videntur, quasi illud decretum ad Maiestatis tuæ dignitatem existimationemque imminuendam pertineret: eum rumorem contra omnem veritatem æquitatemque spargendo, subditos tuos ea ratione se à debita Maiestati tuæ obedientia subducere velle. Ita vt videatur Maiestas tua eiusmodi illorum instinctu tandem eo pellecta fuisse, vt Ducem Albanum ex Hispaniis huc cum exercitu mitteret, vt vi atque armata manu subditos tuos ad id cogeret atque adigeret, ad quod ipsi sua sponte summa cum obedientia animique demissione semper praesto fuerunt. Ac tametsi gubernatores, harum Prouinciarum ciuitatesque ipsae iustis de causis vereri poterant, se graues iniurias accepturos per vim externi militis, & gubernationem cuiusdam gubernatoris exteri, nulloque consanguinitatis iure cum Maiestate tua coniuncti, quique in eos inueterato quodam odio flagraret. Tametsi etiam non deessent ipsis rationes, quibus ei aditum impedire possent: tamen quum is Maiestatis tuae nomine veniret, vt manifeste declararent, se neque de rebellando cogitasse, neque ab obedientia Maiestatis tuae deflexisse, idcirco optimo conscientiae suae testimonio, atque aequitate freti, benevole honorificeque, & ipsum, & quotquot Maiestati tuae visum fuit in eius comitatu mittere, exceperunt, portis vrbium reseratis, locis munitioribus in eius manum potestatemque traditis, praesidiis admissis: idque eo tantum nomine, quod eam Maiestatis tuae voluntatem esse diceret, nimirum vt ea ratione de fidelitate obedientiaque tuorum subditorum certi exploratique aliquid habere posset, qui tanquam rebellionis rei peragebantur. Quae cum ita sint, debebat profecto Albanus omni ratione Maiestatem tuam eiusmodi subditorum tuorum fidelis obedientiae obseruantiaeque certiorem facere: & priusquam vim aliquam inferret, rem ipsam propius cognoscere, solidamque decorum querelis instructionem instituere, in eo praecipue, quod in illa Episcoporum obtrusione, atque Inquisitionis institutione contra diuina humanaque iura fesc grauari querebantur, vt iis rebus vere fideliterque ad Maiestatem tuam perscriptis, in omnibus salutaria ex iure & aequo remedia adhiberentur.
units.tr: However, not long afterwards this very decree was revoked by those same men whom we mentioned before, who seem to have painted this to Your Majesty and persuaded you that that edict tended to diminish the dignity and reputation of Your Majesty. Against all truth and fairness they spread the rumour that your subjects wished by this means to withdraw from their due obedience to Your Majesty. So it seems that Your Majesty, moved at last by the urging of such men, was led to send the Duke of Alba here from Spain with an army, to compel and force your subjects by violence and armed hand to do what they had always been ready to do of their own accord, with the greatest obedience and humility of spirit. And although the governors of these provinces and the cities themselves could with good reason fear that they would suffer grievous wrongs from the force of foreign soldiers and the government of a foreign governor, who was joined to Your Majesty by no bond of kinship and who burned with an old-standing hatred against them, and although they had reasons by which they could have blocked his entry, nevertheless, since he came in Your Majesty's name, they wished to show plainly that they had neither thought of rebelling nor turned away from obedience to Your Majesty. Therefore, relying on the best testimony of their conscience and on fairness, they received him and whomever Your Majesty thought fit to send in his train kindly and with honour: they opened the city gates, handed over the stronger places into his hand and power, and admitted his garrisons. They did this only because he said it was Your Majesty's will, namely that by this means he might have some certain and tested knowledge of the loyalty and obedience of your subjects, who were being pursued as if guilty of rebellion. Since this is so, Alba ought in every way to have made Your Majesty certain of the faithful obedience and observance of such subjects, and before using any force, to examine the matter more closely and to draw up a sound statement of the complaints, especially concerning the imposition of bishops and the establishment of the Inquisition, which they complained was being imposed against divine and human law. Once these matters had been truly and faithfully reported to Your Majesty, salutary remedies in accordance with law and justice would have been applied in all of them.

units.la: At vero e contrario, simul ac admissus fuit, & munitiones totius prouinciae occupauit, nullo iuris ordine obseruato, nulloque respectu habito ad iura prouincialia, priuilegiaque Maiestatis ieftatis tuæiuramento confirmata, non solum magnam par-tem Nobilium, quos Maiestas tua magno delectu habito gu-bernaculis harum ditionum admouerat, ad supplicium ne-cemque rapuit, & proscripsit: verum etiam generaliter immu-nitates priuilegiaque omnia perdita, ac rescindenda esse de-clarauit, & ditiones hasce ita tenendas, vt solent quæ de inte-gro armis sunt acquisitæ, in suum suæque factionis hominum commodum, vt ita libere dissoluteque de subditorum tuorum capite & fortunis pro suo arbitratu libidineque statuere pos-set. Ac si vllis verbis exprimi, & Maiestati tuæ ob oculos poni possent immanes violentiæ, inauditæque crudelitates, quibus ab initio suæ gubernationis est grassatus: nimirum direptio-nes, spolia, exterminationes, deuastationes, carceres, vincula, exilia, profligationes, bonorum proscriptiones, incendia, cru-ces, capitum truncationes, discerptiones, aliaq; horrenda & inaudita tormentorum suppliciorumque genera, quibus Ma-iestatis tuæ subditos tam nobiles quam ignobiles, inopes iux-ta atque opulentos, iuuenes ac senes, viduas & pupillos, viros, mulieres, iuuenculas cuiuscunque status, dignitatis, conditio-nisque essent, immaniter trucidauit, animus Maiestatis tuæ ad eorum commemorationem proculdubio perhorrescceret, in-dignissimeque ferret, sub suo nomine adeo immanem crude-litatem (qualé nunq; aut Phalaris, aut Nero, aut vllus Pharao, Herodes, aut vllus omnino gentilium Tyrannorum excogitauit) exceri in fideles subditos suos, qui sanguine fortunisque suis coronæ regiæque Maiestatis tuæ dignitatem aduersus grauis-simos hostium insultus integram illæsamque conseruarunt.
units.tr: On the contrary, however, as soon as he was admitted and had seized the fortifications of the whole province, without any observance of legal order and without any regard for the provincial laws and the privileges confirmed by Your Majesty's oath, he not only seized and proscribed to execution and death a great part of the nobles whom Your Majesty, after a careful selection, had placed at the helm of these lands, but also declared that all immunities and privileges were generally lost and to be revoked. He ordered these lands to be held as those lands usually are which have been newly acquired by arms, for the advantage of himself and of the men of his faction, so that he might decide freely and lawlessly, according to his own will and lust, concerning the lives and fortunes of your subjects. And if words could express, and set before Your Majesty's eyes, the monstrous violences and unheard-of cruelties with which he has raged from the beginning of his government, namely plunderings, spoliations, expulsions, devastations, prisons, chains, exiles, slaughters, proscriptions of goods, burnings, crosses, beheadings, dismemberments, and other horrible and unheard-of kinds of torture and punishment, by which he has savagely slaughtered your subjects, nobles and commoners alike, the poor as well as the rich, young and old, widows and orphans, men, women, and young girls of whatever rank, dignity, or condition they were, then surely Your Majesty's spirit would shudder at the recollection of them, and would indignantly bear that under his name such monstrous cruelty (such as neither Phalaris, nor Nero, nor any Pharaoh or Herod, nor any of the heathen tyrants ever devised) is vented upon your faithful subjects, who by their blood and their fortunes have kept the dignity of the crown and of Your Majesty's kingship whole and unharmed against the most grievous assaults of enemies.

units.la: Ingentem enim in animo tuo commiserationem excitarent tot miseri innocentesque pueri è patrio solo in exteras igno-tasque regiones profligati, tot miseræ afflictæq; viduæ, tot pu-pilli, denique miserabilis totius prouinciæ eiulatus, quæ adeo immanis tyranni iugo pressa funditus perit.
units.tr: For the many wretched and innocent children, driven from their native soil into foreign and unknown regions, the many wretched and afflicted widows, the many orphans, and finally the pitiful lamentation of the whole province, which, pressed under the yoke of so monstrous a tyrant, is utterly perishing, would surely stir up in your heart a great compassion.

units.la: Ecquis enim erat, qui vel opes facultatesque suas ab illorum auaritia, aut vxores & filias contra eorum libidinem, vitam denique contra sanguinariam ipsorum rabiem tueri posset? Neminì omnino vel nobilitas, vel opulentia, vel anteactæ vitæ præstantia, præclaraue in Rempublicam merita adiumento esse poterant, qui semel in illorum odium incurrisset. Preterea nullo habito respectu ad iurisdictiones &vsitata tribunalia Prouinciarum, præripi iussit facultatem omnibus Iudicibus, tam in criminalib. quam ciuilib. causis cognoscendi de rebus, quæ aliquo modo ad proscriptiones Senatus sanguinarii (quem ipse ex Hispanis hominib. instituit) auctoritate factas pertinere videntur: ita vt neq; Ecclesiasticæ, nec piæ seculares (vt vocant) personæ, nec viduæ aut pupilli, neq; xenodochia, nec leprosorum ædiculæ, nulla orphanotrophia, neq; nosocomia alendis senib. decrepitis instituta, (quib. omnib. partim proscriptorū, partim eorum, de quib. capitale supplicium sumptum erat, bona iusto nomine & hypothecato debito obstricta erant) vllum interuntium inde consequi potuerint. Sed ea omnia Albanus vsurpauit, nullis omnino censib. quib. bona illa onerata erant, persolutis, quantumuis Ordines harum Prouinciarum hac in parte pro defensione miserorum subditorum diligentem atq; diuturnam operam per libellos supplices exhibitos nauarint: quos variis semper Senatusconsultis protraxerunt, atq; iis quidem nullo iure stabilitis, manifesteq; inter se pugnantibus, neque vnquam id impetrare potuerunt, vt earum rerum cognitio ad prouinciales tribunalia, aut vsitatos Iudices deferretur: vt ita miseri subditi de solutione Senatus Albanici auctoritate consequenda desperantes, nomina detulerent, quum singulis creditoribus particulatim lis formalis aduersus fiscalem intentanda fuerit.
units.tr: For who was there who could protect his wealth and property from their greed, or his wives and daughters from their lust, or finally his life from their bloody fury? For those who had once fallen into their hatred, neither noble birth, nor riches, nor the distinction of a past life, nor outstanding merits towards the commonwealth could be of any help at all. Moreover, without any regard for the jurisdictions and customary tribunals of the provinces, he ordered that the power of hearing both criminal and civil cases be snatched from all judges, insofar as these cases seemed in any way to concern the proscriptions made by the authority of the bloody Senate, which he himself set up from Spanish men. Thus neither ecclesiastical persons nor the so-called pious laity, nor widows or orphans, nor hospices, nor the little houses of lepers, nor any orphanages, nor hospitals founded for the feeding of aged and decrepit people (all of which were bound by a rightful name and by a debt secured by mortgage to the goods partly of the proscribed, partly of those whom capital punishment had been taken from) could obtain any redress from it. But Alba seized all those goods without paying any of the charges with which they were burdened, although the Estates of these provinces had, in this matter, made a diligent and long-lasting effort in defence of the wretched subjects by presenting supplicating petitions. These they always delayed by various decrees of the Senate, which were established on no legal basis and clearly contradicted one another, and they never managed to obtain that the cognizance of these matters be referred to the provincial tribunals or the customary judges. So the wretched subjects, despairing of obtaining payment by the authority of the Alban Senate, had to register their names, since a formal lawsuit had to be brought against the treasury separately by each individual creditor.

units.la: Qua in re sumptuum, quos facturi erant, summa nomen ipsum erat superatura.
units.tr: In this matter, the sum of the expenses they were about to incur would have exceeded the very amount of the debt.

units.la: Eadem etiam ratione onera omnia (quæ Chysas vocant) vsurpauit, vnius, duorum, trium, quatuor, quinq;, plus minus assium annuatim, qui maxima ex parte ad ædes pauperib. alendis dicatas pertinent. Quid? quod ne hoc quidem permi-fit, sit, vt quis bonum aliquod nomen alteri cedere, vel in alium transferre posset?
units.tr: By the same method he seized all the levies (which they call Chysas) of one, two, three, four, five, or so asses a year, most of which belong to houses set aside for feeding the poor. And why stop there? He would not even allow a person to cede a good name to another or transfer it to someone else.

units.la: Quot honestissimarum matronarum, quot virginum pu-dicitiam vi expugnarunt, & prostituerunt? iisque vicissim inter se (& quidem nonnullis ad internecionem vsque) sunt abusi?
units.tr: How many chaste matrons and how many virgins' modesty did his men overpower by force and prostitute? And in turn they abused these women among themselves, some to the point of death.

units.la: Quoties maritos vxoribus suis, parentes filiabus adstare coegerunt, vt oculati testes, atque adeo administri adiutoresq; essent horrendae foedissimaeque eorum libidinis? quam vsque adeo foedo & efferato more exercuerunt, vt nos ea absque horrore ne animo quidem cogitatione que concipere valeamus; tantum abest, vt honeste ea Maiestati tuae verbis exprimere possimus.
units.tr: How often did they force husbands to stand by while their wives were violated, and parents while their daughters were, as eyewitnesses and even as servants and helpers of their horrible and most foul lust? They practised it in so foul and savage a manner that we cannot even conceive of it in our minds without horror, let alone express it decently in words to Your Majesty.

units.la: Quam frequens atque vsitatum hoc fuit, vt cum aut maritus aliquis vxorem, aut pater filiam ab illorum vi oppressioneque tueri vellet, veluti rabidi canes excurrerent conclamantes, Hispania, Hispania? eamque ob causam Ciues, quotquot obuios haberent, miserabiliter trucidarent? Quot mulieres grauidas laceraurunt, foetusq; in materno vtero oppresserunt? Quid dicam, quot viros viuos excoriarunt, tympanaque eorum cute obduxerunt? ipsos vero lento igne vstulantes ardentibus forcipibus conuulserunt, aliisque immanibus atque inauditis cruciatibus afficientes, adeo lenta centies queiterata miserorum morte se ob lectarunt? Quot honestas matronas a suis maritis, filias a parentibus auulserunt? At quid obsecro sub sole adeo honestu & sancti, adeoq; religiosum esse aut fingi potest, q; non violarint, contaminarint, coculcarint? Certe apud omnes gentes tantus semper mortuorum sepulturae honos tributus fuit, vt ne barbarissimae quidem crudelissimaeque nationes eum contemnendum violandumue putarint. Caeterum, hic Tyrannus, veluti in Dei humanaeq; naturae ludibrium ac despectum, multorum cadauera, quum per aliquot dies humata fuissent, sepulchris erui, & ad patibulum rapi iussit: eo praetextu, quod hic absque Confessione auriculari decessisset; alter Sacramenta ante obitum non percepissent. Sed reuera nihil aliud causæ erat, quam vt bona possessio esque à demortuis relictæ in fiscum redigerentur.
units.tr: How common and customary it was that, whenever a husband wished to protect his wife, or a father his daughter, from their violence and assault, they would rush out like rabid dogs shouting "Spain! Spain!" and, for that reason, cruelly butcher whatever citizens they met! How many pregnant women did they tear apart, crushing the unborn child in the mother's womb? What more can I say? How many living men did they flay, covering their drums with their skin? Others they tore with red-hot pincers while roasting them over a slow fire, and subjecting them to other monstrous and unheard-of tortures, they prolonged the wretched people's deaths, a hundred times repeated, to a slow end. How many honourable matrons did they tear from their husbands, and daughters from their parents? But what, I ask, under the sun is so honourable, so holy, or so religious that they did not violate, defile or trample underfoot, or at least could be imagined to be so? Certainly among all peoples the honour of burying the dead has always been so great that even the most barbarous and cruelest nations did not think it should be despised or violated. Moreover, this tyrant, as if in mockery and contempt of God and of human nature, ordered the corpses of many men, after they had been buried for some days, to be dug out of their graves and dragged to the gallows, on the pretext that one had died without auricular confession, another had not received the sacraments before death. In truth, however, there was no other cause than that the goods and property left by the dead might be transferred to the treasury.

units.la: Quid vero est inter homines dignius, quid sanctius matrimonio, fonte & origine amicitiæ, politicæque societatis? Vinculo omnis concordiæ, verissimoque gradu omnis honestatis, qua humana societas continetur? Sed ne huius quidem dignitas apud tyrannum valuit, quin potius vxores à suis maritis, maritos ab vxoribus, qui tamen in publico Christianorum coetu coram Deo atque Angelis copulati, sanctissimoque matrimonii vinculo inter se colligati erant, contra Dei præceptum atque institutum, contraque omnia iura auulsit, fictitio quodam prætextu, quod ab hæreticis essent copulati.
units.tr: What is more worthy among men, what more holy than marriage, the source and origin of friendship and of political society? It is the bond of all concord and the most true foundation of all honour, by which human society is held together. But not even this dignity counted for anything with the tyrant. Rather, against God's precept and institution and against all laws, he tore wives from their husbands and husbands from their wives, who had nevertheless been joined in the public assembly of Christians, before God and the angels, and bound together by the most holy bond of marriage. He did this under the fictitious pretext that they had been married by heretics.

units.la: Sed nullam profecto aliam ob causam, quam vt ditiores, formosioresque mulieres militum apparitorumque suorum prædæ exponeret, amorem ac beneuolentiam, quam alter alteri debemus, funditus euertit, trucidans mulieres, quæ suis maritis, filios, qui parentibus in extrema inopia constitutis, pecuniario aliquo subsidio subuenissent, atque adeo qui nuda Epistola eos consolati fuissent.
units.tr: But surely for no other reason than to expose the richer and more beautiful women as booty to his soldiers and attendants, he utterly overturned the love and goodwill we owe one another. He slaughtered women who had helped their husbands, and sons who had assisted their parents, who were in extreme poverty, with some monetary aid, and indeed those who had comforted them merely by a letter.

units.la: Denique, ne quid omnino sacrosanctum diuinumque esset, quod ille non profanaret, & contaminaret, diuinissimum Baptismatis Sacramentum, per quod in societatem Ecclesiæ Dei, atque adeo in ipsum Christi corpus inserti sumus, sceleratissime proculcauit, volens ac iubens, vt puerorum, quos semel rite & legitime ex norma & institutione Filii Dei, in nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus Sancti baptizatos esse constabat, baptismus iteraretur, eo prætextu, quod ab hæreticis essent baptisati. Quod quidem manifeste omnibus tam diuinis, quam humanis legibus, omnibusque Ecclesiæ præceptis, & Conciliorum decretis repugnat.
units.tr: Finally, so that nothing whatever sacred and divine should be left that he did not profane and defile, he most wickedly trampled underfoot the most divine sacrament of Baptism, through which we are incorporated into the fellowship of the Church of God and indeed into the body of Christ itself. He willed and commanded that the baptism be repeated for children who, as was established, had once been duly and lawfully baptized according to the rule and institution of the Son of God, in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, on the pretext that they had been baptized by heretics. This manifestly contradicts all divine and human laws, all precepts of the Church and the decrees of the Councils.

units.la: Ad hæc, quid attinet Maiestati tuæ commemorare infinitas inauditasque exactiones, quas quotidie alias ex aliis excogitauit, iisque miserum populum, vltra quam dici posset, onerauit? Nimirum centesimam, vigesimam & decimam portionem bonorum omnium tam mobilium, quam immobilium, imo etiam omnium mercimoniorum, quæ aut emerentur, aut venderentur, petens ac volens, vt mandato suo re ipsa (dissuadentibus interim atque repugnantibus vniuersis harum Regionum Senatibus atque Ordinibus) satisfieret, neque id quidem ex summa lucri, quod ad venditores peruenire, sed ex integra & capitali rerum vendarum summa vicesimum & decimum nummum exigens.
units.tr: Furthermore, what is the point of recounting to Your Majesty the endless and unheard-of exactions which he devised daily, one after another, and with which he burdened the wretched people beyond what can be told? Namely, he demanded the hundredth, twentieth and tenth part of all goods, movable and immovable, indeed of all merchandise that was bought or sold, insisting that his command be carried out in practice, while all the Senates and Orders of these regions advised against it and resisted. And he exacted this not on the sum of profit that reached the sellers, but on the whole capital value of the goods sold, taking the tenth penny.

units.la: Qua quidem extorsione non solum omnis negotiatio & mercatura ex hisce Regionibus est sublata, verum etiam incolis ratio parandi victus sibi ac liberis plane subtracta.
units.tr: By this extortion not only has all trade and commerce been removed from these regions, but the inhabitants have also been completely deprived of the means of providing a living for themselves and their children.

units.la: Cuius rei summam iniquitatem, cum ordines sæpenumero illi prolixe explicassent, maiorem, quam ipsorum vires facultatesque ferrent, summam ei obtulerunt.
units.tr: Since the Orders had often explained at length the enormous unfairness of this matter to him, they offered him a sum greater than their own strength and resources could bear.

units.la: Cæterum, quantumuis accurate & frequenter Ordines Albano declarare probareque studuerunt, quanta confusio atque absurditas ex adeo pertinaci eius voluntate esseт oritura, rogaruntque, vt iustas ipsorum excusationes Maiestati Tuæ scripto explicaret. nulla tamen ratione ab instituto suo dimoueri potuit, quin potius negata eis in posterum audientia reiecit, nullo saniore consilio admisso, quantumuis etiam Ecclesiastici, & Senatus, atque Ordines harum Prouinciarum sua intercessione laborarint, ita vt hoc pacto vniuersam negotiationem & mercaturam ex hisce Regionibus profligarit, miserosque incolas ob inopiam atque egestatem solum vertere coegerit.
units.tr: However carefully and frequently the Orders strove to declare and prove to Alva how great confusion and absurdity would arise from such obstinate will, and asked him to set out their just excuses in writing to Your Majesty, he could by no means be moved from his purpose. Instead, refusing them any further hearing, he rejected them, adopting no saner counsel, although the clergy, the Senate and the Orders of these provinces laboured hard with their intercession. In this way he destroyed all trade and commerce in these regions and forced the wretched inhabitants, through poverty and want, to leave their homeland.

units.la: Constat tamen, quotiescunque militibus stipendiorum, Solutionem exigentibus satisfaciendum fuit, nullam vnquam ipsum pecuniam ad manum habuisse adeo vt Hispanis militibus octodecim mensium stipendia debuerit, Germanos non paucos ostiatim stipem emendicare, ac nonnullos paupertate, inediaque extingui fit passus, cum nihilominus Ordines summam exactionis subsidii pecuniarii ab ipso ad militum solutionem imperati copulerint. Nihilo interim secius maximam ciuitatum partem praesidiis militaribus onerauit, planeque exhausit, opprimens eas, vltra salgamum, certa pecuniae summa viritim in militum sumptus danda, quam Seruitio vocant: quique ei maiorem summam aut Albano aut eius filio Friderico, aut eorum asseclis tribuebant, primi ab hac Seruitii siue vectigalis seruitute immunes facti fuerunt. Hisce etiam praesidiis potissimum vexauit ciuitates, in ipsis prouinciae viscerib{us} sitas: vrbibus interim maximi momenti, & ad fines prouinciae sitis vacuis ab omni praesidio relictis. Vnde multis in locis facilior rerum ac status est orta mutatio. Quid dicam?? quod, dum milites Hispanos stipendiis suis defraudat, ansam iis praebuit effraeni quadam licentia intemperantiaque grassandi: nimirum bonis viris minandi, verberandi, spoliandi, diripiendi, omnique genere exactionis compilationisque vexandi?
units.tr: It is certain, however, that whenever the soldiers demanding their pay had to be satisfied, he never had any money on hand. So much so that he owed the Spanish soldiers eighteen months' pay, allowed many Germans to beg alms from door to door, and let some perish from poverty and hunger, although the Orders had collected the whole sum of the monetary subsidy imposed upon him for paying the soldiers. Nevertheless, he burdened the greater part of the cities with military garrisons and utterly drained them. Beyond the salt tax, he oppressed them with a fixed sum of money to be paid per head for the soldiers' expenses, which they call the Servitium. Those who gave a larger sum to Alva, or to his son Frederick, or to their followers, were the first to be made immune from this servitude of the Servitium or tax. He also harassed especially the cities lying within the very heart of the province with these garrisons, while cities of the greatest importance, lying on the frontiers of the province, were left empty of any garrison. Hence in many places a change of affairs and of government came more easily. What shall I say? While he defrauded the Spanish soldiers of their pay, he gave them the opportunity to rage with a certain unbridled licence and intemperance: namely, to threaten, beat, despoil, plunder good men, and harass them with every kind of exaction and pillage?

units.la: Quibus omnibus e rebus hisce clarius videri potest, omne illud, quod prae se fert Regiae Maiestatis dignitatisque, & religionis tuendae atque amplificandae studium, nihil aliud esse, quam commentitios quosdam praetextus, quibus insatiabilem suam auaritiam, & sanguinariam crudelitatem obtegere, fucumque aliquem obducere conatur: quum tamen rei veritas plane contraria manibus habeatur, & oculis cernatur, nimirum illum nihilo amplius de Regiae Maiestatis Tuae dignitate, quam de publica totius Prouinciae vtilitate laborare, quam quidem funditus euerti atque interire finit.
units.tr: From all these facts it can be seen more clearly that all that show of zeal for Your Majesty's dignity and for defending and extending religion is nothing but made-up pretexts, by which he tries to conceal his insatiable avarice and bloody cruelty and throw a disguise over them. Yet the truth of the matter lies plainly in hand to the contrary and is seen with the eyes: he cares no more for Your Majesty's dignity than for the public welfare of the whole province, which he allows to be utterly overthrown and to perish.

units.la: Sed quorsum attinet prolixam harum rerum probationem instituere? quasi vero nondum satis reipsa declararit, quorsum omnes eius actiones conatusque pertineant: cum ita eum insatiabili auaritia turgidaque arrogantia occæcarint, atque adeo dementarint, vt veluti trophæum, æternumque rerum, quas diximus, adeo præclare à se gestarum monimentum sibi ipsi in Antuerpiana (quam ipse etiam extruit) statuam æneam exære captiuo, vt in inscript. eius iactat, erexerit, Nobilitatem & Ordines prouinciarum pedibus conculcantem. Prætermisso hoc loco, quid illius statuæ erectione in animo habuerit explicare. Cæterum, vbi vnquam vllis historiis proditum legimus tyrannum aliquem, cum adhuc in viuis esset, statuam sibi erexisse? Certe Romani Cæsares & Reges, qui totum fere terrarum orbem subegerant, interdum statuas vel lapideas vel æneas sibi erigi passi sunt: (quemadmodum hodie Pontifices Romani, qui se Dei vicarios iactitant, idem faciunt) semper tamen iussu auctoritateque Senatus, aut populi, aut saltem eorū consensu bonaq; gratia intercedente id factum fuit. At vero quod ipsi, cum adhuc in viuis essent, tale quippiam decreuerint, nullis exemplis ostendi potest. Ecquod enim euidentius vesanæ cuiusdam dementiæ, intolerabilisque superbiæ, argumentum esse possit?
units.tr: But what is the point of setting out a lengthy proof of these things, as if he had not already declared in fact what all his actions and efforts aim at?
