Thus the most wealthy and splendid city and very great riches were destroyed in a most wretched slaughter in a short time, on 5 November, in the year

units.la: Mars ar Det eXLeX Ant Verpla.
units.tr: March [...] at Antwerp.

units.la: Intelligentes hoc Status 15. Prouinciarum commodum fore existimant, vt fœdere se cum Auraico & Hollandis & Zelandis coniungant, vt se melius contra rebelles tueri possent. Compositi igitur 25. articuli conditionales, quos vide alibi, idque Gandauii 8. Nouemb.
units.tr: The States, understanding that this would be to the advantage of the fifteen Provinces, judged that they should join themselves by covenant with the Prince of Orange, Holland and Zeeland, so that they could better defend themselves against the rebels. Accordingly, twenty-five conditional articles were drawn up (see them elsewhere), and this was done at Ghent on 8 November.

units.la: Comes Rheni Gubernator Flandriæ, accepto milite ex Hollandia, obsidet Hispanos in Castello Gandauensi, & vltimo Nouemb. illud occupat, dimissis Hispanis cum armis & reculis.
units.tr: The Count of the Rhine, Governor of Flanders, having received soldiers from Holland, besieges the Spaniards in the Castle of Ghent, and on the last day of November takes it, the Spaniards being dismissed with their arms and baggage.

units.la: Status occupant vrbem & Castellum Valentiæ.
units.tr: The States occupy the city and castle of Valenciennes.

units.la: Nota. Qui tumultus Groningæ & in Frisia fuerint, & quomodo sese cum confœderatis coniunxerint, & Castellum euerterint Groningenses?
units.tr: Note. What disturbances there were at Groningen and in Friesland, how they joined themselves with the confederates, and whether the Groningers overthrew the castle?

units.la: IOHAN. DE AVSTRIA GVBERNATOR BELGII.
units.tr: JOHN OF AUSTRIA, GOVERNOR OF BELGIUM.

units.la: Ioh. de Austria Luzemburgi aliquandiu subsistit, & pacificationem Statuum vnitorum suo approbatu confirmat, & dimissionem Hispanorum ex Belgio promittit.
units.tr: Don John of Austria stays for some time at Luxemburg, confirms by his own approval the pacification of the united Estates, and promises the withdrawal of the Spaniards from Belgium.

units.la: Hispani Castellum Traiecti in manus Bossu, qui nomine Statuum id obsidebat, tradunt.
units.tr: The Spaniards hand over the castle of Utrecht to Bossu, who was besieging it in the name of the Estates.

units.la: Status cum Austriaco in Marche & Fanime transigunt, compositis nomine Regis in forma Edicti perpetui 19. articulis, quos vide alibi. Februario.
units.tr: The Estates reach an agreement with the Austrian at Marche and Famenne, and in the name of the King the 19 articles drawn up in the form of a perpetual Edict are settled, which see elsewhere. February.

units.la: Hinc illud:
units.tr: Hence that line:

units.la: Venit post MVLtos paXreno Vata Dies.
units.tr: There comes, after many troubles, a day of peace.

units.la: Auraicus & Hollandi de his edocti, vident hoc Edicto quosdam Statuum priuilegia cheruari, vt quod Statibus adimitur ius conuocandi Ordines, & quod ad nouum iuramentum hactenus non vsitatum adigi videantur, violari priuilegia in eo, quod Comes Burensis Louania abductus tam diu captiuus detineatur. Euerti etiam pacificationem nuper Gandauii receptam. Ex iis, vt ex articulis tempore Margarethæ Parmensis dolose factis & acceptis, persecutiones nasci posse. Se igitur has conditiones accipere non posse.
units.tr: The Walloons and the Hollanders, informed of these matters, see that by this Edict certain privileges of the Estates are being overturned: that the right of summoning the Orders is taken away from the Estates, and that they seem to be forced to take a new oath not used until now; that privileges are violated in that the Count of Büren, carried off from Louvain, is still held captive for so long. The pacification recently received at Ghent is also being undone. From these terms, as from the articles framed and accepted deceitfully in the time of Margaret of Parma, persecutions may arise. They therefore cannot accept these conditions.

units.la: Adhæc 1s. Status ostendunt, se pacificationem Gandauii initam retinere, & exteros eliminatos cupere.
units.tr: Besides, on the 1st the Estates show that they keep the pacification entered into at Ghent, and desire that foreigners be removed.

units.la: Ordines vi recuperant Castellum Gandauiense.
units.tr: The Orders by force recover the castle of Ghent.

units.la: Ordines recipiunt & tradunt Castellum Antuerp. Regi & Austriaco, dimissis Hispanis.
units.tr: The Orders receive and hand over the castle of Antwerp to the King and the Austrian, the Spaniards having been dismissed.

units.la: Escouedo Secretarius Regius in iuramenti acceptione dixit: Si hoc facis, iuuet te Deus: sin minus, rapiat te Diabolus corpore & anima.
units.tr: Escobedo, the royal secretary, when the oath was being taken, said: "If you do this, may God help you; if not, may the Devil seize you, body and soul."

units.la: Hispani egressi castello Antuerp. & aliunde, commutatis captiuis discedunt mense Aprili.
units.tr: The Spaniards, having left the castle of Antwerp and elsewhere, depart in April after prisoners have been exchanged.

units.la: Austriacus splendidissime excipitur Bruxellis, & in Gubernatorem generalem iuramento mutuo facto inauguratur.
units.tr: The Austrian is received most splendidly at Brussels, and is installed as governor general after a mutual oath has been sworn.

units.la: Quanquam vulgus, quod Austriacus sclopetarios in sua Guardia haberet, indignabatur, ideoque & ipsi arma sua deponere noluerunt.
units.tr: Although the common people were indignant that the Austrian had musketeers in his guard, the men themselves were unwilling to lay down their arms.

units.la: Austriacus magna pompa Mechliniæ excipitur.
units.tr: The Austrian is received at Mechlin with great pomp.

units.la: Pax nuper inter Austriacum & Status inita non diuturna fuit.
units.tr: The peace recently concluded between the Austrian and the Estates did not last long.

units.la: Nam Austriacus accepta gubernatione, statim, quæ in secretis mandatis acceperat, exequi incipit. Interim is se erga omnes humanissimum præbebat, & eo ipso in suspicionem se adduxit occultarum machinationum.
units.tr: For the Austrian, once he had taken up the government, at once began to carry out what he had received in secret instructions. Meanwhile he showed himself most courteous to everyone, and by this very means aroused suspicion of hidden schemes.

units.la: Conantur ordines pecuniam colligere, vt Germani milites stipendio accepto dimitterentur. Verum Austriacus, etsi dimissionem se promoturum fingit, tamen interim cum Fronsbergio, & Polwileio, & aliis clam agit, vt Antuerpiam & alias Ciuitates arte in suam potestatem redigant.
units.tr: The Orders try to collect money so that the German soldiers may be discharged once their pay has been received. But the Austrian, although he pretends that he will promote their dismissal, meanwhile secretly negotiates with Fronsberg, Polwiler and others, so that by stratagem they may bring Antwerp and other cities under his power.

units.la: Scripserat autem Austriacus literas ad Regem, quibus eum ad bellum instigat, & ostendit, opus esse, vt morbida membra amputentur, vt causa officiorum inter Nobiles & populum æmulationes excitentur, & discordiæ serantur, rebus Belgii nequaquam clementia, verum igne & sanguinis effusione mederi posse.
units.tr: The Austrian, moreover, had written letters to the King urging him to war, and showing that diseased limbs must be amputated, that quarrels must be stirred up between the nobles and the people, that discords must be sown, and that the affairs of Belgium can by no means be healed by clemency but only by fire and the shedding of blood.

units.la: Hæc
units.tr: These things.

units.la: Hæ literæ in Gasconia interceptæ à Rege Nauarræ ad Aurai-cum, & ab hoc ad Ordines missæ sunt, & cum furtiuis literis & numeris essent scriptæ, ab Aldegundio sunt explicatæ.
units.tr: These letters, intercepted in Gascony, were sent by the King of Navarre to Orange, and from him to the Orders; and since they were written in secret characters and numbers, they were explained by Aldegonde.

units.la: Ex his & aliis signis doli ipsius Austriaci patuerunt. Qui hoc sentiens, prætextu, quod Regina Nauarræ Margaretha adueniens honorifice excipienda esset, astu Namurci arcem occupat, tenet & Carlemontem & Marieburgum. Simul sin-git sibi Mechliniæ insidias structas fuisse, quas coactus sit eui-tare.
units.tr: From these and other signs the deceit of the Austrian himself became plain. Perceiving this, on the pretext that Queen Margaret of Navarre was arriving and had to be received with honour, he cunningly seized and held the citadel of Namur, together with Charlemont and Marienburg. At the same time he feigned that snares had been laid for him at Mechlin, which he had been compelled to avoid.

units.la: Ordines se excusant, & Austriaco securitatem, modo Bru-xellas veniat, promittunt. Cumque intelligerent, Endensem cum milite pergere vt Antuerpiam occupet, Champigneum mittunt, qui eum cædit fugatque, & Noyellus Bourfius Or-dinibus militans, Arcem Antuerp. Ordinum commodo oc-cupat.
units.tr: The Orders excuse themselves, and promise the Austrian safe conduct provided he comes to Brussels. And when they learned that Ende was marching with troops to seize Antwerp, they sent Champigny, who struck him down and put him to flight; and Noyelles Bourse, serving the Orders, seized the citadel of Antwerp to the Orders' advantage.

units.la: Ciues Germanis in vrbe tumultuantibus stipendia promit-tunt, vt discedant: sed recusantibus id facere, Auraicus oppor-tune nauibus adueniens eos ita terret, vt nullo accepto stipen-dio aufugerint, & sic Fakerus & Fronspergius Antuerpiam cum dedecore relinquunt.
units.tr: The citizens promise pay to the Germans who were rioting in the city, so that they would leave; but when they refused to do so, Orange arrived opportunely with ships and frightened them so much that they fled without receiving any pay, and thus Verdugo and Fronsberg left Antwerp in disgrace.

units.la: Champigneus post: Bergesonnam capit, Fuggero capto, post Buscumducis & Breda traduntur Ordinibus, Austriaci copiæ hinc inde profligatæ à Champigneo.
units.tr: Afterwards Champigny captured Bergen-op-Zoom; Fugger was taken, and afterwards Bois-le-Duc and Breda were handed over to the Orders; the forces of the Austrian were routed here and there by Champigny.

units.la: Arschotus cum Namurco aufugisset, fit Gubernator Flan-driæ.
units.tr: Arschot, having fled with Namur, became governor of Flanders.

units.la: Ordines ad Regem scribunt, & Austriacum accusant, qui se præsentibus Cæsaris Legatis pacem optare simulat, & dis-cedere se velle, si certus fiat, religionem Catholicam, & Regis auctoritatem ibi fore saluam.
units.tr: The Orders write to the King and accuse the Austrian, who, in the presence of the Emperor's envoys, pretends to desire peace and says he is willing to depart if it is made certain that the Catholic religion and the authority of the King will remain safe there.

units.la: Respondent Ordines, Catholicam religionem restitutam esse, & vigere, & se Regem magis honorare, quam solent ipsi Hispani, & ad Regem scribunt, & alium Gubernatore petunt.
units.tr: The Orders reply that the Catholic religion has been restored and flourishes, and that they honour the King more than the Spaniards themselves are accustomed to do; they write to the King and ask for another governor.

units.la: Interea Austriacus Luzelburgum petit, & Hispanos reuo-cat. Ordines etiam contra se ad bellum parant, & Castellum Antuerp. dirimunt. Euersæ & aliæ arces, vt Gandauii, Traiecti, Insulis, Valentiæ, ne oppida ab iis infestarentur. Exercitum versus Namurcum mittunt.
units.tr: Meanwhile the Austrian makes for Luxemburg and recalls the Spaniards. The Orders also prepare for war against him, and dismantle the castle of Antwerp. The other citadels, at Ghent, Utrecht, Ypres (?), and at Valenciennes, are also razed, so that the towns should not be harassed from them. They send an army toward Namur.

units.la: Editur Apologia à Statensibus, cui Austriacus respondet.
units.tr: The Apology is published by the men of the States, and the Austrian replies to it.

units.la: Germani milites, qui in Buscoduco, sub Oberstein fuerunt, coacti sunt urbe cedere. Et Fronspergius Bergum Statibus restituit.
units.tr: The German soldiers who were in Bois-le-Duc, under Oberstein, were compelled to leave the city. And Fronsberg restores Bergen to the Estates.

units.la: Ordines ab Auraico opem petunt, & eum ex Hollandia accersitum, & Antuerpiæ splendidissime exceptum in Rhuevvart, i. e. custodem pacis, & gubernatorem Brabantiæ eligunt. Qui Catholicam religionem permittit. Octob.
units.tr: The Orders seek aid from Orange, and, having summoned him from Holland and received him most splendidly at Antwerp, they elect him Ruward (that is, guardian of the peace) and governor of Brabant. He permits the Catholic religion. October.

units.la: Inuiderunt hunc honorem Auraico præcipui Proceres Belgii. Arschotus, Egmondanus, & multi alii, sine generalium Ordinum scitu, vocant Matthiam Archiducem Austriæ Caesaris fratrem, vt eius obtentu Prouinciarum gubernationem vsurpare possent. Id vbi suboluit Gandauensibus, Ducem Arschotum, cum aliis eiusdem factionis proceribus capiunt, sed eos rursus dimittunt.
units.tr: The chief nobles of Belgium, Arschot, Egmont and many others, envied Orange this honour; without the knowledge of the General Orders they summon Archduke Matthias of Austria, brother of the Emperor, so that under his patronage they might usurp the government of the Provinces. When this came to the knowledge of the men of Ghent, they seized the Duke of Arschot with other nobles of the same faction, but afterwards released them again.

units.la: Cometa visus in Belgio in Nouembri, quem mors Iohannis Austriaci & effusio sanguinis in dimicationibus sequuta.
units.tr: A comet was seen in Belgium in November, which was followed by the death of John of Austria and the shedding of blood in battles.

units.la: Iohannes Austriacus contra Matthiam apud Cæsarem conqueritur. Et bellum de integro suscitat.
units.tr: John of Austria complains to the Emperor against Matthias. And he stirs up war afresh.

units.la: Status occupant Espont, & deducunt exercitum ad Namurcium.
units.tr: The Estates occupy Esponts and lead their army to Namur.

units.la: Austriacus D. Henger & Mandragon Duces belli constituit.
units.tr: The Austrian appoints Count Egmont (?) ... Dukes Henger and Mandragon as commanders of the war.

units.la: MATTHIAS ARCHIDVX GVBERNATOR, CVIVS VICARIVS EST Auraicvs.
units.tr: Matthias the Archduke and Governor, whose vicar is Auraicus.

units.la: Interea Matthias Archidux Austriæ venit Antuerpiam, & quanquam à suis desertus esset, tamen persuasione Auraici, (Austriaco pro hoste publico declarato) ab Ordinibus, certis legibus in Gubernatorem eligitur, cui Auraicus constituitur vicarius, & fiunt vtrinque iuramenta.
units.tr: Meanwhile Matthias, Archduke of Austria, came to Antwerp. Although he had been deserted by his own men, he was nevertheless elected Governor by the Orders, under certain laws, through the persuasion of Auraicus, after Austria had been declared a public enemy. Auraicus was appointed his vicar, and oaths were exchanged on both sides.

units.la: Baro deSelles ex Hispania appellens pacis conditiones proponit, per quas pacificationi Gandauensi derogatur.
units.tr: Baron de Selles arrived from Spain and proposed terms of peace, by which the Pacification of Ghent was undermined.

units.la: Austriacus Parmensem cum suis Hispanis & Italis in Belgium rursus inuehit, quibus fretis Belgis bellum indicit.
units.tr: Austria again brought Parma into Belgium with his Spanish and Italian troops, and relying on them, declared war on the Belgians.

units.la: Papa vero crucem suam vulgo cruciatam contra eosdem publice denuntiat.
units.tr: The Pope publicly proclaimed his crusade against the same people.

units.la: Gimi vicarius Lalaingi summi Ducis exercitus Hatnum iussus castra Namurco mouet, & à Ioh. Austriaco maximam cladem accipit, vltimo Ianuarii.
units.tr: Gimi, vicar of Lalaing, the supreme commander's army, was ordered to Hannut and moved his camp from Namur. On the last day of January he received a very great defeat from John of Austria.

units.la: Ioh. Austriacus occupat Gible & Bouinges, post victoriam suam prosequens Louanium, Arschot, Thinei, Sichen, Diest, deuincit.
units.tr: John of Austria occupied Gembloux and Bouvignes and, pursuing his victory, subdued Leuven, Aarschot, Tienen, Zichem and Diest.

units.la: Andius siue Alanzo frater Regis Galli, audita clade ad Namurc. operam suam offert Statibus.
units.tr: Anjou, or Alençon, brother of the King of France, on hearing of the defeat at Namur, offered his services to the States.

units.la: Ordines post multos tandem labores Ambsterodamum adipiscuntur. Feb.
units.tr: After many labours, the Orders at last obtained Amsterdam. February.

units.la: Niuella post oppugnationem deditur Hispanis. Februar.
units.tr: Nivelles surrendered to the Spanish after a siege. February.

units.la: Cum Wormatiæ Comitia celebrarentur, supplicant Status Cæsari pro pace obtinenda, interprete Aldegundo.
units.tr: While the Diet was being held at Worms, the States petitioned the Emperor to secure peace, with Aldegundus as interpreter.

units.la: Philippivilla, Soignies, Roene, Binche, Beaumont, Walecourt, Mabuge ad generalem Pardonnam sese Austriaco dedunt.
units.tr: Philippeville, Soignies, Rœulx, Binche, Beaumont, Walcourt and Maubeuge surrendered themselves to Austria under the general pardon.

units.la: Status auxilium apud Anglam petunt, & obtinent Martio.
units.tr: The States sought help from England and obtained it in March.

units.la: Dissidia in Frisia.
units.tr: Dissensions in Friesland.

units.la: Campena & Dauentria à Rennebergio obsessæ & captæ.
units.tr: Campen and Deventer were besieged and captured by Rennenberg.

units.la: Ordines in Ecclesiasticis & Politicis rebus leges & Statuta edunt ad normam pacificationis Gandauensis, & iusiurandum obedientiæ & fidelitatis ab incolis suis exigunt, quod Iesuitæ & alii præstare recusant, & honeste ex urbe educuntur.
units.tr: The Orders issued laws and statutes in ecclesiastical and political matters, according to the norm of the Pacification of Ghent, and demanded an oath of obedience and fidelity from their inhabitants. The Jesuits and others refused to take it, and were honourably escorted out of the city.

units.la: Monachi Sodomitæ in Flandria comburuntur.
units.tr: Sodomite monks were burned in Flanders.

units.la: Historia fratris Cornelii concionatoris.
units.tr: The story of Brother Cornelius, the preacher.

units.la: Ordines de magno exercitu colligendo deliberant, in eum finem ad Casimirum & alios scribunt, simulque Ducis Andii siue Alenzonii auxilium (tractatu super ea re cum eo habito) adscitcunt.
units.tr: The Orders deliberated on raising a large army. To that end they wrote to Casimir and others, and at the same time secured the aid of Duke Anjou, or Alençon, having negotiated with him on that matter.

units.la: Articuli pactorum cum Alenzonio 13. Augusti initi videantur in historia.
units.tr: The articles of the agreements made with Alençon on 13 August are set out in the history.

units.la: Ordinum copiæ undique colliguntur.
units.tr: Forces of the Orders were gathered from everywhere.

units.la: Exercitum lustrat Matthias Belgii Gubernator.
units.tr: Matthias, Governor of Belgium, reviewed the army.

units.la: Lanoius Gallus, quod strategorum omnium haberetur præstantissimus, ex Galliis evocatur, & in tribunum militarem constituitur, conueniunt prope.
units.tr: Lanoy the Frenchman, because he was considered the most outstanding of all the commanders, was summoned from France and appointed military tribune. They gathered nearby.

units.la: Agmen Ioh. Casimiri Antuerpiam appropinquat.
units.tr: The army of John Casimir approached Antwerp.

units.la: Austriacus circa 30. M. milites habuit.
units.tr: Austria had about 30,000 soldiers.

units.la: Primarius Legatus militiæ Parmensis fuit.
units.tr: Parma was the chief envoy of the army.

units.la: Austriacus in signo crucifixum depinxit hac inscriptione: In hoc signo vici Turcas; in hoc signo vincam hereticos.
units.tr: Austria painted a crucifix on his banner with this inscription: "In this sign I conquered the Turks; in this sign I shall conquer the heretics."

units.la: Velitatum est ad Arschot multas horas.
units.tr: There was skirmishing at Aarschot for many hours.

units.la: Ordinum milites egregie restiterunt Hispanicis in summo calore, ita vt Scoti aliqui tantum indusiis ad femora ligatis præliarentur. Austriacus amisit 900. Ordines pauciores, Iulio. Ordines Arschotum capiunt & discedunt: redeunt Hispani & reliquos trucidant. Austriacus in Namurcensem regionem recedit.
units.tr: The soldiers of the Orders resisted the Spanish splendidly in the height of the heat, so that some Scots fought wearing only breeches tied at the thighs. Austria lost 900 men, the Orders fewer. July. The Orders captured Aarschot and withdrew; the Spanish returned and slaughtered the rest. Austria retreated into the Namur region.

units.la: Veniunt Cæsaris, Galli & Anglæ Legati tractaturi de pace. Ordines conditiones scribunt, & Gandauensem pacificationem seruari optant. Legati Austriaco persuadere volunt, ut discedat, sed ille renuit, ita nulla est facta transactio.
units.tr: Envoys of the Emperor, of France and of England came to treat about peace. The Orders wrote down their conditions and wished the Pacification of Ghent to be kept. The envoys wanted to persuade Austria to withdraw, but he refused, so no agreement was reached.

units.la: Reformatæ Religionis defensores (protestantes) Matthiç & Ordinibus generalibus supplicem libellum totius Belgii incolarū nomine offerunt 22. Iun. religionis libertatem (salua et Papistica) petentes, adductis vrgentibus rationibus, quum non solum Imperatores aliquot, sed & Papa Iudæis Synagogas gogas permittat. Dilata responsione alterum libellum supplicem iisdem offerunt 7. Iulii magnam modestiam promittentes.
units.tr: Defenders of the Reformed religion (Protestants) offered Matthias and the General Orders a humble petition on behalf of all the inhabitants of Belgium on 22 June, asking for liberty of religion (with the Papal religion also preserved), and bringing forward pressing reasons: not only several emperors, but even the Pope, permit synagogues to the Jews. After the answer was deferred, they offered the same authorities another humble petition on 7 July, promising great moderation.

units.la: Archidux Matthias, Auraicus, Consilium Status, & Ordines generales, libertatem vtriusq; religionis ciuitatibus concedunt, ne alius alium moleste, cū vtrisq; contra Hispanos dimicandum sit. Sed pax haec religionis causa fuit multorum incommodorum.
units.tr: Archduke Matthias, Auraicus, the Council of State and the General Orders granted liberty of both religions to the cities, so that neither party should molest the other, since both had to fight against the Spanish. But this peace was the cause of many troubles.

units.la: Data igitur templa pro exercitio religionis reformatae Antuerpiae, Bruxellae, Mechliniae, Bergis, Bredae, Lyrae, Brugis, Yperae, In Frisia, Geldria, & alibi.
units.tr: Therefore churches were given for the exercise of the reformed religion at Antwerp, Brussels, Mechelen, Bergen, Breda, Lier, Bruges, Ypres, in Friesland, Gelderland and elsewhere.

units.la: Choros Pontificii seruant.
units.tr: The Papists kept their choirs.

units.la: Champignicus Bruxellae reformatae religioni obsistens capti-uatur a ciuibus.
units.tr: Champagny, who opposed the reformed religion at Brussels, was captured by the citizens.

units.la: Ioh. Imbyfius cum aliis paucis Gandauii sibi potentiam acquirunt, bona Ecclesiastica diripiunt, ex campanis bombardas conflant.
units.tr: John Imbyze, with a few others, won power for himself at Ghent, plundered church property, and melted down church bells to make cannons.

units.la: Arthesia & Hannonia acerrime sese opponunt paci religionis publico scripto.
units.tr: Artois and Hainault most fiercely opposed the peace of religion in a public document.

units.la: His turbis Catholica religio expellitur, solaque reformata tota ciuitate instituitur, auctoritate ac voluntate eorum tantum, qui religionis pacem acceptare abstinate recusant.
units.tr: By these disturbances the Catholic religion was expelled, and the reformed religion alone was set up throughout the whole city, by the authority and will of only those who refused to abstain from accepting the peace of religion.

units.la: Archidux Matthias, Auraicus, Consilium Status, diuersas cum suis conditiones, etiam ciues Antuerpienses & Bruxellenses eo mittunt Legatos, qui tumultuantes ad frugem bonam reducant: Verum admonitiones, testificationes ac postulationes omnes in cassum tunc temporis adhibentur.
units.tr: Archduke Matthias, Auraicus and the Council of State sent them various conditions, and also sent envoys to the citizens of Antwerp and Brussels to bring the rioters back to sound sense. But all admonitions, testimonies and demands were then in vain.

units.la: Plures huius mali occasiones fuere; imprimis autem scriptum quoddam, quod Ordinum Hannoniae deputati typis ediderė, quoad exercitii reformatae religionis postulationem & ad Archiducis Matthiae literis & de pace religionis summarium deliberandi causa missum respondent: quibus acerrime se opponunt omnesque tum primates tum plebeios his rebus assentientes perfidos declarare videntur, sequeque vitae, ac facultatum periculo, resistere prorsus velle testificantur.
units.tr: There were several occasions for this evil. Above all, there was a certain printed writing, which the deputies of the Orders of Hainault published in reply to the demand for the exercise of the reformed religion, and to the letter of Archduke Matthias sent for the purpose of deliberating on a summary of the peace of religion. In it they opposed these measures most fiercely, and seemed to declare all, both nobles and commoners, who assented to them, to be faithless. They testified that they were wholly prepared to resist, at the risk of life and property.

units.la: Hanc factiosorum causam acriter tuebantur Artefiæ & Hannoniæ Nobiles, qui crescere cupientes nihil non gloriæ & potentiæ sibi arrogabant, & Auraico dignitatem inuidebant, tum & Walonicæ Prouinciæ; & sic discordia nata, quæ deinceps causa fuit, vt Status paulatim disiungerentur, & à Parmensi debellarentur.
units.tr: The nobles of Artois and Hainault defended this cause of the factious most fiercely. Desiring to grow, they claimed for themselves every kind of glory and power, and envied Auraicus his dignity. So too did the Walloon province. Thus discord arose, which afterwards was the cause that the States were gradually separated and were defeated by Parma.

units.la: Valentinus Motta Gubernator Greuelingæ in Flandria Regi reconciliatur, literas super hac reab eo obtinens, qui sua auctoritate reliquos quoque ad defectionem ab Ordinibus inuitat. Fuit inter Gallicas siue Walonicas Prouincias, & inter Flandros siue Gandauenses acris disensio seu discordia, quam Dux Matthias & Ordines Belgici componere omni studio nituntur, vt sic iunctis armis ac animis hosti resistant, sed frustra. Nam factiones odiaque ita creuerunt, vt ad arma vtrinque ventum sit.
units.tr: Valentin Motta, Governor of Gravelines in Flanders, was reconciled to the King, obtaining letters on this matter from him, and by his authority he invited the rest, too, to defect from the Orders. There was a bitter dissension or discord between the French, or Walloon, provinces and the Flemings, or men of Ghent. Duke Matthias and the Belgian Orders strove with all zeal to settle it, so that, with arms and minds joined, they might resist the enemy, but in vain. For the factions and hatreds grew so great that both sides came to arms.

units.la: Quum enim diuersæ essent Walonum regiones sub Montignio, Hesso, Cupresso, Egmondano, Bourso, aliisque tribunis, quibus stipendia non exoluebantur, ea maxime de causa, quod Walonicæ Prouinciæ designatas contributiones subterfugerent, subsidiaque ad generales Prouincias non conferrent: tandem eorum agmina quædam in Flandricos agros, maxime iurisdictionis Gandauensis, hostiliter incendiis, latrociniis, stupris grassantur, atque per omnem hunc Flandricum tractum violentis incendiariisque exactionibus, intra octo aut nouem menses trecenta florenorum millia extorquent, Ecclesiasticos Gandauensium limitibus expulsos palam ac manifeste protegunt fouentque. Et Nobiles Gandaui captiuos inhumaniter tractari indignantur causanturque. Hæ cohortes Gandauensibus Paternoster Knecht / id est, sphærularum precatoriarum milites: vulgo Malecontenti, quod nomen vltro assumebant: Francis Leo blanqxeux: id est, albi oculi, ab quibus nempe, quibus intimo morbo laborantibus oculi albescunt, agnominabantur.
units.tr: For the Walloon regions were divided among Montigny, Hesse, Cuypers, Egmont, Bours and other tribunes, to whom pay was not handed over, chiefly for this reason: the Walloon provinces were evading the contributions assigned to them and not contributing subsidies to the general provinces. At last some of their companies raided the fields of Flanders, especially the jurisdiction of Ghent, with hostile fires, robberies and rapes. Through all this Flemish tract, by violent and incendiary exactions, they extorted three hundred thousand florins within eight or nine months, and they openly and manifestly protected and fostered the ecclesiastics who had been expelled from the bounds of Ghent. The nobles complained indignantly that the captives at Ghent were treated inhumanly. These cohorts were called by the Ghentish "Paternoster Knechts", that is, soldiers of the prayer beads; commonly they were called "Malcontents", a name they assumed of their own accord; by the French they were called "blancs yeux", that is, white eyes, from which name those afflicted with an inner disease, whose eyes turn white, are also called.

units.la: MaLe Content IInCVnCtanter CVnCtaeXIgVnt.
units.tr: Malecontents demand everything without ceasing.

units.la: Gandauenses de hac iniuria grauiter apud Archiducem & Consilium queruntur, iussi vt rationem militibus satisfaciendi ineant, contributionem detrectant, sed petulantem militem conducentes cum Malecontentis velitantur, crebrius varia fortuna, & aliquando victores Walones persequuntur, & Glayonii vxorem secum abducunt, & cum Montignii vexillo, quod ceperant, terram verrent. Quem contemptum Malecontenti Duce Montignio vlturi Flandriam irruunt, & Meninas ad Lisam fluuium capiunt & muniunt.
units.tr: The Gandavians complain bitterly of this wrong before the Archduke and the Council. Ordered to make arrangements to pay the soldiers, they refuse the levy. Instead they hire unruly troops and skirmish with the Malecontents, with varying fortune. At times they defeat the Walloons and pursue them, carry off the wife of Glayon, and, with Montigny's standard which they had captured, sweep the ground. The Malecontents, eager to avenge this insult under Duke Montigny, invade Flanders and seize and fortify Menen on the River Lys.

units.la: Gandauenses irritati necant duos captiuos, Hesselium Consiliarium consilii sanguinarii ab Albano instituti, & Vissium, sine praemonitione & lata ante sententia, de arbore eos suspendentes, & barbas eorum praescissas pileis suis imponentes.
units.tr: The enraged Gandavians kill two prisoners, Hessel, a councillor of the bloody council set up by Alva, and Vis. They hang them from a tree without warning and without any sentence first being pronounced, and they cut off their beards and place them on their own caps.

units.la: Io. Casimiri exercitus cum fines Belgii attigisset, procedere noluit, nisi pecunia daretur (Pecuniae deerant propter Artesiensium & Hannonienfium defectionem, qui nihil conferre voluerunt.) Sic factum vt serius ad Ordinum castra pertingeret. Post tres menses, quum vnius mensis stipendium accepissent, procedit exercitus Ordinum, vt Alenzonio iungatur, & Austriacum ad pugnam eliciat. Sed is se castris continet.
units.tr: When the army of John Casimir reached the borders of the Netherlands, it refused to advance unless it was paid. (The money was short because of the defection of the Artois and Hainault provinces, which would contribute nothing.) So it happened that it reached the camp of the States later than it should have. After three months, when they had received one month's pay, the army of the States set out to join Alençon and to draw the Austrian out to battle. But he kept himself within his camp.

units.la: Alenzonius Bingium & alias vrbeculas capit, quod Casimiri exercitus ei non iungeretur (Erat enim zelotypia quaedam inter Alenzonium & Casimirum) & loca idonea, quibus aegroti milites reficerentur, non haberet, militem dimittit, qui Malecontentis deinde militat.
units.tr: Alençon took Binche and other small towns, because Casimir's army did not join him. (There was some jealousy between Alençon and Casimir.) Lacking suitable places where his sick soldiers could recover, he dismissed the soldiers, who then served the Malecontents.

units.la: Quum pecunia deesset, & aliae difficultates apparerent, Ordinum exercitus a Boffumo & Lanoio abhoste in commodiora loca deducitur.
units.tr: When money ran short and other difficulties arose, the army of the States was led by Boffumo and Lanoy to more convenient quarters, away from the enemy.

units.la: Io. Austriacus moritur vel peste, vel animi moerore, 1. Octobr. Corpus Namurcum, & post in Hispaniam defertur.
units.tr: John of Austria died on 1 October, either of the plague or of mental anguish. His body was taken to Namur and afterwards conveyed to Spain.

units.la: Escouedus eius Secretarius & Consiliarius in itinere versus Hispaniam à duobus sclopetariis interimitur.
units.tr: Escovedo, his secretary and councillor, was killed by two arquebusiers on the journey towards Spain.

units.la: Ordines frustra moliuntur Atrebato potiri.
units.tr: The States attempt in vain to seize Arras.

units.la: Nota Sebastiani Lusitaniæ Regis expeditionem in Bar-bariam. Interierunt uno die tres Reges : Sebastianus in acie : Mahometus ( quem Sebastianus in Regnum reducere voluit ) in flumine : Muleius Malucus , qui oppugnabatur, exesu lactis in ardore, obtenta iam victoria. Et in uno tentorio tria Regia feretra ponebantur.
units.tr: Note the expedition of Sebastian, King of Portugal, into Barbary. Three kings died on one day: Sebastian in battle; Mahomet, whom Sebastian wanted to restore to his kingdom, in a river; and Muley Malluch, who was under attack, worn out by the heat, though victory was already won. And in one tent three royal coffins were placed.

units.la: ALEXANDER FARNESIVS DVX PARMENSIS GVBERNATOR BELGII.
units.tr: ALEXANDER FARNESE, DUKE OF PARMA, GOVERNOR OF THE NETHERLANDS.

units.la: M.D.LXXIX. Auraicus volente Matthia, & Consilio Status, Legatus venit, & dissidia ac turbas apud Gandauos sedat, agitque ut Gandauenses etiam Catholicam religionem ibi relinquant, & bona Ecclesiastica Papistis reddant, & pecuniam Ordinibus conferant, generalibus se adiungant, &c. Ut pareant, ab Antuerpiensibus proceribus Belgis, Bruxellensibus, & Legatis Reg. Angliæ monentur. Reconciliantur itaque Gandauenses, & pacem religionis recipiunt, & componuntur articuli quidam conditionales.
units.tr: In 1579, with Matthias willing and the Council of State consenting, the envoy of Orange came and settled the quarrels and disturbances among the people of Ghent. He worked to make the Ghent people also leave the Catholic religion there, to return the ecclesiastical goods to the Papists, to contribute money to the Estates, and to join the general union, etc. To make them comply, they were admonished by the Antwerp nobles, the Belgian nobles, the people of Brussels, and the envoys of the King of England. The Ghent people were therefore reconciled, accepted the peace of religion, and certain conditional articles were agreed upon.

units.la: Walones pacem prorsus respuunt.
units.tr: The Walloons utterly rejected the peace.

units.la: Gandauenses questi, Ecclesiasticos fœdus rupisse, ideoq; eos urbe pellunt, & religionis pacem rumpunt, 9. Martii, auctore Imbyfio & sectatoribus.
units.tr: The Ghentish complained that the churchmen had broken the covenant, and therefore they drove them out of the city on 9 March, at the instigation of Imbyse and his followers, and broke the peace of religion.

units.la: Ioh. Casimirus in Angliam abit. Eius milites è Belgio discedunt.
units.tr: John Casimir went off to England. His soldiers left the Netherlands.

units.la: Parmensis 8. Ianuarii arcem Carpensem expugnat, & cum exercitu Antuerpiam pergit. Obsidione cingit Traiectum inferius videlicet Mastricum.
units.tr: On 8 January Parma stormed the citadel of Carpen and marched with his army to Antwerp. He laid siege to Maastricht, that is, Lower Traiectum.

units.la: Montignius & Malecontenti fœdus cum Motteo nomine Regis Hispani iungunt. Artesia & Hannonia Regi Hisp. conciliantur. Ordines Maastrichio subuenire non valent, ideo Parmensis id expugnat, 29. Iunii in festo Petri. Vehementer obsessi se defenderunt, cum etiam mulieres operas praestarent. Sed cum continue vrgerentur, & somnum caperet vellent, Hispani aggeres superant, & in vrbem irrepunt, ac obuios quosque cedunt.
units.tr: Montigny and the Malcontents made a league with Motte in the name of the King of Spain. Artois and Hainault were reconciled to the King of Spain. The States could not bring help to Maastricht, so Parma took it on 29 June, the feast of St Peter. The besieged defended themselves fiercely, the women too lending their services. But when they were pressed without pause, and wished to take some sleep, the Spaniards surmounted the ramparts, crept into the town and cut down everyone they met.

units.la: Interea institutus fuit Procerum Conuentus Coloniae, & per Caesaris & multorum Principum Legatos tractatum de pace. Caesariani articulos pacificationis Ordinibus proponunt, quos vide in Meterano.
units.tr: Meanwhile an assembly of nobles was held at Cologne, and through the envoys of the Emperor and of many princes a treaty of peace was discussed. The Imperialists put forward articles of pacification to the States; see them in Meteren.

units.la: Ordines Prouinciarum sententias super his requirunt.
units.tr: The provincial States asked for their opinions on these matters.

units.la: Acta Lugduni Batauorum typis expressa sunt.
units.tr: The proceedings were printed at Leiden.

units.la: Imbysius Gandaui tumultuatur.
units.tr: Imbyse stirred up a tumult at Ghent.

units.la: Imbysius & socii 14. articulos edunt, quare Auraicus Gadauum venire non debeat. Contra trium membrorum ciuitatis consilio 5. articuli facti, quos Auraicus, si in vrbem veniat, se seruaturum iurare debeat.
units.tr: Imbyse and his associates published fourteen articles giving reasons why Auraicus ought not to come to Ghent. Against this, five articles were drawn up by the council of the three members of the city, which Auraicus must swear to observe if he came into the town.

units.la: Gandauenses computant, quantum contribuerint, potuisse in Regione Flandrica ad 30. tonnas auri colligi.
units.tr: The Ghentish reckoned how much they had contributed, and it was calculated that some thirty tons of gold could have been raised in the region of Flanders.

units.la: Ordines videntes, quod Parmensis distractionem confoederatorum moliretur, & quod Malecontenti perniciem reformatorum vnice quaerent, denuo foedus renouant Traiecti. Articuli compositi 26. Ianuarii.
units.tr: The States, seeing that Parma was plotting to break up the confederates, and that the Malcontents were seeking only the destruction of the Reformed, renewed their league again at Utrecht. The articles were agreed on 26 January.

units.la: Casimiro iam in Angliam profecto, equites eius omnes cum literis salui conducti Parmensis e Belgio discedunt.
units.tr: Casimir having now gone to England, all his horsemen were safely escorted out of the Netherlands by Parma's letters.

units.la: Deinceps multi confoederatorum paulatim ad Parmensem incipiunt deficere.
units.tr: After this, many of the confederates gradually began to desert to Parma.

units.la: Auraicus Gandauum venit, senatum insolito more creatum remouet.
units.tr: Auraicus came to Ghent and removed the senate, which had been created in an unusual manner.

units.la: Imbysius discessit, & in Frankenthal ditionis Ioh. Casimiri Palatini ad Dathenum insignem Reformatorum concionatorem, cui multa harum turbarum adscripta imputataque fuerunt, concessit.
units.tr: Imbyse left, and went to Frankenthal in the territory of John Casimir the Palatine, to Dathenus, the famous preacher of the Reformed, to whom much of these troubles was ascribed and imputed.

units.la: Malecontenti oppidum Mosense capiunt. Parmensis ex contracontractu, extraneos milites extra Walonum Malecontento- rum Prouincias abire iubet. Haec res etiam Mechlinienses ad defectionem ab Ordinibus pellexit.
units.tr: The Malcontents took the town of Mouzon. Parma, by a counter-move, ordered foreign soldiers to leave the provinces of the Walloon Malcontents. This affair also enticed the people of Mechelen to desert the States.

units.la: Ordinum milites Malecontentis Menenias noctu, astu admunt, inde Workum expugnant. Vide pulchrum stratagema.
units.tr: Soldiers of the States took Menen by stealth at night from the Malcontents, and from there they stormed Workum. See the fine stratagem.

units.la: Rennebergius Ordinum in Frisia praefectus Groningenses, vt in officio maneant, hortatur. Sed quum se grauari ab eo quererentur, militem conduxerunt, ita vt Rennebergius vrbem obsidione cinxerit, eamque deinde 10. Iunii ceperit. Idem etiam Couerdam munit.
units.tr: Rennenberg, the commander of the States in Friesland, urged the Groningers to remain loyal. But when they complained that they were being oppressed by him, they hired soldiers, so that Rennenberg surrounded the city with a siege, and then took it on 10 June. He also fortified Coevorden.

units.la: Rustici ibi Desperati dicti male tractantur.
units.tr: The peasants there, called the Desperate, are treated badly.

units.la: Cum in tractatione Coloniensi pax constitui non potuit, consultatum est Gandaui ab Ordinibus, quid porro sibi faciendum esse putarent. Ibi Auraicus typis edit consilium, & iudicium suum super 4. articulos. Sept.
units.tr: When no peace could be settled at the Cologne negotiations, the States consulted at Ghent about what they thought ought to be done next. There Auraicus published in print his counsel and judgment on four articles, in September.

units.la: I. Pacem cum Hispano citra perniciem, multis adductis causis, & allatis exemplis vindictae irritatorum Regum, iniri non posse.
units.tr: (1) A peace with the Spaniard cannot be made without ruin, for many reasons adduced and examples given of the vengeance of kings who have been provoked.

units.la: II. Contributionem in administrationem belli necessariam esse.
units.tr: (2) Contributions are necessary for the conduct of the war.

units.la: III. Eligendum esse Francifcum Alenzonium, Regis Galliae fratrem in Ducem Brabantinum propter multas graues causas.
units.tr: (3) Francis Alençon, brother of the King of France, must be chosen as Duke of Brabant, for many weighty reasons.

units.la: Postremo, quomodo Prouinciae administrari possint? Nec Statibus hoc consilium displicet, & concluditur, vt Alanzonius in Principem patriae recipiatur. De his vide declarationem prolixam in Meterano.
units.tr: Finally, how can the provinces be governed? The States did not dislike this counsel, and it was concluded that Alençon should be received as Prince of the country. On these matters see the long declaration in Meteren.

units.la: M. D. LXXX. Auraicus in Hollandiam & Frisiam proficiscitur turbarum componendarum causa.
units.tr: In 1580 Auraicus set out for Holland and Friesland to calm the disturbances.

units.la: Postquam Arthefia & Hannonia, relictis reliquis Prouinciis, Regi reconciliatae, promissum exercitum instruxerunt. Parmensis principio Ianuarii iubet oppugnare Mortaniam Hannoniae vrbeculam, tribus cohortib. praesidiariorum Scotorum & Anglorum munitam.
units.tr: After Artois and Hainault, leaving the other provinces, were reconciled to the King, they drew up the army they had promised. At the beginning of January Parma ordered an attack on Mortagne, a small town of Hainault, defended by three companies of Scottish and English garrison troops.

units.la: Qua vi expugnata Fanum Amandi capit.
units.tr: Having taken it by force, he captured Saint-Amand.

units.la: Inde Tornaci & circa Insulas considet exercitus, & quidam Hispani ex pacto cum Arthesiis & Hannonienfibus Belgio cedunt.
units.tr: From there the army settled at Tournai and around the islands, and some Spaniards by agreement with the Artois and Hainault men left the Netherlands.

units.la: Bruxellenses capiunt Nouellam.
units.tr: The people of Brussels took Nivelles.

units.la: Auraicus cum Matthia Archid. Bredam abit, & ad componendas turbas in Hollandiam & Frisiam concedit.
units.tr: Auraicus went with Archduke Matthias to Breda, and withdrew to Holland and Friesland to settle the disturbances.

units.la: In Frisia Rennebergio, qui ad Hispanos defecerat, Leuarda eripitur. Mittit Rennebergius Secretarium quendam Leuardam, dum nondum capta esset, cum chartis nudis, quibus tamen nomen ipsius subscriptum fuit, vt is pro occasione rerum, nominis sui auctoritate, necessaria huc illuc perscriberet & praeciperet. Ibi is captus est, & in earum chartarum vnam coactus est scribere ad praefectum Harlingensem, vt Requikio Capitaneo Ordinum Harlingam, quam obsidebat, traderet, quod in vila Rennebergeri subscriptione continuo fecit.
units.tr: In Friesland Leeuwarden was snatched from Rennenberg, who had gone over to the Spaniards. Rennenberg sent a certain secretary to Leeuwarden, before it was taken, with blank papers bearing his own signature, so that he might write and direct whatever was needed, as the occasion arose, under the authority of his name. He was captured there, and was forced to write on one of those papers to the commander of Harlingen, telling him to surrender Harlingen, which Requesens, captain of the States, was besieging; and this he did at once, under the signature of Rennenberg, which was entirely false.

units.la: In Frisia imaginēs passim deturbantur.
units.tr: In Friesland images are pulled down everywhere.

units.la: Mechlinia ab Ordinibus capitur. Cum enim anno 1579. instigatore potissimum Petro Lupo Monacho, consentiente Bourfio vrbis Gubernatore, Matthia Archid. & Auriaco frustra eos dehortantibus, adscito milite Parmensē, ab Ordinibus defecissent, ibi anno 1580. Aprili Noricius Tempelæus, & Carolus Lieuinus tribuni, cum Anglis Mechliniam summo mane pluribus locis inuadunt, in foro maxima ciuium & religiosorum turba, inter quos & Lupus ille fortissime pugnans, cadit.
units.tr: Mechelen was taken by the States. For in 1579, at the instigation chiefly of Peter Wolf, a monk, with the consent of Bours, governor of the city, and although Archduke Matthias and Orange had tried in vain to dissuade them, they had defected from the States after taking in Parma's soldiers. Then in April 1580, the tribunes Noricius Tempelaer and Charles Lievens, with the English, attacked Mechelen early in the morning in several places. In the market-place there was a great crowd of citizens and of the religious, among whom that Wolf, fighting most bravely, fell.

units.la: Dici non potest, quam miserabiliter Angli omnia ad multos dies deuastarint. Fuit hæc ab illa, quæ facta est anno 1572. direptione, vastatio altera & sæuior huius ciuitatis.
units.tr: It cannot be told how miserably the English laid waste everything for many days. This devastation was a second and more savage one of this city, after the plunder of 1572.

units.la: 6. Aprilis circa vesperam toto Belgio ingens fuit terræ motus, qui Colonia Lutetias vsque & vlterius in Angliam Eboracum vsque peruasit, ipsum mare concussum, tanquam ex abysso eleuatum, cum tamen tranquillum nulla aura commoueretur, tellus bis tanto terrore quassata, vt templorum & turrium lapides passim diffissi, labefactati & excussi fuerint.
units.tr: On 6 April, about evening, there was a huge earthquake throughout the whole of the Netherlands, which spread from Cologne as far as Paris and further, even to York in England; the sea itself was shaken, as though lifted up out of the abyss, although it was calm and no breeze stirred; the earth was shaken twice with such terror that the stones of churches and towers were split, loosened and knocked down in many places.

units.la: Lanonius obsidens Engelmunster, quam Malecontenti tenuerant, in curia Marquati, qui pontem, vti iussus erat non deiecerat, à superueniente Burggrauio Gandauiensi gio vincitur, & capitur, qui deinde pro Egmundano liber dimittitur.
units.tr: Lannoy, besieging Engelmunster, which the Malcontents had held, was overcome in the manor of Marquette, because he had not thrown down the bridge as he had been ordered. He was overwhelmed by the Burgrave of Ghent, who came up, and was captured; he was afterwards released free on Egmont's terms.

units.la: Ordines capiunt Diestum, Sichemum & Arschotum, oppida.
units.tr: The States took Diest, Sichem and Aarschot, towns.

units.la: Niuella à Parmensi capta.
units.tr: Nieuwpoort was taken by Parma.

units.la: Mater Parmensis in Belgium ad filium venit vt ibi præesset, sed frustra.
units.tr: Parma's mother came into the Netherlands to her son, to preside there, but in vain.

units.la: Anna Philippi Regis Hispan. vxor Maximiliani Imp. filia moritur, superstite Philippo vnico filio, tunc circiter annum nato.
units.tr: Anne, daughter of Philip, King of Spain and wife of the Emperor Maximilian, died, leaving Philip, her only son, then about a year old.

units.la: Dominus de Selles per stratagema capitur in oppido Bonchan, quod paulo post Malecontenti, cum ipsis promissa proditio pessime successisset, obsident & deditione capiunt. Selles in captiuitate moritur.
units.tr: Lord de Selles was taken by a stratagem in the town of Bouchain. Soon afterwards, when the betrayal promised to them had gone very badly, the Malcontents besieged it and took it by surrender. Selles died in captivity.

units.la: Ordines mittunt proceres, qui cum Alanzonio, vt Dux sit Belgii, paciscantur.
units.tr: The States sent nobles, who negotiated with Alençon that he should be Duke of the Netherlands.

units.la: Matthias Archid. videns se à multis Prouinciis, Walonibus potissimum, & Belgas ab Imperio & aliis deseri, Ordinibus gubernaculum, ad quod vocatus erat, resignat, & sequenti anno è Belgio discedit.
units.tr: Archduke Matthias, seeing that he was being deserted by many provinces, chiefly the Walloons, and by the Netherlanders, who were deserting him for the Empire and others, resigned to the States the government to which he had been called, and the following year left the Netherlands.

units.la: Conduntur leges militares in Belgio.
units.tr: Military laws were established in the Netherlands.

units.la: Franciscus Draco, postquam totum orbem terrarum circumnauigasset, cum magnis opibus post triennium in Angliam redit, & Eques Auratus creatur.
units.tr: Francis Drake, after he had sailed round the whole globe, returned to England after three years with great riches, and was created a Knight.

units.la: In Frisia Rennebergius obsidet Steinbek, & obsidio sequenti Februario soluitur.
units.tr: In Friesland Rennenberg besieged Steenbergen, and the siege was lifted the following February.

units.la: Miles quidam Germanicus propius ad repagulum Waltportæ accedens, Deum dire blasphemat, & Hohenloio & Ordinibus conuitia dicit. Sed voce bene obseruata quidam præsidiarius in tenebris collimat, & globo linguam illius petit, vltione diuina in blasphemum.
units.tr: A certain German soldier, coming nearer to the barrier of the Waltport gate, blasphemed God dreadfully and hurled insults at Hohenlohe and the States. But a garrison soldier, having carefully marked the voice in the darkness, aimed and shot a bullet at the blasphemer's tongue, a divine vengeance upon the blasphemer.

units.la: Nota. Epistolas Schenkii, Rennebergii & Conputi mutuas, ludicras & mordaces.
units.tr: Note: the mutual letters of Schenk, Rennenberg and Conputus, playful and biting.

units.la: Concertatio inter Philip. Hispan. & Antonium, de Regno Portugalliæ illo hunc expellente.
units.tr: Contest between Philip of Spain and Antonio over the kingdom of Portugal, the former expelling the latter.

units.la: Albanus moritur Lisbonæ 17. Decembris ætatis 79. cum ad Portugalliam prorsus domandam sese accinxisset.
units.tr: Alba dies at Lisbon on 17 December, aged 79, just as he had girded himself to subdue Portugal completely.

units.la: Hispanus Auraicum proscribit tanquam hæreticum, perfidum, turbarum Belgii auctorem, & Christiani orbis pestem, & promittit 25. M. coronatorum, & nobilitationem illi, qui eum occiderit, Iulio mense. Auraicus contra acrem Apologiam edit, Ordines eundem etiam vehementer excusant & commendant.
units.tr: The Spaniard proscribes Orange as a heretic, a traitor, the author of the troubles of the Netherlands and a pest of the Christian world, and in July promises 25,000 crowns and nobility to whoever kills him. Orange publishes a sharp Apology, and the States also vigorously excuse and commend him.

units.la: Moritur Orosbek Episcopus Leodiensis, in cuius locum eligitur Ernestus Bauarus. 28. Decembris.
units.tr: Orosbek, Bishop of Liège, dies, and Ernest of Bavaria is elected in his place, 28 December.

units.la: M.D.LXXXI, Bruxellis tumultus à Papistis excitatur, ideo exercitium Papisticæ Religionis ibi suspenditur, & sistitur, publico edicto, & expurgantur templa à reliquis fictitiis Diuorum. Idem fit Antuerpiæ, mense Maio.
units.tr: In 1581 at Brussels a tumult is stirred up by the Papists, so the exercise of the Papist religion there is suspended and stopped by public edict, and the temples are cleansed of the remaining fictitious images of the saints. The same happens at Antwerp in May.

units.la: Collegiati opificum Antuerp. petunt quædam altaria è summo templo auferri, quod & obtinent à Magistratu, & exercitium Religionis Papist. tantum in duobus locis permittitur.
units.tr: The collegiates of the Antwerp workers ask that some altars be removed from the high church; they obtain this from the magistrate, and the exercise of the Papist religion is permitted in only two places.

units.la: Parmensis in Fliesslingenses machinationes non procedunt.
units.tr: Parma's machinations against Flushing do not succeed.

units.la: In Frisia arx Stanera à Sanoyo capta & euersa.
units.tr: In Friesland the fortress of Stanera is taken and overthrown by Sanoy.

units.la: Nieuortius à parte Statuum loca munita Rennebergio cedere cogitur, verum Noricius Rennebergium postea vincit, fugatq; Iul.
units.tr: Nieuwort, on the side of the States, is forced to yield his fortified places to Rennenberg; but Noricius afterwards defeats Rennenberg and routs him, July.

units.la: Rennebergius moritur phthisi, ex dolore animi contracta, quod olim à Statibus defecisset. Ei suffectus est à Parmensi Iaspar spar Verdugo, qui Noritium temere confligentem magna pugna, & multis caesis vincit. Idem frustra obsidet Niuezio-lam.
units.tr: Rennenberg dies of consumption, brought on by grief of mind because he had once defected from the States. In his place Parma appoints Jaspar Verdugo, who, when Noricius rashly engages him, defeats him in a great battle with many slain. The same man besieges Niuezio-lam in vain.

units.la: Iselhemius à Schenkio ante Goram cum suis capitur.
units.tr: Iselhemius is captured with his men by Schenk before Gorcum.

units.la: Seditiones militum in Brabantia, ob non numerata stipendia.
units.tr: Mutinies of soldiers in Brabant, because their wages had not been paid.

units.la: Ordines Regem omni suo iure, quod in Prouincias Belgicas habebat, excidisse declarant, sigillaque eius omnia ac insignia frangunt: Idque ob innumeras causas, 26. Iulii.
units.tr: The States declare that the King has lost every right he had in the Belgic provinces, and they break all his seals and insignia, for innumerable causes, 26 July.

units.la: Et Alenzonius declaratur Princeps Belgarum.
units.tr: And Alençon is declared Prince of the Belgians.

units.la: Annus is continetur in his verbis :
units.tr: The year is contained in these words:

units.la: EXIMVnt BeLgae DeIVgosVIse, RegIs IberI.
units.tr: THE BELGIANS BREAK FREE FROM THE YOKE OF THE IBERIAN KING.

units.la: Teneremunda obsessa, & expugnata.
units.tr: Tenremunde is besieged and taken by storm.

units.la: Auraici ad Ordines oratio. Vide Historiam.
units.tr: Orange's speech to the States. See the History.

units.la: FRANCISCVS HERCVLES DVX ANDEGAVENSIS, PRINCEPS STATVVM.
units.tr: FRANCIS HERCULES, DUKE OF ANJOU, PRINCE OF THE PROVINCES.

units.la: Breda Auraici Propria Ciuitas, cum arce egregia, proditione praesidiariorum noctu à Malecontentis capitur vastaturque, pube Ciuium ingenti caesa. Lindanus extemplo Iesuitas eo collocat. Malecontenti in Brabantia 70. currus spoliant.
units.tr: Breda, the native city of Orange, with its splendid citadel, was taken at night by the Malcontents through the treachery of the garrison and laid waste, with a great slaughter of the townsmen. Lindanus at once posted Jesuits there. The Malcontents in Brabant plundered seventy wagons.

units.la: Status contra capiunt Endehofen, & Gisslai, quae tamen à Malecontentis rursus recuperantur.
units.tr: The States took Endhoven and Gheertruidenberg instead, though these were soon recovered by the Malcontents.

units.la: Parma obsidet, & demum obtinet Dornek tolerabilibus conditionibus.
units.tr: Parma besieged Dorn and at last obtained it on tolerable terms.

units.la: Postquam Anoyus gubernator Cameraci, Ordinum consensu, & metu potentiae Parmensis, superiore anno cum Alenzonio transegisset, & Gallum militem praesidio accepisset: Parmensis metuens ne Gallus ibi sedem stabilem figeret, omnibus modis Cameracum obsidere conatur. Itaque intercepto commeatu omni ad summam inopiam Cameracenses adegit. Nota Exemsta ad eum Senatum pro iisdem scribunt, atque incercedunt. Sed Senatus hoc denegat prætendens, pacem illam religionis Augustanam Confessionem tantum in iis locis concessisse, in quibus locis tempore pacis illius initæ in vsu fuit: Coloniæ autem eam tunc in vsu non fuisse.
units.tr: After Anjou, governor of Cambrai, had made a treaty with the Duke of Alençon the year before, with the consent of the States and out of fear of Parma's power, and had received a French garrison, Parma, afraid that the French would establish a permanent base there, tried by every means to besiege Cambrai. Having intercepted all supplies, he reduced the people of Cambrai to extreme want. The people of Nijmegen wrote to the Senate on their behalf and interceded. But the Senate refused this, alleging that the peace had granted the Augsburg Confession only in those places where it was in use at the time the peace was made, and that it had not been in use at Cologne at that time.

units.la: Gebhardus Truchsesius. Archiepiscopus Coloniensis ad Comitia Augustana non venit. Itaque Capitulum misit Fridericum Saxoniæ, & Lawenburgi Ducem Chorepiscopum. Episcopus hoc indigne ferens, etiam suos eo mittit, qui tentent an possent obtinere, vt Gebhardus matrimonium contrahere absque iactura Archiepiscopatus posset. Sed nihil est effectum.
units.tr: Gebhard Truchsess, Archbishop of Cologne, did not come to the Diet of Augsburg. The chapter therefore sent Frederick of Saxony, Duke of Lauenburg, as coadjutor. The bishop, taking this ill, also sent men of his own there to try whether he could obtain that Gebhard might contract marriage without losing the archbishopric. But nothing was achieved.

units.la: Gebhardus Episcopus ex Westphalia Bonnam venit. Sed ægre est admissus, quia cum comitatu venit, is milites quoque in sui protectionem sibi adiungit.
units.tr: Gebhard, bishop, came from Westphalia to Bonn. But he was admitted with difficulty, because he came with a retinue, and he also brought soldiers with him for his own protection.

units.la: Altercatum est de possessione clauium Ciuitatis. Episcopus militem in vicinia Bonnæ aluit, à quibus ciues sibi metuebant.
units.tr: There was a dispute over possession of the keys of the city. The bishop maintained soldiers in the neighbourhood of Bonn, which made the citizens fear for themselves.

units.la: Gregor. XIII. P. datis amicis literis, Episcopum ab incepto dehortatur.
units.tr: Pope Gregory XIII, by sending friendly letters, urged the bishop to abandon his undertaking.

units.la: Dux Iohannes Palat. Bipont. Bonnam ad Episcopum venit promoturus negotium eius apud Capitulum.
units.tr: Duke John Palatine of Zweibrücken came to Bonn to the bishop, intending to advance his cause with the chapter.

units.la: M. D. LXXXIII. Capitulum multa de Episcopo queruntur, eumque à proposito auocare studént. Dehortatur eundem Cæsar, ad quem se Episcopus excusat.
units.tr: In 1583 the chapter complained much about the bishop and strove to turn him from his purpose. The emperor also urged him to give it up, and the bishop excused himself to the emperor.

units.la: Intercesserunt apud Capitulum etiam Electores seculares.
units.tr: The secular electors also interceded with the chapter.

units.la: Die constituto 28. Ianuarii misit Episcopus ad conuentum Capituli Comitem Solmensem, Wittingensem, & Krichingensem. Solmensis in consessu Capitulares hortatur, vt Episcopo morem gerant, & seuerius loquitur. Altero die Iohannes Palatinus Bip. in eodem consessu idem postulat. Sed Capitulares die 1. Februarii contra Episcopum concludunt. Et sic Principes Colonia discedunt.
units.tr: On the appointed day, 28 January, the bishop sent to the assembly of the chapter the Counts of Solms, Wittgenstein and Krichingen. Solms urged the members of the chapter to comply with the bishop, and spoke rather harshly. On the next day John Palatine made the same demand in the same assembly. But on 1 February the members of the chapter resolved against the bishop. And so the princes left Cologne.

units.la: Interim Episcopus curauit, sibi matrimonio copulari per Ministrum Iohannis Palatini Bonnae in aedibus Kriechingensis Agnetem Mansfeldicam. Et sic Publico Scripto Clero matrimonium, & populo libertatem religionis permisit.
units.tr: Meanwhile the bishop arranged to be married to Agnes of Mansfeld in the house of the Count of Krichingen at Bonn, by a minister of John Palatine. And so by public writing he allowed the clergy to marry and the people liberty of religion.

units.la: Interea Capitulares Friderico illo Saxone Duce occupaverunt Episcopatus quaedam praecipua loca, vt Bruel, Kaiserswerd, &c.
units.tr: Meanwhile the members of the chapter, by means of that Saxon duke Frederick, seized certain principal places of the bishopric, such as Brühl, Kaiserswerth, and others.

units.la: Dicebatur Parmensis cum exercitu aduentare, ideo Elector & caeteri Bonna discedunt Dillebergam.
units.tr: It was rumoured that Parma was approaching with an army, so the elector and the others left Bonn for Dillenburg.

units.la: Habitus super negotio hoc Episcopi Conuentus Wormatiae.
units.tr: A convention at Worms was held on this matter of the bishop.

units.la: Summus Pontifex Episcopum excommunicat, & Episcopatu deiicit, & dignitatibus priuat, aliumque Episcopum eligi mandat Aprili.
units.tr: The supreme Pontiff excommunicated the bishop, deposed him from the bishopric and deprived him of his dignities, and ordered another bishop to be elected in April.

units.la: Hinc apertum bellum oritur.
units.tr: From this open war arose.

units.la: Comes Ifenbergius Salentinus, qui prius Archiepiscopatum ducta vxore resignauerat, ex parte Capituli Dux belli fuit. Engelbertus von der Lipp pro Gebhardo militauit.
units.tr: Count Johann of Isenburg-Grenzau, who had earlier resigned the archbishopric when he married, was the commander in war on the side of the chapter. Engelbert von der Lippe fought on behalf of Gebhard.

units.la: Electores a Caesare petunt, curet, vt Hispani ex partibus & terris Imperii amandentur. Caesar iubet vtramque partem ab armis discedere.
units.tr: The electors asked the emperor to see to it that the Spaniards were removed from the regions and lands of the Empire. The emperor ordered both parties to lay down their arms.

units.la: Omnes agnati & cognati, inter quos & mater fuit, Episcopum monent & orant, vt a proposito discedat: quibus ipse respondet, se pium opus caepisse, & se pro promouenda gloria Dei non solum vniuersas suas opes, verum etiam sanguinem impensurum.
units.tr: All the agnates and kinsmen, among whom was his mother, warned and begged the bishop to abandon his purpose. To them he replied that he had undertaken a pious work, and that for the advancement of the glory of God he would expend not only all his resources but even his blood.

units.la: Priore nuncio Apostolico, qui Coloniam ire volebat, a Iohanne Casimiro in ipsius ditione impedito, venit alter. Iohan. Casimirus detinet. Andreas Austriacum Cardinalem Ferdinandi Euipontani filium, & se propterea ad Caesarem excusat.
units.tr: When the first papal nuncio, who wanted to go to Cologne, was hindered in John Casimir's territory, another came. John Casimir detained him. Andreas, the Austrian cardinal, son of Ferdinand of Innsbruck, and on that account excused himself to the emperor.

units.la: Conuocati, qui ius eligendi Episcopum habent, die 22. Maii, & eligitur in Episcopum Colonienfem Ernestus Dux Bauaria eligitur in Episcop. Coloniens.
units.tr: The men who have the right of electing a bishop were summoned on 22 May, and Ernest, Duke of Bavaria, was elected Bishop of Cologne.

units.la: R Dux Bauariæ, Gebhardus Capitulum, ne alium eligant, hortatur. Idem faciunt Iohan. Casimirus & Iohannes Palatini.
units.tr: The Duke of Bavaria, and Gebhard, exhorted the chapter not to elect another. John Casimir and John Palatine did the same.

units.la: Senatus Colon. innumeros ciues ordinant, qui Ciuitatem, ne seditio aut incursus militaris existat, tueantur.
units.tr: The Senate of Cologne appointed countless citizens to guard the city, so that no sedition or military attack should arise.

units.la: Legatus Apostolicus Solmensem & Winnebergensem, Capitulares Colon. vt hæreticos excommunicat.
units.tr: The papal legate excommunicated the Counts of Solms and Wittgenstein and the members of the Cologne chapter as heretics.

units.la: Nauarræus Segurium ad Principes Protestantes Germaniæ mittit, vt fœdus ineatur pro causa Belgarum & Coloniensi.
units.tr: Navarrese sent Segur to the Protestant princes of Germany, so that an alliance might be made for the cause of the Belgians and for the cause of Cologne.

units.la: Petrus Beutrichius, qui apud Iohan-Casimirū fuit, Vascones adducit, incenditur oppidum & Collegium in Deutschè Regione Coloniæ.
units.tr: Peter Beutrich, who had been with John Casimir, brought in Gascons; a town and a college in the German region of Cologne were set on fire.

units.la: Ioh. Casimirus cum copioso exercitu Bonnæ appulit, & ibi in vicinia pagos & arces spoliauit.
units.tr: John Casimir with a large army landed at Bonn, and there in the neighbourhood he plundered villages and fortresses.

units.la: Cæsar Casimiro & Gebhardo mandat, vt à bello discedant.
units.tr: The emperor ordered Casimir and Gebhard to withdraw from the war.

units.la: Habetur conuentus Francoforti, vt Ernestus & Truchses conciliarentur. Demum Truchses petit, vt Electoralis dignitas vna cum Westphalia sibi dum vixerit relinquatur, Ernesto vero Principi titulus Archiepiscopi, & quæ nunc occupet oppida & loca; alias se Martis aleam subiturum.
units.tr: A meeting was held at Frankfurt so that Ernest and Truchsess might be reconciled. At last Truchsess asked that the electoral dignity, together with Westphalia, be left to him for as long as he lived, and that Ernest have only the title of archbishop, and keep whatever towns and places he now occupied; otherwise he would take his chance in the game of war.

units.la: Imperat: Carolo Truchses. & Neuenario mandat, vt loca & clenodia ad Episcopatum pertinentia Ernesto restituant.
units.tr: The emperor ordered Charles Truchsess and Neuenar to restore to Ernest the places and treasures belonging to the bishopric.

units.la: Ioh-Casimirus deficiente etiam pecunia suos dimittit, & mortuo fratre Ludouico Elector. Heidelbergens. domum properat.
units.tr: John Casimir, as money also failed, dismissed his men, and on the death of his brother Louis the Elector Palatine he hastened home.

units.la: Vascones in Veltkirchen combusti, cæsi.
units.tr: The Gascons were burnt and slain at Veltkirchen.

units.la: Ferdinandus Ernesti frater occupat Popelsdorf, & obsidet Godesbergarcem vicinam.
units.tr: Ferdinand, brother of Ernest, occupied Poppelsdorf and besieged the nearby fortress of Godesberg.

units.la: Newenar præsidiis munit arces Bedberg & Huls. Hanc Chorepiscopus Saxo obsidet. Sed Truchsesianis Newenario & EdelHenrich aduentantibus, editur ibi prælium, cæsis Ernestianis Valonibus. Godesberg pulvere tormentario subiecto atque incenso disiicitur, deinde duro assultu demum occupatur, caesis, praeter paucos, omnibus.
units.tr: Neuenar fortified the castles of Bedburg and Hülchrath with garrisons. The Saxon coadjutor besieged the latter. But when Truchsessian forces under Neuenar and Edelheim arrived, a battle was fought there, and the Ernestian Walloons were slain. Godesberg was taken by a charge: gunpowder was laid under it and set alight, and it was thrown down; then after a hard assault it was at last occupied, all the defenders being slain except a few.

units.la: Bonna ab Ernesto obsessa.
units.tr: Bonn was besieged by Ernest.

units.la: Bonnenses praesidiarii milites capiunt Carolum Truchsesium Ducem suum & Capitaneum, & paucos alios, & tradunt eum & urbem Bonnam Ernesto, acceptis 4. M. coronatorum, & Carolus in Popelsdorff abductus est.
units.tr: The garrison soldiers of Bonn seized Charles Truchsess, their duke and captain, with a few others, and handed him and the city of Bonn over to Ernest, having received 4,000 crowns; and Charles was led away to Poppelsdorf.

units.la: Nota. Iussus est Ernesti Bombardarius ad nauim Archiepiscopale, quae Bonnae iuxta urbis moenia in Rheni littore stabat, collimare, eamque in profundum deiicere. Tormenti ictum de industria direxit in aedes, quas habitabat Carolus Truchsesius. Erant autem illae, Telonium, hoc ictu globus tres muros perforauit, & recta in Caroli cubile penetrauit, in quo ipsius ensem ad lectum pendentem medium fregit, & cuspidem in aduersum parietem sic adegit, & tanta vi fixit, ut amoueri postea non potuerit, in eoque memoriae causa relinquatur.
units.tr: Note: Ernest's gunner was ordered to aim at the archiepiscopal ship, which was lying at Bonn beside the city walls on the bank of the Rhine, and to sink it in the deep. He deliberately directed the shot at the house where Charles Truchsess lived. This was the custom-house. With this shot the ball pierced three walls and went straight into Charles's bedchamber, where it broke in the middle the sword hanging by his bed, and drove the point into the opposite wall with such force that it could not afterwards be removed, and it is kept there as a memorial.

units.la: Porro Scipionem militaris suae praefecturae sceptrum & insigne, medium quoque perrupit.
units.tr: Moreover, it also broke in the middle the sceptre and insignia of Scipio's military command.

units.la: Denique ex charta descriptionis Germaniae totius ad parietem appensa, omnem, in quo Gebhardus Truchsesius salutis anchoram fixerat suae, Westphaliam prorsus auulsit, secumque abstulit.
units.tr: Finally, from the chart of the whole of Germany hung on the wall, it tore away entirely Westphalia, in which Gebhard Truchsess had fixed the anchor of his safety, and carried it off with it.

units.la: Haec dum fierent, Carolus in inferiori cubiculo illi, in quo hoc accidit, subiecto versabatur, reque cognita, o, inquit, malum omen. Aliis eiaculationibus illa nauis fuit depressa.
units.tr: While these things were happening, Charles was lying in the lower room beneath the one in which this occurred; and when he learned of it he said, "Oh, bad omen." The ship was sunk by other discharges.

units.la: Postridie euentus prodigium confirmauit. Nam Garolus a suis militib. captus, & Ernesto traditus est die Carolo Magno sacra.
units.tr: The next day the event confirmed the portent. For Charles was captured by his soldiers and handed over to Ernest on the day sacred to Charlemagne.

units.la: Capta Bonna, Manrichius Hispanus duos Euangelicos concionatores deprehendit, incarcerauit, & noctu colligatis manibus & pedibus in Rhenum praecipitauit, quorum alter Iohann. Northusius, mirabiliter ruptis alteris vinculis, naui inlit-
units.tr: When Bonn was taken, the Spaniard Manrique seized two Evangelical preachers, imprisoned them, and at night, with their hands and feet bound, threw them into the Rhine. One of them, John Northus, miraculously broke his other bonds, swam to the ship,

units.la: in littore adhæsit, vbi dentibus cætera vincula exoluens in terram ad salices appendens, euasit & gemebundus circum mœnia obrepens vestes à quodam excubitorum deiectas accepit, ac excubias cuitans. Coloniam mane ante portam venit & intromissus est. Is deinde Heidelbergam venit, sed non optima membrorum constitutione præditus.
units.tr: and clung to the bank, where, loosing the remaining bonds with his teeth and hanging down to the ground by the willows, he escaped; and groaning, crept around the walls, took clothing that had been thrown down by a certain sentry, and avoided the guards. He came to Cologne in the morning before the gate and was admitted. He then came to Heidelberg, but was not in the best condition of body.

units.la: Ernestus ferit & capit Bedberg, Martio.
units.tr: Ernest attacks and takes Bedberg, in March.

units.la: Exercitus Truchsesii victus est ab Hispanico Ernesti exercitu, Duce Ferdinando fratre Ernesti, & captus est EdelHenrich, Martio circa Burg & Dotechem.
units.tr: The army of Truchsess was defeated by the Spanish army of Ernest, led by Duke Ferdinand, brother of Ernest, and Edelhenrich was taken, in March, near Burg and Dotechem.

units.la: Reklingenhausen traditur Ernesto.
units.tr: Rekklinghausen is surrendered to Ernest.

units.la: Gebhardus Truchses. Delphos ad Auraicum concedit, Deinde Argentoratum, vbi Capituli Decanus erat, & ibi cum vxore priuatus vixit, vbi & ipse & frater Carolus vixerunt.
units.tr: Gebhard Truchsess withdrew to Delphi on the Aur, then to Strasbourg, where he had been dean of the chapter; and there he lived deprived of office, with his wife, as did he and his brother Charles.

units.la: DE INITIO TVRBARVM BONNENSIVM SIC QVIDAM.
units.tr: ON THE BEGINNING OF THE BONN TROUBLES, AS SOME RELATE IT.

units.la: GEBHARDVS præshe quum ferret Episcopus alma, Munia qui Regum gessit in urbe trium, Aufonii vellet quod sicitare linquere Papæ, Sanctaque legitimi vincula inire tori. (Ante parum castam sueuit nam ducere vitam, Vt gens plerunque religiosa solet.) Magna fuit Iano & feruens in Principe zelus, Sancta propagandi dogmata, Christe, tua. Ergo hanc accitus rem promouisse laborat, Cui sacer antistes additus ipse fui. Illic ingresso, Fabrici, tibi, candide, dixi: Sit bona Bonna mihi, nec sit iniqua tibi. Ad templi proceres, à Præsule scripta feruntur, In quo sunt Regum condita membra trium.
units.tr: Gebhard, when he held the bishopric of the bountiful city and had served as the office of the three kings' city, wished to leave the Ausonian Pope and enter the holy bonds of lawful marriage. (For he had formerly lived a rather chaste life, as a religious people usually do.) In the prince there was great and fervent zeal for the holy doctrines of your faith, O Christ, and for spreading them. Therefore, summoned to this business, he laboured to advance it, and I myself was added to him as a sacred bishop. When I entered there, I said to you, Fabricius, my candid friend: may Bonn be good to me, and may it not be unjust to you. The writings of the Prelate are carried to the nobles of the temple, in which lie buried the bodies of the three kings.

units.la: Ut sibi concedant uxorem ducere, saluo Officio, & saluo sedis honore sua. Asserit, & castus quod Episcopus esse maritus Debeat, ex scriptis, optime Paule, tuis, Datque fidem, quod nullam haeres, de corpore partem, Ipse velit loculis appropriare suis, Velle sacerdotes se respondere fatentur, Luna peragrasset menstrua quando polum. Interea bello se accingunt, arma capessunt, Et forti subigunt oppida plura manu. Concio tunc verbi Bonna, atque Colonia in alma Intra aedes habita est plurima, nulla palam. Unus erat Sacrificulus cum Praesule vilis. Non locus est Mystis Mars ubi Regna tenet. Plurima tunc vidi, sed non ego talia vidi, Quae re, quae tali, digna fuere, loco. Nobilitas Scalium poscebat Westphala Vinum, Nam notat ingentes aurea Scala scyphos. Coena fere ad mediam protracta est uuida noctem, Prandia post medium coepta fuere diem. Hospitium diro quoddam flagrauit ab igni, Index venturi flamma erat illa mali. Ista videns Praesul: Dominus nisi moenia seruet, Ipse: vigil frustra tunc vigilabit: ait: Praesulis in magno, qua vidi cunque cubili, Fortia pro doctis arma fuere libris, Enses, bombardae, calcaria, pocula, sicae. Et iure hac manibus praetulit arma suis. Nam satis haud usquam, aut a quoquam tutus agebat, Insidiis quod erant omnia plena malis, Librorum nihil hic non ulla volumina vidi, Concordis praeter Biblia pulchra Libri. Aureus hic codex, Osiandro interprete, nuper Wirtembergensi a Principe missus erat.
units.tr: That they may be allowed to take a wife, saving their office and saving the honour of their see. He asserts, and from your writings, excellent Paul, that a bishop ought to be chaste and a husband; and he gives his word that he will not appropriate to his own purses any part of the body of the heir. The priests confess that they will reply when the moon has traversed the monthly circuit of the sky. Meanwhile they gird themselves for war, take up arms, and with a strong hand subdue many towns. Then the preaching of the Word was held at Bonn and at the nourishing Cologne, within the houses, very often, but never openly. There was one wretched little priest with the Prelate. The mysteries have no place where Mars holds the kingdom. I saw many things then, but never did I see such things as were worthy of such a place and such a company. The nobility demanded wine of Westphalia by the ladder, for the golden ladder marks huge cups. The feast was drawn out almost to the middle of the wet night; the dinners began after midday. A certain inn blazed with a dreadful fire; that flame was a sign of the coming evil. Seeing this, the Prelate said: unless the Lord keeps the walls, the watchman watches in vain, he said. In the great bedchamber of the Prelate, wherever I looked, the strong arms were placed in front of the learned books: swords, guns, spurs, cups, and daggers. And rightly did he put these arms before his own hands. For nowhere was he safe enough, or safe from anyone, since all things were full of deadly snares.
