Among the books I saw nothing here but volumes of every kind, except the fine Bibles of the Concord book. This golden codex, with Osiander as translator, had lately been sent by the Prince of Württemberg.

units.la: Obtulit hunc Præsul librum mihi deinde legendum, Legi, & eum mecum, dum fuga facta, tuli. Cur etenim propriis emerem mihi sumptibus illum, Ob quem ego sensissem tædia multa, librum. Westphale, si superas, insignis, Abele, Machaon, Salve iterum ac iterum, dulcis amice, mihi, Tu prescripsisti pulchram domino ipse diætam, Ne biberet clari plusve minusve meri. Questus es haud raro versis nullo ordine rebus, Sæpe locum monitus non habuisse tuos. Sedimus in curru, ut meminisi, & legimus hymnos, Currus & illius Præsulis ille fuit, Damonis à nobis est mentio facta maligni, Acrior eversus currus & ille fuit. En, male, dicebas Damon sibi, dicier, haud vult, Hinc est quod subita præcipitemur humo. Tuque humeros magno, & scapulas, confracta, dolore, Sensisti multas tormina longa dies. Ipse genus circum mediocrem sentio plagam, Surgimus & cæptum rursus inimus iter. Vive, vale, si vivis adhuc, carissime Abele, Non potes illius non meminisse rei. Gallus erat Belgis factus protector Alanzo, Imperium contra, fortis Ibere, tuum. Urbs est turrigeris ingens Antuerpia muris, Quæ iacet ad ripas Scaldis opime tuas. Hanc sub amicitia prætextu Gallica pubes Intrat, & infesto subdere Marte parat. Civica sed contra ruit, & rapit arma iuventus, Proque focis pugnat fæmina virgo suis. Sternitur hostis humo, vel ab urbe repellitur, at pars De muro in fossas præcipitata ruit. Fama ea cum nostras Bonna peruenit ad aures, Hæc clades, clades est mea, Præsul ait.
units.tr: The Prelate then offered me this book to read; I read it, and when flight was made I carried it off with me while it lasted. For why should I have bought that book for myself at my own expense, a book over which I had felt so much weariness? Westphalian, if you are still living, distinguished Abel, Machaon, hail again and again, my sweet friend. You yourself prescribed for the lord a fine diet, so that he might not drink more or less of the bright wine. You often complained, in no set order, that things were thrown into confusion, and you were often warned that your place was not there. We sat in the carriage, as I remember, and we read hymns; the carriage was also that of the Prelate. When the name of the wicked Damon was mentioned by us, the carriage was overturned, and it was more violent. Look, you were saying badly that Damon does not wish to be called his own; hence it is that we were suddenly thrown down to the ground. And you, with your shoulders and shoulder-blades broken, felt the long torment of many days in great pain. I myself feel a moderate wound around my hip; we rise and again enter upon the road we began. Live, farewell, if you are still alive, dearest Abel; you cannot fail to remember that event. The Frenchman had been made protector of the Belgians, Alençon, against the empire, your strength, brave Spaniard. The city is Antwerp, great with its towers, which lies on the banks of your rich Scheldt. Under the pretext of friendship the French youth enters it and prepares to subject it with hostile war. But the citizen youth rushes against them and seizes arms, and the virgin woman fights for her hearths. The enemy is laid low on the ground, or is driven back from the city; but part of them, thrown from the wall, falls headlong into the ditches. When this report reached our ears at Bonn, the Prelate said: this is a disaster, a disaster for me.

units.la: Ominis haud fallax id erat: succedere nostrasNam res est visum tunc minus atque minus.
units.tr: That was no false omen: for affairs turned out to be ever less and less favourable to us, as it then seemed.

units.la: Parmensis Masam miles superauerat amnem,Famaque, quod Bonnam vellet adire, fuit:Nos animis trepidare fugamque capessere Bonna,Et cito Westphalicas exuperare nives.
units.tr: The Parmese soldier had crossed the river Maas, and there was a rumour that he wished to approach Bonn. We, our spirits trembling, took to flight from Bonn, and quickly passed beyond the Westphalian snows.

units.la: Mox petere auxilium à Ducibus, quos Saxona tellus,Brandenburgensis, quosq; habet ora soli,Quosq; Palatina domus educat inclita gentis,Et quos Hassorum continet Aula Duces.
units.tr: Soon they sought help from the dukes whom the Saxon land, the Brandenburg, and the shore of the soil hold, and whom the illustrious Palatine house brings up of its race, and whom the court of the Hessian dukes contains.

units.la: Verborum multum, tantique probatio captiMagna, sed auxilii praesidiyq; parum.
units.tr: Much talk and a great proof of so great an enterprise, but little help and protection.

units.la: Quem lapidem solus nequeas portare, caueto,Altero ut adscito sollicitare velis.
units.tr: Beware of the stone you cannot carry alone, lest you wish to bring in another to share the burden.

units.la: Fallitur is qui spem promissa in fœdera ponit.Nil aude nisi quod perficere ipse potes.
units.tr: He is mistaken who places his hope in promised alliances. Dare nothing except what you can accomplish yourself.

units.la: Arnsperga & Brula facta est pia concio in ade,Sacra Papistarum pellere spesque fuit.
units.tr: At Arnsberg and Brühl a pious preaching was held in the temple; it was a sacred hope to drive out the Papists.

units.la: Irrita sed tenucs spes illa recessit in auras,Capta animis propera res fuit illa manu.
units.tr: But that vain and slender hope vanished into the air; that affair was taken from the minds of men by a hasty hand.

units.la: Post Dillebergam & Marpurgum venimus, illineIuimus ad patrios per loca tuta Lares.
units.tr: After Dillenburg and Marburg we came there, and by safe ways we went to our ancestral homes.

units.la: Nec mora, fulmineus Mars exardescit utrinque,Praesulis assertor Ian-Casimirus erat.
units.tr: Without delay, Mars blazed up like lightning on both sides; the defender of the bishop was John Casimir.

units.la: Ille sed est patrias subito revocatus ad urbes,Mortuus Elector cum Ludovicus erat,Gebhardo pulso, mox factus Episcopus alter,Ernestus, Bauarum quem tulit ora, fuit.
units.tr: But he was suddenly recalled to his native cities, since the Elector Ludwig had died; with Gebhard driven out, another was soon made bishop, Ernest, whom the shore of Bavaria had brought forth.

units.la: Captus ubi Comes, es Drukses, dein Carole, Bonna,Pracones verbi forte fuere duo,Hi, noctu manibus pedibusque ad terga ligatis,In Rheni tumidas precipitantur aquas.
units.tr: When the Count of Dreux was taken, then Charles, at Bonn, by chance two heralds of the Word were seized; these, at night, with hands and feet bound to their backs, were hurled into the swollen waters of the Rhine.

units.la: Alter obit, rapidis emergit fluctibus alter,Non nisi divina conseruatus ope.
units.tr: One died; the other emerged from the rushing waves, preserved by nothing but divine help.

units.la: Qui post Gebhardi praco fuit exulis, & post Intrauit muros Eiteloberga tuos. Heu mihi, quam multum profusum est sanguinis, illis, Bellona cades dum viguere, locis. Heu quam falso bonas decepit opinio mentes, Quae dederant causas ad mala tanta leues. Perfacile est cuiùs urbem percellere, at illam Rursus in integrum sistere difficile est. Verum non ideo male quod cadit, impia res est. Fine pio coepta est quae prius atque bono. Gratia sit Christo, me incendia talia quod non Vt reliquos flammis corripuere suis.
units.tr: He who after Gebhard was the herald of the exile, and after him entered your walls, Eiteloberg. Alas, how much blood was spilt there, in those places where Bellona's slaughter flourished! Alas, how falsely an opinion deceived good minds, which had given trivial causes for such great evils. It is very easy to overthrow a city, but to restore it again to its former state is difficult. Yet it is not for this reason that what falls falls badly; it is an impious thing. It is a thing begun with a pious end, and one that was first undertaken for a good purpose. Thanks be to Christ that such fires did not seize me, as they seized the rest with their flames.

units.la: DE ALENZONIO, QVI VRBES BRABANTIÆ ET ANTVERPIAM SIBI SVBIVGARE VOLVIT.
units.tr: On Alençon, who wished to subjugate the cities of Brabant and Antwerp to himself.

units.la: Dux Brabant. Alenzonius Endouiam Buscoducis vicinam capit 7. Ianuarii. Post etiam Helmonta, Horsta & alia loca, sic vt vicinæ vrbes sibi timerent.
units.tr: The Duke of Brabant, Alençon, took Eindhoven, near 's-Hertogenbosch, on 7 January. Afterwards he also took Helmond, Horst and other places, so that the neighbouring cities feared for themselves.

units.la: Dux Brabant. longo tempore postulabat auxilia à fratre Rege Galliæ, quæ Rex ea conditione promisit, si se Belgæ hæredem instituere vellent earum Regionum, quod Ordines detrectant.
units.tr: For a long time the Duke of Brabant had been asking his brother, the King of France, for help. The King promised it on the condition that the Belgians would make him heir of those regions, which the Estates refused.

units.la: Cordatiores quidam Regi consulunt, ne fratri opem ferat, sed eum ad summam inopiam redigi sinat, vt tandem se in Regię Maiestatis potestatem prorsus dedere cogatur. Sic Rex à fratre partem Belgicarum Regionum & Ciuitatum nactus, easdem, quibus volet, conditionibus ac legibus sibi devinciet, subiicietque. Rex operam det, vt Hispanis commeatus intercludatur, quod fiet, si exercitum ad Mosam disponat, & Luzemburgum Theonis villam & Mommedium superare studeat, & frequenti excursione & depopulatione messes & fructus corrumpat atque comburat. Hæc consilia cum Dux percepit, variæ mox ipsum & familiares diffidentiæ & suspiciones inuaserunt, & consilio cum iuuenibus desperantibus inito, suis rebus prospicere, & præcipua Belgii loca occupare, & pro suo arbitrio gubernare cogitauit.
units.tr: Some of the more prudent advisers counselled the King not to bring help to his brother but to let him be reduced to utter want, so that he would at last be forced to give himself entirely into the power of the royal majesty. In this way the King, having obtained part of the Belgian regions and cities from his brother, would bind and subject them to himself on whatever terms and laws he chose. The King should take care to cut off supplies from the Spaniards. This would happen if he stationed an army on the Meuse and strove to overcome Luxembourg, Thionville and Montmédy, and by frequent raids and plundering he destroyed and burned the crops and harvests. When the Duke learned of these plans, various distrusts and suspicions soon seized him and his close associates. Having entered into a plan with desperate young men, he resolved to look to his own affairs, to occupy the chief places of Belgium and to govern them at his own pleasure.

units.la: Itaque cum suis amicis decernit, ut uno eodemque die constituto Galli ubicunque possent loca munita, præcipue autem ubi in præsidiis erant, occuparent, Antuerpiam vero ipse cum suis inuadere statuit.
units.tr: So with his friends he decided that on one fixed day all the French should seize strongly fortified places wherever they could, especially where they were in garrison. He himself resolved to attack Antwerp with his men.

units.la: Per Chamoysum itaque Duynkirchen die 16. Ianuar. occupat, post etiam Teneromundam &c. Galli etiam Brugis eadem tentant, sed eiiciuntur ex urbe.
units.tr: Accordingly, through Chamois he seized Dunkirk on 16 January, and afterwards Tenremonde, etc. The French also tried the same at Bruges, but they were thrown out of the city.

units.la: Dux Anno M.D.LXXXIII, 14. & 15. Ianuarii ad suburbia Antuerpiana iusserat venire suum exercitum, nempe circiter quatuor millia Heluetiorum, ingentesque peditum & equitum Gallorum copias, iunctis iis, qui longo ante tempore ibidem loci manserant, multos præterea prætextu nobilitatis in urbem, & in suum palatium venire, secretoque arma parare mandarat, ea nocte portam Cronebergam suo palatio vicinam vi occupare, & per eam suas copias tecte ac tacite introducere, atque postridie summo mane urbe pro suo libitu potiri meditans. Verum cum 16. Ianuar. sinister rumor de Gallis ad aures quorundam peruenisset, Aloftanus tunc temporis Antuerpiæ Consul, id Duci eodem vespere significat, rogatque ut ad Ciuium securitatem catenas platearum maturius tendere, & laternas cum candelis accensis præ foribus pendere liceat, quod quidem Dux annuit, posteaquam diffidendi nullam ansam dari contra suos milites, utpote, qui sibi & urbi auxilio venissent, multaq; insuper alia declarasset. Postquam vero se id, quod conceperat, sedate taciteque perficere nequaquam posse videt, statuit vi aut quocunque alio modo experiri, absque longiore mora, eo, quod in aliis urbibus idipsum eadem quoque die tentaretur.
units.tr: In the year 1583, on 14 and 15 January, the Duke had ordered his army to come to the suburbs of Antwerp: about four thousand Swiss, and large forces of French infantry and cavalry, joined by those who had long before stayed in that place. He had also commanded many others, under the pretext of nobility, to come into the city and into his palace, and to prepare arms in secret. He planned that on that night he would seize by force the Kronenburg gate, close to his palace, and through it secretly and quietly lead his troops in, and so, very early the next morning, take control of the city at his pleasure. But when on 16 January a sinister rumour about the French reached the ears of some people, Aloft, then Consul of Antwerp, reported this to the Duke that same evening, and asked that chains be stretched across the streets earlier, for the safety of the citizens, and that lanterns with lit candles be hung before the doors. The Duke agreed to this, after he had declared that no ground for distrust should be given against his soldiers, who had come to help him and the city, and after he had said much else besides. But when he saw that he could by no means carry out quietly and secretly what he had conceived, he resolved to try by force or by some other means, without longer delay, since the same thing was being attempted that same day in other cities.

units.la: Postridie Ianuarii, nempe die 17. cum vir quidam nobilis
units.tr: On the day after, that is 17 January, a certain noble

units.la: Gallus reformatæ religioni addictus, quem hic non nominare præstat, secreto præmonuisset, Ducem firmiter statuisse eo die vrbem inuadere cum omni suo exercitu: Dux Consulibus & Tribunis Ciuitatis, ipsique Principi Auraico multis admodum seriis grauibusque argumentis demonstrat, nihil sinistri suspicandum de suo exercitu; imo huiusmodi delatores iure puniri debere:
units.tr: Frenchman, attached to the reformed religion, whom it is better not to name here, had privately forewarned them that the Duke had firmly resolved to attack the city that day with his whole army. The Duke demonstrated to the Consuls and Tribunes of the city, and to the Prince of Orange himself, with many very serious and weighty arguments, that nothing sinister was to be suspected of his army; indeed, such informers ought to be punished by law.

units.la: Longo denique sermone exponit propensum suum animum amoremque maximum erga Prouincias Belgicas, præcipue erga ciuitatem Antuerp. omnesque suspicandi occasiones amouere conatur: quod quidem tunc facilius præstare potuit, quod nulla adhuc euidentia signa huius inceptionis apparerent. Cumq; Auraicus ei consuleret, vt suspicionis auertendæ causa in vrbe maneret, id se facturum affirmat. Sed quia certo sciebat, nuntios earum rerum, quæ in aliis vrbibus acta erant, non diu expectaturos, voluit omnino id, quod instituerat, effectum reddere, rogatque Principem Auraicum, vt nonnullas ob causas in castra quoque veniat. Verum Princeps nihil tunc adhuc mali suspicans, id ei recusat.
units.tr: At length, in a long speech, he set out his well-disposed mind and his greatest affection towards the Belgian provinces, and especially towards the city of Antwerp, and tried to remove every occasion for suspicion. This he could more easily do at that time, because as yet no clear signs of this undertaking were appearing. And when Orange advised him to remain in the city in order to avert suspicion, he affirmed that he would do so. But since he knew for certain that the messengers would not be long in coming with news of what had been done in the other cities, he wanted to bring about entirely what he had planned, and he asked the Prince of Orange to come also to the camp for certain reasons. But the Prince, suspecting no harm as yet, refused him.

units.la: Ciues, qui ob sinistrum hunc rumorem præcedente nocte excubias diligenter egerant, portas toto eo die clausas custodierunt, & edicto publico milites omnes vrbem exire iusserunt.
units.tr: The citizens, who because of this sinister rumour had carefully kept watch during the previous night, kept the gates closed all that day, and by public edict ordered all soldiers to leave the city.

units.la: Dux mature pransus se apparat, extra vrbem in castra æquitare volens, eoque prætextu catenas & repagula platearum, quæ ad duas portas ducunt, aperiri, soluique mandat: dicebant enim sui satellites, se ignorare per vtram exire vellet. Vt autem aduenienti summo cum honore portæ aperirentur, Tribuni ciuium Iacobus à Falia, Rubræ, Iacobus Virendelius Kipdorpiæ portæ adstabant, paucis admodum ciuibus comitati, & quod hora prima prandii tempus esset, plurimique prandendi causa domum abiissent: eiusque vici habitatores & Kipdorpiæ portæ vicini incolæ tunc alio loco excubias agerent.
units.tr: The Duke, having dined early, got himself ready, wishing to ride out of the city into the camp. On that pretext he ordered the chains and barriers of the streets leading to the two gates to be opened and loosed. His attendants said that they did not know through which gate he wished to go out. And so that the gates might be opened for his arrival with the greatest honour, the Tribunes of the citizens, James of Falais for Rode, and James Virendelius, stood at the Kipdorp gate, accompanied by very few citizens. It was the first hour after noon, and many had gone home to dine; the inhabitants of that quarter and the neighbours of the Kipdorp gate were keeping watch at another place.

units.la: Dux circiter duocntis equitibus viris, tum nobilibus, tum aliis, omnibusque suis corriphæus custodibus Heluetiis & Gallis comitatus, versus portam Kipdorpiam equitat, hic nonnulli suorum prope & supra pontem concedunt, locumque dant Duci & proceribus transeuntibus, obuiam veniunt nonnullæ equitum turmæ, honoris, vt videbatur, exhibendi causa. Simul ac vero Dux cum Duce Montpentiero, Comite Laualio, & aliis huius doli ignaris secundum pontem versatilem transiit, vbi ciues excubitores aperto capite stabant, quidam Gallus nobilis se crus fregisse exclamat, (quod quidem fingebat, vt tali symbolo signoque reliquos ad arma concitaret) cui cum quidam ciues, inter alios autem cohortis ciuium satelles, Keysernis opitulari vellent, satelles ab eodem vulneratur. Ocyus quoque plurimi ciues excubitores ab ipsius Ducis aulicis laeduntur ac trucidantur: inter quos tanquam præcipuus Adrianus Virendelius Tribunus, reliqui eduntur.
units.tr: The Duke, accompanied by about two hundred horsemen, both noblemen and others, and by all his chosen guards, Swiss and French, rode towards the Kipdorp gate. Here some of his men went ahead near and over the bridge and made room for the Duke and the nobles as they passed, and several troops of horsemen came to meet them, apparently to show honour. But as soon as the Duke, with the Duke of Montpensier, the Count of Laval and others ignorant of this trick, had crossed the swing bridge where the citizen guards stood with heads bare, a certain French nobleman cried out that he had broken his leg (which he was pretending, so that by this signal he might rouse the others to arms). When some citizens, and among them a guard of the citizens' company, wished to help him at Keyser's, the guard was wounded by him. Very quickly also very many of the citizen guards were wounded and butchered by the Duke's courtiers. Among them Adrian Virendelius, a Tribune, was singled out, and the rest were carried off.

units.la: Mox ducenti equites Aulici maximo cum impetu in vrbem reuertuntur, cum nonnullis aliis. Deinde totus exercitus, postquam Dux ipse capitis pileo subleuato ipsis signum dedisset, versus vrbem tendere visus: ingrediuntur festinantes septendecim Gallorum peditum cohortes signis erectis, & quatuor equitum turmæ, sexcentiq; lanceariï, & multi præterea alii, qui omnes vna mente atque voce conclamant: Ville gaignee, viua la messe tua, tua. Prope portam domo incensa sociis signum edunt vrbem esse captam, & vt totus exercitus intrare properet.
units.tr: Straightaway two hundred courtier horsemen came back into the city with great violence, together with others. Then the whole army, after the Duke himself had raised his cap as a signal to them, seemed to make for the city: seventeen companies of French infantry with raised standards hurried in, and four troops of horse, six hundred lancers, and many others besides, who all shouted with one mind and voice: "Town won! Long live the Mass! Kill, kill!" Near the gate they set a house on fire as a signal to their comrades that the city was taken, and that the whole army should hurry to enter.

units.la: Dux ipse, qui iuxta pontem deflexerat, copias omnes accelerare iubet cum Holuetiorum agminibus, vrbemque superatam clamat, proinde ingredi festinent, verum ne spolient prohibet.
units.tr: The Duke himself, who had turned aside near the bridge, ordered all the troops to hasten, with the Swiss companies, and cried that the city was overcome; therefore they should hurry to enter, but he forbade them to plunder.

units.la: Primi vtraque moenia portæ vicina occupant: alii vnam partem vsque ad portam Cæsareum inuadunt, vbi ocyus tormentis bellicis potiuntur, eaque contra ciuitaCiuitatem vertunt, alii per plateam Kipdorpiam vsque ad pontem vinearium, alii per plateam nouam oblongam adipsam vsque Bursam, siue mercatorum basilicam, alii per alia loca vicina discurrunt, variisque clamoribus vociferantur, Trucidate, &c.
units.tr: The first men seized both walls near the gate. Others attacked one part as far as the Caesar gate, where they quickly gained control of the siege artillery and turned it against the city. Others ran through the Kipdorp street as far as the Vinearii bridge, others along the long new street as far as the Burse, or the merchants' hall, and others ran through other neighbouring places, shouting with various cries: Slaughter them, etc.

units.la: Ciues simulac se tam hostiliter obrui vident, quidam ocyus cum armis ex aedibus erumpunt, & primo numeri admodum pauci magnis Gallorum cateruis se opponunt, paruo quidem, sed denso agmine, eosque vlterius tendere prohibent, tensis paulatim vbique catenis.
units.tr: As soon as the citizens saw that they were being overwhelmed so hostilely, some quickly burst out of their houses with arms, and at first very few in number, they opposed the large bands of the French with a small but dense line, and they prevented them from advancing further, stretching chains across the streets gradually everywhere.

units.la: Deus omnipotens, cui soli Ciuitas Antuerpiensis gloriam, honorem, salutemque recuperatam merito adscribere debet, ciues ita animauit, vt omnibus fere vrbis Regionibus & plateis hostes terga vertere, & summo cum dedecore vrbem relinquere, altis e moenibus in fossas aquis plenas se praecipitare compulerint, postquam porta integra hora & amplius potiti, & erectis vexillis non procul a foro grassati fuerant.
units.tr: Almighty God, to whom alone the citizens of Antwerp rightly owe the glory, honour and recovered safety, so encouraged the citizens that the enemy turned their backs in almost all the regions and streets of the city, and, with great disgrace, compelled them to leave the city, to throw themselves from the high walls into the water-filled ditches, after they had held the gate intact for an hour and more, and had raged, with banners raised, not far from the forum.

units.la: Tantus in hoc conflictu fuit Ciuium ardor, vt multi, quibus glandes plumbei in promptu non erant, nummos marsupiis ocyus depromptos, dentibusq; mansos, suis sclopetis accommodarint exploserintque.
units.tr: Such was the ardour of the citizens in this conflict that many, who had no lead balls ready, loaded their muskets with coins quickly taken from their purses and bitten by their teeth, and then fired them.

units.la: Nonnulli ex aedibus & locis quibusdam, praecipue campis iaculatoriis, Caesareae portae & moenibus vicinis, plurimos equites peditesque prostrauerunt, tandemque moenia & propugnacula ab vtroque portae latere recuperarunt.
units.tr: Some, from houses and certain places, especially the shooting grounds near Caesar's Gate and the nearby walls, struck down very many horsemen and foot soldiers, and at last recovered the walls and bulwarks on both sides of the gate.

units.la: Hic D. Tyanum virum nobilem Merodanae familiae, Alosti Gubernatorem, qui Gallorum partes fouere videbatur, se vltra loricas vrbis in fossas e moenibus praecipitare compellunt, & postquam enatasset, glande in caput adacto, eminus occidunt.
units.tr: Here they forced Tyanus, a nobleman of the Merode family and governor of Alost, who seemed to favour the French side, to throw himself from the walls, past the city's breastworks, into the ditch. After he had swum across, they killed him from a distance with a ball driven into his head.

units.la: Ciues moenibus recuperatis, mox tormentis muralibus eos, qui extra vrbem erant, impetunt, praecipue Heluetios, qui vrbem versus tendebant, eamque nondum superatam suo magno malo sentiebant.
units.tr: Once the walls were recovered, the citizens at once attacked with the wall artillery those who were outside the city, especially the Swiss who were making for the city and who were feeling, to their great cost, that it had not yet been conquered.

units.la: Egregia profecto facinora hic à ciuibus fuere perpetrata. Pistor quidam nudus è pistoria sua officina prosiliens, arrepta pala, equitem sternit, equumque ipse celeriter conscendit, effugitque, cum se ab hostibus circumdari atque impeti videret.
units.tr: Truly remarkable deeds were performed here by the citizens. A certain baker, naked, leapt out of his bakehouse, seized a shovel, and knocked down a horseman. He quickly mounted the horse himself and escaped, when he saw that he was surrounded and attacked by enemies.

units.la: In ædibus quibusdam angularibus è regione portæ Kipdorpiæ quidam strenui Ciues è fenestris magna sclopetorū frequentia in ipsam vsq; portam iaculantur, multosq; in introitu sternunt, strati aliis intrare volentibus impedimento sunt, plurimi, qui ex vrbe fugere conabantur, glandibus creberrimis feriuntur, vnde porta mox cæsorum cadaueribus repletur, eratque stragis aceruus altior sesquihominis statura, & admodum amplus, stratorumque multi se motitabant, membrisq; palpitabant, ita vt introitus exitusque per portam cadauerum multitudine impediretur.
units.tr: In some corner houses opposite the Kipdorp Gate, certain brave citizens fired from the windows with a great volley of muskets right into the gate itself, and struck down many at the entrance. The fallen hindered others who wished to enter. Very many who tried to flee the city were struck by very dense volleys of balls, so that the gate was soon filled with the corpses of the slain. There was a heap of carnage higher than a man's height and very large, and many of the fallen were still stirring and their limbs twitching, so that entrance and exit through the gate were impeded by the multitude of corpses.

units.la: Dux, qui extra vrbem erat, cum porta expugnata suos maximo impetu irruere videt, Proceribus & Nobilibus, qui ei tunc aderant, & huius machinationis ignari erant, suam mentem aperit, cumque hi factum dolerent, amicorumque casum lamentarentur, & nonnulli victoriam non esse solidam, sed facile aduersa breui posse euenire, dicerent, ipse vrbem certo suam esse, & suorum 4.M. & amplius iam vi inuasisse aiebat: cumque quosdam è muris se in fossas præcipitare videret, multo audentius vrbem victam afferebat, & Ciues fugientes salutem quærere. Verum simul ac suos hos esse, & in se suaque agmina explodi tormenta videt, desperans è tormentorum ia &u vlterius recedit.
units.tr: The commander, who was outside the city, saw his men rushing in with the greatest force now that the gate had been stormed. He disclosed his plan to the nobles and grandees who were then with him and were ignorant of this scheme. When these lamented the event and bewailed the fate of their friends, and some said that the victory was not secure, but that adverse events could easily follow soon, he insisted that the city was surely his, and said that he had already taken it by force with his 4,000 and more men. And when he saw some throwing themselves from the walls into the ditches, he reported with much greater boldness that the city was conquered and that the fleeing citizens were seeking safety. But as soon as he saw that these were his own men, and that artillery was being fired upon him and his troops, he gave up hope of escaping the cannon fire and withdrew further away.

units.la: Ciues interea hostium ingentes cateruas mactant.
units.tr: Meanwhile the citizens slaughtered huge crowds of the enemy.

units.la: Princeps Auraicus, qui in arce extrema vrbis parte longissime sita tunc erat, nuntio primo credere noluit, ad mœnia autem festinans, reputat seditionem siue tumultuationem esse, tormenta explodi prohibet: verum postquam è mœnibus prospicit serio agi, perculsus admiratione ac perturbatione hæret.
units.tr: The Prince of Orange, who was then in the citadel, at the farthest and most distant part of the city, at first refused to believe the messenger. Hastening to the walls, he judged it to be a sedition or tumult, and forbade the artillery to be fired. But after he saw from the walls that it was in earnest, he stood transfixed, struck with astonishment and dismay.

units.la: Cum iam Gallorum nemo amplius se defendere videretur, ciues portam cadaueribus refertam claudere moliuntur, nonnulli strata corpora transcendunt, extremam cataractam clausuri: eam autem Ciues quidam e sagittariorum Collegio (qui se in domuncula excubitoria supra pontem inclusos seruarant) iam obseruarant, atque hoc modo hostes, qui extra vrbem adhuc erant, ab aliis separarant.
units.tr: When no one of the French seemed to defend himself any longer, the citizens strove to close the gate, crammed with corpses. Some climbed over the heaped bodies, intending to close the last portcullis. But certain citizens of the archers' guild, who had kept themselves shut up in a little watch-house above the bridge, had already observed this, and in this way separated the enemies who were still outside the city from the others.

units.la: Deinde portam cadaueribus vacuant, atque hoc quidem labore diutius, quam hostium mactatione, occupati fuerunt.
units.tr: Then they emptied the gate of corpses, and indeed they were occupied longer with this labour than with the slaughter of the enemy.

units.la: Quidam eorum, qui stragem transcenderant, mihi retulerunt, quam horribile ac triste fuerit spectaculum, videre tot occisorum vulneratorumque corpora, quorum fere omnium capita aliqua parte eminebant, vt ora halitum spiritumque reciperent. Inuenti inter mortuos plurimi viui, quibus ciuium misericordia fuit vita concessa, tandem porta exonerata clauditur.
units.tr: Some of those who had crossed the heap of the dead told me how horrible and sad a sight it was to see so many bodies of the slain and wounded, of nearly all of whom some part of the head stuck up, so that their mouths could take in breath and air. Very many living men were found among the dead, and the citizens' mercy granted them their lives. At last the gate, now unloaded, was shut.

units.la: Maxima vtrinque clades facta, Ciues amplius 80. in ipso conflictu ceciderunt, complures lethalibus vulneribus confecti paulo post e vita discesserunt. Casus, vt diximus, Tribunus Virendelius, insuper strategus Balthasar Thasius, qui vigiliis praefectus fuerat, primasque omnium, qui Gallorum furori restiterunt, Reynerus Michaldus, & Iaspar Paleo, satelles maior Legionis, sub Consule Philippo Schonhouio, qui cum Duce inter aulicos extra vrbem equitans, sinistro rumore percepto, mirabiliter euasit, & propere dicti satellitis maioris opera tendi catenas curauit. Cecidit autem hic satelles ad latus Schonhouii glande ictus. Ceciderunt & multi alii fortiter pugnando, non sine sua suorumque posteriorum laude ac gloria immortali, vtpote qui sanguinem pro patria effuderunt.
units.tr: The loss was very great on both sides. The citizens fell in the very clash, more than 80, and several, worn down by deadly wounds, died shortly afterwards. Among those who fell, as we said, were Tribune Virendelius, and also the strategist Balthasar Thasius, who had been put in charge of the watches, and Reynerus Michaldus and Jaspar Paleo, the foremost of all who resisted the fury of the French; and Paleo was the senior sergeant of the legion, under Consul Philip Schonhoven. Schonhoven, riding with the Duke among the courtiers outside the city, heard the sinister rumour and escaped in a remarkable way. Through the efforts of the said senior sergeant he promptly arranged for chains to be stretched across. This sergeant fell, struck by a ball, at Schonhoven's side. Many others also fell fighting bravely, not without praise and immortal glory for themselves and their descendants, as men who had poured out their blood for the fatherland.

units.la: Nec minori laude digni strenuissimi, fidelissimiq; Ciues alii, qui absque vllo militum subsidio animo virili, iunctis viribus, non sine summi Numinis ope, vrbem incolumem conseruarunt. runt. Nulla hic diuersarum Religionum ergo controuersia audita, Catholici, Confessionistæ, Reformati, simul omnes, quod probos Ciues decet, præstiterunt.
units.tr: Equally worthy of praise were the other most vigorous and most faithful citizens, who, without any help from soldiers, with manly courage and joined forces, and not without the aid of the Supreme Godhead, preserved the city unharmed. No controversy between the different religions was heard here. Catholics, Confessionists and Reformed, all together, did what upright citizens ought to do.

units.la: Galli cæsi sepultique in vrbe in mœnibus numerati vltra M D. præter eos, qui aut læsi effugerunt, aut postea in vrbe animā exhalarunt; aut extra vrbem tormentis à Ciuibus vulnerati interierunt, quorum ingens numerus fossa capacissima in mœnibus sepultus. Inter hos multi viri nobiles, magnæ auctoritatis, numero 320. & vltra, nempe Comes Agnianus & filius, Comes Castelruslus, Marscalci Byroni filius, D. Saisseuallius, Viluordæ Gubernator, filius D. Mirambrani, plu-resque alii, quorum nonnulli reformatæ Religioni addicti perfidæ machinationis ignari fuere.
units.tr: The French who were slain and buried in the city, counted on the walls, were more than 1,500, besides those who fled wounded, or who later breathed their last in the city, or who died outside the city, wounded by the citizens' artillery. Their huge number was buried in a very capacious ditch by the walls. Among these were many noblemen of great authority, numbering 320 and more: namely Count Agnianus and his son, Count Castelruslus, the son of Marshal Byron, Lord Saisseval, governor of Viluorda, the son of Lord Mirambrani, and several others, some of whom, attached to the Reformed religion, were ignorant of the treacherous scheme.

units.la: Multi se miro modo seruarunt, imprimis Iustinus Nassouius, Atraici filius naturalis. Ciues victores reliquis victis superstitibus pepercerunt.
units.tr: Many saved themselves in a remarkable way, above all Justinus Nassau, the natural son of Atraicus. The victorious citizens spared the remaining survivors among the vanquished.

units.la: Complures, qui inter occisos iacuerunt, releuarunt; refouerunt atque curarunt.
units.tr: Several of those who lay among the slain they raised up, revived and tended.

units.la: Captus Comes Feruaquens, Episcopus Constantiensis, multique alii nomine clari circiter bis mille, qui postmodo liberi dimittuntur.
units.tr: Captured were Count Feruaquens, bishop of Constance, and many other men famous by name, about two thousand in all, who were afterwards released.

units.la: Itaque Duci pessime cessit temerarium hoc inceptum: vide mœrore & animi ægritudine tandem contabuit.
units.tr: So this rash enterprise turned out very badly for the Duke, and at last he wasted away with grief and mental anguish.

units.la: Hoc vespere Dux in arce Berchemia mansit, & duos Ciues Antuerpianos, quos extra vrbem repererat, eodem vespere misit in vrbem cum literis, quibus declarabat, se, postquam solita sua prudentia ac patientia vitam periculis expositset, multos viros nobiles & strenuos milites amisisset, omnemque operam præstitisset, qua Prouinciis Belgicis propensum suum animum eas e miseriis liberandi declararet; tandem vero frustra se niti videret, (cuius rei testimonium atque argumentum in aliud tempus magis idoneum differebat,) & ruinam extremam Belgio imminere prospiceret, idque magna sui honoris iactura, iam propensum suum animum mutasse, multas ob causas: maxime cum se adeo indignis modis excipi videret, ut vere dicere posset, summam auctoritatem penes alios esse. Imprimis autem se summopere commotum ignominiis hoc die sibi illatis, nulla personae, status aut ordinis ducalis habita ratione, & hinc quidem adeo exacerbatum, ut hac occasione facinus istud hoc die perpetratum fuerit, non sine ingenti animi sui dolore ac poenitentia. Cum vero voluntas sua adhuc propensa sit in Rempubl. & in bonos incolas Belgii, se haec illis voluisse significare, ut certiores reddatur, quid de sua Celsi. statuerint, id se scire cupere, ante quam ea, quae animo propositum, aggrediatur. Proinde rogare, ut id per hos cives significent, &c.
units.tr: That evening the Duke stayed in the citadel of Berchem, and the same evening he sent two Antwerp citizens, whom he had found outside the city, back into the city with a letter. In it he declared that, after he had exposed his life to danger with his customary prudence and patience, had lost many noble men and brave soldiers, and had made every effort to show his well-disposed mind towards the Belgian provinces, and to free them from their miseries, he had at last seen that he strove in vain. (He was deferring the proof and evidence of this to a more suitable time.) Foreseeing the extreme ruin hanging over Belgium, and with great loss to his honour, he had now changed his well-disposed mind, for many reasons: chiefly because he saw himself received in such unworthy ways that he could truly say supreme authority lay with others. He was above all deeply moved by the indignities offered him that day, with no regard for his person, rank or ducal status, and was so exasperated by them that this deed was committed that day on this occasion, not without great grief and repentance of his mind. But since his will was still well-disposed towards the Commonwealth and the good inhabitants of Belgium, he wished to signify these things to them, so that he might be informed what they had decided about His Highness, which he wished to know before he undertook what he had proposed in his mind. Therefore he asked that they signify this through these citizens, and so on.

units.la: Antuerpienses nihil ad haec respondent, & deinde, postquam etiam ex alterius Ducis literis intelligunt, haec sibi tanquam turbarum auctoribus imputari, rem omnem ut gesta erat Typis edunt, &c.
units.tr: The Antwerpers made no response to this. Then, after they also learned from another duke's letter that these things were being imputed to them as the authors of the disturbances, they published the whole matter in print, just as it had happened, and so on.

units.la: Rex Galliae mittit ad Ordines, ut cum fratre reconcilientur. Id quod & Auraicus prolixo scripto suadere videtur. Ordines igitur certas ob causas iterum cum Duce pacisc untur.
units.tr: The King of France sent to the Estates, urging that they be reconciled with his brother. The Prince of Orange also seems to urge the same in a lengthy writing. The Estates therefore, for certain reasons, again treated with the Duke.

units.la: Quidam Cornelius Hogeus se Caroli V. Imper. filium professus, & a Rege Hispano animatus, seditione mouere studuit, sed deprehensus, capite truncatus & in 4. partes dissectus est. Martio.
units.tr: A certain Cornelius Hogeus, who claimed to be a son of Emperor Charles V and was encouraged by the King of Spain, tried to stir up sedition. He was caught, beheaded, and his body cut into four parts. March.

units.la: Tres diuersimode insidiantur vitae Auraici.
units.tr: Three men made various attempts on the life of Auraicus.

units.la: Alenzonius animaduertens, auctoritatem suam apud Belgas minui, Dunkerkio, Caletum, & inde in Galliam reuertitur.
units.tr: Alenzonius, realising that his authority among the Belgians was dwindling, withdrew from Dunkirk and Calais and returned from there to France.

units.la: Qui vindex adiit, post expraedator abiit, Hoc fuit Alanzo gens Stadiana tibi.
units.tr: He came as an avenger, and afterwards left as a plunderer. This, Alenzo, is what the Stadian people have done to you.

units.la: Auraicus ducit filiam Chastillonii Galli, quae fuit D. Teligni uxor in Laniena Parisan 1572. necati.
units.tr: Auraicus married the daughter of Chastillon, the Frenchman, who had been the wife of D. Teligny, killed in the Parisian slaughter of 1572.

units.la: Parmensis Duynkerkam graviter obsidet, quam Chanoysius tandem dedere coactus est, Iulio.
units.tr: Parma laid siege to Dunkirk in earnest, and Chanoysius was at last forced to surrender it. July.

units.la: Et sic Parm. occasionem potiundi maris accepit. Nam deinde & Neoportum, Vernam & Dixmundam in suam potestatem redigit.
units.tr: And so Parma got the opportunity to gain control of the sea. For next he brought Nieuwpoort, Furnes and Dixmude under his power.

units.la: Byronius cum suis Gallis & Heluetiis ex Belgio discedit.
units.tr: Byron left the Netherlands with his Frenchmen and Swiss.

units.la: Endhouia cum Diesto & Westerloo Mansfeldio deduntur.
units.tr: Enghien, together with Diest and Westerlo, was handed over to Mansfeld.

units.la: Ordines Woudam occupant.
units.tr: The Estates occupied Woudrichem.

units.la: Gandauienses in hac perturbatione & periculo rerum Imbysium priorem suum Consulem, & Petr. Dathenum ex Frankenthalio Casimiri, vbi vixerunt, reuocant.
units.tr: In this upheaval and danger, the people of Ghent recalled their former consul Imbyze, and Petrus Datheen from Frankenthal, the place of Casimir where they had been living.

units.la: Parmensis occupat Burcht pagum, & se munit, vt Gandauiis, Mechlinis, & Bruxellensibus Comitatum intercipiat.
units.tr: Parma seized the village of Burcht and fortified it, so as to cut off the county from Ghent, Mechelen and Brussels.

units.la: Brugenses bis conantur obsessis in Ipern commeatum adferre, sed bis caeduntur.
units.tr: The Bruges men twice tried to bring supplies to the besieged at Ypres, but twice they were cut down.

units.la: Brugenses excitatis fortalitiis, caeteras terras aquis immissis obtegunt.
units.tr: The Bruges men raised fortifications and flooded the rest of the land with water.

units.la: Sed demum aequis conditionibus dedunt se Regi.
units.tr: But in the end they surrendered to the King on fair terms.

units.la: Parmensis Gandauiis amnes interuertit.
units.tr: Parma diverted the rivers at Ghent.

units.la: Taxis astu occupat Zutphaniam, contra quem Auraicus frustra mittit Holochum.
units.tr: Tassis cunningly seized Zutphen, against whom Auraicus sent Holloch in vain.

units.la: Imbysius Consul metuens sibi ab Auraico, inclinat eo, vt Ciues misso Legato ad Parmensem Hispano se addicant, sed statim rursus repugnant, & tyrannice agunt.
units.tr: Consul Imbyze, fearing Auraicus, was inclined to persuade the citizens to send an envoy and submit themselves to the Spaniard; but they at once changed their minds again and acted tyrannically.

units.la: Post anno sequenti sese dedunt Parmensi, soluta ingenti pecunia.
units.tr: The following year they surrendered to Parma, after paying a huge sum of money.

units.la: Acre bellum in Archiepiscopatu Colonien si.
units.tr: A fierce war in the Archbishopric of Cologne.

units.la: Regio Westhensis & Alostum hosti produntur.
units.tr: The district of Waas and Aalst were betrayed to the enemy.

units.la: Gregorius XIII. P. edit fulmen excommunicationis in Henric. Regem Gall. & Nauarrae, & in Condaeum reformatae religionis antesignanos.
units.tr: Pope Gregory XIII issued a thunderbolt of excommunication against Henry, King of France and Navarre, and against Condé, the champions of the reformed religion.

units.la: M.D.LXXXIV. Prodito Alosto Gandauenses & Brugenses de reconciliatione agere coeperunt. Imbysius dum Teneromundam hosti tradere conatur, apprehenditur & capite plectitur.
units.tr: In 1584, after Aalst was betrayed, the people of Ghent and Bruges began to negotiate for reconciliation. While Imbyze was trying to hand Tenremonde over to the enemy, he was seized and executed.

units.la: Ipera obsessa opprimitur.
units.tr: Ypres, under siege, was overcome.

units.la: Brugæ etiam astu & technis Chymai corruptæ & proditæ cum Parmensi conueniunt.
units.tr: At Bruges too, by the trickery and devices of Chimay, the city was corrupted and betrayed, and came to terms with Parma.

units.la: Auraicus, misso Comite Holochio, adiuncto exercitu Truchsesii Electoris Colon. inde expulsi, obsidet Zutphaniam, sed frustra.
units.tr: Auraicus sent Count Holloch, with an army added from Truchsess, the Elector of Cologne, from whom they had been expelled, and besieged Zutphen, but in vain.

units.la: Malecontenti, nullis obstantibus, occupant terras Waes, Axel, Hulst, denique & Gandauium.
units.tr: The malcontents, with no one opposing them, occupied the lands of Waas, Axel, Hulst and finally Ghent.

units.la: Publicis edictis cauetur, ne commeatus ad Prouincias Regi parentes vehatur.
units.tr: By public edicts it was provided that no supplies be carried to the provinces obedient to the King.

units.la: Alanzonius Dux Brabantiæ in Galliis moritur. Encomia ipsius vide in Meterano.
units.tr: Alenzonius, Duke of Brabant, died in France. For his eulogies see in Meteren.

units.la: Auraicus sclopeto traiicitur à Balthasaro Gerarte Burgundo, qui mortis crudelissimo supplicio constantissimus interim ipse afficitur.
units.tr: Auraicus was shot through with a musket by Balthasar Gerard, a Burgundian, who in the meantime himself underwent the most cruel death with the greatest constancy.

units.la: Auraici mors publice lugetur, eius corpus honorifice sepelitur. Et succeditin Gubernatione filius Mauricius.
units.tr: Auraicus's death was publicly mourned, and his body was honourably buried. And his son Maurice succeeded him in the government.

units.la: MAVRICIVS FILIVS AVRAICI DUX STATVVM.
units.tr: MAURICE, SON OF WILLIAM, LEADER OF THE STATES.

units.la: Parmensis munimenta & valla ad Scaldim occupat.
units.tr: Parma seizes the fortifications and ramparts on the Scheldt.

units.la: Idem ad fortalitium Lillo male excipitur.
units.tr: The same man is repulsed at the fort of Lillo.

units.la: Inde aggreditur, & occupat fortalitium Lifkenhok in detrimentum Antuerpiensium & vicinorum, ripam passim praesidiis munit.
units.tr: From there he advances and takes the fort of Lifkenhoek, to the loss of Antwerp and its neighbours, and fortifies the bank everywhere with garrisons.

units.la: Teneromundam & Viluordam expugnat.
units.tr: He storms Termonde and Vilvoorde.

units.la: Gandenses se Parmensi dedunt, qui arcem ibi restaurat.
units.tr: The men of Ghent surrender to Parma, who restores the citadel there.

units.la: Parmensis operas instituit, vt Scaldis fluuii transitum interccludat. In eum finem pontem ex nauibus compositum in eo struit, & valla multa in ripa fluminis erigit. Antuerpienses sub Aldegundo se tuentur, sed valde confuse.
units.tr: Parma sets about blocking the crossing of the Scheldt. To that end he builds a bridge of ships across the river and raises many ramparts on the bank. The Antwerpers defend themselves under Marnix of Aldegonde, but very confusedly.

units.la: Parmensis pacem illis proponit, ad quam vbi respondissent, ille rursum institit.
units.tr: Parma offers them peace, and when they have replied, he presses on again.

units.la: Prouinciae Belgicae deliberatione inter se habita concludunt, vt Regi Galliae se submittant, ad quem ea de causa Legatos mittunt, quos benigne quidem Rex audit, sed superuenientibus tum Coniuratorum & Hispanizatorum turbis, vnde bellum ciuile renatum, Rex honeste se ad illos excusat.
units.tr: The provinces of Belgium, after deliberating among themselves, resolve to submit to the King of France and send envoys to him for this purpose. The King hears them kindly, but when the disturbances of the Conspirators and the Spanish partisans arise, from which civil war was renewed, the King honourably excuses himself to them.

units.la: M. D. LXXXV. Neomagum in Parmensis cedit potestatem. Eandem fortunam secutae sunt Bruxellae & Mechlinia rerum penuria coactae.
units.tr: 1585. Nijmegen comes under the power of Parma. Brussels and Mechelen, forced by shortage of supplies, share the same fate.

units.la: Antuerpienses vnam atque alteram nauim, vastae molis, puluere tormentario, & magnis saxis molaribus impletas extruunt, & eas ad effringendum pontem a Parmensi in Scalda constructum emittunt.
units.tr: The Antwerpers build one and then another ship of huge bulk, filled with gunpowder and great millstones, and launch them to break the bridge that Parma has built across the Scheldt.

units.la: Postquam ignis puluerem nitratum attigit, tantum subito fragorem sonitumque adeo horribilem excitauit, vt coelum ruere terraque perire putaretur: vndas commotas, perturbatas, extra alueum effusas profluxisse, restagnantemque amnem tanta aquarum copia Calloaum munitionem repleuisse, vt ad genua vsq; in aquis stantes milites detinuerit, & funes bombardicos, atque igniaria omnia extinxerit: lapides ingentes extra nauem, puluueris bombardici violentia, in aera longe lateque volitasse, flammam sex pontis naues abstulisse, multas quoque alias carinis inuersis prorsus euertisse ac diruisse.
units.tr: When the fire reached the nitrated powder, it produced such a sudden crash and so dreadful a noise that the sky seemed to fall and the earth to perish. The waves, stirred up and disturbed, were thrown out beyond their channel and flowed forth, and the river, held back, filled the Calloo fort with so great a mass of water that it held the soldiers standing in water up to their knees, and it extinguished the fuses and all the fire-devices. By the violence of the gunpowder, huge stones flew through the air far and wide beyond the ship. The flame carried off six ships of the bridge, and many others it utterly overturned and wrecked, keels upturned.

units.la: Inopinata huius machinae violentia fuere in Parmensis exercitu desiderati circiter octingenti, inter quos Marchio Risborgius Gandaui Burggrauius generalis strategus totius equitatus, qui ab Ordinibus ex ambitione ad Hispanum desciuerat, occubuit & Roblesius, &c.
units.tr: By the unexpected violence of this engine about 800 men were lost from Parma's army, among them Marquis Risbourg, Burgrave of Ghent and general commander of the whole cavalry, who out of ambition had gone over to the Spaniard from the States, and Robles, etc.

units.la: Parmensis ruptum pontem reparat.
units.tr: Parma repairs the broken bridge.

units.la: Aditus vnus ex reliquis in aggere dicto Couwenstein, occupatur, sed cum multo sanguine rursus amittitur.
units.tr: One of the remaining approaches, on the embankment called Couwenstein, is taken, but it is lost again with much bloodshed.

units.la: Qua de re animus Antuerpiensibus labefactatus est, & de pace cogitare coeperunt. Tandem presli frumenti penuria, & spem auxilii reliquam non videntes, bonis conditionibus cum Parmense transigunt, qui post triumphans in vrbem ingreditur, ibique arcem restaurat.
units.tr: By this the spirits of the Antwerpers were shaken, and they began to think of peace. At last, with a shortage of grain pressing them and seeing no hope of help left, they conclude terms with Parma on good conditions. He afterwards entered the city in triumph and there restored the citadel.

units.la: Tum leges de valore monetae facit.
units.tr: Then he makes laws concerning the value of the coinage.

units.la: Foederatae Prouinciae ad Reginam Angliae insignes mittunt Legatos, qui Principatum ei offerunt, recusat quidem Principatum, verum Prouinciis auxilium certissimum Regina promittit, causasque Typis euulgat, Fließingam & Brilam pignori accipit, eoque Comitem Liceßrium mittit.
units.tr: The United Provinces send distinguished envoys to the Queen of England, who offer her the sovereignty. The Queen indeed refuses the sovereignty, but promises the Provinces most certain aid, publishes the reasons in print, takes Flushing and Brill in pledge, and sends the Earl of Leicester there.

units.la: Schenkius militiam Hispanicam deserit.
units.tr: Schenk deserts the Spanish military service.

units.la: Schenkii, Newenarii & Villersii milites à Ioh. Baptistae Taxii copiis caeduntur.
units.tr: The soldiers of Schenk, Neuenar and Villers are cut down by the forces of John Baptist Tassis.

units.la: Philippi Regis Hispaniae filia secunda, Duci Sabaudiae nubit.
units.tr: The second daughter of Philip, King of Spain, marries the Duke of Savoy.

units.la: Turca & Rex Persarum Hispano donamittunt.
units.tr: The Turk and the King of Persia send gifts to the Spaniard.

units.la: Nouesium à Newenario & Clotho capitur, quod tamen Parmensis sequenti anno insigni stratagemate incendio facto recuperat.
units.tr: Neuss is captured by Neuenar and Klot, though Parma recovers it the following year by a notable stratagem, causing a fire.

units.la: In Amisio amne inter Ordinum classiarios & Embdanos discordia oritur.
units.tr: A quarrel arises on the river Ems between the naval men of the States and the men of Emden.

units.la: Ordinum copiae dum fossas & aggeres iaciunt, Neomagum obsessuri, ab Handepennio propelluntur.
units.tr: While the forces of the States are throwing up ditches and embankments, intending to besiege Nijmegen, they are driven off by Hohenlo.

units.la: Anno M. D. LXXXVI. Iohan. Baptist. Taxius glaciei ope & commoditate adiutus, aliquos Ordinum milites caedit.
units.tr: In 1586 John Baptist Tassis, aided by the ice and the advantage it gave him, cuts down some soldiers of the States.

units.la: Aurei Velleris honore quidam ornantur.
units.tr: Certain men are honoured with the Golden Fleece.

units.la: Sixtus Pontifex Obelyscos Romae erigit.
units.tr: Pope Sixtus erects obelisks at Rome.

units.la: Prouinciae foederatae Liceßrium Anglum in Gubernatorem generalem accipiunt, Anglorum Regina aegre id ferēte.
units.tr: The United Provinces accept the Englishman Leicester as Governor-General, and the Queen of England takes this with reluctance.

units.la: Licestrius disciplinam militarem promulgat. Vetat quęcun- quecum hoste commercia, maximo pręmiatorum, seu prę-donum liberorum commodo & lucro.
units.tr: Leicester promulgates military discipline. He forbids all trade with the enemy, to the great profit and gain of the rewarded, or rather of the pirates' children.

units.la: Schenkius in expeditione Werlæ admodum strenue se ge- rit.
units.tr: Schenk acquits himself very vigorously in the expedition to Werl.

units.la: Parmensis Graviam obsidione cingit, quæ commeatu ab Hohenloo paulo ante inuecto deditur. Hac de causa Hemer-tus Grauiæ gubernator capite pleƈtitur.
units.tr: Parma surrounds Groningen with a siege, and it is surrendered, its supply of grain having been brought in shortly before by Hohenlo. For this reason Hemertus, governor of Groningen, is beheaded.

units.la: Parmensis Ventoam obsidet & capit, vt & Nouesium.
units.tr: Parma besieges and takes Venlo, and likewise Neuss.

units.la: Mauricius capit Axelam.
units.tr: Maurice takes Axel.

units.la: Licestrius Doesburgo potitur.
units.tr: Leicester gains possession of Doesburg.

units.la: Licestrius leui prælio cum Parmensis exercitu apud Zut-phaniam consligit. Valla & propugnacula Zutphaniæ obsidet & capit.
units.tr: Leicester engages in a light skirmish with Parma's army near Zutphen. He besieges and takes the ramparts and fortifications of Zutphen.

units.la: Ordines apud Licestrium conqueruntur.
units.tr: The States complain to Leicester.

units.la: Licestrius confusum incompositumque relinquens statum in Angliam reuertitur. Conspirationibus in Anglia ortis.
units.tr: Leicester leaves the state confused and disordered and returns to England. Conspiracies arise in England.

units.la: M.D. LXXXVII. Regina Scotiæ Maria, cum antea mortī adiudicata erat, in Anglia capite truncatur.
units.tr: M.D. LXXXVII. Mary, Queen of Scots, who had previously been condemned to death, is beheaded in England.

units.la: Notanarrationem de Statu & Politia Angliæ.
units.tr: A narrative on the state and polity of England is to be noted.

units.la: Narrationem item de Stephano Batorio Rege Poloniæ.
units.tr: Likewise a narrative concerning Stephen Báthory, King of Poland.

units.la: Discordia & suspiciones inter Licestrium, milites Prouin-ciales & Hohenloi.
units.tr: Discord and suspicions between Leicester, the provincial soldiers and Hohenlo.

units.la: Discordia Vltraiecti.
units.tr: Discord at Utrecht.

units.la: Parmensis Woudam capit.
units.tr: Parma takes Woudrichem.

units.la: Parmensi Stanleius Dauentriã, Iorcus Zutphaniam tradit.
units.tr: Stanley hands Deventer over to Parma, and Yorke hands Zutphen over.

units.la: Hac de causa Prouinciæ Mauritio summam imperandi po-testatem dant, & cum Licestrio epistola missa expostulant. Id-que in peiorem partem accipitur. Huius rei gratia Baro de Bukhorst in Hollandiam mittitur.
units.tr: For this reason the Provinces give Maurice the supreme power of command, and they send a letter of complaint to Leicester. It is taken in the worse part. On this account Baron de Bockhorst is sent into Holland.

units.la: Maxima annonæ caritas. Rapida pestis & luporum ingens numerus in Belgii Prouinciis Parmensi subditis.
units.tr: Very great dearth of food. A rapid plague and an immense number of wolves in the Belgian provinces subject to Parma.

units.la: Summa præmente penuria, 800. & amplius naues ex Belgio Ostlandiam frumenti conquirendi causa petunt.
units.tr: With the shortage pressing hard, 800 and more ships from Belgium head for East Friesland to seek grain.

units.la: T 3
units.tr: T 3

units.la: Draco duas contra Hispanos expeditiones suscipit. Candiscius iter circum orbem terrarum conficit. Haupennius ab Hohenloo caeditur. Geldria Ciuitas à Baddone Scoto hostiti traditur.
units.tr: Drake undertakes two expeditions against the Spanish. Cavendish completes a voyage round the world. Haupennius is cut down by Hohenlo. The city of Geldern is betrayed to the enemy by Baddon the Scot.

units.la: Slusa obsessa & tormentis valde concussa, Parmensi dedi-tur.
units.tr: Sluis, besieged and greatly battered by artillery, is surrendered to Parma.

units.la: Licestrii querelis, & de sua auctoritate ad Iunium epistolis permoti Ordines, summam auctoritatem & gubernationis formam, quam Rege Hispano relicto tenuerunt, & potestatem ipsi concessam exponunt, & Hohenloum reconciliare student.
units.tr: Moved by Leicester's complaints and by letters to Junius about his authority, the States set out the supreme authority and the form of government they held after the Spanish King was abandoned, and the power conferred on them, and they strive to reconcile Hohenlo.

units.la: Licestrius de Ordinibus conqueritur libro Typis edito.
units.tr: Leicester complains of the States in a book published in print.

units.la: Respondent Ordines, & suam auctoritatem formamque gubernationis Equitum auratorum, Nobilium & Comitatum, quas Ordines repraesentant, Licestrio proponunt & exponunt.
units.tr: The States reply, and set out and explain to Leicester their authority and form of government, as represented by the Knights, Nobles and Counties.

units.la: Licestrius Reginae nomine pacificationem proponit, eam Ordines detrectant.
units.tr: Leicester proposes pacification in the Queen's name; the States reject it.

units.la: Regis interceßio per Ranzouium facta ab Ordinibus recusatur.
units.tr: The King's intercession, made through Ranzau, is refused by the States.

units.la: Recusationis causa Rex offensus, Hollandis Ostlandiam versus per Zontam navigantibus 30. M. florenorum extorquet.
units.tr: The King, offended by the refusal, extorts 30,000 florins from the Hollanders sailing through the Zuiderzee towards East Friesland.

units.la: Maioris discordiae metu Ecclesiae & Traiectenses ad Ordines scribunt, utrisque respondetur.
units.tr: Fearing greater discord, the Churches and the men of Utrecht write to the States, and both sides are answered.

units.la: Conspiratio Leydae.
units.tr: Conspiracy at Leiden.

units.la: Anglorum fautores puniuntur.
units.tr: Supporters of the English are punished.

units.la: Negotiis Belgii varie & exacte disceptatis in Anglia, Regina Licestrium revocat domum, eumque gubernationem deponere & resignare iubet.
units.tr: With the affairs of the Netherlands variously and thoroughly debated in England, the Queen recalls Leicester home and orders him to lay down and resign the government.

units.la: Meppela capitur.
units.tr: Meppel is captured.

units.la: Fabianus à Donaw expeditionem militarem pro Nauarræo in Galliam facit, verum rebus parum prouide administratis profligatur.
units.tr: Fabian von Donau leads a military expedition into France on behalf of Navarre, but since matters were poorly managed without foresight, it is routed.

units.la: Nauarrus tamen Ducem Ioyesium superat & delet.
units.tr: Yet Navarre defeats and destroys Duke Joyeuse.

units.la: Rex Gall. ex vrbe Parisiorum à Guisianis & eorum fœderatis pellitur.
units.tr: The King of France is driven from the city of Paris by the Guisards and their allies.

units.la: Schenkius Bonnam vrbem in gratiam Gebhardi Episcopi, qui Argentoratimorabatur, capit vigesimo tertio die Decembris.
units.tr: Schenk captures the city of Bonn on 23 December, in the interest of Bishop Gebhard, who was staying at Strasbourg.

units.la: Vrbs victa rursus à Parmensis exercitu obsidetur & capitur.
units.tr: The conquered city is again besieged by Parma's army and taken.

units.la: Angliæ Regina pacificationem denuo proponit.
units.tr: The Queen of England again proposes pacification.

units.la: Ordines quid contra sentiant, ostendunt.
units.tr: The States show what they think of it.

units.la: Regina nihilominus delegatos in Flandriam mittit, qui frustra de pace agunt.
units.tr: Nevertheless the Queen sends delegates into Flanders, who negotiate for peace in vain.

units.la: Anno M.D.LXXXVIII. Præsidiarii in Medeblik seditiosi reprimuntur.
units.tr: M.D.LXXXVIII. The seditious garrison at Medemblik is suppressed.

units.la: Gertrudebergenses, & alii pecunia numerata pacantur.
units.tr: The men of Gertruidenberg and others are pacified with money paid out.

units.la: Ruffetus Fliesingæ Gubernator offensus Walachriam domare frustra conatur.
units.tr: Ruffet, governor of Vlissingen, offended, tries in vain to subdue Walcheren.

units.la: Hispanica classe aduentante, simultas seu zelus inter Anglam & Ordines tollitur.
units.tr: With the Spanish fleet approaching, the rivalry or zeal between England and the States is set aside.

units.la: Maximilianus Archidux in Polonia capitur.
units.tr: Archduke Maximilian is captured in Poland.

units.la: Rex Daniæ moritur.
units.tr: The King of Denmark dies.

units.la: Iohannes Baptista de Taxis in obsidione Bonnæ globo capvt transmisso succubuit, & Coloniæ cum maxima solemnitate sepultus est, 26. April.
units.tr: John Baptist de Tassis succumbed in the siege of Bonn when a cannonball passed through his head. He was buried at Cologne with the greatest solemnity, on 26 April.

units.la: Notetur mirabilis euentus huius anni, nempe expeditio nauialis ab Hispano suscepta, quæ in Belgio quidem acta non est, sed in Belgarum perniciem parata, videlicet, quo pacto Rex Hispaniarum expeditionem contra Anglos & Belgas diu ante animo conceptam, communicato consilio cum Pont. Ro. susceperit, vt regnum Angliæ subiugaret, & Religioni suæ Catholicæ restitueret, eaqz ratione despectu contemptuqz suis apud
units.tr: Note the remarkable event of this year, namely the naval expedition undertaken by the Spaniard. It was not carried out in Belgium, but was prepared for the ruin of the Belgians; that is, how the King of Spain, having long before conceived in mind an expedition against the English and the Belgians, undertook it after communicating his plan with the Roman Pontiff, so that he might subjugate the kingdom of England and restore it to his Catholic religion, and in this way, with contempt and scorn among his own people,

units.la: Nauar. Ioyesium: Nauarrus. Schenk Bonnam: Schenkius. Anno M.D.LXXXVIII. Medeblik. Maxim. Archid. Polon. capitur. Rex Dan. moritur. De expeditione nauali Hispanorum contra Anglos memorabili. apud Anglos honoremque ab illis sibi ereptum (qui ante annos 34. ad Pontificias leges eos coegerat) multasque alias iniurias, quas alta mente repositas coseruabat, vlciscceretur. Deinde quod eandem hanc viam commodissimam iudicaret, qua Belgicarum Prouinciarum sibi hæreditariam possessionem recuperaret, reclusa Belgis per Angliam navigatione, quod gravissimis argumentis, evidentissimisque rationibus certo & facile perfici posse arguebatur, consideratā tanta omnium rerum necessariarum copia & apparatu, quo prospecti erant hi, qui remisiam instituebant, quā particularius iam describemus.
units.tr: Navarrus, Joyeuse: Navarrus. Schenk, Bonn: Schenkius. In 1588: Medemblik. Maximilian, archduke and Polish claimant, is captured. The King of Denmark dies. On the memorable naval expedition of the Spaniards against the English, which the Spanish king undertook to punish the English for the honour that they had snatched from him (they had forced them under Papal laws some thirty-four years earlier), and for the many other injuries that he had stored up in his deep mind and nursed. Next, because he judged that this same route was the most convenient by which he might recover the hereditary possession of the Belgic Provinces, by shutting off the Belgians' passage through England. This, it was argued, could be carried out surely and easily by the gravest arguments and the clearest reasons, given such a great abundance and preparation of all necessary things with which those who were setting out this fleet were provided, which we will now describe in more detail.

units.la: Cum Rex iam plus quam 20. annis bellum cum Belgis parvo cum fructu gessisset, deliberatione cum suis habita, visum ei est ipsos mari rursum oppugnare, quod aliquoties quidem ante hac fuerat tentatum, sed non iis quibus opus fuerat viribus, ad quam expeditionem nunc adhibere debuit potentiam, quod Anglos haberet hostes; quorum Insula ita sita est, ut navigantibus in illis partibus plurimum prodesse vel incommodare posset. Ea gratia primum illam inuadendam censuit, persuasus à Secretario Escouedo, aliisque viris rerum peritis Hispanis & Belgis, itemque ab Anglis multis transfugis facilio-rem esse dictæ Insulæ expugnationem, quam Hollandiæ aut Zelandiæ. Ad hæc accedebat, quod Hispani iudicarent, longe vtilius Regi suo fore, vt Angliam & Belgium semel classe domaret, quam vt potentem classem perpetuo alere cogeretur, ad vtriusque Indiæ navigationem liberam, tutamque à Drako Anglo, & eius similibus conseruandam.
units.tr: Since the King had already waged war against the Belgians for more than twenty years with little profit, after deliberation with his advisers he resolved to attack them again by sea. This had been tried several times before, but not with the forces that were needed. For this expedition he now had to employ his full strength, because he had the English as enemies, whose island is so placed that it could greatly help or hinder those sailing in those parts. For this reason he decided to attack that island first, persuaded by the secretary Escovedo and other experienced Spanish and Belgian men, and likewise by many English deserters, that the conquest of the said island would be easier than that of Holland or Zeeland. Added to this, the Spaniards judged that it would be far more useful to their king to subdue England and Belgium once with a fleet than to be forced to keep a powerful fleet permanently, to keep the navigation to both Indies free and safe from Drake the Englishman and his like.

units.la: In hunc finem Rex multo iam tempore syluas quamplurimas excidi, nauesq; ex iis ædificari per Italiam & Hispaniam iusserat, magnosque præterea apparatus ad eam rem requisitos fecerat, vt sunt æneorum tormentorum conflatio, annonæ militumque passim conscriptio & congregatio, adeo vt circa initium anni 1588. tantam tamque potentem Classem confecerit, & Vlysponam in Portugalliam aduexerit, quantam mil-lis ante seculis Oceanus vidit. Vnius classis descriptionem Hispani valde copiose & particulariter factam, Typisque mandatam publicarunt, in qua numerus, nomina, & magnitudo nauium, numerus nautarum & militum, qui classe illa vehebantur; item quantitas tormentorum, armorum, globulorum, funiculorum ad intendendas bombardas paratorum, pulueris nitrosi, annonae, & omnis denique apparatus classici ponebantur. His omnibus addita etiam ibi erant nomina Praefectorum, Capitaneorum, & Nobilium voluntariorum, quorum tanta fuit multitudo, ut vix vlla alicuius nominis apud Hispanos esset familia, aut quidam inter eos vir primarius, qui non in classe illa haberet fratrem, filium aut consanguineum, qui omnes inuincibili ista (uti eam appellabant) classe aeternam laudem & gloriam se acquisituros, aut maximis in Anglia & Belgio opibus & dignitatibus potituros se putabant.
units.tr: To this end the King had for a long time ordered very many forests to be felled and ships to be built from them in Italy and Spain, and had also made great preparations needed for the purpose, such as the casting of bronze guns, and the collection and enrolment of supplies and soldiers everywhere. So by about the beginning of 1588 he had assembled so great and so powerful a fleet, and brought it to Lisbon in Portugal, as the ocean had not seen in a thousand years before. The Spaniards published in print a very full and detailed description of this one fleet, in which were set out the number, names and size of the ships, the number of sailors and soldiers who were carried in that fleet, likewise the quantity of guns, arms, shot, ropes prepared for stretching the cannons, saltpetre powder, provisions, and in short every kind of naval equipment. To all this were added the names of the commanders, captains and volunteer nobles, whose number was so great that there was hardly any family of note among the Spaniards, or any leading man among them, who did not have a brother, son or kinsman in that fleet. They all thought that by that invincible fleet (as they called it) they would win eternal praise and glory, or would gain the greatest wealth and dignities in England and Belgium.

units.la: Quid autem quaeque Regio & Prouincia Hispaniarum contulerit Praefectorum, militum, armorum, nauium & tormentorum, & aliorum apparatuum, &c, eorum catalogum vide in Meterano.
units.tr: As for what each region and province of Spain contributed of commanders, soldiers, arms, ships, guns and other equipment, etc., see the catalogue of these in Meteren.

units.la: Dum Hispani classem hanc parant, Parmensis etiam Regis mandato in Belgio apparatum magnum fecit, quo Hispanis subueniat, multas ad eum finem naues aedificans, nauclerोs & fabros Iesuiticae sectae ex Italia ad id accersens.
units.tr: While the Spaniards were preparing this fleet, Parma also, by the King's command, made great preparations in Belgium to help the Spaniards, building many ships for this purpose and summoning shipmasters and carpenters from Italy, of the Jesuit sect.

units.la: Totam reliquorum apparatuum descriptionem vide in Meterano, &c.
units.tr: For a full description of the remaining preparations see Meteren, etc.

units.la: Pontifex etiam Romanus Sixtus Quintus ad expeditionem istam promouendam, crucem, vti contra Turcas & infideles solet, publicauit, cum maximis indulgentiis, quae passim Typis sunt mandatae. Has Bullas Angli & Belgae ludibrio habentes dixerunt, Diabolum latronis instar vias passim occupare, nec tales saluiconductus literas curare. Sunt qui affirmant, Pontificem Regnum Angliae cum titulo Defensoris fidei Regi Hispaniae donasse, mandasseque, vt id ea lege inuaderet, vt deuictum regnum tanquam Romanae sedis feudatarius tarius & tributarius possideret. In hunc finem Pontifex au-ri milionem seu 10. M. Coronatorum obtulit, quorum dimi-dium presenti pecunia, reliquum vero vbi Regnum Angliæ, aut celebris aliquis eius portus ab eo esset subiungatus.
units.tr: The Roman Pontiff Sixtus V also, to promote that expedition, published a crusade, as he is accustomed to do against the Turks and infidels, with the greatest indulgences, which were printed and circulated everywhere. The English and the Belgians, treating these bulls with mockery, said that the Devil, like a robber, was everywhere occupying the roads, and that they did not care for such safe-conduct letters. Some affirm that the Pontiff gave the King of Spain the kingdom of England with the title of Defender of the Faith, and ordered him to invade it on this condition: that, once the kingdom was conquered, he should hold it as a vassal and tributary of the Roman See. To this end the Pontiff offered a million gold crowns, or ten hundred thousand, half of which was to be paid now, and the rest when the kingdom of England, or some famous port of it, was subjected to him.

units.la: Papa Wilhelmum Alanum Anglum Cardinalem in An-gliam misit, qui sententiam Papæ contra Reginam Angliæ tanquam hæreticam promulgaret, & vt omnes Hispaniæ Regi obedirent, mandaret. Vide cætera ibidem.
units.tr: The Pope sent the English Cardinal William Allen into England, to proclaim the Pope's sentence against the Queen of England as a heretic, and to order that all should obey the King of Spain. See the rest there.

units.la: Angli & vnitæ Belgarum Prouinciæ defensionem quidem aliquam pararunt, sed non pro magnitudine periculi, quod à tanto apparatu erat metuendum, idque cum fama constans apud eos de tota expeditione tanto tempore fuisset.
units.tr: The English and the united provinces of the Belgians did prepare some defence, but not in proportion to the magnitude of the danger that was to be feared from so great a preparation, and this although for a long time there had been a constant rumour among them about the whole expedition.

units.la: Verum credebant quibusdam, qui dicerent, classem hanc parari ad naues, quæ ex Hispania in Indias prosi-ciscerentur, tuto conducendas: quod eo videbatur verisimilius, quod naues vsque adeo essent magnæ & vastæ, vt Hispani eas vadoso, periculosoq; mari Britannico nunquam commissuri videntur.
units.tr: Indeed, they believed some who said that this fleet was being prepared to escort safely the ships that were sailing from Spain to the Indies. This seemed the more probable because the ships were so large and vast that the Spaniards seemed never likely to entrust them to the shallow and dangerous British sea.

units.la: Tandem cum Rex Galliæ in fine Maii Reginæ Angliæ di-sertis verbis nunciaret, vt sibi caveret, quia certior iam factus erat, tantam inuasionem ei imminere, vt metueret, ne omnis eius tam militum quam nauium vis sufficeret ad eas è finibus suis arcendas, &c.
units.tr: At last, when the King of France at the end of May told the Queen of England in plain words to take care of herself, since he was now certain that so great an invasion was threatening her that he feared all her strength of soldiers and ships would not suffice to keep them from her shores, etc.

units.la: Regina tum diligentius se armare cæpit, &c.
units.tr: The Queen then began to arm herself more diligently, etc.

units.la: Maiores instruxit circiter 100. minores circiter 40. aut 50. Eas dispositit per portus sub præfectis, Carolo Howardo, Francisco Draco.
units.tr: She equipped about 100 larger ships and about 40 or 50 smaller ones. She distributed these among the harbours under commanders, Charles Howard and Francis Drake.

units.la: Terra etiam per omnem Angliam populus armabatur.
units.tr: Throughout all England the people also were being armed.

units.la: Sunt inter Nobiles Anglos quidam, quos Recusantes vocant, hoc est Papistas. Hos, ne quid nocere possent, Regina certis locis constitui iussit, expresse mandans vt humaniter & amice exciperentur.
units.tr: Among the English nobles there are some whom they call Recusants, that is, Papists. Lest these should do any harm, the Queen ordered them to be placed in certain places, expressly commanding that they be received humanely and kindly.

units.la: Prouinciæ Hollandiæ & Zelandiæ etiam se ad defensionem parárunt, non magnas naues Hispanorum, quæ dicebantur, sed paruas quas Parmensis in Flandria parabat metuentes. Habuerunt igitur supra 90. naues paruas, obsederuntque iis omnes Flandriæ portus incipientes à Scaldi fluuio siue à Liloo oppido, pergentesque Grauelingam usque fere Caletum, maritimasque omnes suas Ciuitates firmo præsidio muniuerunt.
units.tr: The provinces of Holland and Zeeland also prepared for defence, fearing not the large ships of the Spaniards, as they were called, but the small ones which Parma was building in Flanders. They therefore had more than 90 small ships, and with these they blockaded all the ports of Flanders, beginning from the river Scheldt or the town of Lillo, and extending as far as Gravelines, nearly to Calais, and they fortified all their maritime cities with a strong garrison.

units.la: Zelandiæ Admiralius Iustinus Nassouius stationem illam accepit cum 35. nauibus, non ita magnis, sed optime instructis tormentis, nautis classiariis magno numero etiam 1200. militibus, in eaque statione tam diligenter excubauit, ut Parmensis cum sua classe per nullum Flandriæ portum in mare progredi potuerit.
units.tr: Justinus Nassau, Admiral of Zeeland, took up that station with 35 ships, not very large but excellently equipped with guns, with a great number of sailors and marines, and also 1,200 soldiers. He kept watch at that station so diligently that Parma with his fleet could not put out to sea through any port of Flanders.

units.la: Interea classis Hispanica ex portu Vlisponensi soluens in mare processit, 29. Maii anno 1588. Præfecto ei duce Medinæ Sidoniæ, atque Portum Coroniæ in Gallicia cursum direxit: vbi insuper militem bellicumque apparatum assumpsit, quia portus iste inter Hispanicos Angliæ est proximus.
units.tr: Meanwhile the Spanish fleet, sailing out from the port of Lisbon, put out to sea on 29 May 1588, under the command of the Duke of Medina Sidonia, and directed its course to the port of Corunna in Galicia, where it took on yet more soldiers and war supplies, because that port is the nearest of the Spanish ports to England.
