units.la: Dum nauigarent tanta insurrexit tempestas, vt classis tota dispergeretur, adeo vt postquam ad suos rediit Dux, circiter octuaginta naues tantum repererit, ad quas reliquæ paulatim conuenerunt, octo exceptis, quæ malos perdiderunt.
units.tr: While they were sailing, so great a storm arose that the whole fleet was scattered, so that when the Duke returned to his own, he found only about eighty ships, to which the rest gradually gathered, except eight, which lost their masts.

units.la: Cum iam Classis in Coronia se refecisset, mandatagueindies à Rege acciperet, vt iter accelararet, die 21. Iulii nauigauit, & die 29. Iulii venit ad ostium freti seu canalis Anglici.
units.tr: When the fleet had already refitted at Corunna, and was receiving orders from the King day by day to hasten its journey, it set sail on 21 July, and on 29 July it came to the mouth of the strait, or the English Channel.

units.la: Admiraldus Carolus de his certior factus, subito Pleymontha die 29. Iulii hora quarta pomeridiana, quasdam naues e portu eduxit.
units.tr: Admiral Charles, having been informed of this, at once on 29 July at four in the afternoon led some ships out of the harbour of Plymouth.

units.la: Circa meridiem diei 30. Iulii conspecta ab Anglis est classis Hispanica, quæ vento Austro-Africo recta Pleymontham ferebatur.
units.tr: Around midday on 30 July the Spanish fleet was sighted by the English; it was being carried straight towards Plymouth by a southwest wind.

units.la: Sed portum eum praeternauigauit, quam insecutae naues Anglicanae, ventum Hispanis praeripientes, eius commoditate classem Hispanicam adoriebantur, vbi pluribus tormentorum ictibus sese inuicem petebant.
units.tr: But he sailed past that harbour, and the English ships that followed, seizing the wind from the Spaniards, used its advantage to attack the Spanish fleet, where they fought one another with many blows of artillery.

units.la: Die 31. Iulii Angli adeo appropinquabant, vt Hispanos Musqueti, vt vocant, ictu possent pertingere, ibi Admiraldus Anglorum creberrimis tormentorum ictibus Vice-Admiraldum Hispanorum infestabat. Hispani dum animaduertentes agilitatem Anglicarum nauium in exonerandis ab omni parte in hostem, conglobati manserunt in forma semilunii, paruis vtentes velis, ne alii aliis celerius irent.
units.tr: On 31 July the English came so close that they could reach the Spaniards with musket shot, as they call it. There the English Admiral kept harassing the Spanish Vice-Admiral with very frequent blasts of artillery. The Spaniards, noticing the agility of the English ships in unloading their guns on the enemy from every side, kept themselves massed in the form of a half-moon, using small sails so that they would not outpace one another.

units.la: Dumque hoc modo progrediuntur, imo ex maioribus eorum triremibus (quas Galiassas vocant) magna vi tormentorum oppugnatur, adeo, vt classis totius ordo in angustum eius causa cogeretur. Quo factum est, vt principalis Galeona Ciuiliae, qua vehebatur Petrus Valdesius & alii, malum ex violenta proximae nauis collisione fregerit, atque ita classem assequi non potuerit.
units.tr: As they advanced in this way, their larger galleys (which they call galleasses) were assailed with great force of artillery, so that the whole line of the fleet was crowded into a narrow space. As a result, the flagship Ciuiliae, in which Peter Valdés and others were travelling, broke its mast in a violent collision with a neighbouring ship, and so was unable to rejoin the fleet.

units.la: Primo Augusti Drakius Valdesii illam nauem obuiam habuit, ad quam speculatores suos emisit, intellectoque, quod Valdesius adhuc cum 450 viris in ea esset, dedi eam sibi petiit. Valdesius honoris sui causa conditiones prius aliquas proponi, easque per suos ad Drakium deferri iussit, qui Valdesio respondit, otium iam sibi non dari contrahendi. Si vero dedere sese vellet, experietur se clementem & humanum. Sin mortem oppetere pugnando statuisset, sentiret eum virum. Ex quo responso Valdesius cum suis intelligens, se in manus Drakii ipsius incidisse, celebritate nominis eius commoti, se ipsi dediderunt, humanumque illum sunt experti.
units.tr: On 1 August Drake came upon that ship of Valdés and sent his scouts to it. Learning that Valdés was still aboard with 450 men, he demanded its surrender. Valdés, for the sake of his honour, ordered that some terms first be proposed and carried through his men to Drake. Drake replied that no time was now given him for negotiating. If he wished to surrender, he would find Drake merciful and humane; but if he had resolved to meet death by fighting, he would find him a man. On hearing this reply, Valdés and his men understood that they had fallen into the hands of Drake himself, and, moved by the renown of his name, they surrendered and found him humane.

units.la: Ipse Valdesius cum Nobilibus & 40. aut 50. ad ipsum pertinentibus in Drakii nauim conscenderunt. Reliqui Pleymontham sunt delati, vbi sesquiannum ad redemptionem sunt asseruati. Eodem die incensa est nauis magna, & ab Anglis capta, su- pererat adhuc multum pulueris nitrosi, &c.
units.tr: Valdés himself, with the nobles and forty or fifty men attached to him, went aboard Drake's ship. The rest were carried to Plymouth, where they were kept for a year and a half awaiting ransom. On the same day a great ship was set on fire and taken by the English; a large quantity of nitrous powder was still left in it, etc.

units.la: Die Martis 2. Aug. cum classis iam esset ex aduerso Portlandiæ ventus ab Aquilone flare coepit, atque ita factum est, vt Hispani ventum nacti sint fauentem ad inuadendos Anglos. Sed Angli, quod minores haberent naues & agiliores, venti prærogatiuam rursum Hispanis præripuerunt. Quo Hispani ad pugnam magis incitati, quam antea videbantur. Sed cum Angli ab initio diei omni genere tormentorum, tam magnorum quam paruorum, continuo & indefesse eos impugnarent, Hispani rursum, agmine facto, naues suas omnes in arctum conglobarunt, vt facile appareret eos non inuadere alios, sed defendere tantum se velle, & ad præscriptum sibi locum pergere, qui fuit prope Duynkerkam, vt ibi cum Permensevires iungerent, qui paruis suis nauibus, quasi sub vmbra magnarum tutius ire statuerat, atque ita totam expeditionem circumspecte instituerat.
units.tr: On Tuesday, 2 August, when the fleet was already off Portland, a wind began to blow from the north, and so it happened that the Spaniards got a favourable wind for attacking the English. But the English, because their ships were smaller and more nimble, again snatched the advantage of the wind from the Spaniards. The Spaniards were more stirred to battle than they had seemed before. But since the English, from the start of the day, assailed them continually and tirelessly with every kind of artillery, great and small, the Spaniards again drew up in formation and crowded all their ships together into a tight mass. It was clear that they were not attacking others but wished only to defend themselves and to make for the place assigned to them, near Dunkirk, where they were to join the forces of Parma, who had resolved to go more safely under the shadow of the large ships with his small vessels; and so he had carefully arranged the whole expedition.

units.la: Hæc erat omnium cruentissima pugna, in qua Admiralius in medio hostium pugnans, & videns quendam proculstantem compellabat his verbis: O Georgi, quid facis? spem meam & opinionem de te eludes? mene deseres? Quibus ille incitatus continuo accedit, & hostes aggreditur, virique fortissimi officium facit. Nomen huius Capitanei erat Georgius Kenner, vir multa prælia marina expertus.
units.tr: This was the bloodiest of all the battles. In the midst of the enemy, the Admiral was fighting, and, seeing a certain captain hanging back, he addressed him in these words: "O George, what are you doing? Will you mock my hope and opinion of you? Will you desert me?" Stirred by these words, the man at once went forward, attacked the enemy, and performed the duty of a most brave man. The name of this captain was George Kenner, a man experienced in many sea battles.

units.la: In hoc conflictu expugnata ab Anglis est magna quædam nauis Veneta, cum aliquot minoribus.
units.tr: In this encounter the English took a large Venetian ship, along with several smaller ones.

units.la: Crescebat interea Anglorum classis, ad quam ex omnibus Regni portubus, naues & homines confluebant, quia omnes eo tanquam ad Campum verae laudis & gloriae adipiscendę debitumque patriae seruitium præstandi confluebant.
units.tr: Meanwhile the English fleet was growing, and ships and men were flocking to it from all the ports of the kingdom, because everyone gathered there as to a field of true praise and glory, and to render the service they owed their country.

units.la: Nomina illorum clarorum virorum vide in historia, &c.
units.tr: For the names of those famous men, see the history, etc.

units.la: Atque ita factum est, vt numerus nauium Anglicarum supra centesimum surrexerit. Quae cum Doueriam appropinquarent, ad numerum 100. aut 120, fuerunt auctae, non tamen eius magnitudinis, vt Hispanos oppugnare possent, exceptis 22. aut 23. Reginae nauibus maioribus, quae solae fere sua praesentia hosti opinionem aliquam de viribus classis Anglicae reliquerunt, cuius nautae & milites ad vndecim millia aestimabantur.
units.tr: And so it came about that the number of English ships rose above one hundred. As they approached Dover, they were increased to a number of 100 or 120, but they were not of such size as to be able to attack the Spaniards, except for 22 or 23 larger ships of the Queen, which almost alone, by their presence alone, left the enemy with some impression of the strength of the English fleet. Its sailors and soldiers were estimated at eleven thousand.

units.la: 3. Augusti pugna solum fuit inter maiores triremes (Galeasas) & Anglos. Et licet Hispani eo die praerogatiua gaudebant, tamen Anglos superare nequiuerunt.
units.tr: On 3 August the fighting was only between the larger galleys (galleasses) and the English. And although the Spaniards rejoiced that day in their advantage, they were unable to overcome the English.

units.la: Eo die Anglorum classis in quatuor partes est distributa.
units.tr: On that day the English fleet was divided into four squadrons.

units.la: 4. Augusti cum Hispani iam essent ex aduerso Insulae Vectis, Admiralius Angliae comitatus optimis suis nauibus maxima vi & horrendo impetu Admiraldum Hispaniae, qui in media sua erat classe, est aggressus.
units.tr: On 4 August, when the Spaniards were already off the Isle of Wight, the Lord Admiral of England, accompanied by his best ships, attacked with great force and terrible impetus the Admiral of Spain, who was in the middle of his fleet.

units.la: Quod vbi vidit Hispanus, adiutus potentissimis suis nauibus contra iuit, terribilem pugnam cum Anglo ingrediens. Opponebatur enim latus lateri, simulque tormenta omnia in se mutuo eiaculabantur, 300. aut 400. pedum spacio a se mutuo distantes.
units.tr: When the Spaniard saw this, he came forward, aided by his most powerful ships, entering into a dreadful battle with the Englishman. For side was set against side, and all their artillery was discharged at one another from a distance of 300 or 400 feet.

units.la: 5. Augusti Admiraldus Angliae ornat quosdam balteo equestri, qui se in pugna viriliter gesserant, & accipit nuntium, Guisianos in Gallia Hispanis nullum, quod timebat, auxilium mittere.
units.tr: On 5 August the Lord Admiral of England decorated certain men with a knight's belt, who had acquitted themselves manfully in the battle, and he received word that the Guisians in France were sending the Spaniards no help, which was the thing he feared most.

units.la: 6. Augusti Hispani anchoras eiecerunt in conspectu Caleti, tendentes versus Duynkerkam, vt Parmensis classis iungeretur. Angli has sequentes anchoras valde prope eiecerunt.
units.tr: On 6 August the Spaniards cast anchor in sight of Calais, heading for Dunkirk, so that they might join the fleet of Parma. The English, following them, cast anchor very close to them.

units.la: Parmensis audiens de classe Hispanica, 7. Augusti vota beatae Mariae Hallensi in Hannonia (quam religionis causa visitarat) fecerat, indeque discedens Brugas septimo Augusti venit.
units.tr: When Parma heard of the Spanish fleet, on 7 August he made a vow to the Blessed Mary of Halle in Hainaut (which he had visited for religious reasons), and leaving there, he came to Bruges on 7 August.

units.la: 7. Augusti Duynkerkam proficiscens sonitum bombardarum audiuit.
units.tr: On 7 August, proceeding towards Dunkirk, he heard the sound of cannon.

units.la: Die 9. Augusti Duynkerkam venit, cum iam Hispanorum classis omnis praeternauigasset, nec interea vlla ipsius nauis ad classem egredi, aut suppetias ei ferre fuerat ausa, praemetu triginta quinque Hollandicarum & Zelandicarum navium, quae sub Imperio Admiraldi Iustini Nassouii ibi excubias agebant, & nullam Hispanicam navim admittebant.
units.tr: On 9 August he came to Dunkirk, when the whole Spanish fleet had already sailed past, and in the meantime none of his ships had dared to put out to join the fleet or bring it help, for fear of thirty-five Dutch and Zeeland ships, which under the command of Admiral Justinus of Nassau kept watch there and admitted no Spanish ship.

units.la: Videtur autem ipsius Parmensis Hispanorumque ea fuisse expectatio, ut naves omnes Anglicae & Belgicae statim, visa Hispanorum & Parmensium classe, fugerent, & loco ipsis cederent, solumque id darent operam, quo se defenderent, portusque suos & loca maritima ab invasione tuerentur.
units.tr: It seems, however, that this was the expectation of Parma himself and of the Spaniards: that as soon as they saw the Spanish and Parmese fleet, all the English and Belgian ships would flee and yield their place, and would apply themselves only to defending themselves and protecting their harbours and maritime places from invasion.

units.la: Consilium itaque & institutum eorum fuit, ut Parmensis leuibus suis nauibus tanquam sub umbra & alis Hispanicae classis omnes suas copias, arma & apparatum omnem bellicum adduceret, iunctisque ita viribus invasionem faceret, aut dum Anglica classis pugna contra Hispanicam implicaretur, praeternauigaret, oramque aliquam invaderet, quam commodissimam iudicasset. Quod (ut ex captiuis intellectum postea est) facere statuebant per fluuium Tamesim, in cuius ripis, cum haud difficulter viginti aut triginta veteranorum suorum millia primo appulsu collocare se posse putaret, facile ea ratione Londinum Angliae metropolim occupari posse, cum suis credebat, quia parvae naves fluminis ripas legentes copias terrestres fuissent comitatae, tum quod vrbs parum esset munita, & facilis expugnatu, ob Ciuium mollitiem & belli dissuetudinem, qui continuo & indefesso labore superari facile possent, siquidem primo impetu non expugnarentur.
units.tr: Their plan and design therefore was that Parma, with his light ships, as though under the shelter and wings of the Spanish fleet, would bring over all his troops, arms and every kind of military equipment, and that, joining forces in this way, he would make the invasion, or, while the English fleet was engaged in battle with the Spanish, would sail past and attack whatever shore he judged most suitable. As was learned afterwards from prisoners, they intended to do this by way of the river Thames. He believed that on its banks, where he could without much difficulty station twenty or thirty thousand of his veteran soldiers at the first landing, London, the metropolis of England, could easily be seized in that way, as he and his men thought, because small boats following the river banks would accompany the land forces; and also because the city was poorly fortified and easy to storm, owing to the softness of its citizens and their unfamiliarity with war, who could easily be overcome by continual and tireless labour, if indeed they were not overcome at the first onset.

units.la: Spes etiam non parua eos fouebat, plures Reginae futuros inobedientes & immorigeros, qui praesenti rerum administratione non essent contenti, ut Papistae, & alii. Item, qui Reginae Scotiae partibus fauebant, quae opportune tum recens mortis supplicio fuerat affecta, quos omnes turbas & factiones excitaturos expectabant.
units.tr: They were also greatly encouraged by the hope that many of the Queen's subjects would prove disobedient and unruly, being discontented with the present administration of affairs, as Papists and others were; likewise those who favoured the cause of the Queen of Scots, who had just then been opportunely put to death, and whom they expected would stir up all kinds of disturbances and factions.

units.la: Cum igitur Hispanorum classis in anchoris prope Caletum iam staret, vt interea cum Parmenfi consilia agitaret, quid sibi pro Regis mandato, & præsenti rerum statu præcipue esset faciendum. Iamque (vt postea intelligemus) inter se statuissent 12. Augusti, die videlicet veneris, coniunctis viribus animisque, cuius causa venerant, exequi: Admiraldus Angliæ Reginæ literis (7. Augusti) ex aula admonitus, classem Hispanicam statione illa & anchoris fugandam aut inuadendam censuit, eaque gratia, vt illa præscripsit, statim octo naues e vilioribus & abiectioribus, quas præ manibus habebat, sublatis ex iis rebus, quæ precii alicuius videbantur, puluere nitrolo, pice sulphurata, omnibus eius generis materiis ad incendia excitanda compositis repleuit: machinasque bellicas & bombardas puluere bombardico, ferramentis saxisque instruens, naues ita 7. Augusti die dominico, secunda hora post mediam noctem, vento & æstu secundis dimisit. Quæ cum iam aliquantum progressæ essent, desertæ ab iis, qui eas gubernabant, & incensæ recta in Hispanicam classem ferebantur: quare incendium de nocte tantum Hispanis terrorem, trepitudinemque incussit (metuebant enim ne eiusmodi hæ essent, quales erant Infernales illæ naues, quas puluere bombardico & saxis repletas, ante triennium in obsidione Antuerpiæ Frider. Ienebelli ad pontem à Parmenfi in Scaldi extructum effringendum confecerat) vt amputatis statim anchorarum rudentibus & cordis, erectis velis in apertum Oceanum satis confuse se receperint.
units.tr: Therefore, while the Spanish fleet already lay at anchor near Calais, they were to deliberate with Parma meanwhile about what they should do, according to the King's command and the present state of affairs. And now (as we shall learn afterwards) they had decided between themselves that on 12 August, namely on Friday, they would carry out, with united strength and spirit, the purpose for which they had come. The Lord Admiral of England, admonished by letters from the court (of 7 August), judged that the Spanish fleet must be driven off or attacked from that station and its anchorage. For this purpose, as those letters prescribed, he at once filled eight of the meaner and more worthless ships that he had at hand, after removing from them whatever seemed of any value, with nitrous powder, sulphurous pitch, and all materials of that kind compiled for kindling fires; and furnishing them with war machines and bombards loaded with gunpowder, iron and stones, he sent the ships off on 7 August, a Sunday, at the second hour after midnight, with wind and tide in their favour. When they had gone some distance, deserted by those who steered them, they were set alight and carried straight towards the Spanish fleet. The fire by night struck great terror and confusion into the Spaniards, for they feared that these were like those infernal ships which Frederick Genebelli had built three years before, at the siege of Antwerp, filled with gunpowder and stones, to break the bridge which Parma had built across the Scheldt. So, cutting at once the cables and ropes of their anchors, and raising their sails, they withdrew in some disorder into the open ocean.

units.la: In qua trepidatione ingens triremis Prætoria, vulgo Galeassa Capitanea, alterius cuiusdam nauis rudentibus implicata adeo fuit, vt clauus eius laxatus & amissus ea ratione fuerit. Quare cum iam gubernari amplius non posset, impetu fluxus marini ad littus Caletanum in vadum quoddam deiicitur, vbi statim à multis Anglicis nauibus minoribus (quas Pinassas vocant) oppugnatur. Quæ cum machinis tormentisque suis quidam
units.tr: In this confusion the great flagship galleass, commonly called the Capitana galleass, became so entangled in the cables of another ship that her rudder was loosened and lost. Since she could no longer be steered, the force of the tide drove her onto a shoal off the Calais shore, where many smaller English ships (which they call pinnaces) immediately attacked her.

units.la: Anglici adornant 8. naues, quas incensas & ardentes noctu contra Hisp. Classem mittunt.
units.tr: Some of the English equip eight ships, set them on fire, and send them at night against the Spanish fleet.

units.la: Vnde territi Hispani fugiunt.
units.tr: Terrified by this, the Spaniards flee.

units.la: Triremis Hispan. classium amittit. dam eam percuterent, quia cominus cum ea congredi non audebant, Admiraldus Angliæ prælongam suam scaphàm cum 100. selectissimis suis militibus, Præfecto eius Prestano, eo misit. Horum aduentu alii audaciores facti, hostilem nauim inuadunt, quibus se opponit Gubernator, idemque quatuor Galearum Præfectus Hugo de Moncada eo fortius pugnans, quod è continenti suppetias sibi allaturas Parmensem consideret.
units.tr: The Spanish galleass is lost. Since they did not dare to engage her at close quarters, the English Admiral sent his very long pinnace, with 100 of his picked soldiers under its commander Preston, to strike her. By their arrival others, bolder now, attack the enemy ship. The pilot opposes them, and so does Hugo de Moncada, commander of four galleys, who fights all the more fiercely because he expects Parma to send help from the mainland.

units.la: Interea cum iam pugnam aliquandiu sustinuisset, globo sclopeti in capite percussus cecidit, multique ibi cum eo Hispani fuere interfecti, reliquorum plerique, vt se seruarent, in mare desilientes submersi fere omnes sunt. Euasit inter alios generalis classis inspector (quem illi vocant Viador General) Antonius Mauriques paucis comitatus, qui primus in Hispaniam certum nuntium de eis, quæ classi euenerant, tulit.
units.tr: Meanwhile, after he had held out in the fight for some time, Moncada was struck on the head by a musket ball and fell, and many Spaniards with him were killed. Most of the rest, trying to save themselves, leapt into the sea, and nearly all of them drowned. Among others, the general inspector of the fleet (whom they call the Viador General), Antonio Mauriques, escaped with a few companions. He was the first to carry certain news to Spain of what had befallen the fleet.

units.la: Ingens ista & vasta triremis, qua 300. mancipia ad remos sedentia, & 400. alii milites vehebantur, spacio trium horarum direpta ibi fuit, inuentaque inter alia sunt 50. millia Ducatorum thesauri Regii. Tandem cum mancipia solutis compedibus effugissent, Angli nauem incendere volebant, quod Caleti Præfectus Gourdanus permittere ipsi noluit, ob præiudicium & damnum, quod inde oppido & portui Caletano euenire potuisset, Anglos propterea tormentis inde arcens.
units.tr: That huge and vast galleass, which carried 300 slaves seated at the oars and 400 other soldiers, was plundered there over three hours, and among other things 50,000 ducats of royal treasure were found. At last, when the slaves had escaped from their shackles, the English wanted to burn the ship. The commander of Calais, Gourdan, would not allow this, because of the harm and damage that could have come from it to the town and harbour of Calais, and so he kept the English away with his artillery.

units.la: Cum iam 8. Augusti mane Hispana classis post dictam confusionem in ordinem se redegisset, maxima vi rursus ab Anglis oppugnantur, in conspectu Graueliugensium, vbi rursus venti prærogatiuam Hispanis Angli eripuerunt, qui commoditatem loci in statione Caletana perdere, ventique prærogatiuam prope Duynkerkam sibi eripi passi sunt, potius quam ordinem mutarent, aut vires suas iam coniunctas inter se & connexas separarent, solum ad defensionem se parantes.
units.tr: On the morning of 8 August, when the Spanish fleet had restored its order after the said confusion, it was attacked again with great force by the English, in sight of Gravelines. There again the English snatched the advantage of the wind from the Spanish. They had not wished to lose their favourable position at Calais, and when the advantage of the wind was taken from them near Dunkirk, they preferred not to change their formation, nor to separate their forces, now joined and linked together, and prepared only for defence.

units.la: Etsi autem inter Anglicanas naues multæ præstantes essent, & insignes, vix tamen 22. aut 23. earum fuerunt, quæ Hispanos (quæ nonaginta erant) magnitudine æquarent, aut adoriri eas commode possent. Quare Anglicanæ vtentes sua prærogatiua, hoc est, facilitate, qua ventis in quosuis partes facile verruntur, Hispanis sæpe proximè imminebant, tamque arcte eos vrgebant, vt hasta se mutuo contingere possent: atque ita modo vnum, modo alterum latus Hispanis præbentes, tormenta omnia, paruasque bombardas, & sclopeta in eos exonerabant, integrum diem in hoc violento pugnæ genere sine intermissione consumentes, donec puluis tormentarius & globuli eos deficerent, ibi destiterunt, satis habentes, quod Hispanos Caleto & Duynkerka fugassent: eoque modo, quo minus Parmensis copiis se iungerent impedire, & vento ipsis erepto, ab oris suis illos depulissent.
units.tr: Although many of the English ships were excellent and distinguished, there were scarcely twenty-two or twenty-three of them that matched the Spanish ships in size (and there were ninety Spanish ships) or could conveniently attack them. Therefore the English, using their advantage, that is, the ease with which their ships are turned by the wind in any direction, often bore down very close upon the Spanish and pressed them so tightly that they could almost touch each other with their spears. Thus, presenting now one side and now the other to the Spanish, they discharged all their guns, small cannon and muskets at them, spending the whole day in this kind of violent fighting without pause, until the gunpowder and shot ran out for them. There they stopped, content that they had driven the Spanish from Calais and Dunkirk. In this way they had prevented them from joining Parma's forces, and, having taken the wind from them, had driven them away from their own shores.

units.la: Hispani magnam eo die suorum cladem acceperunt; transuerberatis, perforatisque plurimis eorum navibus, magnamque contra tormentorum vim in Anglos eiaculati sunt: qui damnum quidem aliquod sunt passi, non tamen quod comparari cum aliis posset.
units.tr: The Spanish suffered heavy losses that day. Many of their ships were pierced and holed through, and they fired back at the English with great force of artillery. The English did suffer some damage, but not such as could be compared with the Spanish losses.

units.la: Nullam enim alicuius nominis aut navem aut virum desiderarunt. Accurata enim inquisitione habita, toto tempore, quo classis Hispanica Anglicas vicinasque oras prætereuecta est, Angli vltra centum e suis amisisse non inueniuntur: Idque cum navalis illius equitis Drakii navis plusquam quadragesies tormentis fuerit percussa, cubiculum eius bis globo traiectum, & sub finem pugnæ nobilis cuiusdam lectus, cui fessus incumbebat, impetu globi sub eo fuerit sublatus. Et huiusmodi acciderunt plura, e quibus animaduerti manifeste potest, Deum Anglos non sine miraculo conseruasse.
units.tr: For they lost no ship or man of any name. After careful inquiry, it was found that during the whole time the Spanish fleet sailed past the English and neighbouring shores, the English lost not more than a hundred men. This is so although the ship of the naval knight Drake was struck by artillery more than forty times, his cabin was pierced twice by a ball, and near the end of the fight a bed on which a certain weary nobleman was leaning was lifted from under him by the force of a ball. Many such things happened, from which it can clearly be seen that God preserved the English, and not without a miracle.

units.la: Eo die 2. aut 3. naues Hispan. sunt summersæ. Duæ Galeonæ, quod essent perforatæ, deseruntur, & vna a Flies-singensibus capta, altera ad Flandriam tendens oppugnata & capta est.
units.tr: On that day two or three Spanish ships were sunk. Two galleons, because they were holed, were abandoned, one was captured by the men of Flushing, and the other, heading for Flanders, was attacked and captured.

units.la: Vexillum in templo Lugduni Batauorum suspensum tantæ est longitudinis, vt in summis lacunaribus affixum solum contingat.
units.tr: A banner hung in the church at Leiden is of such length that, fixed to the highest vault, it just touches the floor.

units.la: Eodem fere tempore alia quædam nauis minor ad littus Flandricum, circa Blankebergam necessitate impulsa contra tumulos arenosos effracta, victores saluos emisit.
units.tr: At about the same time another, smaller ship, driven by necessity onto the Flemish coast near Blankenberge, was wrecked against the sandy hillocks, and let its crew go safe and sound.

units.la: Ita Deus non Anglos modo, sed Zelandos etiam potentissimas hostium suorum naues ostendere voluit, vt iis visis agnoscerent, quam exiguas contra tantam potentiam vires haberent, ni Deus animum, prouidentiam & fortitudinem eis dedisset, ipseque multis locis pro ipsis pugnasset.
units.tr: Thus God wished to show the English and the Zeelanders alike the most powerful ships of their enemies, so that on seeing them they might recognise how small their own forces were against such power, unless God had given them courage, foresight and strength, and had himself fought for them in many places.

units.la: 8. Die Augusti classis Hispanica Duynkerkam præternaui-gans, persequentibus eam Anglis, postmodo fugam parauit. Quam Anglorum pars vsque ad 11. vel 12. Augusti persecuta est, pars ad Flandricum littus appulit, vt Parmensi, si forte egredi vellet, vna cum cæteris prohiberet.
units.tr: On 8 August the Spanish fleet, sailing past Dunkirk with the English pursuing, afterwards prepared its flight. Part of the English pursued it until 11 or 12 August; part put in to the Flemish shore, so that together with the rest they might prevent Parma from coming out, should he perhaps wish to.

units.la: Parma classem Hispanicam reuersuram esse putabat: ideo se diligenter parat. Verum ea, capto circuitu per Scotiam & Hyberniam, iacturam multarum nauium patiens, domum redit. Et ex 134. nauibus Hispanicis tantum 35. sunt reuersæ.
units.tr: Parma thought the Spanish fleet would return, so he diligently made ready. But the fleet, having made the circuit by Scotland and Ireland and suffering the loss of many ships, returned home. Of 134 Spanish ships, only 35 came back.

units.la: In huius rei memoriam Zelandi nummum argenteum & æneum cudi iusserunt, qui in vna parte contineret arma Zelandiæ, cum hac inscriptione: Soli Deo gloria. In altera magnæ aliquot naues cum his verbis: Classis Hispanica. Et in circumferentia eius: Venit, Iuit, Fuit. Anno 1588.
units.tr: In memory of this, the Zeelanders had silver and bronze coins struck. On one side they bore the arms of Zeeland with this inscription: "Glory to God alone." On the other were several large ships with these words: "Spanish fleet." And around the edge: "It came, it went, it was. 1588."

units.la: Cuderunt & alium nummum, in cuius vna parte nauis erat fugiens, & mergens, in altera parte quatuor viri flexis genibus orantes, Deoque gratias agentes, cum hoc dicto: Homo proponit, Deus disponit, 1588.
units.tr: They also struck another coin: on one side was a ship fleeing and sinking, and on the other four men kneeling and praying, giving thanks to God, with this saying: "Man proposes, God disposes. 1588."

units.la: Dum admirabilis & supra fidem potens hæc classis Anglicas oras legebat, omnesque iam viderent & audirent, quod ante credere non poterant, populus omnis per Angliam
units.tr: While this admirable fleet, powerful beyond belief, was off the English shores, and everyone now saw and heard what before they could not believe, the whole people throughout England

units.la: ad Deum precibus suis & supplicationibus se conuertit. Præcipue vero exterarum nationum Ecclesiæ, (quibus maxima timendi causa, quibusque nominatim Hispani dira fuerant minati) continua ieiunia & supplicationes suis indicebant, vt Dei iram, furoremque ob peccata sua sibi iam imminentem auerterent, quod scirent, preces vnicum esse contra omnes hostes, calamitates, necessitatesque, refugium, solatium & medicinam, afflicto oppressoque humano generi.
units.tr: turned to God with their prayers and supplications. Especially the churches of foreign nations, for whom the cause of fear was greatest, and against whom the Spaniards had threatened dire things by name, appointed continual fasts and supplications, that they might avert the wrath and fury of God, now hanging over them for their sins. They knew that prayer is the only refuge, solace and remedy against all enemies, calamities and needs for afflicted and oppressed mankind.

units.la: Huiusmodi dies precum instituti etiam sunt per vnitas Belgii Prouincias.
units.tr: Days of prayer of this kind were also appointed throughout the united provinces of the Netherlands.

units.la: Cum iam classis Hispana aliquo tempore abiisset, dies Festus in Anglia mandato Reginæ, & in vnitis Belgarum Prouinciis iussu Ordinum publice indictus est, quo omnes templum conuenire, Deoque laudes & gratias ibi dicere iubebantur, iniunctumque ministris est, vt ad id populum sedulo adhortarentur. Is dies fuit 29. Nouembris, qui totus in ieiuniis, continuis precibus, & gratiarum actionibus consumptus ibi est.
units.tr: When the Spanish fleet had been gone for some time, a feast day was publicly proclaimed in England by the Queen's command, and in the united provinces of the Netherlands by order of the States. All were bidden to assemble in the churches and give praise and thanks to God there, and the ministers were charged to urge the people diligently to this. That day was 29 November, and it was spent entirely in fasting, continual prayer and thanksgiving.

units.la: Ipsa etiam Angliæ Regina Londini de tam gloriosa sua, suorumque liberatione Christiane triumphauit, morem Romanorum imitata, curruque triumphali per vrbem Londinensem (comitantibus eam solemniter omnibus Regni Ordinibus & Officiariis) vestibus triumphalibus vecta est a Palatio suo ad templum primarium Diuo Paulo sacrum, e quo deictorum Hispanorum insignia & vexilla pendebant, stabantque. Ciues omnes Londinenses ab vtroque latere platearum per societates suas, & ambacta cum signis & baneriis suis, erantque plateæ vtrinque vestitæ panno aureo, quæ cum dictis baneriis magnificum & splendidum valde reddebant prospectum. Regina in templo ingressa cum Clero & auliciis suis Deo gratias egit; publicamque cocionem in cœmiterio coram se haberi mandauit, cuius nullum aliud fuit argumentum, quam vt Deo laus, honor & gloria redderetur, nomenque Dei gratiarum actionibus extolleretur, verbisque suis populum lum alloquuta ad idem faciendum est adhortata, ad quæ populus maxima acclamatione ei longissimam felicissimamque vitam à Deo dari est precatus, ad confusionem hostium ipsius.
units.tr: The Queen of England herself also celebrated in London, as a Christian, her own and her people's glorious deliverance, imitating the custom of the Romans. She was carried in a triumphal chariot, dressed in triumphal robes, through the city of London, with all the orders and officers of the kingdom solemnly accompanying her, from her palace to the chief church, sacred to St Paul, from which hung and stood the insignia and banners of the defeated Spaniards. All the citizens of London, on both sides of the streets, came with their companies and guilds, bearing their own signs and banners, and the streets were hung on both sides with cloth of gold, which with the said banners made a very magnificent and splendid prospect. The Queen, entering the church with her clergy and courtiers, gave thanks to God. She then ordered a public sermon to be held before her in the churchyard, whose sole purpose was that praise, honour and glory should be rendered to God and his name extolled with thanksgivings. Addressing the people in her own words, she exhorted them to do the same. To this the people, with the greatest acclamation, prayed God to grant her a very long and most happy life, to the confusion of her enemies.

units.la: AD SERENISSIMAM ANGLIÆ REGINAM THEODORVS BEZA.
units.tr: TO THE MOST SERENE QUEEN OF ENGLAND, THEODORE BEZA.

units.la: S Trauerat innumeris Hispanus nauibus æquor,Regnis iuncturus sceptra Britanna suis.Tanti huius rogitas quæ motus causa? superbosImpulit Ambitio, vexit Auaritia.Quam bene te Ambitio mersit vanissima, ventus:Et tumidos tumida, vos superastis aquæ.Quam bene totius raptores orbis auarosHausit inexhausti iusta vorago maris.At tu, cur venti, cui totum militat æquor,Regina, ô mundi totius una, decus.Sic regnare Deo perge ambitione remota,Prodiga sic opibus perge iuuare pios,Vt te Angli longum, longum Anglis ipsa fruaris,Quam dilecta bonus, tam metuenda malis.
units.tr: The Spaniard had crossed the sea with countless ships, about to join the British sceptres to his own kingdoms. Why do you ask what cause moved so great an enterprise? Ambition drove him on, proud and restless, and Greed carried him along. How well did most vain Ambition sink him, and the wind, and the swelling waters overcame him, swollen themselves. How justly did the vast sea's whirlpool swallow those greedy plunderers of the whole world. But you, Queen, for whom the whole sea fights, sole glory of the entire world: reign thus for God, with ambition put aside; thus pour out your wealth to help the pious; so that the English may long enjoy you, and you them, as beloved by the good as you are feared by the wicked.

units.la: ET ALIVS.
units.tr: ANOTHER.

units.la: R Ex Erebi & Romæ, Gallorum & Iberidos ore,Et grauis horrendis pontus & aura minis,In tua fata simul conspirauere tot hostes,Posthabito, Christi gens studiosa, Papa:At tu freta Deo, & causæ bonitate tot hostesImpia tot forti vincis & arma manu.Fisa Deo gens, perge Deo, confidere tantum,Non vindex causam deseret ille suam. Parmenfis Tolen Infulam Zelandicam frustra expugnare conatus, inde ad obsidendam Bergam conuersus, operam etiam ibi perdidit.
units.tr: From the mouths of Erebus and Rome, of the Gauls and of Iberia, and from the sea and air heavy with dreadful threats, so many enemies have conspired together against your fate, having set aside, O Christ's zealous people, the Pope. But you trust in God, and by the goodness of your cause you conquer so many impious foes with a strong hand and arms. People who trust in God, go on; trust only in God: he, the avenger, will not desert his cause. Parma, having tried in vain to storm the island of Tholen in Zeeland, then turned to besiege Bergen, and there too lost his labour.

units.la: Moritur Comes Liceftriæ.
units.tr: The Earl of Leicester dies.

units.la: Oppidum Wachendonk obsessum à Petro Ernesto Mansfeldio, Schenkii auxilio & commeatu destitutum, salua vita & rebus, deditur. Decemb.
units.tr: The town of Wachendonk, besieged by Peter Ernest of Mansfeld and deprived of Schenk's help and supplies, surrenders, its lives and goods being spared. December.

units.la: Vltraiectenses turbę tandem componuntur opera Comitis Moerfæ, Ciuibus cum iis, qui secessionem inde fecerant, & Hollandis reconciliatis.
units.tr: The disturbances at Utrecht are at last settled through the efforts of the Count of Moers, the citizens being reconciled with those who had seceded from them, and with the Hollanders.

units.la: Varia belli stratagemata à Præsidiariis Ordinum & Schenkii edita.
units.tr: Various military stratagems devised by the garrison of the Estates and by Schenk.

units.la: Cameracenses, etiamsi hostilia multa paterentur, neutraliter se gerunt.
units.tr: Cambrai, although it suffers many hostilities, keeps itself neutral.

units.la: Cum coniurati in Gallia sub nomine Sanctæ Ligæ Regnum iam nimis aperte affectarent, Rex duos Guisios fratres Blesii interficiendos curat.
units.tr: When the conspirators in France, under the name of the Holy League, were already too openly aiming at the kingdom, the King had the two Guise brothers killed at Blois.

units.la: Anno M. D. LXXXIX. paulo post cædem Guisiorum moritur Regina mater.
units.tr: In 1589, shortly after the slaughter of the Guises, the queen mother dies.

units.la: Sorbona Parisiensis Regi nullam amplius obedientiam à subditis deberi censet, cuius sententiam Papa confirmat, dum Regem excommunicat. Hinc maiores Ciuitates ab eo deficiunt, quæ causa fuit cur Nauarrensi se iunxerit.
units.tr: The Sorbonne of Paris judges that subjects owe the king no further obedience, and the Pope confirms this judgment by excommunicating the king. Hence the greater cities revolt from him, which was the reason he joined himself to the Navarrese.

units.la: Parisienses cum Duce suo Aumolio ad Seulis profligantur, quo successu Rex Parisiensem obsidionem aggreditur, in qua ad vicum D. Claudæ à Monacho Iacobo Clemete interficitur.
units.tr: The Parisians, with their leader Aumale, are routed at Senlis; with this success the King attacks Paris by siege, and in the siege, at the village of St Cloud, he is killed by the monk Jacques Clément.

units.la: Moriens coram primis regni officiariis, totoque exercitu, Nauarręum successorem suum in regno declarat, qui regnum cum vtriusque religionis concessione suscepit, iamq; vires omnes ad debellandos coniuratos intendit.
units.tr: Dying, in the presence of the chief officers of the kingdom and the whole army, he declares the Navarrese his successor in the kingdom. The Navarrese takes up the kingdom with the concession of both religions, and now bends all his strength to crushing the conspirators.

units.la: In Belgio mouent seditionem præsidiarii Gertrudenbergenses. Hos obsidet Mauritius, quare partim vindictæ, partim auaritiæ causa oppidum Parmensi vendunt, quo nomine tanquam patriæ proditores proscribuntur. Mansfeldius Haymentum, Heylam, & alias arces quasdam occupat, vbi Hispani seditionem mouent.
units.tr: In Belgium the garrison of Gertruidenberg stirs up a mutiny. Maurice besieges them, whereupon they, partly for revenge and partly out of greed, sell the town to the Parmesans, for which they are proscribed as traitors to their country. Mansfeld occupies Haymentum, Heyla and certain other strongholds, where the Spaniards stir up a mutiny.

units.la: Varrabonus expugnat Blienbekam.
units.tr: Varrabonus storms Blienbeck.

units.la: Noritsius & Dracus expeditionem in Hispaniam cum Rege Portugalliæ suscipientes, dysenteria & aliis morbis (quibus maior pars militum absumpta est) impediti, nihil operæ pretium præstiterunt, quam quod in itinere multas naues frumento onustas ceperunt.
units.tr: Norris and Drake undertook an expedition into Spain together with the King of Portugal, but were hindered by dysentery and other diseases, which carried off most of the soldiers, and accomplished nothing worthwhile, except that on the way they captured many ships laden with grain.

units.la: Ianitzari & Spachii, Constantinopoli seditione mota, partem vrbis incenderunt.
units.tr: The Janissaries and the Spahis, after a sedition broke out at Constantinople, set fire to part of the city.

units.la: Parmensis ægrotans de multis, quibus offensus erat, apud Regem conqueritur.
units.tr: Parma, sick, complains to the King about the many things that have offended him.

units.la: Schenkius infeliciter Neomagum occupare tentans sub- mergitur, & honeste sepelitur, Augusto.
units.tr: Schenk, attempting unsuccessfully to seize Nijmegen, is drowned, and is honourably buried. August.

units.la: In Frisia Wilhelmus Nassouius aliquot arces & munimenta occupat.
units.tr: In Friesland William Nassau occupies several fortresses and defences.

units.la: Hollandi & Zelandi classium apparatum adornant.
units.tr: Holland and Zeeland make ready their fleets.

units.la: Comes de Moers vi pulueris nitrati succensi interimi- tur.
units.tr: The Count of Moers is killed when a charge of gunpowder is set alight.

units.la: Berkenses obsessi auxilium aliquoties accipiunt, & Varra- bonus profligatur, tandem tamen vrbs deditur.
units.tr: The people of Berken, besieged, receive help several times, and Varrabonus is routed; at last, however, the town surrenders.

units.la: Commeatus Steinbergensibus obsessis aduectus profligatis auxiliaribus intercipitur.
units.tr: Supplies brought to the besieged people of Steinbergen are intercepted once their auxiliaries have been routed.

units.la: Parmensis frustra Aquisgrano, aliisque Imperii Ciuitatib. insidiatur, dominium in ipsas sibi aperte vendicans, edicto nullam amplius neutralitatem admittens.
units.tr: Parma makes vain attempts to lay snares for Aachen and other cities of the Empire, openly claiming dominion over them and, by an edict, admitting no further neutrality.

units.la: M.D.XC. Bello in Gallia durante, respirant, & reficiunt se quodammodo Prouinciae vnitae, interea tam rerum ad Religionem spectantium, quam ciuilium & bellicarum curam rationemque habentes.
units.tr: In 1590, while the war in France goes on, the United Provinces take breath and in some measure recover themselves, meanwhile taking care and thought both for matters pertaining to religion and for civil and military affairs.

units.la: Prouinciae Regi reconciliatae male administrantur, militibus stipendia non soluuntur. Inter hos Hispani præcipue excitato tumultu vrbem Cortricensem in Flandria occupant.
units.tr: The provinces reconciled to the King are badly governed, and the soldiers are not paid. Among these, the Spaniards especially, stirring up a tumult, seize the city of Kortrijk in Flanders.

units.la: Adolphus Comes Newenar Ciuitatem & telonium Berk in suam potestatem redegerat, & postquam id per septennium obtinuerat, Ernestus Elector Colonienſ. id opera Caroli Mansfeldii rursus sibi vendicat, 3. Febr.
units.tr: Adolf, Count of Neuenahr, had brought the city and toll-station of Bergh under his power, and after holding it for seven years, Ernest, Elector of Cologne, reclaims it for himself through the efforts of Charles of Mansfeld. 3 February.

units.la: Mauritius Comes Nassouius opera Hierangeri, naue, in qua sub Cespitibus foco seruientibus (Dorff) milites latebant, vrbem Bredanam capit. Vbi quondam Troia inducto equo capta est, Mense Martio. Quam obrem Dux Parmensis per Mansfeldium copias suas eam rursus obsidendi causa vndique colligit, nihil tamen tentatur.
units.tr: Maurice, Count of Nassau, through the work of Hierange, takes the city of Breda by a ship in which soldiers lay hidden beneath peat serving as fuel (Dorff), just as Troy was once taken when the wooden horse was brought in. March. Because of this, the Duke of Parma gathers his forces together from every side through Mansfeld in order to besiege it again, but nothing is attempted.

units.la: Mauritius exercitum suum educit, propugnaculum Knottenberg e Regione vrbis Neomagensis erigi curat.
units.tr: Maurice leads out his army and has the bulwark Knotenburg erected opposite the city of Nijmegen.

units.la: Philippus Rex Hispan. sub praetextu protegendi iuuandique proceres Catholicos Gallos, bello Gallico se se immiscet.
units.tr: Philip, King of Spain, under the pretext of protecting and aiding the Catholic nobles of France, meddles in the French war.

units.la: Sixtus V. Pont. id temporis moritur.
units.tr: Pope Sixtus V dies at this time.

units.la: Comes Egmondanus cum valido exercitu in Galliam ad ducem Maynium proficiscitur, qui paulo post a Rege Nauarreo caeditur, Egmondano ipso in praelio occumbente.
units.tr: Count Egmont sets out for France with a strong army to join Duke Mayenne, who shortly afterwards is cut down by the King of Navarre, Egmont himself falling in the battle.

units.la: Vrbs Parisiensis a Rege obsidetur, ea ad extremitatem fere redacta, Regio autem exercitu inopia annonae laborante, auxilio Ducis Parmensis obsidione liberatur, Sept.
units.tr: The city of Paris is besieged by the King, and is brought almost to extremity; but the royal army, suffering from lack of provisions, is freed from the siege by the help of the Duke of Parma. September.

units.la: Status obsident Neomagum, quod a Carolo Mansfeldio defenditur, Iulio.
units.tr: The Estates besiege Nijmegen, which is defended by Charles of Mansfeld. July.

units.la: Parmensis oppidum Corbeil, quod paulo ante occuparat, iterum relinquit, & quamplurimis ex suis desideratis in Belgium reuertitur.
units.tr: Parma again abandons the town of Corbeil, which he had occupied a little before, and returns to Belgium with a great many of his men missing.

units.la: Mauritius Hemerda, Heila & munimentis prope Eischoft Heidem & Robental, iuncta Sternberga, potitur.
units.tr: Maurice takes Hemmen, Heila, and the fortifications near Eischoft, Heidem and Robental, together with Sternberg.

units.la: Hispani Britanniam inuadunt.
units.tr: The Spaniards invade Britain.

units.la: Conuentus Rhenenſ. & Westphal. Circulorum Coloniae habetur, inde Legati tam ad Ducem Parmensem, q; ordines Prouinciarum vnitarum mittuntur, qui restitutionem locor. Imperio subiectorum postulabant. His Ordines respondent, eius rei causam praesertim in Hispanos transferentes. Cum Colonienssibus & Leodiensibus de Neutralitate seruanda agunt.
units.tr: An assembly of the Rhenish and Westphalian Circles is held at Cologne; from it envoys are sent both to the Duke of Parma and to the Estates of the United Provinces, demanding the restoration of places subject to the Empire. To these the Estates reply, laying the blame for that matter chiefly on the Spaniards. They also negotiate with Cologne and Liège about keeping to neutrality.

units.la: Anno M.D.XCI.Imperator denuo reconciliationem cum Rege apud Ordines tentat, sed frustra.
units.tr: In 1591 the Emperor again tries to bring about a reconciliation with the King before the Estates, but in vain.

units.la: Status capiunt fortalitium ante Zutphen hoc astu: Qui-dam milites induunt vestes muliebres, & fingunt quasi secaturæ gramina pro pecudibus à Statibus fugarentur, ad portam confugiunt, & sic admissi custodes obtruncant, & fortalitium obtinent. Post continuo etiam vrbem sibi vendicant. In cuius obsidione Comes Eberfteinius globo petitus periit, Maio.
units.tr: The Estates capture the fort before Zutphen by this trick: some soldiers put on women's clothing and pretend to be cutting grass for cattle. Driven off by the Estates' men, they flee to the gate; admitted there, they cut down the guards and gain possession of the fort. Afterwards they also make themselves masters of the town. In its siege Count Eberstein was struck by a cannonball and perished. May.

units.la: Mauritius Dauentriam tormentis quatit, & deditione oc-cupat, 10.Iun.
units.tr: Maurice batters Deventer with artillery and takes it by surrender. 10 June.

units.la: Occupat & propugnaculum Delfziel cum aliis quibusdam locis.
units.tr: He also seizes the bulwark of Delfzijl, together with some other places.

units.la: Parmensis Knothenburg obsidet & oppugnat, eum Mauritius in Beloniam cum exerciru rediens, obsidionem soluere compellit, multis ex ipsius Equitibus cœsis, & confestim in Flandriam tendens, oppido Hulst potitur, & regionem Wa-sianam tributariam facit.
units.tr: Parma, besieging and attacking Knodenburg, is forced by Maurice, who returns into Belgium with his army, to abandon the siege, many of his horsemen being slain. Immediately heading into Flanders, Maurice takes the town of Hulst and makes the region of Waas tributary.

units.la: Parmensēque id impedire conante, & exercitum suum mittente in Geldriam reuersus, Neomagum tandem in potestatem redigit.
units.tr: While Parma tries to prevent this and sends his army, Maurice returns to Gelderland and at last brings Nijmegen under his power.

units.la: Prædones, vulgo Freybeuteri appellati, puniuntur.
units.tr: Pirates, commonly called Freebooters, are punished.

units.la: Angli, nauibus suis bellicis inopinato adortis, nauem Re-giam, la Reuengæ dictam, quamuis diu fortiterque resisteret, amittunt. Hoc damni tamen oppressis quibusdam nauibus, ex Orientali India mercibus onustis relarciunt, vnde Regis mercatura patefit.
units.tr: The English, attacking unexpectedly with their warships, lose the royal ship called the Revenge, although it resisted long and bravely. Nevertheless, with some ships damaged, they make good this loss with ships laden with goods from the East Indies, by which the King's trade is opened up.

units.la: Capitaneus Tempel noctu Petarto admoto, conatur per-rumpere portas Andernaci, sed irrito conatu, 29.Iulii.
units.tr: Captain Tempel, at night, with a petard applied, tries to break through the gates of Andernach, but the attempt fails. 29 July.

units.la: Bellum Gallicum nouo exercitu à Principe Anhaltino ex Germania adducto recrudescit, & contra Pontifex fœderatos Gallos milite & Bullis iuuat.
units.tr: The French war breaks out afresh with a new army brought from Germany by the Prince of Anhalt; the Pope, on the other side, aids the allied Gauls with soldiers and bulls.

units.la: Vrbs Rotomagensis à Rege obsessa,
units.tr: The city of Rouen is besieged by the King.

units.la: Parmensis cum exercitu in Galliam reuertitur.
units.tr: Parma returns with his army into France.

units.la: AnnoM.D.XCII. Parmęsis in itinere in Galliâ la Ferra ca-pta Rotomagum obsidione liberat, quem tamen Rex statim Sequanam transfire, & in Belgium recedere cogit. Ita Roto-magum & Luteria rursus obsidentur & coangustantur.
units.tr: In 1592 Parma, on the march in France, takes La Fère and relieves Rouen from the siege; but the King at once forces him to cross the Seine and withdraw into Belgium. Thus Rouen and Paris are again besieged and hard pressed.

units.la: Legati Imperatoris Bruxellas veniunt, ad pacem cum Pro-uinciis vnitis transfigendam.
units.tr: Envoys of the Emperor come to Brussels to bring about a peace with the United Provinces.

units.la: Ordines scriptis respondent, & tractationem certis de cau-sis recusant, vndeiis locis bellum quoque denuo redintegra-tur.
units.tr: The States replied in writing and, for certain reasons, refused to negotiate; in several places the war was renewed again.

units.la: Mauritius oppugnat Steinwik, quo potitus confestim ar-cem Couerdanam adoritur, machinis bellicis ferit suffodit-que.
units.tr: Maurice attacked Steenwijk, and having taken it at once, he moved against the citadel of Coevorden, striking and undermining it with siege engines.

units.la: Eam Verdugo liberare conatur; verum quamplurimis suo-rum militum cæsis repellitur, & arx sese dedit.
units.tr: Verdugo tried to relieve it, but after very many of his soldiers had been slain he was repulsed, and the citadel surrendered.

units.la: Wilhelmus Cliuiæ, Iuliæ & Montis Dux moritur,
units.tr: William, Duke of Cleves, Jülich and Berg, died.

units.la: Parmensis rursus expeditionem in Galliam adornat, sed di-em suum obit Atrebati, cum paulo ante Comes Fontanus in Belgium venisset.
units.tr: Parma again prepared an expedition into France, but he met his end at Arras, shortly after Count Fuentes had come into the Low Countries.

units.la: Petrus Ernestus Com. Mansfeldius, Gubernator Luzelburg. Gubernationem Belgii, ex confirmatione Regia, vsque ad ad-uentum Ernesti Archiducis Austriaci continuat.
units.tr: Peter Ernest, Count of Mansfeld, governor of Luxembourg, continued in the government of the Netherlands, by royal confirmation, until the arrival of Archduke Ernest of Austria.

units.la: Nobiles Belgiæ Regi addicti ab eo variis titulis, honoribus, officiisque cohonestantur, & decorantur.
units.tr: The Netherland nobles devoted to the King were honoured and adorned by him with various titles, dignities and offices.

units.la: Verdugo & Barlemont Couertensibus opem ferre fata-gunt, sed repelluntur. Idcirco obsessi dedunt se Statibus. Sep-temb.
units.tr: Verdugo and Barlemont strove to bring aid to the people of Covering, but they were driven back. Therefore the besieged gave themselves up to the States. September.

units.la: M. D. XCIII. Mortuo Parmensi Petrus Ernestus Com. Malsfeldius vsque ad Ernesti Archiducis aduentum in guber-natione à Rege confirmatus, Consilio Comitis Fontani, statu-it bellum summa seueritate gerere. Lytra inter milites hinc in-de, vulgo quartier, & contributiones sustulit. Quare etiam Prouinciæ vnitæ, fide publica & clientela data, vulgo Saluo-guardiis reuocatis & sublatis in Luzenburgicum ducatum vs-que omnia depręʒdantes euagantur. Mauritius Gertrudenberg arctissima obsidione cingit, suaque castra ita munit, vt à Mansfeldio nullo modo opprimi posset, & tandem oppidum sese dedere cogitur.
units.tr: In 1593, after the death of Parma, Peter Ernest, Count of Mansfeld, confirmed by the King in the government until the arrival of Archduke Ernest, on the advice of Count Fuentes, resolved to wage war with the utmost severity. He abolished the lodging of soldiers in turn, commonly called quartering, and the contributions. Wherefore the United Provinces, having revoked and withdrawn their safe-conducts, commonly called safeguards, roamed everywhere through the Duchy of Luxembourg, plundering everything. Maurice surrounded Gertruydenberg with a very close siege, and fortified his camp so that it could in no way be overwhelmed by Mansfeld; at last the town was forced to surrender.

units.la: Inde Mansfeldius propugnaculum Greuecourt inuadere cogitat, sed magna suorum iactura & periculo à Mauritio repellitur.
units.tr: Thereupon Mansfeld planned to attack the outwork of Grevenkoet, but with great loss and danger to his men he was repulsed by Maurice.

units.la: Idem frustra praesidiarios in Buscumducis introducere tentat.
units.tr: He likewise tried in vain to introduce a garrison into Bois-le-Duc.

units.la: Comes Solmensis proficiscitur in Flandriam, Mansfeldici milites in finibus tumultuantur.
units.tr: Count Solms set out for Flanders, and Mansfeld's soldiers mutinied in the border regions.

units.la: In Gallia confoederati cum Duce Maynio bonis admonitionibus nolunt auscultare, sed Parisiis congregantur, noui Regis eligendi gratia, ab Hispanis in Regem eligendus proponitur Ernestus Archidux, in vxorem ducturus Infantam filiam Regis Hispaniae. Sed is displicet, & magis fauetur Guisio, verum sufficienti exercitu, quo ad hoc indigebant, non instructi, magnae inter eos oriuntur contentiones.
units.tr: In France the confederates, with Duke of Mayenne, would not heed good advice, but gathered at Paris to choose a new king. The Spaniards proposed that Archduke Ernest be elected king, to marry the Infanta, the daughter of the King of Spain. But he was displeasing, and Guise was more favoured; yet, not having an adequate army, which they needed for this, they were not equipped, and great disputes arose among them.

units.la: Rex Gallicus Nauarraeus multorum consilio fit Catholicus, audit Missam, Ducem Niuernensem ad Pontificem, absolutionem impetrandi causa, ablegat. Hanc Pontifex metu Regis Hispaniae denegat. Quam ob rem multi Nobiles & Ciuitates ad Regem deficiunt.
units.tr: The King of France, Navarre, on the advice of many, became Catholic, heard Mass, and sent the Duke of Nevers to the Pope to obtain absolution. The Pope refused this out of fear of the King of Spain. For this reason many nobles and cities revolted from the King.

units.la: Anglia & Prouinciae vnitae in foedere contracto firmiter persistunt.
units.tr: England and the United Provinces remained steadfast in the alliance they had made.

units.la: Reformata in Gallia Regi sibi & ipsismet imminens periculum demonstrant. Eis Rex humaniter respondet.
units.tr: The Reformed in France pointed out to the King the imminent danger to himself and to them; the King replied to them kindly.

units.la: Mauritius in Belgio multas ciuitates etiam Brugas tentat, sed conatu irrito.
units.tr: Maurice attempted in the Low Countries many cities, even Bruges, but his attempt was in vain.

units.la: Tempestate multae naues Hollandicae summerguntur.
units.tr: In a storm many Dutch ships were sunk.

units.la: ERNESTVS ARCHIDVX AVSTRIÆ MAGNIFICE IN BELGIO EXCIPITVR.
units.tr: Archduke Ernest is magnificently received in Belgium.

units.la: Groningenses apud Caesarem & Regem conquerantur, à Comite Wilhelmo, qui etiam propugnacula Beling, Woldziel & Wede occupat, valde coangustantur.
units.tr: The Groningers complain to the Emperor and the King that Count William, who also occupies the strongholds of Beling, Woldziel and Wede, is pressing them very hard.

units.la: Verdugo & Com. Montensis Otmarsen, aliaque loca recuperant.
units.tr: Verdugo and Count of Mont recover Otmarsen and other places.

units.la: Com. Wilhelmus propugnaculum in Bourtringa extruit, quæ cum superatu esset difficilis, D. Comitem vi adoritur, hic se animose defendit, hanc ob causam retrocedens, Couerdam tota hyeme obsidet.
units.tr: Count William builds a stronghold at Bourtringa. When this proved difficult to take, he attacks the Count (Verdugo) by force. The Count defends himself bravely, and for this reason William withdraws and besieges Couerden through the whole winter.

units.la: Carolus Mansfeldius occupat Capellas, & in Belgium redit.
units.tr: Charles Mansfeld seizes Capellas and returns to Belgium.

units.la: Groningenses per glaciem Delfzielam conscendere conantur, sed repelluntur.
units.tr: The Groningers try to climb up to Delfzijl over the ice, but are driven back.

units.la: Hac æstate Stratagema in vrbem Traiect. à Mauritio institutum non succedit, hostem tamen obsidionem Couerdensem relinquere cogit, Aprill. & Groningam obsidet, quæ maxima vi tormentorum & suffossionibus & cuniculis oppugnata, tandem sese conditionibus dedidit.
units.tr: This summer a stratagem devised by Maurice against the city of Utrecht does not succeed; nevertheless it forces the enemy to abandon the siege of Couerden in April. He then besieges Groningen, which, after being attacked with the greatest force of artillery, by mines and by tunnels, finally surrenders on terms.

units.la: Ernestus Archidux Antuerpiam venit, scribit ad Prouincias vnitas cum oblatione, si reconciliationem petant, ipsæmet conditiones præscribant.
units.tr: Archduke Ernest comes to Antwerp and writes to the United Provinces, offering that, if they seek reconciliation, they themselves may prescribe the terms.

units.la: Statusrespondent, se ex prioribus rebus de futuris coniecturam sumere, ideoque ob Hispanorum perfidiam de pace tractare non posse, Mense Maio.
units.tr: The States reply that they judge future matters from past events, and therefore, because of Spanish treachery, they cannot treat of peace, in May.

units.la: Lopetius Reginam Angliæ interficere conatur, eodem modo Michael Remis, & Petrus Furius Mauritium, sed omnes deprehensi, pœnas luunt.
units.tr: Lopez tries to kill the Queen of England, and Michael Remis and Peter Furius try to kill Maurice in the same way, but all are caught and pay the penalty.

units.la: Philippus Nassouius in Lucemburgensi tractu damna dat.
units.tr: Philip Nassau does damage in the district of Luxembourg.

units.la: Hispani vincunt Statuum militem inter Vesaliam & Lippiam. Iohannes & Philippus Nassouii fratres in conflictu perePunt, Solmensis capitur.
units.tr: The Spanish defeat the soldiers of the States between Wesel and Lippe. John and Philip Nassau, brothers, perish in the fighting, and the Count of Solms is taken.

units.la: Ratisbonæ Comitia celebrantur, in quibus Imperatori contra Turcas auxilium promittitur.
units.tr: The Diet is held at Regensburg, at which aid against the Turks is promised to the Emperor.

units.la: Controuersiæ sunt ibidem inter protestantes, Elector FrideriFridericus IV. ibi fidei suæ Confessionem offert.
units.tr: Disputes arise there among the Protestants; Elector Frederick IV there offers his Confession of faith.

units.la: Prouinciæ vnitæ ad Baptismum filii Regis Scotiæ inuitantur.
units.tr: The United Provinces are invited to the baptism of the son of the King of Scotland.

units.la: Rex Gallus multos ex subditis ad reconciliationem admittit.
units.tr: The French King readmits many of his subjects to reconciliation.

units.la: Iohannes Castelius adolescens Regem Galliæ cultro in faucibus lædit.
units.tr: John Castel, a young man, wounds the King of France in the throat with a knife.

units.la: Iesuitæ è Gallia eliminantur.
units.tr: The Jesuits are expelled from France.

units.la: Rex Galliæ Regi Hispan. bellum denunciat, huic præficit Ducem Bullioneum, eique Ordines ex Hollandia in Luxemburgum subsidium mittunt.
units.tr: The King of France declares war on the King of Spain, and sets over it Duke de Bouillon; the States of Holland send auxiliaries to him in Luxembourg.

units.la: Itali tumultuantur, & ab Ordinibus iuuantur.
units.tr: The Italians stir up tumults and are aided by the States.

units.la: M.D.XCV. Ernesto Archiduce de obsidione Cameracen- se cogitante, Prouinciis Galliæ valde minatur, & bellum à Rege Galliæ publicatur.
units.tr: In 1595, while Archduke Ernest is planning a siege of Cambrai, he threatens the provinces of France severely, and war is proclaimed by the King of France.

units.la: Idem facit Rex Hispan. contra Principem Barnensem, hoc est, Nauarræum, qui confœderatos in protectionem suscipit. Hanc ob causam Ducatum Burgundiæ inuadunt Galli.
units.tr: The King of Spain does the same against the Prince of Béarn, that is, the Navarrese, who takes the confederates under his protection. For this reason the French invade the Duchy of Burgundy.

units.la: Ernestus Archidux Gubernator Belgii moritur 10. Februar. Interea Comes de Fuentes Fontanus est cum auctoritate.
units.tr: Archduke Ernest, Governor of Belgium, dies on 10 February. Meanwhile Count de Fuentes Fontanus holds the authority.

units.la: Hieraugerius insidiis capit arce Hoy, quæ est Episcopi Leodiensis. Nam duo milites in vestitu rusticano victualia & literas ab Episcopo, tanquam breui subsequuturo, bacchanaliorum tempore se ad ferre simulant, & sic intromissi, cum plures etiam aduolassent, Præfectum & alios occiderunt, & vrbem simul occuparunt. Sed id Hispani paulo post vi & deditione iterum recuperarunt.
units.tr: Hieraugerius, by an ambush, takes the citadel of Hoy, which belongs to the Bishop of Liège. For two soldiers, dressed as countrymen, pretend that they are bringing provisions and letters from the Bishop, who is to follow shortly, at the time of the carnival; and so admitted, when more had also flown in, they kill the commandant and others, and at the same time seize the town. But the Spanish soon afterwards took it back again by force and by surrender.

units.la: Comes Hohenlous vxorem Ducit Principis Auraici filiam natu maximam.
units.tr: Count Hohenlohe marries the eldest daughter of the Prince of Orange.

units.la: Prouinciæ vnitæ renouant Ordinationes monetarias.
units.tr: The United Provinces renew their monetary ordinances.

units.la: Ex Indiis 14. auri miliones Lisibonæ appulerunt.
units.tr: Fourteen million gold pieces arrive at Lisbon from the Indies.

units.la: Magnus Turcarum Imperator moritur.
units.tr: The great Emperor of the Turks dies.

units.la: Christiani præparant expeditionem contra nouum Imp. Turcicum. Huic præficitur Carolus Mansfeldius è Belgio in Vngariam vocatus.
units.tr: The Christians prepare an expedition against the new Turkish Emperor. Charles Mansfeld, called from Belgium to Hungary, is set over it.

units.la: In vrbe & ditione Embdensi seditiones.
units.tr: Seditions in the city and territory of Emden.

units.la: Ordines Prouinciarum vnitarum per nouam viam naues mittunt in Tartariam & Chimam.
units.tr: The Orders of the United Provinces send ships by a new route to Tartary and China.

units.la: Drakius & Hawkius in Anglia classem adornant.
units.tr: Drake and Hawkins prepare a fleet in England.

units.la: Duynkerkani magnas in mari prædas agunt.
units.tr: The Dunkirkers carry out great plunders at sea.

units.la: Rex Galliæ satisfacit reformatis, multi se cum illo reconciliant.
units.tr: The King of France makes satisfaction to the Reformed, and many reconcile themselves with him.

units.la: Verdugo in Ducatu Luzemburgico ab oppido Ferte repelitur, & Hispani ex Han eiiciuntur.
units.tr: Verdugo is driven back from the town of Ferte in the Duchy of Luxembourg, and the Spanish are expelled from Han.

units.la: Fontanus potitur arce Chateletana.
units.tr: Fontanus takes possession of the citadel of Châtelet.

units.la: Iterum instituitur tractatio de pace inter Prouincias vnitas & Regem, sed ab Hispanis suspenditur.
units.tr: Negotiations for peace between the United Provinces and the King are again set on foot, but are suspended by the Spanish.

units.la: Albertus Archid. Cardinalis in Belgio expectatur.
units.tr: Archduke Albert, Cardinal, is awaited in Belgium.

units.la: Dorlantium ab Hispanis obsidetur & capitur.
units.tr: Dorlan is besieged and taken by the Spanish.

units.la: Mauritius exercitum educit, inuadit propugnacula hostium in Flandria, tentat Grollam, sed frustra.
units.tr: Maurice leads out his army, attacks the enemy's strongholds in Flanders, tries Grol, but in vain.

units.la: Velitatio Mauritianorum cum Hispanis prope Wesaliam, in quo Comes Nassouius Philippus, & Comes Solmensis vulnerati, paulo post Berkæ moriuntur. Comes Ernestus Ludovicus captus lytro redimitur.
units.tr: A skirmish of Maurice's men with the Spanish near Wesel, in which Count Philip Nassau and the Count of Solms are wounded; shortly afterwards they die at Berg. Count Ernest Louis is taken and is ransomed for money.

units.la: Carolus Mansfeldius in Vngaria moritur dysenteria, antea Princeps à Cæsare nobilitatus.
units.tr: Charles Mansfeld dies of dysentery in Hungary; he had previously been ennobled as a Prince by the Emperor.

units.la: Cameracum à Fontano obsidetur & capitur.
units.tr: Cambrai is besieged and taken by Fontanus.

units.la: Vrbs Wirda stratagemate occupatur, & Comes Henricus deMonte captus in Hollandiam missus, vbi lytro soluto dimittitur.
units.tr: The town of Wirda is seized by a stratagem, and Count Henry de Monte is taken and sent to Holland, where he is released on payment of ransom.

units.la: Albertus Cardinalis Belgium gubernaturus venit in Italiam, & Philippus Princeps Auraicus Romam.
units.tr: Archduke Albert, about to govern Belgium, comes into Italy, and Prince Philip of Orange goes to Rome.

units.la: Philippus Dux Arschotanus moritur.
units.tr: Duke Philip of Arschot dies.

units.la: Langhar in Castellaun capite truncatur.
units.tr: Langhar is beheaded at Castellaun.

units.la: M. D. XCVI. excursiones Gallorum & Hispanorum vtrinq.
units.tr: In 1596 the French and Spanish make raids on each other.

units.la: Chriftophorus Mondragonius moritur.
units.tr: Christopher Mondragon dies.

units.la: Albertus Archidux Luzemburgum venit, quo Fontanus Elector Colon. & alii ipsum salutatum veniunt. Dux Pastranus moritur.
units.tr: Archduke Albert comes to Luxembourg, where Fontanus, the Elector of Cologne and others come to greet him. Duke Pastrana dies.

units.la: Guisius Massiliam eminus obsidet.
units.tr: Guise besieges Marseilles from a distance.

units.la: Ordinum Hollandiæ ad Principem Auraicum literæ. Eiusdem responsum.
units.tr: Letter of the Estates of Holland to the Prince of Orange, and his reply to it.

units.la: Excursiones Gallorum in agrum Atrebatensem.
units.tr: Raids of the French into the territory of Arras.

units.la: Albertus Archidux Bruxellæ magnifice excipitur.
units.tr: Archduke Albert is magnificently received at Brussels.

units.la: Massilienfis vrbis status, eiusq; à Rege Gallo recuperatio.
units.tr: The state of the city of Marseilles, and its recovery from the King of France.

units.la: Archiepiscopus Cameracensis moritur.
units.tr: The Archbishop of Cambrai dies.

units.la: Nauarræus Nobilitatem conuocat.
units.tr: The Navarrese summons the nobility.

units.la: Albertus Archid. Gubernator offert Hollandis pacem,
units.tr: Archduke Albert, Governor, offers peace to the Hollanders.

units.la: Comes Buranus cum fratre aut sorore colloqui petit.
units.tr: Count Bourg asks to confer with his brother or sister.

units.la: Belli initia sub Alberto Cardinali, qui Ferensibus commeatum conuehi curat.
units.tr: The beginnings of war under Cardinal Albert, who takes care that supplies are carried to the men of Ferre.

units.la: Caletensibus bellum parat, eorumque suburbia expugnat.
units.tr: He prepares war against the men of Calais and storms their suburbs.

units.la: Caletum deditur Alberto, & arx expugnatur.
units.tr: Calais is surrendered to Albert, and the citadel is stormed.

units.la: Hollandorum excursio in Brabantiam.
units.tr: A raid of the Hollanders into Brabant.

units.la: Caritas annonæ in castris Gallorum & Belgarum.
units.tr: Scarcity of provisions in the camps of the French and the Belgians.

units.la: Mauritius, Bulion & Stratus in Hagen congregati sunt.
units.tr: Maurice, Bouillon and Strouts meet together at The Hague.

units.la: Armada Hispanica cepit septem naues Anglicanas.
units.tr: The Spanish Armada captures seven English ships.

units.la: Albertus obsidet & capit Ardresiam.
units.tr: Albert besieges and takes Ardres.

units.la: Ferra deditur Nauarræo.
units.tr: Ferre is surrendered to the Navarrese.

units.la: Classis Anglicana ad expeditionem paratur. Eius Præfectorum rescriptum. E portu discedit.
units.tr: The English fleet is prepared for an expedition. The letter of its commanders. It sets sail from port.

units.la: Vrbem Calis Malis in Aa de Luzia inuadit, occupat, diripit, atque incendit cum multis nauibus atque aliis rebus.
units.tr: It attacks, seizes, plunders and burns the town of Calais, Malo, on the Aa of Lucia, together with many ships and other goods.

units.la: Hulstensis obsidio & deditio.
units.tr: The siege and surrender of Hulst.

units.la: Albertus Archidux Ambianum ex insidiis capit.
units.tr: Archduke Albert takes Amiens by ambush.

units.la: M.D.XCVII. Mauritiani profligant Hispanos, & Tournhaut vrbem capiunt.
units.tr: In 1597 Maurice's men rout the Spanish and capture the town of Tournhout.

units.la: Ambianum amissum à Rege Galliæ iterum obsidetur.
units.tr: Amiens, lost, is besieged again by the King of France.

units.la: Hollandi Vendlonæ insidias struunt, sed frustra.
units.tr: The Hollanders lay an ambush at Venlo, but in vain.

units.la: Duynkerkani grassantur mari. Duo prædones crudelissimo supplicio affecti.
units.tr: The Dunkirkers rage at sea. Two pirates are put to a most cruel death.

units.la: Hispanis inuasio Steinbekii male cedit.
units.tr: The Spanish invasion of Steinbeck turns out badly.

units.la: Galli munituri Ream ad Mosab Hispanis impediuntur.
units.tr: The French, about to fortify Rheinberg on the Maas, are hindered by the Spanish.

units.la: Nauis Statuum ad Cales capta.
units.tr: A ship of the States is taken at Calais.

units.la: Mauritius obsidet & capit Bergad Rhenum, mox & Moers.
units.tr: Maurice besieges and takes Berg on the Rhine, and soon after Moers.

units.la: Deinde transmisso Rheno in Frisia obtinet Grol. Septemb.
units.tr: Then, crossing the Rhine, he gains possession of Groningen in Friesland, in September.

units.la: Beuort vi capit, tum & Aldese accipit.
units.tr: He takes Beuvré by force, and then receives Oldeneel.

units.la: Expugnat & Linden, & sic Frisia potitur, Nouemb.
units.tr: He also storms Lingen, and thus gains possession of Friesland, in November.

units.la: Armada Anglicana tres naues ex India cum opib. adducit,
units.tr: The English Armada brings three ships from India with riches.

units.la: Antonius di Portugal ducit Mauritii Sororem, Status e- is annuos sumptus largiuntur.
units.tr: Antonio of Portugal marries Maurice's sister; the States grant him an annual allowance.

units.la: M. D. XCVIII. Etsi pro pace inter Reges est laboratum, tamen Status & Albertus inuicem hostiliter agunt. Ianuar.
units.tr: In 1598, although labour has been spent on peace between the Kings, nevertheless the States and Albert act hostilely toward one another, in January.

units.la: Status passim se muniunt, & militem in Rheinberg collocant.
units.tr: The States fortify themselves in various places and station soldiers in Rheinberg.

units.la: Albertus itidem in Artris & Hennegaw militem collocare volens repulsam patitur.
units.tr: Albert likewise, wishing to station soldiers in Artois and Hainault, suffers a repulse.

units.la: Comes Hermannus Statibus prædam adimit.
units.tr: Count Hermann takes booty from the States.

units.la: Comes Camerlandiæ Anglus in portu Lisibonæ prædam agit Iun.
units.tr: The English Count of Cumberland makes a raid on booty in the port of Lisbon, in June.

units.la: Naues ex Norduegia cum 300. homin. ad Scaldim vi tempestatis pereunt.
units.tr: Ships from Norway with 300 men perish in the Scheldt through the violence of a storm.

units.la: Sicarius Mauritium perempturus necatur.
units.tr: An assassin who was to kill Maurice is put to death.

units.la: Status causas edunt, quare pacem inire cum Hispanis non possint, idque picturis quibusdam figurant.
units.tr: The States publish the reasons why they cannot enter into peace with the Spanish, and set them forth in certain pictures.

units.la: Hispani Antuerp. propter defectum salarii tumultuantur. Aug.
units.tr: The Spanish at Antwerp stir up tumults because of lack of pay, in August.

units.la: Status aliquot ciues Antuerp. exeuntes in Bürgerhost / vi auferunt.
units.tr: The States seize by force some citizens of Antwerp who were leaving, and carry them off into the Bürgerhost.

units.la: Alberto Archid. promissa est Infanta Hispaniæ, Regis Philippi filia, cum 17. prouinciis Belgii & Comitatu Burgundiæ in dotem. Ideo cum habitum Cardinal. deposuisset, operam dat, vt Status sibi iurent. Pars igitur Statuum ei, sed nomine Infantæ, iurant, & sua priuilegia seruari petunt. Albert. abdicato Archiepiscopatu Toletano, ex quo tamen quotannis recipiat 5.M. Ducator. ad ducendam Infantam Hispan. Isabellam vocatur, & substituto in Gubernatorem Andrea Cardinale, patruele, 13. Sept. discedit, & per Luzelburg & Lutream in Italiam magno comitatu proficiscitur.
units.tr: The Infanta of Spain, daughter of King Philip, is promised to Archduke Albert, with the seventeen provinces of Belgium and the County of Burgundy as her dowry. Therefore, having laid aside the cardinal's habit, he takes pains that the States swear allegiance to him. Some of the States therefore swear to him, but in the name of the Infanta, and ask that their privileges be preserved. Albert, having renounced the Archbishopric of Toledo, from which nevertheless he receives 5,000 ducats yearly, is summoned to lead the Spanish Infanta Isabella, and, having appointed as Governor his cousin Cardinal Andrew, sets out on 13 September through Luxembourg and Lorraine for Italy, with a great retinue.

units.la: Franciscus Mendoza Admiralius Arragon, Hispanici exercitus in Belg. Præfectus, cum exercitu 30. M. transit Mosam ad Rormund & ad Rhenum tendit.
units.tr: Francisco Mendoza, Admiral of Aragon and commander of the Spanish army in the Netherlands, crosses the Maas at Roermond with an army of 30,000 and makes for the Rhine.
