units.la: Barlot contra præsidiarias Statuum naues infra Coloniam bombardas collocat, & eas abire cogit, quæ sic vsque ad Berk perfugiunt.
units.tr: Barlot places cannon against the States' guard ships below Cologne and forces them to withdraw; they flee as far as Berck.

units.la: Admiral occupat Orsoy Ciuitatem Ducis Cliuensis, & ripam Rheni vastat.
units.tr: The Admiral seizes Orsoy, a town of the Duke of Cleves, and lays waste the bank of the Rhine.

units.la: Comes Mauritius se quoque contra parat, & exercitum suum lustrat.
units.tr: Count Maurice also prepares to resist and reviews his army.

units.la: Consiliarii Cliuens. congregati, & vim deprecati, cum essent neutrales, nihil ab Admiralio impetrant. Sed is Comitatum Moers & Alpe, secus quam promisisse dicebatur, inuadit, Sept.
units.tr: The councillors of Cleves meet, appeal against the violence, but since they are neutral they obtain nothing from the Admiral. He nevertheless attacks the county of Moers and Alpen in September, contrary to what he was reported to have promised.

units.la: Hispani arcem Broech vi occupant, ibi Worichius à Daim Comes Falkenstein, & Oberstteinen. Dominus in Broech, misere occiditur & comburitur, 10. Octob.
units.tr: The Spaniards take the fortress of Broich by force. There Worich of Daun, Count of Falkenstein, and the lord of Oberstein are cruelly killed and burned in Broich, on 10 October.

units.la: Hispani oppugnant vrbem Berk, postquam puluis tormentarius calido globo tactus maximum detrimentum in vrbe dedit, ingrediuntur & Dinslaken & Holt, prædas agunt vtraq; ripa Rheni, & quia Isela fluuius exundauerat, ideo peruagantur Cliuiam, Westphaliam Episcopat. Monaster. & postulant sibi vrbes Rees, Emerich, Xanten, Gorch, Calkar, vnde incolæ passim aufugerút. Vrbem Wesel 100. M. Taler. & M. modiis frumenti multát, occupát Rees, Emerich, Dotekú, Schuleburg.
units.tr: The Spaniards besiege the town of Berck. After a hot cannonball struck the gunpowder store, causing great damage in the town, they enter it, and also Dinslaken and Holten. They plunder both banks of the Rhine, and because the river Issel had flooded, they roam freely through Cleves, Westphalia and the bishopric of Münster, demanding for themselves the towns of Rees, Emmerich, Xanten, Goch and Kalkar, so that the inhabitants fled in all directions. They fine the town of Wesel 100,000 thalers and many measures of grain, and seize Rees, Emmerich, Dottendorf and Schüttdorf.

units.la: Conuentus in Dortmund, inde ad Cæsarem & Principes scribunt, ibi Com. Mauritius indicat, sibi æque vt hostibus Hispanis licere vrbes Imperii inuadere, 29. Sept.
units.tr: A meeting is held at Dortmund, and from there they write to the Emperor and the princes. There Count Maurice declares that it is as lawful for him as for the Spanish enemies to invade the towns of the Empire, 29 September.

units.la: Imperator monet Albert. Archid. & Andream Cardinal. & Admiralium, tum Status, ne loca Imperii molestent, Nouem. Hispani Boucholtz Elect. Colon. vrbem ingressi sunt, diffugiunt incolæ 300. ædibus vacuis relictis, ingrediuntur, & Haltren, Dulmen, Werinc, Vreden, cum Ahaus, Broken, Rhene, & alias Episcop. Monaster. vrbes spoliant.
units.tr: The Emperor warns Archduke Albert, Cardinal Andreas, the Admiral and also the States not to molest the places of the Empire, in November. The Spaniards enter the town of Bocholt, belonging to the Elector of Cologne; the inhabitants flee, leaving 300 houses empty. They enter Haltern, Dülmen, Werne, Vreden with Ahaus, Borken, Rhede, and plunder other towns of the bishoprics and monasteries.

units.la: Osnabruk & Padeborn Episc. multant. In hisce grassationibus Hispani erga quosuis ferinam immanitatem exercuerunt. Moniales & alias virgines inaudita violentia constupraunt, fœtus grauidarum, vt dicebatur, exciderunt.
units.tr: They fine the bishops of Osnabrück and Paderborn. In these ravages the Spaniards showed savage brutality towards everyone. They violated nuns and other virgins with unheard-of violence, and, so it was said, caused pregnant women to miscarry.

units.la: Status cogunt Hispanos Emerico cedere, quam Duci Cliuensi restituunt. Dec.
units.tr: The States force the Spaniards to withdraw from Emmerich, which they restore to the Duke of Cleves, in December.

units.la: Admiral bonas leges dat, sed parum seruatas.
units.tr: The Admiral issues good laws, but they are little observed.

units.la: Hispani occupant Alen, Bekum & multas alias.
units.tr: The Spaniards occupy Alen, Bekum and many other places.

units.la: Elect. Colon. hæc grauamina Mauritio significat.
units.tr: The Elector of Cologne reports these grievances to Maurice.

units.la: In Episcopatu Monast præfectura Cloppenburg. 4. Taler præfectura Vechta plus, præfectura Sassinberg & Stromberg amplius Hispanis pendere coguntur.
units.tr: In the bishopric of Münster, the district of Cloppenburg is compelled to pay the Spaniards four thalers, the district of Vechta more, and the districts of Sassenberg and Stromberg yet more.

units.la: Incolæ Markiæ ab Hispanis expilantur, occupant Recklingenhausen.
units.tr: The inhabitants of the Mark are plundered by the Spaniards, who occupy Recklinghausen-Hausen.

units.la: Status occupant Seuenar, Hesdin & telonarium.
units.tr: The States occupy Sevenaer, Hesdin and a toll-station.

units.la: Conuentus Iuliacensium & Bergenf. Consiliariorum Dusseldorpi. Quidam Hispani Essenam inuadunt, occupant & Calcar, & immaniter agunt.
units.tr: A meeting of the councillors of Jülich and Berg is held at Düsseldorf. Certain Spaniards invade Essen, also seize Kalkar, and behave monstrously.

units.la: Ann. M. D. XCIX, Duynkerkii Dantiscanam, & Angli io. Hamburg. naues cum frumento rapiunt. Ianuar.
units.tr: In 1599, at Dunkirk, the Danzig and the English ships of Hamburg are seized with their grain, January.

units.la: Admiralius Vesaliæ per nuntium Apostolicum curat Euangelica templa in vsum Missarum consecrari.
units.tr: At Wesel, the Admiral, through the papal nuncio, arranges for Protestant churches to be consecrated for use as Masses.

units.la: Hispani Gochum sibi vendicant, spoliant.
units.tr: The Spaniards claim Goch for themselves and plunder it.

units.la: Iidem Emericum iterum occupant.
units.tr: The same men occupy Emmerich again.

units.la: Admirantis Legati ad Imp. ituri à Statibus cum magna præda abducuntur.
units.tr: The envoys of the Admiral setting out to the Emperor are carried off by the States, together with a great booty.

units.la: Milites Statuum noctu irruunt in Assel prope Bokum, & fratrem Capitanei Lactucam obtruncant, præda deportata fugant, & Com. Fridericum de Berg & complices cedunt, tum Comitem de Busquoi & commilitones capiunt. Kerpenses quidam ad Coloniam à Statensibus spoliantur. Mart.
units.tr: Soldiers of the States suddenly rush at night into Assel near Bocholt, cut down the brother of the captain Lactuca, and drive off the booty they carried away. They put to flight Count Frederick of Berg and his accomplices, then capture Count de Busquoy and his fellow soldiers. Certain people from Kerpen are plundered by the Staters near Cologne, in March.

units.la: Omnia infesta latrociniis circa Rhenum.
units.tr: Everything around the Rhine is hostile and full of robberies.

units.la: Cardinal. Andr. cum Procerib. consilia confert in Maastricht. Status obsid… Thetikum, & vi capiunt, omnibus caesis.
units.tr: Cardinal Andreas confers with the nobles on plans at Maastricht. The States besiege Tiel (Thetikum?), and take it by force, with all inside put to the sword.

units.la: Ob licentas sublatas minantur Flandriae & Brabantiae vastationem, nisi geminas deinceps contributiones pendere velint.
units.tr: Because their licences have been withdrawn, they threaten the devastation of Flanders and Brabant unless these people are willing to pay double contributions from now on.

units.la: Status prope Emerich pecora abacturi erant, quos quum persequerentur Hispani ex insidiis hi circumveniuntur & capiuntur unus Comes, 4. Capitanei, in quibus nothus Mansfeldii, caesis multis militibus, multis dimissis.
units.tr: The States were about to drive off cattle near Emmerich; when the Spaniards pursued them, these men were surrounded by an ambush and captured: one count, four captains, among them a bastard of Mansfeld, with many soldiers killed and many dismissed.

units.la: Status occupant Deuenter, & arcem Cliuensi Duci pertinentem, ne Hispani eam occuparent.
units.tr: The States occupy Deventer, and the fortress belonging to the Duke of Cleves, so that the Spaniards should not seize it.

units.la: In Hispania Hollandicae naues detinentur, homines in iis existentes vt haeretici affliguntur, sensim suspensi vstulantur & exuruntur, inter quos Consulis Enkehusii filius fuit.
units.tr: In Spain, Dutch ships are detained, and the men on them are tormented as heretics: they are gradually hanged, burned and set on fire; among them was the son of the consul Enkhuizen.

units.la: Status prohibent nauigationes in Hispan. iubent Hispanos infestari mari, & nauem Hispan. onustam multis Indicis bonis capiunt, Hispanos praecipitant.
units.tr: The States prohibit voyages to Spain, order that the Spaniards be harassed at sea, and seize a Spanish ship laden with many Indian goods, and throw the Spaniards overboard.

units.la: Naues & miles Andernacum mittuntur, ad adducendam Cliuensi Principi sponsam Lotharingicam.
units.tr: Ships and soldiers are sent to Andernach to bring a Lorraine bride to the Prince of Cleves.

units.la: Status deprædantur Hal prope Dueft.
units.tr: The States plunder Hall near Duffel.

units.la: Status militem circa 18. M. comparant, 3. M. equites, prohibent mercimon. cum Hisp. Prouinciis.
units.tr: The States raise about 18,000 soldiers, 3,000 of them horse, and forbid trade with the Spanish provinces.

units.la: Hispani congregantur ad Rees & Emericum, post ad fortalitium Schenkianum descendunt, præsente Cardinale Andrea. Sed quia deprehendunt fortius esse, quam vt capi posset, deserto eo ad Bomlerwert proficiscuntur, quo & Maur. cótedit.
units.tr: The Spaniards gather at Rees and Emmerich, then march down to the Schenck fortress, with Cardinal Andreas present. But because they find it too strong to be taken, they abandon it and make for Bommelerwaard, where Maurice also encamps.

units.la: Andr. Cardinalis venit in Herzogenbusch, ei vrbi praesidium impositurus, quod Ciues recusant.
units.tr: Cardinal Andreas comes to 's-Hertogenbosch, intending to impose a garrison on that town, which the citizens refuse.

units.la: 4. M. Bosknechti à Zelandis ad Bommelenses mittuntur, sed quum iis ii non indigerent, eosdem remiserunt.
units.tr: Four thousand Bosch... (soldiers) are sent from Zeeland to the Bommelers, but since they did not need them, they sent them back.

units.la: Nuncius Apostol. Wesalia cum suis Iesuitis videns Deformationem non processuram, rursus discedit, Ciues vt refractarios vehementer accusans.
units.tr: The papal nuncio at Wesel, seeing that the Reformation will not go forward, departs again with his Jesuits, bitterly accusing the citizens of being obstinate.

units.la: Hispani occuparunt fortalitium Creuecour ad Mosam, & Bomel vehementer obsederunt, & 19. Mai. magna vi fossam proxime vrbem obtinent, & Stadianos profligant, occisis 200. Sequenti nocte Stadiani Hispanos rursus depellunt, caesis 300. Die 21. Angli & Galli ad 8. M. castra Hispan. ita aggressi sunt, vt aliquot Capitaneos Hispan. ceperint.
units.tr: The Spaniards seized the fortress of Crèvecœur on the Maas and strongly besieged Bommel, and on 19 May, with great force, they gained the ditch close to the town and routed the Stadians, 200 being killed. The following night the Stadians drove back the Spaniards again, 300 being killed. On the 21st the English and French attacked the Spanish camp with about 8,000 men in such a way that they captured several Spanish captains.

units.la: C. naues ex Hollandia soluunt.
units.tr: Thirty ships sail from Holland.

units.la: Hispani obsidionem Bommel soluunt, quum circa 4. M. hominum amisissent.
units.tr: The Spaniards abandon the siege of Bommel, having lost about 4,000 men.

units.la: Comes Embdanus litem cum Ciuibus 4. dominis feudi committit.
units.tr: The Count of Emden commits a lawsuit with the citizens to four lords of the fief.

units.la: Hollandiae naues cum vnionibus ex India redeunt.
units.tr: Dutch ships return from the East Indies with pearls.

units.la: Anglica classis Lagos in Portugallia combussit, & Insulam Amoderam, vbi saccarum crescit, vastauit.
units.tr: The English fleet burned Lagos in Portugal and laid waste the island of Amoderam, where sugar grows.

units.la: Milites quasi vulneribus obligatis in Herzogenbusch vrbem, quae praesidium accipere noluit, introducuntur, vt sic praesidium imponeretur, sed dolo cognito expulsi sunt.
units.tr: Soldiers, as if with bandaged wounds, are brought into the town of 's-Hertogenbosch, which refused to receive a garrison, so that a garrison might thus be imposed; but the trick being discovered, they were expelled.

units.la: Hispani Rossum se conferunt.
units.tr: The Spaniards betake themselves to Roosendaal.

units.la: Exercitus Statuum manet prope Herwarden, & se munit, & subinde inter se velitantur, & Hispani equites obruituri Stadienses duriter excipiuntur, Comite quodam occiso.
units.tr: The army of the States remains near Herwarden and fortifies itself; meanwhile they skirmish with one another, and when the Spanish horse, about to overwhelm the Stadians, attacked, they were met fiercely, a certain count being killed.

units.la: Naues ex OstIndia piper aduehunt, Rex Bantae reliquas in Maloco misit, vbi merces nauibus imponerent, cum quo de mercimoniis contrahitur.
units.tr: Ships from the East Indies bring pepper; the King of Banda sent the rest to Ambon, where the goods were to be loaded onto the ships, and a trade agreement is made with him.

units.la: Hollandi Canariam occupant, & magnum damnum inferunt. Attelandado contra magnas naues armat, Hollandos oppugnaturus.
units.tr: The Dutch seize the Canaries and inflict great damage. Attelandado arms great ships against the Dutch, intending to attack them.

units.la: Laberlottus Varcum astu capere voluit. Nam milites immisit specie rusticorum legumina venditurorum, qui custodes portarum caederent, sed cum eorum vnus colleeturus dissipatos diceres deprehensus esset armatus, dolus apparuit.
units.tr: Laberlotto wanted to take Vaerk by cunning. For he sent soldiers in the guise of countrymen who would sell vegetables; they were to kill the gate guards, but when one of them, armed, was caught as if scattering what he was supposed to be gathering, the trick became apparent.

units.la: Duca di Mantua & Duca di Niuers veniunt Antuerpiam, dona mittunt Mauritio, hic illis vicissim.
units.tr: The Duke of Mantua and the Duke of Nevers come to Antwerp; they send gifts to Maurice, and he in return to them.

units.la: Rex Scotiae in armis est, cupiens scire, quis ab obitu Reginae in Anglia praesse debeat. StaStatus prædam raptant, sed ab Hispanis quidam cum præda deprehenduntur.
units.tr: The King of Scots is in arms, wishing to know who ought to rule England after the death of the Queen. The States plunder the booty, but some men are caught with the booty by the Spaniards.

units.la: Albertus Archid. Bruxellis splendidissime cum Infanta exceptus die 5. Sept. Ciuium, qui obuiam procedebant, 3. M. erant, inter quos 700. russis tibialibus, ceruleis caligis, candidis thoracibus & pileis, cum plumis eorund. colorum (qui Infantæ peculiares erant) ornati, vexilla 5. habuerunt, Proceres rubro holosérico insignes: tormenta emissa. Ad portam 12. Nobiles tectorium deauratum (ein Himmel) gestabat. Omnes clerici & religiosi ad S. Codoliæ templum obuii Albertum & Infantam exceperunt, orationem habente Episcopo Mechlin. Templum ingressi ad capsam Sacramenti procubuerunt. Inde equis candidis rursus insidentes, Infanta dextram occupante, per arcus triumphales perrexerunt ad palatium.
units.tr: Archduke Albert was received at Brussels most magnificently with the Infanta on 5 September. The citizens who came forward to meet them numbered 3,000, among whom were 700 in red stockings, blue breeches, white breastplates and caps, adorned with plumes of their colours (which were peculiar to the Infanta); they had five banners, and the nobles were distinguished by red silk. Cannon were fired. At the gate twelve nobles carried a gilded canopy (ein Himmel). All the clergy and religious met Albert and the Infanta at the church of St Goedele, the Bishop of Mechlin giving an oration. Having entered the church, they prostrated themselves before the tabernacle of the Sacrament. Then, mounting white horses again, with the Infanta on the right, they proceeded through the triumphal arches to the palace.

units.la: In primo arcu præsentabantur, Philippus II. Rex Hispan. coram eo Phil. III. & Infanta, cui arbor apponebatur cum 17. ramis, & totidem insignibus 17. Prouinciarum. In aliis imago Philippi III. in aliis pugnæ Alberti ad Cales, Andres & Hulst ostentabantur.
units.tr: At the first arch there were displayed Philip II, King of Spain, and before him Philip III and the Infanta; there was a tree set beside her with 17 branches and as many emblems of the 17 provinces. On the others were shown an image of Philip III, and scenes of Albert's battles at Calais, Andernach and Hulst.

units.la: In foro præsentabantur 17. virgines inter se dimicantes, inter eas Belgica ad cœlum cum gemitu respiciens, ex parte versus Hollandiam, nigro, ex altera parte amœno habitu induta. Extabat & pictura Alberti & Infantæ sedentium in campo, vbi multæ sagittæ colligatæ erant, Concordiam significantes, Deo cœlitus super eos respiciente. Iuxta erant mare & Balenæ, quæ eos deuoraturæ videbantur. Stabat & arbor cum fructibus: infra vero ignis cum Inscriptione: MIHI MORS. & Salamandra cum inscriptione: MIHI VITA. Fuerunt & arcus plures omnes affabre facti & carminibus decorati. Ante palatium pyramis excelsa, multis Cæsarum Austriac. figuris exornata, in cuius fastigio stabat virgo cum vexillo, &c.
units.tr: In the marketplace were displayed seventeen virgins fighting among themselves. Among them was Belgica, looking up to heaven with a groan, dressed in black on the side facing Holland and in pleasant attire on the other side. There was also a painting of Albert and the Infanta sitting in a field, where many arrows were bound together, signifying concord, with God looking down on them from heaven. Nearby were the sea and whales, which seemed about to devour them. A tree with fruit stood there too, and below it a fire with the inscription MIHI MORS, and a salamander with the inscription MIHI VITA. There were also several arches, all skilfully made and decorated with verses. In front of the palace stood a tall pyramid, adorned with many figures of the Austrian Caesars, and on its summit stood a virgin with a banner, etc.

units.la: Hanc tamen splendidissimam pompam perpetuæ pluuiæ obscurabant & defœdebant.
units.tr: Yet this most splendid pageant was dimmed and spoiled by constant rain.

units.la: Naues Statuum in Canari 6. M. hominum occiderunt, Inquisiquisitionem captiuarunt, Episcopum cum Gubernatore combusserunt.
units.tr: The ships of the States at Canary killed 6,000 men, captured the Inquisition, and burned the bishop together with the governor.

units.la: Ad Ostende in Flandria multa fortalicia facta sunt, vt excursiones Statuum impedirentur: verum Status nihilominus eruperunt.
units.tr: At Ostend in Flanders many forts were built so that the sorties of the States might be hindered; nevertheless the States broke out.

units.la: Hispani & Status ad Bommel & Thylo resident, illi Leodiensem agrum praedantur, quod stipendia deessent.
units.tr: The Spaniards and the States are stationed at Bommel and Thiel; the former plunder the country of Liège because their pay was lacking.

units.la: Hispani occupant Wert in Kempen.
units.tr: The Spaniards seize Wert in the Kempen.

units.la: Dux Mantuanus cum bona gratia e Belgio in Italiam reuertitur.
units.tr: The Duke of Mantua returns from Belgium to Italy with good grace.

units.la: Magnae deliberationes Brabandinorum, qui iurare iussi, nihil de priuilegiis suis detrahi volunt, & vrgent vt Albertus stet promissis ante abitum in Hispan. factis, quod videlic. vellet exteras nationes ex Belgio eliminare.
units.tr: Great deliberations of the Brabanters, who were ordered to swear an oath; they wish nothing to be taken away from their privileges, and they urge that Albert keep the promises made before his departure into Spain, namely that he would expel foreign nations from Belgium.

units.la: Spinolae Hispani naues, cum ex Schleus, vbi latebant, excurrere vellent ad praedandum, ab 8. nauibus Hollandicis cohibitae, & regredi coactae sunt.
units.tr: When the Spanish ships of Spinola wished to sally forth from the Sluis, where they had been hiding, to plunder, they were checked by eight Dutch ships and forced to turn back.

units.la: Hispani ad Coloniam naues, boues, equos & carros rapiunt.
units.tr: The Spaniards seize ships, oxen, horses and carts at Cologne.

units.la: Rheno ab Hispanis occupato, commercia iacent, salis pretium accrescit.
units.tr: With the Rhine occupied by the Spaniards, trade lies dead and the price of salt rises.

units.la: Rex. Hispan. multis captiuis rebellibus parcit.
units.tr: The King of Spain spares many captured rebels.

units.la: Antuerpienses recusant accipere militem Hispan. in castellum.
units.tr: The Antwerpers refuse to receive a Spanish soldier into the citadel.

units.la: Generales Status recusant Alberto dare petitam pecuniam, ante vtrinque praestitum iuramentum.
units.tr: The General States refuse to give Albert the money he asked for, because of the oath sworn on both sides beforehand.

units.la: Hollandicae naues cum saccaro ex Brasilia redeunt.
units.tr: Dutch ships return from Brazil with sugar.

units.la: Hispani tractum ad Mosam valde grauant.
units.tr: The Spaniards gravely oppress the district along the Meuse.

units.la: Hispani relinquentes Rees, cum magna praeda ad Essen rapta, rursus a ciuibus Vesal. spoliantur.
units.tr: The Spaniards, leaving Rees, having seized a great booty at Essen, are in turn plundered by the citizens of Wesel.

units.la: Lis inter Comitem Enno & Embdenses componitur opera Statuum.
units.tr: The dispute between Count Enno and the people of Emden is settled through the efforts of the States.

units.la: Pax inter Albert. Archid. & Anglam Bolognię tractata non procedit. Iurafnentum ab Alberto & multis ciuibus vtrinque præsti-tum, legibus antiquis confirmatis.
units.tr: The peace between Archduke Albert and England, negotiated at Boulogne, does not go forward. An oath was sworn on both sides by Albert and many citizens, with the ancient laws confirmed.

units.la: Legatus Lotharing. apud Albertum pro genero Iuliacensi intercedit, vt ipsius ditioni parcatur.
units.tr: The envoy of Lorraine intercedes with Albert on behalf of his son-in-law of Jülich, that his territory be spared.

units.la: Ecclesia Gallica clandestina Coloniæ dissipata, multa graui deprehensis irrogata.
units.tr: The French Church at Cologne, meeting in secret, was broken up, and many of those caught were punished with severe penalties.

units.la: Cæsar Commissarios ad Status destinarat, Salentinum & alios. Verum Status eos audire noluerunt, respondentes, (antequam iis aditum permitterent) se, cum pace sollicitentur, iam anno 1591. Cæsari &c. & anno 96. Electoribus & Principibus super hoc capite satis respondisse. Et sibi nunc plus iniuriæ inferri, quam a Rege defuncto sit illatum, dum iura, libertas, Leges, Religio per Hispanos violentur, dum membra imperii tam iniuriose ab ipsis habeantur.
units.tr: The Emperor had sent commissioners to the States, Salentin and others. But the States were unwilling to hear them, replying (before they would grant them access) that, although they were being pressed for peace, they had already given a sufficient answer on this point to the Emperor in 1591, and to the Electors and Princes in 1596. And that now greater injury was being inflicted on them than had been inflicted by the late King, while their rights, liberty, laws and religion are violated by the Spaniards, and the members of the Empire are treated so unjustly by them.

units.la: Ideo se meliora sperare & pacem incertam inire non posse &c.
units.tr: Therefore they could not hope for better things, nor enter into an uncertain peace, etc.

units.la: M.DC. Status die 13. Ian. mane ex insidiis occupant arcem Wachdendunck in Geldria, postquam ab eo præsidio iam decennium eliminati fuissent, & ibidem multas bombardas consequuntur.
units.tr: In 1600 [M.DC. = 1600 read as the year], on 13 January in the morning, the States seized by surprise the citadel of Wachtendonk in Guelders, after the garrison had already been driven out for ten years, and there they captured many cannons.

units.la: Hispani contra multis militibus communiunt Rheinberg.
units.tr: The Spaniards fortify Rheinberg with many soldiers against them.

units.la: Naues ex India multas milliones attulerunt, & sic Hispani, ob pecuniæ penuriam tumultuantes, sunt placati.
units.tr: Ships from India brought many millions, and so the Spaniards, rioting from lack of money, were pacified.

units.la: Status minantur Aquensibus, qui Euangelicos premebant.
units.tr: The States threaten the people of Aachen, who were oppressing the Evangelicals.

units.la: Mauritius animaduertens, Hispanos in fortalitio San. Andreæ ringi & stomachari, propter non soluta stipendia, Hagâ egredientes, & per Dort & Hemer veniens, fortalitium Greve-cour, quod Hispani, cum primo venissent ad Bomel, occupauerant, deditione recepit. Postea arce Alem occupata, obsedit propugnaculum S. Andreæ, & in Aprili globorum ictibus verberat. Et licet obstarent inundationes, tamen illud postea deditione accepit.
units.tr: Maurice, perceiving that the Spaniards in the fort of St Andrew were grumbling and fretting because their pay had not been paid, set out from The Hague, and coming by way of Dordrecht and Hemmer, received by surrender the fort of Grevecoeur, which the Spaniards had seized when they first came to Bommel. Afterwards, having taken the castle of Alem, he besieged the bulwark of St Andrew and in April battered it with cannon balls. And although the inundations stood in the way, nevertheless he later took it by surrender.

units.la: Comitia Bruxellis.
units.tr: The assembly at Brussels.

units.la: Hispani in Diest, Haumont, &c. rebellantes multant confecconfœderatos suos, Berg. in Hennegaw, Valenzin & Dor- nek.
units.tr: The Spaniards, rebelling at Diest, Haumont, etc., punish their confederates; Bergen in Hainault, Valenciennes and Dornik.

units.la: Comitissa Walpurg in Moers obit, & ditionem Mauritio Nassouiensi & Bethburg. dicat, quam tamen Dux Iuliacensis tanquam feudum occupat.
units.tr: The Countess Walpurga dies at Moers and bequeaths her dominion to Maurice of Nassau and Bentheim, which nevertheless the Duke of Jülich seizes as a fief.

units.la: Naues cum aromatibus ex India Ambsterdamum veniunt.
units.tr: Ships with spices come from India to Amsterdam.

units.la: 25. Iunii interlocutio fit vtrorumque Statuum de pace in Berg, sed sine effectu.
units.tr: On 25 June a conference of both States concerning peace takes place at Bergen, but without effect.

units.la: Mauritius classe traiicit in Flandriam, & fortalitio Philippinæ,& oppido Oudeburg occupatis, venit in Ostende. Accepit deinde & muniuit castra Isabellæ Alberti & Smaeskirke dicta. Exin obsidens Neoport. partem exercitus vltra alueum duxit, partem inter Neoport. & Ostende reliquit cum Capitaneo Ernesto Casimiro Nassouio.
units.tr: Maurice crosses into Flanders with his fleet, and having taken the fort of Philippine and the town of Oudenburg, he comes to Ostend. He then took and fortified the camp of Isabella of Albert, called Smaeskerke. Afterwards, besieging Nieuport, he led part of the army across the channel, and left part between Nieuport and Ostend with the captain Ernest Casimir of Nassau.

units.la: Albertus vero Archid. celerrime subsequens, prædicta fortalitia recuperat, & Hollandos in iis crudeliter trucidat, metum videlicet hosti incussurus. Hoc resciens Mauritius, mandat vt Ernestus Albertum accessu prohibeat, & simul reliquam partem copiarum, ipsemet præuius, per medias aquas aluei, ad reliquum exercitum traducit.
units.tr: But Archduke Albert, following very swiftly, recovered the aforesaid forts, and cruelly slaughtered the Hollanders in them, evidently intending to strike fear into the enemy. Learning this, Maurice orders Ernest to prevent Albert's approach, and at the same time, going on ahead himself through the midst of the waters of the channel, he leads the remaining part of the forces across to the rest of the army.

units.la: Interim Albert. Ernestum est aggressus, & circiter 700. cum quibusdam Capitaneis cæsis transitum occupauit. Venere in conspectum mutuum duo isti exercitus, aduersa acie vtrinque probe instructi & dispositi. Principio Com. Ludouicus Nasso: cum suis equitibus fugam simulauit, & sic Hispanos equites allexit vt sequerentur, qui bombardarum ictibus sunt petiti, Hispani circiter 5. M. cum solido clamore ruentes Mauritianos primo ad 170 passus retrocedere coegerunt. Ibi Mauritius suos animando ad constantiam est cohortatus; nunc scilicet tempus & locum esse fortiter dimicandi, hinc mare, illinc hostem fugam occludere. Miles animo recepto Hispanos repulit & priorem locum obtinuit. Ex illo Hispanorum plures aduentantes denuo Mauritianos repressrunt. Anceps & pericu-
units.tr: Meanwhile Albert attacked Ernest and, having about 700 killed, together with some captains, seized the crossing. The two armies came into view of one another, each well drawn up and arranged in opposing battle lines. At the start Count Lewis of Nassau, with his horsemen, feigned flight, and so drew the Spanish horsemen on to pursue, who were struck by cannon fire. The Spaniards, about 5,000 strong, charging with a loud shout, forced the Maurician troops first to retreat about 170 paces. There Maurice, encouraging his men to steadfastness, exhorted them: now was the time and place to fight bravely, the sea on one side and the enemy on the other cutting off flight. The soldiers, taking heart, repulsed the Spaniards and regained their former position. After that, more Spaniards arriving pressed the Maurician troops back again. The fight was long, uncertain and dangerous for the Maurician troops.

units.la: riculosa Mauritianis pugna diu. Verum Mauritius Capitaneo de Veer,vt prælium iniret iniunxit,qui prompto animo re-spondit,se iam fidem suam Statibus probaturum, & sic deinde fortissime hostem inuasit. Mauritius, vbi Capitaneo Gend mandauisset, vt ad latus cum suis equis consisteret, & vbi hostem cedere videret, statim in eum irrueret, prælium auspiciis diuinis redintegrauit, & hostem cedere coegit. Ibi Capitaneus Gend impressionem fecit, & sic vtrinque ordinis dissipatione facta Mauritius memorabili victoria factus est superior, 2. Iul.
units.tr: But Maurice ordered Captain de Veer to join battle, who answered with a ready mind that he would now prove his loyalty to the States, and so he then attacked the enemy most bravely. Maurice, having instructed Captain Gent to stand at the flank with his horsemen, and to rush straight at the enemy when he saw them give way, renewed the fight under divine auspices and forced the enemy to yield. There Captain Gent made an attack, and so, with the ranks thrown into confusion on both sides, Maurice became the superior by a memorable victory, on 2 July.

units.la: Ex parte Hispanorum cæsa ad 6. M. inter quos multi strenui Capitanei. Captus est Admirandus de Arragonia, cum multis Capitaneis. Ex Mauritianis desiderati sunt circ. 4. M. Ipse Albertus vulneratus & bis à suis ex periculo vitæ ereptus est. Mauritius Admirandum interrogauit, quomodo ei tyrocinium hoc belli Hollandicum placeret? Eos enim is tyrones antea vocabat.
units.tr: On the Spanish side about 6,000 were slain, among them many brave captains. Admiral of Aragon was captured, with many captains. Of the Maurician troops about 4,000 were missing. Albert himself was wounded and twice snatched from danger of his life by his own men. Maurice asked Admiral of Aragon how this Dutch apprenticeship in war pleased him, for he had previously called them apprentices.

units.la: Mauritius deinde Neoport. obsessurus fortalicia Isabellæ & Claræ dicta, vult expugnare.
units.tr: Afterwards Maurice, intending to besiege Nieuport, wishes to storm the forts called of Isabella and Clara.

units.la: Laberlot insignis Capitaneus Alberti, volens inspicere operas Mauritianorum, sclopeto in capite ictus & occisus est.
units.tr: Laberlot, a distinguished captain of Albert, wishing to inspect the works of the Maurician troops, was struck in the head by a musket shot and killed.

units.la: Albertus contra, undiquaque militem ex præsidiis adsciscens, obsidionem Neoporti impedire & hostem concludere contendit.
units.tr: Albert, on the other hand, drawing soldiers from every garrison on all sides, strives to hinder the siege of Nieuport and to shut in the enemy.

units.la: Consiliarii Statuum, qui cum Mauritio fuerunt, in Hollandiam sunt reuersi, adductis secum supra 90. vexillis hosti ereptis.
units.tr: The councillors of the States who had been with Maurice returned to Holland, bringing with them more than 90 standards seized from the enemy.

units.la: Comes Philippus à Benting & alii nomine Statuum generalium Brabandinorum, in Berg ad Som, cum Statibus vnitis agunt de pace, quibus Aduocatus vnitorum respondet, suos dominos pacem ex animo optare, sed se propter tyrannidem Hispanorum pacem firmam sibi polliceri non posse, & exempla quædam recensuit, & inter illa etiam hoc, quod Albertus curauit quandam virginem propter religionem crudeliter viuam defodi,& quod Admirans in quosuis sæuierit, opus fore, vtrique Status Hispanos eliminent, si pax iniri debeat. Deinde narrat, in transactione inter Albertum Archiducem & Infantam ita omnia composita esse, vt Status vniuersi pro mancipiis Hispanorum sint deputati, & dicit, se subdubitare, num Legati hi tractationem mutuam effectui apud Albertum reddere possint. Postremo affert & hoc, se cum aliis Principibus & Rebuspub. confœderatos esse, cum quibus omnia consilia essent communicanda. Dederunt autem & literas ad Status generales, eadem fere scribentes, quæ Aduocatus in congregatione illa erat prolocutus.
units.tr: Count Philip of Bentheim and others, in the name of the General States of Brabant, at Bergen op Zoom, treat of peace with the United States; to whom the advocate of the United States replied that his masters sincerely desired peace, but that on account of the tyranny of the Spaniards they could not promise themselves a firm peace; and he recounted certain examples, and among them this, that Albert had taken care that a certain virgin was buried alive, cruelly, on account of her religion; and that the Admiral had raged against whomsoever, so that, if peace were to be made, both States must eliminate the Spaniards. He then reported that in the agreement between Archduke Albert and the Infanta everything had been so arranged that all the States of the Netherlands were assigned to the slaves of the Spaniards; and he said he doubted whether these envoys could bring about the mutual negotiation with Albert. Finally he added also that he himself was allied with other Princes and commonwealths, with whom all plans were to be shared. They also gave letters to the General States, writing almost the same things as the advocate had spoken at that assembly.

units.la: Mauritius read Neoportum infecta in Hollandiam se recepit, relicto præsidio in Ostende circa s. M. militum. Hollandi desperantes de defensione fortalitia Albertini, illud demoliti sunt, & recesserunt.
units.tr: Maurice withdrew to Holland with his army, leaving a garrison at Ostend near the sea, after reading Nieuwpoort. The Hollanders, despairing of defending the fortress of the Archduke's men, demolished it and withdrew.

units.la: Cuidam Hispano nauis inæstimabilis pretii erepta in Zelandiam deuehitur.
units.tr: A Spanish ship of inestimable value was seized and carried off to Zeeland.

units.la: Vulgatur edictum Placati, vt in Ducatu Brabandino de singulis furnis soluantur 20. Stibari ad bellum contra Hollandos.
units.tr: An edict of the Placard was published that 20 stivers be paid from every hearth in the Duchy of Brabant for the war against the Hollanders.

units.la: Duynkerkii piscatoribus halecum magnum damnum inferunt.
units.tr: The Dunkirk fishermen suffer great losses at the hands of the herring fleet.

units.la: Status ab Aquensibus contributionem postularunt, qua denegata molas cupri incenderunt.
units.tr: The States demanded a contribution from the people of Aachen, and when it was refused they burned the copper mills.

units.la: Mauritius conatus est militem in Werth tumultuantem prehensare, sed frustra, quia stipendia ab Archiduc. soluuntur.
units.tr: Maurice tried to seize the soldiers who were rioting at Wert, but in vain, because their pay was being paid by the Archduke.

units.la: Equites Statenses Axelensibus exactiones imperant, sed nihil auferunt, ideo molendina exurunt.
units.tr: The horsemen of the States impose levies on the people of Axel, but take nothing, and so they burn the mills.

units.la: Hispani omnia fortalitia circa Ostende firmant;
units.tr: The Spaniards strengthen all the fortresses around Ostend.

units.la: Bruxellæ à generalibus Statibus contributiones petuntur, illi contra petunt, vt Hispani ex Belgio dimittantur, sed frustra.
units.tr: Contributions are demanded at Brussels by the States-General. They in turn demand that the Spaniards be dismissed from the Netherlands, but in vain.

units.la: Statenses in Limburg grassantur.
units.tr: The States' troops ravage in Limburg.

units.la: Hollandi à suis tertiam partem bonorum exegisse dicebantur.
units.tr: It was said that the Hollanders had exacted a third of the goods of their own people.

units.la: Statenses Statensis expilant Ferchenses, & prope Rhenum prædantur.
units.tr: The States' soldiers of Statensis plunder Verchen and raid near the Rhine.

units.la: Cliuenses & Bergenses grauantur contribuere ad elocatio-nem Sibyllæ, propterea quod mercimonia occluso Rheno iaceant, sed tamen magnam summam promittunt.
units.tr: The people of Cleves and Berg are burdened with contributing to the hire of the Sibyl, because trade lies idle with the Rhine closed; nevertheless they promise a large sum.

units.la: Ann. M. DC I. Equites Brabantini, qui neutrales Ciuitates non debuerant lædere, Bordebotniam grauant, sed repellun-tur.
units.tr: In the year 1601, horsemen from Brabant, who ought not to have harmed the neutral cities, harass Bordeboten, but they are driven back.

units.la: Status astu occupant arcem Cracaw.
units.tr: The States cunningly seize the citadel of Krakau.

units.la: Statenses inferunt munitiones & commeatum in Wachtendunk, quos Hispani in Moers nihil impedire potuerunt.
units.tr: The States bring munitions and supplies into Wachtendonk, which the Spaniards at Moers could not hinder at all.

units.la: Comparantur naues in Hollandia ad visendas Indias.
units.tr: Ships are being fitted out in Holland to visit the Indies.

units.la: Præsidiarii in Rheinberg cuiusdam Capitanei Neomagiensis vxorem manibus truncant, & vociferantem occidunt. Capitaneus igitur quosdam ex iis deprehensos trucidat.
units.tr: The garrison at Rheinberg cut off the hands of the wife of a certain captain of Neumagen, and kill her as she cries out. The captain therefore butchers some of those of them whom he has caught.

units.la: Status Legatum mittunt ad Regem Galliæ.
units.tr: The States send an envoy to the King of France.

units.la: Filius Com. Haure ante Ostende globo occisus.
units.tr: The son of Count Haure is killed by a cannonball before Ostend.

units.la: Status lustrant suum militem.
units.tr: The States review their soldiers.

units.la: Hispani in Rheinberg eripiunt Duci Cliuensi quædam bona curribus ex Hollandia apportata. Dux contra nauem frumentariam ad illos spectantem Dusseldorpii detinet.
units.tr: The Spaniards at Rheinberg snatch from the Duke of Cleves certain goods brought from Holland by cart. The Duke in turn detains at Düsseldorf a grain ship belonging to them.

units.la: Statenses occupant Lamburg, & in ea Præfectum Episcop. Colon. & passim prope Coloniam prædantur.
units.tr: The States' men seize Lamberg, and in it the prefect of the Bishop of Cologne, and they plunder here and there near Cologne.

units.la: Leodienses minantur se Gallo adhæsuros, nisi Hispani auocentur, & sic ab iis liberantur.
units.tr: The people of Liège threaten that they will join the Frenchman unless the Spaniards are called away, and so they are freed from them.

units.la: Status Brabant. & Flandr. tergiuersantur magnam illam summam Alberto pendere, & ne portam nouam ad arcem suam faciat, per quam Hispani in vrbem Bruxel. introduci possent, intercedunt.
units.tr: The States of Brabant and Flanders evade paying Albert that great sum, and they intervene so that he does not make a new gate to his citadel, through which the Spaniards could be brought into the city of Brussels.

units.la: Hollandi Hispanicam nauem deprædantur.
units.tr: The Hollanders plunder a Spanish ship.

units.la: Albertus vetat quicquam ex Hollandia comparari.
units.tr: Albert forbids anything to be bought from Holland.

units.la: Admirant. Dux Hispan. superiore anno à Princip. Mauritio captus, dicebatur soluta magna pecunia, & restitutis vtrinque captiuis, & facta promissione, quod nunquam quicquam contra Hollandos moliri velit, liber dimittendus, sed non est factum.
units.tr: Admiral. The Spanish general, who had been taken by Prince Maurice the previous year, was said to be set free on payment of a large sum of money, with prisoners returned on both sides, and a promise made that he would never attempt anything against the Hollanders; but this was not done.

units.la: Miles in fortalitio Isabellæ Alberti stomachosior, donec facta est solutio.
units.tr: The soldiers in Albert's fortress of Isabella were more irritated until the payment was made.

units.la: Status arcte obsident Rheinberg.{a} Hispani eruptione facta multos occidunt: illi proxime vrbem castra promouent, sed dum fortalitium lunare volunt dissipare, puluere bombardico subiecto, ipsimet eo igni abrepti sunt. Hispani munitionem illam retinent.
units.tr: The States closely besieged Rheinberg. The Spaniards, making a sortie, kill many; the others advance their camp close to the town, but while they wish to destroy the crescent-shaped fort, having laid gunpowder under it, they are themselves swept away by that fire. The Spaniards retain that stronghold.

units.la: Albertus Arch. obsidet Ostende cum maximo exercitu, 5. Iulii, & proxima loca facile occupat. Ostende commodo portu opportunissima ab Anno 1572. ab vnitis Statibus coepta est muniri, sic vt anno 1583. se contra Parmensem defenderit. Anno 1585. La Motte cum ipsius magno detrimento ab ea depulsus est, maxime vero munita est ad aduentum Alberti Archiducis anno 1596. cum Cales & Hulst captæ sunt. In vere etiam anni 1601. magis fortificata est. Hæc vrbs toti Flandriæ maxime incommodat, adeo vt Flandri ad prohibendas eruptiones 17. fortalitia in circuitu construere, & militem in iis alere maximis cum sumptibus hactenus coacti sint. Isti igitur Alberto sumptus promittunt, vt Ostende obsideat, qui die 5. Iulii Fridericum de Monte misit ad eam obsidendam, ipse cum reliquo exercitu deinde subsecutus.
units.tr: Archduke Albert besieges Ostend with a very great army on 5 July, and easily occupies the nearby places. Ostend, most suitable for its convenient harbour, began to be fortified by the United States in 1572, so that in 1583 it defended itself against Parma. In 1585 La Motte was driven from it with great loss to himself; it was strongly fortified especially at the arrival of Archduke Albert in 1596, when Calais and Hulst were taken. In the spring of 1601 it was fortified even more. This city is a great burden to all Flanders, so much so that the Flemings, to prevent sorties, have hitherto been forced to build seventeen fortresses round about and to maintain soldiers in them at the greatest expense. They therefore promise money to Albert so that he may besiege Ostend; on 5 July he sent Frederick de Monte to besiege it, and followed later himself with the rest of the army.

units.la: In vrbe Capitaneo de Noot 21. vexilla fuerunt, vxores & liberi in Zelandiam missi. Obsessi obsidentes multis globorum ictibus exceperunt. Comes Mauritius misit Generalem de Veer & alios cum 34. vexillis, 15. Iulii. Venerunt præterea multa vexilla Anglorum.
units.tr: In the town there were 21 standards under Captain de Noot; wives and children had been sent to Zeeland. The besieged received the besiegers with many blows of cannonballs. Count Maurice sent General de Veer and others with 34 standards on 15 July. Moreover, many English standards came.

units.la: Die 17. Iulii Veer erupit, sed cum detrimento. Nam & milites eius ex succenso puluere læsus est.
units.tr: On 17 July de Veer made a sortie, but with loss; for his soldiers were also injured by the exploding gunpowder.

units.la: Hispani nauem cum 18. Ciuibus oppresserunt, inuenta est alia via & statio, qua naues exonerarentur.
units.tr: The Spaniards sank a ship with 18 citizens; another route and station was found by which ships could be unloaded.

units.la: Die 29. aquæ immissæ sunt in Hispanorum castra. Venerunt 10. vexilla Italorum.
units.tr: On 29 the waters were let into the Spanish camp. Ten Italian standards came.

units.la: Die 6. Augusti veniunt 800. Angli,
units.tr: On 6 August 800 Englishmen arrive.

units.la: Die 10. Hispani maxime tonant.
units.tr: On 10 the Spaniards thunder hard.

units.la: Die 13. redeunt quædam Ciuium vxores. Generalis Veer læsus, ventus commotis vndis Hispanorum fossas dissipat. Hispani nomine transfugarum Anglorum schedas sagittis illigatas ad Anglos immiserunt, vt & illi transfugerent, venerunt ad M. Angli, ne Hispani priores fierent, diffossus est agger, & aqua castris immissa.
units.tr: On 13 some of the citizens' wives return. General de Veer was wounded; the wind, stirring the waves, scattered the Spanish trenches. The Spaniards, in the name of English deserters, shot letters tied to arrows into the English lines, so that they too might desert. Four hundred Englishmen came to the sea-wall so that the Spaniards should not get the upper hand; the dyke was dug through, and water was let into the camp.

units.la: Die 22. Aug. Capitaneus quidam Anglus è muris prospiciens globo petitus occubuit.
units.tr: On 22 August an English captain, watching from the walls, was struck by a cannonball and fell.

units.la: Die 23. 60. naues cum milite recente appellunt.
units.tr: On 23 sixty ships with fresh soldiers put in to shore.

units.la: Die 24. eruptio magna, sed inanis. Albertus militem collocauit in Waes & Schluis, vt irruptionem Mauritii, quam is mari moliebatur, impediret.
units.tr: On 24 a great sortie, but fruitless. Albert stationed soldiers at Waes and Sluis to hinder the incursion by Maurice, which he was planning by sea.

units.la: Duo vexilla ordinata ad restinguenda incendia ab immissis globis flammiuomis excitata.
units.tr: Two standards were ordered to put out the fires kindled by the fire-throwing balls that had been shot in.

units.la: Ad 28. August. Hispani iam 50. M. globorum ferreorum pondere 40. & 50. librarum in vrbem eiaculati sunt. Mons arenæ in vrbe sic dictus, ita ferreis globis oppletus est, vt ex eo ferri mons dici mereretur.
units.tr: By 28 August the Spaniards had already hurled 50,000 iron balls weighing 40 and 50 pounds into the city. The so-called sand-hill in the city was so filled with iron balls that it deserved to be called an iron hill.

units.la: Sub finem Augusti Hispanorum iam supra 4. M. obsessorum circa 400. homin. occubuerant.
units.tr: Toward the end of August, more than 4,000 of the Spaniards, and about 400 men of the besieged, had already fallen.

units.la: Albertus sua castra circumquaque muniuit, ne auxiliariis copiis ad obsessos pateret.
units.tr: Albert fortified his camp on all sides, so that the auxiliary forces could not reach the besieged.

units.la: Hispani fortalitium mari ab Hollandis extructum occupant.
units.tr: The Spaniards occupy a fort built by the Hollanders on the sea.

units.la: Ostendani portum, quem amiserant, recuperant, & M. homines recipiunt, & tribus diebus erumpunt, ita multi vtrinq; ceciderunt.
units.tr: The Ostend harbour, which they had lost, is recovered; 4,000 men are received, and for three days they make sorties, so that many fell on both sides.

units.la: In vrbe ad 10. M. hominum fuisse relatum.
units.tr: It was reported that there were about 10,000 men in the city.

units.la: Hispani in Rheinberg longos cuniculos subter vrbem a Mauritio actos animaduertentes, cum eo transigunt, & expli-catis catis vexillis discedunt. Status ibi fortalitium Schenkianoilli par excitant.
units.tr: The Spaniards at Rheinberg, noticing long mines dug under the town by Maurice, come to terms with him, and with their standards unfurled they withdraw. The States there raise the fort of Schenkenschanz as a counterpart.

units.la: Mauritius comitatum Moers, quem à morte Comitissæ Dux Iuliac. tenuit, minis coactum sibi vendicat.
units.tr: Maurice, forced by threats, claims for himself the county of Moers, which the Duke of Jülich had held since the death of the countess.

units.la: Equites Statenses in Teutsch irrumpunt, & per triduum prædantur, & lytra extorquent.
units.tr: Horsemen of the States burst into Teutschland, plunder for three days, and extort ransom.

units.la: Milites Com. Bergensnauem in Rheno spoliant, & cum in alia naue aurum reperissent, illud, abiecta illa priore præda, auferunt.
units.tr: Soldiers of Count Berg plunder a ship on the Rhine, and when they found gold on another ship, they threw away the earlier booty and carried off the gold.

units.la: Septem naues cum pipere ex India veniunt Ambsterdamum valore 4o. Tonnarum auri, vt ferebatur.
units.tr: Seven ships with pepper came from India to Amsterdam, worth 40 tons of gold, as it was reported.

units.la: Hispanorum Regi ex noua Hispania 8. milliones auri advenisse perhibebatur, & plures ex Peru expectari.
units.tr: It was said that 8 million gold had arrived for the King of Spain from New Spain, and that more was expected from Peru.

units.la: Ostendani erumpentes in Castris Hispan. stragem ediderunt, nam Hispani improuidi fuerunt, ideo Archidux nonnullos cum Capitaneo eorum laqueo puniri iubet.
units.tr: The people of Ostend, bursting out, caused slaughter in the Spanish camp, for the Spaniards were careless; therefore the Archduke orders some of them, together with their captain, to be punished by the noose.

units.la: Flandri & Brabandi Alberto magnam pecuniam promittunt.
units.tr: The people of Flanders and Brabant promise Albert a large sum of money.

units.la: Obsessi erumpunt, sed cum magna sua clade.
units.tr: The besieged make a sortie, but with great loss to themselves.

units.la: Naues Hispan. captis insignibus aliquot Hollandis, & magna præda acquisita, Duynkirchii appulerunt.
units.tr: Spanish ships, with several Hollander ensigns captured and a great booty acquired, put in at Dunkirk.

units.la: Conte Ioh. Iacomo in Resenthal decem naues lignis, bombardis & aliis in Ostenden apportandis repletas exussit.
units.tr: Count John Jacob at Rosenthal burned ten ships filled with wood, bombards and other things to be brought into Ostend.

units.la: Culina Archiducis ex flamma bombardæ accensa conflagrat.
units.tr: The Archduke's kitchen burned down, set on fire by the blast of a bombard.

units.la: Mauritius, occupatis & munitis Einhofen, Bokstal & Helmond Brabantiæ oppidis, die 31. Octobr. cum 12. M. homin. & 42. tormentis Buscumducis obsedit, tribus munitionibus circum extructis, & erumpentibus fugatis. Putabatur fore, vt Graue vrbs obsideretur, ideo pagani res suas in Busco seruandas attulerunt. Verum Mauritius subito conuersus Buscum obsedit.
units.tr: Maurice, having occupied and fortified the Brabant towns of Eindhoven, Boxtel and Helmond, on 31 October besieged 's-Hertogenbosch with 12,000 men and 42 cannon, three fortifications having been built around it, and those who sallied out were put to flight. It was thought that Grave would be besieged, so the country people brought their goods to be kept in Bois-le-Duc. But Maurice, turning suddenly, besieged Bois-le-Duc.

units.la: Innumeri in ea vrbe sunt religiosi, qui & ipsi ad conducendum militem pecuniam impendunt.
units.tr: There are countless churchmen in that city who also spend money on hiring soldiers.

units.la: Quidam Angli ab Hispanis conducti Ostendam prodere volebant, sed deprehensi & plexi sunt.
units.tr: Some English men, hired by the Spaniards, intended to betray Ostend, but they were caught and executed.

units.la: Iam supra centies mille ictus in Ciuitatem illati, ita vt vrbs miserè dissipata & vastata iaceat.
units.tr: More than a hundred thousand blows have already been struck against the city, so that the town lies wretchedly broken and laid waste.

units.la: Status iam ad 5. milliones auri impenderunt.
units.tr: The States have already spent about five million gold pieces.

units.la: Mittelburgi & Flicssingæ miserabilia sunt nosocomia miserrimorum hominum vulneratorum, qui aut manibus, aut pedibus, aut aliis membris mutilati sunt.
units.tr: At Middelburg and Vlissingen there are pitiful hospitals for the most wretched wounded men, who have been maimed in their hands, feet or other limbs.

units.la: Mauritius propius vrbem Buscum castra metatur, obsidionem vrget, & aquas circumquaque immittit, ne subsidia vrbi accedere possint.
units.tr: Maurice pitches his camp nearer to the town of Bois-le-Duc, presses the siege, and lets water in on every side, so that no relief can reach the town.

units.la: Exorta flamma in fortalitio Alberti ad Ostenden, multas ædiculas & contubernia cum reculis & sarcinis exustit.
units.tr: A fire broke out in Albert's fort at Ostend and burned many little huts and tents with their baggage and equipment.

units.la: Naues 60. cum 80. M. floren. & commeatu Ostendanis illatæ.
units.tr: Sixty ships carrying 80,000 florins and provisions were brought in to the Ostenders.

units.la: Albertus Archid. Buschianis circiter 800. equites, quorum quisque 8. libras pulueris tormentarii gerebat, subsidio immittere voluit, sed ad 300. illorum sunt cæsi, & multi in aquis perierunt. Eliguntur & multæ aliæ copiæ opitulaturæ obsessis. Mauritius cuniculos sub vallum vrbis duxit, & propugnaculum lunare oppugnauit.
units.tr: Archduke Albert wished to send about 800 horsemen as reinforcements to the people of Bois-le-Duc, each carrying eight pounds of gunpowder, but about 300 of them were cut down, and many perished in the waters. Many other forces are also being chosen to bring aid to the besieged. Maurice led mines under the wall of the town and attacked the crescent-shaped outwork.

units.la: Hispani Zelandicos piscatores halecum persequuntur, & captos miserè torquent & occidunt, non Hollandis modo, sed vniuersæ Europæ detrimentum inferentes.
units.tr: The Spaniards pursue the Zeeland herring fishermen and, having taken them, cruelly torture and kill them, causing harm not only to the Dutch but to all Europe.

units.la: Naui s prædatoria Duynkerkianorum tempestatibus in Hollandiam eiecta capta est, cęsis prædonibus.
units.tr: A Dunkirk privateer ship was driven onto the coast of Holland by storms and captured, and its pirates were cut down.

units.la: Quidam Principes pro Euangelicis ad permittendum exercitium Confessionis Augustt. apud Senatum Colonienf. intercedunt.
units.tr: Some princes intercede on behalf of the Evangelicals with the Senate of Cologne, asking that the exercise of the Augsburg Confession be permitted.

units.la: Ostendani munitionem Reuelin vi ventorum læsam reficiunt.
units.tr: The Ostenders are repairing the outwork called the Reveline, which was damaged by the force of the winds.

units.la: Mauritius obsidionem Buschiducis soluit, iniquitate frigoris cedere coactus.
units.tr: Maurice lifts the siege of Bois-le-Duc, compelled to withdraw by the harshness of the cold.

units.la: Hispani naues saxis plenas fundo maris merserunt, vt ingressum nauium in vrbem Ostendam impedirent, verum sine effectu.
units.tr: The Spaniards sank ships full of stones to the bottom of the sea, to block the entry of ships into the city of Ostend, but without effect.

units.la: In fine Decemb. Hispani Ostenden vehementer impetiuerunt, sic vt obsessi extenso albo signo colloquuturos se significarent. Missi igitur ab Archiduce sunt, qui cum Capitaneo Veer, in Ostenda, de deditione pacisce-rentur: Verum cum die 26. Decemb. 600. & 27. die 800. milites in vrbem venissent, nihil de deditione est actum.
units.tr: At the end of December the Spaniards attacked Ostend fiercely, so that the besieged, by hanging out a white sign, signalled that they would hold talks. Men were therefore sent by the Archduke, who were to negotiate the surrender with Captain Veer in Ostend; but when 600 soldiers came into the town on 26 December and 800 on the 27th, nothing was done about surrender.

units.la: An. M. DC.II. Hispani naues saxis impletas fundo demittunt, occlusuri Ostendanis ingressum, & omnia ad generalem oppugnationem comparant, quod animaduertens Capitaneus Veer, cum se imparem tanto conatui intelligeret, dato signo, cum Alberto tractaturum se ostendit. Interea autem dum vtrinque obsides permutantur, & colloquium instituitur, milites & commeatus obsessis importantur. Sic induciae triduanae solutae.
units.tr: In the year 1602 the Spaniards sank ships filled with stones to the bottom, intending to block the entrance for the Ostenders, and they prepared everything for a general assault. Captain Veer, realising that he was unequal to so great an effort, gave a signal and showed that he would treat with Albert. Meanwhile, while hostages were exchanged on both sides and a parley was arranged, soldiers and provisions were brought into the besieged town. Thus the three-day truce was broken.

units.la: Hispani igitur delusionem hanc vlturi, die 7. Ianuar. vehementissime ingenti impetu adoriuntur & oppugnant ciuitatem: sed obsessi contra se fortissime defendunt. Multi tunc Capitanei, & innumeri Hispani occubuerunt.
units.tr: The Spaniards, therefore, wishing to avenge this deception, on 7 January attacked and assaulted the city with the greatest violence and a huge rush; but the besieged defended themselves most bravely against them. Many captains then fell, and countless Spaniards too.

units.la: Allatus iterum obsessis miles & annona.
units.tr: Soldiers and provisions were again brought in to the besieged.

units.la: Hispani ob non soluta stipendia tumultuantur, sed sumpto supplicio de tumultus auctoribus, cohercentur.
units.tr: The Spaniards, because their wages had not been paid, rose in tumult, but after punishment was inflicted on the instigators of the tumult, they were brought under control.

units.la: Hispani Ostendanis 4. naues frangunt.
units.tr: The Spaniards break four ships at Ostend.

units.la: Albertus Archid. ex vertigine capitis lapsus, vena secta restituitur.
units.tr: Archduke Albert, having fallen from dizziness in the head, was restored by bloodletting.

units.la: Statenses grassantur ad Coloniam.
units.tr: The Dutch States raid as far as Cologne.

units.la: Ostendani corrumpunt & auferunt Instrumenta ab Hispanis facta ad obstruendum portum ciuitatis.
units.tr: The Ostenders corrupt and carry off the tools made by the Spaniards for blocking the harbour of the town.

units.la: Fluctus nimii vehementer incommodant Ostendanis.
units.tr: Excessive waves greatly trouble the Ostenders.

units.la: Proditores in Hulst deprehensi & plexi.
units.tr: Traitors were caught at Hulst and executed.

units.la: Nouus portus apertus ad Ostendam.
units.tr: A new harbour has been opened to Ostend.

units.la: Quidam praesidiarii Antuerpiae rebellant: sed plectuntur.
units.tr: Some garrison soldiers at Antwerp rebelled, but they were punished.

units.la: Statenses ceperunt Comitem Adolphum Bergensem prope Herzogen Busch. Status maximum militem colligunt.
units.tr: The Dutch States captured Count Adolph of Bergen near Herzogenbusch. The States are gathering a very large force of soldiers.

units.la: Episcopus Harlemensis Ambsterodami 200. M. florenorum à Papistis in gratiam Alberti collegisse dicebatur.
units.tr: The Bishop of Haarlem was said to have collected 200,000 florins at Amsterdam from Papists for the favour of Albert.

units.la: Spinola cum 8. Galeotis præsto est, vt Oftendanos impediat.
units.tr: Spinola is at hand with eight galleys, to hinder the Ostenders.

units.la: Middelburgi appulerat nauis cum preciosis mercibus ex Barbaria, quas visum iuerant domini mercium, postquam egressi sunt nautæ, signa lætitiæ cum tormentis dantes, cum ignis puluerem tormentarium succendisseт, omnes cum mercibus miserrime dissipati & enecati sunt.
units.tr: A ship had arrived at Middelburg from Barbary, carrying precious merchandise, which the owners of the goods had wished to see. After the sailors had disembarked, giving signs of joy with cannon-fire, when they had set light to the gunpowder, all were most wretchedly scattered and killed together with the goods.

units.la: Ciuitas Graue ad Mosam sita antiquitus ad Ducatum Geldriæ spectauit, postea à Principe Auraico empta est, in cuius potestate fuit, vsque dum Parmensis eam obsedit, & deditione cepit, ideoque ab Hispanis hactenus possessa fuit.
units.tr: The town of Grave, situated on the Meuse, anciently belonged to the Duchy of Guelders; afterwards it was bought by the Prince of Orange, in whose power it was until Parma besieged it and took it by surrender; and therefore it has hitherto been held by the Spaniards.

units.la: Comes Mauritius in regressu ex Brabantia capta Helmond, Grauiam obsedit circa medium Augustum, & Mosam binis pontibus coniunxit, & castra sua circa totam vrbem fortissime muniuit, ne forinsecus vis ei inferri posset. Admirandus Alberti Capitaneus supremus cum magno exercitu conatur obsessores inuadere atque obruere, sed Mauritiani moniti sese pararunt, & aduentantes ita exceperunt, vt cum detrimento fugam dare cogerentur. In exercitu Statuum Veer, qui in Ostende fuerat, globo ad caput petitus occubuit.
units.tr: Count Maurice, on his return from Brabant after taking Helmond, besieged Grave around the middle of August, joined the Meuse with two bridges, and fortified his camp most strongly all around the town, so that no force could be brought to him from outside. Albert's supreme captain, a man to be admired, with a great army tried to attack and overwhelm the besiegers; but the men of Maurice, having been warned, prepared themselves and received the approaching enemy in such a way that they were forced to flee with loss. In the army of the States, Veer, who had been at Ostend, was struck in the head by a cannonball and fell.

units.la: Ex Hispanis multi ad Statenses transierunt, quibus Mauritius aliquid viatici dedit & dimisit. Cum autem obsessi idem vrgerentur, tandem tolerabilibus conditionibus sese dediderunt, & impune cum suis armis exierunt 19. Sept.
units.tr: Many Spaniards went over to the Dutch States, and Maurice gave them some travel money and dismissed them. But when the besieged were pressed in the same way, they at last surrendered on tolerable conditions and went out unharmed with their arms on 19 September.

units.la: Statenses obseruarunt 500. Equites deportantes res Alberti Bruxellas, & eos inuadentes dissiparunt, 50. ceperunt, & 24. mulos cum supellectili precioso abstulerunt.
units.tr: The States watched 500 horsemen carrying Albert's goods to Brussels, attacked and scattered them, took fifty, and carried off twenty-four mules with precious household goods.

units.la: Hollandi rescientes Spinolam cum 8. Galeotis & 9. nauib. aduenturum, eundem obseruarunt, inuaserunt, superarunt, plurimas naues ceperunt, cæteras dissiparunt: in qua Spinola vehebatur, ea Caletum appulit. Nacti ibi sunt magnam vim auri, plurimum argenti, 500. Sclauos libertate donarunt, circa 130. optimates ceperunt.
units.tr: The Dutch, learning that Spinola was coming with eight galleys and nine ships, watched for him, attacked, overcame him, captured most of the ships and scattered the rest. The ship in which Spinola was travelling put in at Calais. There they found a great quantity of gold and much silver; they freed 500 slaves and took about 130 nobles prisoner.

units.la: Equites in Wachtendonck & Moers nouum Gubernatorem in Erklenz adorti, ipso & multis equis ipsius potiti sunt.
units.tr: Horsemen at Wachtendonck and Moers attacked the new governor at Erkelenz, and took him and many of his horses.

units.la: Plurimae naues Ostendam vectae, eique optime prouisum est.
units.tr: Many ships have been carried to Ostend, and it has been very well provisioned.

units.la: Ostendani adhuc libero ingressu & egressu mari fruuntur.
units.tr: The Ostenders still enjoy free entry and exit by sea.

units.la: In exercitu Alberti Equites circa 5. M. quos Meutinantes vocant, tumultuantur, & proprio iuri se venditare satagunt. Occupant Hochstraten, ditionem Leodiensem 40. M. Carolinorum multant, ab Antuerpiensibus etiam multam & munitiones postulant. Ciuitatulam Iambles propeNamur occupant. Duas compagnias equitum, in quos inciderant, ad se transire cogunt, & Wert occupant. Ab Episcopatu Coloniensi à Cliuensibus, & Aquisgranensibus singulis 600. Thaleros efflagitant, quos isti renuunt, & Alberto scribunt, vt grassationes istas amoliatur, aut se de auxilio contra ipsos sibi prouisuros apud eos, qui id non sint denegaturi.
units.tr: In Albert's army about 5,000 horsemen, whom they call Meutinantes, have risen in tumult and are doing their best to sell themselves for their own profit. They have seized Hochstraten, exacted 40,000 Carolus guilders from the territory of Liège, and demand a fine and fortifications from the people of Antwerp as well. They have seized the little town of Jambes near Namur. They forced two companies of horsemen, whom they had encountered, to come over to them, and they have taken Wert. From the Bishopric of Cologne, and from the people of Cleves and Aachen, they demand 600 thalers each, which these refuse, and they write to Albert, asking him to put a stop to these raids, or else to provide for their own protection against them, from those who will not deny them such help.

units.la: Rex Hispan. pro rebellibus eos declarat.
units.tr: The King of Spain declares them rebels.

units.la: Nuntius Apostolicus agit cum Meutenantibus hisce, qui respondent, vt prius abrogetur declaratio banni à Rege contra eos facti.
units.tr: The Apostolic Nuncio negotiates with these Meutenantes, who reply that the declaration of outlawry made against them by the King must first be revoked.

units.la: Statenses ductore Ludouico Nassouio, fortassis metuentes ne grassatores isti etiam Lucemberg. terras expilent, praeuenturi eos cum 6. M. secus Rhenum ascendunt, Iuliacensem Ducatum pertranseunt, & in Lucemburg. ditionem irruunt, & vrbem S. Viti gemina oppugnatione & deditione obtinent, magnas trabes Rhedis ductantes pro bombardis ostentarunt, & sic Vitenses terruerunt.
units.tr: The States, under the leadership of Louis of Nassau, perhaps fearing that these raiders might also plunder the lands of Luxembourg, went ahead of them with 6,000 men, sailing up the Rhine, passed through the Duchy of Jülich, rushed into the territory of Luxembourg, and took the town of St. Vith by a double assault and surrender. They displayed large beams drawn on carts as if they were cannon, and so terrified the men of Vith.

units.la: Similiter & Bestenach & Vianden obtinent, à singulis maximam multam exigentes, & in vniuerso Lucemburgo circiter ter 300. pagos & arces, quod contributionem iussu Gubernatoris recusassent, igni vastant, incipiendo proxime ab horto Gubernatoris Lucemburg. Petri Ernesti Mansfeldii.
units.tr: Likewise they took Bastogne and Vianden, exacting a very large fine from each, and throughout the whole of Luxembourg they laid waste with fire about 300 villages and fortresses, because they had refused to pay the contribution ordered by the Governor, beginning close by the garden of the Governor of Luxembourg, Peter Ernst of Mansfeld.

units.la: Spoliarunt & Monasterium Himrod, Sprengersbach & Machern in ditione Treuirensi. Quærenti Episcopo Nassovius respondit, velle se prædatores, si nominentur, plectere & damnum compensare. Abduxerunt innumeras pecudes & homines, tum officiarios & Abbatem S. Huperti, à quibus multam extorserunt. Octob.
units.tr: They also plundered the monastery of Himmerod, Sprengersbach and Machern in the territory of Trier. When the Bishop asked, Nassau replied that he was willing to punish the plunderers, if they were named, and to make good the damage. They carried off countless cattle and people, and also the officials and the Abbot of St. Hubert, from whom they extracted a fine. October.

units.la: Albertus mandat Friderico Bergensi, vt cum præsidiariis quibusdam Statenses persequatur, sed milites sequi renuit, nisi fiat solutio stipendii.
units.tr: Albert orders Frederick of Bergen to pursue the Dutch with some garrison troops, but he refused to follow the soldiers unless the wages were paid.

units.la: Equites Henrici Berg. etiam ad portas Colonienses hominibus insidiantur, & Canonicum ad S. Cunibertum abstraxerunt.
units.tr: The horsemen of Henry of Bergen also lie in wait for men at the gates of Cologne, and they have dragged off a canon of St. Cunibert.

units.la: Status exauctorant militem Capitanei Veer, & Anglos, quos ductore Wilhelm. Nassovio Embdenses conscripserunt contra Com. Embdensem.
units.tr: The States discharged the soldiers of Captain Veer, and the English whom the Embden men had enlisted under the leadership of Wilhelm of Nassau against the Count of Embden.

units.la: Hispani Geldrenses circa Coloniam grassantur, & nauem Dusseldorp. spoliant.
units.tr: The Spanish Gelderlanders run riot around Cologne and plunder a ship from Düsseldorf.

units.la: Albertus vrbibus Geldrensibus, licet deprecantibus & inuitis, præsidia valida imponit.
units.tr: Albert imposes strong garrisons on the Gelderland towns, although they plead against it and are unwilling.

units.la: Cum Hollandi ad status Brabantinos scripsissent, responderunt isti, se Hispanos eliminare non velle, Hollandos nunc ope Principum German. victorias obtinere, quos non perpetuo sint habituri auxiliatores, se contra causaque valere, causamque tuentibus armis, nempe Monarchis defensoribus, initi.
units.tr: When the Hollanders wrote to the Brabant States, those replied that they did not wish to drive out the Spaniards; the Hollanders were now winning victories with the help of the German Princes, who would not always be their helpers; they themselves were stronger against the cause, and had entered into it with arms, namely with the Monarch as defender of the cause.

units.la: Embdani submittunt & concredunt sese Protectioni Statuum generalium.
units.tr: The Embdeners submit and entrust themselves to the protection of the States General.

units.la: Exponuntur venum à mercatoribus Mittelburgensibus res preciosissimæ ex Indiis aduectæ.
units.tr: Very precious goods brought from the Indies are put up for sale by Middelburg merchants.

units.la: Cheriant Mayor Ostendam Hispanis prodere voluit, sed captus & ibidem supplicio affectus est. Meutenenses in Hochstraten nuntii Apostolici scriptum de pace concerpunt, & à vicinis locis & Ducatibus exactiones cogunt.
units.tr: Cheriant, the mayor, wanted to betray Ostend to the Spaniards, but was captured and put to death there. The Meutenians tore up the papal nuncio's written peace proposal at Hochstraten, and extorted exactions from neighbouring places and duchies.

units.la: Tres milites voluerunt Castellum Cameraci Meutinensibus prodere, sed sunt strangulati.
units.tr: Three soldiers wanted to betray the castle of Cambrai to the Meutenians, but they were strangled.

units.la: M.DC.IIII. Meutinenses respondent ad literas proscriptorias, & suam causam tuentur multis exemplis.
units.tr: In 1604 the Meutenians answered the letters of proscription and defended their cause with many examples.

units.la: Tres naues auro onustæ ex India Mittelburgum redeunt.
units.tr: Three ships laden with gold return from India to Middelburg.

units.la: Hollandi cum Portugalensibus nauibus committunt prelium nauale in Indiis.
units.tr: The Hollanders engage the Portuguese ships in a naval battle in the Indies.

units.la: Hispani per fraudem occupant Wachtendunck.
units.tr: The Spaniards take Wachtendonk by treachery.

units.la: Rex Galliæ ingentem pecuniam Statibus mittit.
units.tr: The King of France sends a great sum of money to the States.

units.la: Regina Angliæ Elisabetha pie defuncta electus & proclamatus est Rex Angliæ, Galliæ & Irlandiæ serenissimus Iacobus VI. Rex Scotiæ, vt qui à Margaretha filia Henrici VII. Regis Angliæ, Galliæ & Irlandiæ genus trahit, quæ Margaretha prognata est ex Elisabetha Regis Eduardi IV. filia, &c. Nomina dominorum in hac proclamatione præsentium vide alibi, quæ proclamatio facta est die 24. Martii An. 1603.
units.tr: Queen Elizabeth of England having died piously, the most serene James VI, King of Scotland, was elected and proclaimed King of England, France and Ireland, as he is descended from Margaret, daughter of Henry VII, King of England, France and Ireland, which Margaret was born of Elizabeth, daughter of King Edward IV, and so on. For the names of the lords present at this proclamation see elsewhere; the proclamation was made on 24 March 1603.

units.la: Capitaneus Grauendonk multos Statenses equites ad Kempen cædit.
units.tr: Captain Grauendonk cuts down many States' horsemen at Kempen.

units.la: Meutinantes ab Aquensibus & Iuliacensibus exigunt contributiones.
units.tr: The Meutenians exact contributions from the Aachen and Jülich people.

units.la: Statenses equites cædunt Henrici Bergensi. Equites, April.
units.tr: The States' horsemen cut down the horsemen of Henry of Berg, in April.

units.la: Hispani Ostendanis tres munitiones adimunt, & ex erecta munitione valde lædunt obsessos.
units.tr: The Spaniards take three fortifications from the Ostenders at Ostend, and by a raised fortification greatly harm the besieged.

units.la: Ordines mittunt Comitem Ernestum ad muniendum Rheinberg, ne Albertus suas copias eo mittat.
units.tr: The Orders send Count Ernest to fortify Rheinberg, lest Albert send his forces there.

units.la: Regina Angliæ defuncta splendidissime sepelitur in præsentia 5. M. hominum, legauit illa pro anubus vetulis 500. flor. annuas pensiones.
units.tr: Queen Elizabeth of England, having died, is buried most splendidly in the presence of 5,000 people; she bequeathed 500 florins a year as pensions for old women.

units.la: Friderici Spinolæ & Statuum grauis & periculosa navalis pugna ante Ostendam, in qua occumbit Spinola, Iunii.
units.tr: A grave and dangerous naval battle of Frederick Spinola and the States before Ostend, in which Spinola perished, in June.

units.la: Iacobus VI. R. Scotiæ coronatur in Regem Angliæ die 25. Iul. Pestis in Angliafæuit.
units.tr: James VI, King of Scotland, is crowned King of England on 25 July. Plague rages in England.

units.la: Quidam Anglici Magnates vitæ Regis insidiati sunt.
units.tr: Some English nobles plotted against the life of the King.

units.la: Albertus obsidet Meutinenses in Hochstraten, qui iurant Mauritio. Is igitur eos propugnat.
units.tr: Albert besieges the Meutenians at Hochstraten, who swear allegiance to Maurice. He therefore defends them.

units.la: Ostendani erumpentes lædunt Hispanos.
units.tr: The Ostenders, sallying out, harm the Spaniards.

units.la: Rex Hispaniæ negotiationes quibusuis nationibus in suis Regnis publico diplomate concedit, & æstimationem mercium ponit, &c.
units.tr: The King of Spain grants trade to all nations in his kingdoms by public decree, and sets the valuation of goods, etc.

units.la: Hispani nauem Ordinum ad Ostendam capiunt, quæ ægrotos vehebat, & ex iis duodecim necauerunt. Cum autem Mauritius munitionem nouam Hispanorum occupasset, & 100. milites coepisset, coniecit in urnam 188. schedulas nudas, & 12. patibulo notatas, & singulos ex urna singulas schedulas auferre iussit, qui igitur signatas ceperunt, hi suspensi sunt, præter vnum, qui intercessionibus liber euasit.
units.tr: The Spaniards capture a ship of the Orders near Ostend which was carrying the sick, and they drowned twelve of them. But when Maurice had occupied a new Spanish fortification and taken 100 soldiers, he threw 188 blank slips and 12 marked with a gallows into an urn, and ordered each man to draw one slip from the urn; those who drew the marked slips were hanged, except one, who was freed by intercession.

units.la: Mauritius obsidione cinxit Buscumducis, erectis munitionibus, ex quibus vrbem tormentis quateret, & Hispanicis castris magis magisque appropinquauit.
units.tr: Maurice laid siege to Bois-le-Duc, raising fortifications from which he could batter the town with artillery, and drew ever closer to the Spanish camp.

units.la: Ciues obsessi rogarunt Albertum, vt ipse in castra veniret, & vrbem propugnaret.
units.tr: The besieged citizens asked Albert to come himself into the camp and defend the town.

units.la: Cum victualia Rheno adueåta obsessis adducerentur, prohibitum hoc est à Statibus.
units.tr: When supplies were brought up the Rhine to the besieged, the States forbade this.

units.la: Marquis Malaspina à Meutinensibus captus in castris Mauritii honorifice exceptus est, & cum is & Templo bambularent, ambobus his ictu ex vrbe pedes sunt læsi, vnde mortui sunt.
units.tr: Marquis Malaspina, captured by the Meutenians, was received with honour in Maurice's camp; and while he and Templo were walking about, both were struck by a shot from the town, by which they were wounded in the feet, and so died.

units.la: Cum Albertus in Buscoducum venit, Mauritius biduum vehementer in vrbem fulminauit.
units.tr: When Albert came to Bois-le-Duc, Maurice thundered vehemently against the town for two days.

units.la: Hispani prætextu, quod vrbem transire vellent, (ante enim Ciues eos intromittere nunquam voluerunt) eam occupant.
units.tr: The Spaniards, on the pretext that they wished to pass through the town (for the citizens had never before been willing to admit them), seized it.

units.la: Hispani Meutinenses ibi sunt aggressi, sed repulsi. Hispani etiam castra Mauritii per insidias voluerunt inuadere. Verum insidiæ sunt detectæ, plexis proditoribus Gallis.
units.tr: The Spaniards attacked the Meutenians there, but were repulsed. The Spaniards also tried to attack Maurice's camp by ambush. But the ambush was detected, the traitors being French and executed.

units.la: Mauritius obsidionem soluit, 8. Nouemb. Statenses prædas agunt in regione Iuliacensi, spoliata arce Gelenkirchen.
units.tr: Maurice raised the siege on 8 November. The States carry off booty in the Jülich region, and the fortress of Gelenkirchen is plundered.

units.la: Buscoducenses æque vt in obsidione grauantur, & inopia lignorum laborant.
units.tr: The people of Bois-le-Duc are burdened just as during the siege, and suffer shortage of wood.

units.la: Statenses petulanter agunt in Duitsch.
units.tr: The States act wantonly in Düsseldorf.
