units.la: Ad Ostendam magnæ vtrinq; molitiones fiunt, & Spinola multa minatur & machinatur.
units.tr: Great efforts are made on both sides at Ostend, and Spinola threatens and contrives much.

units.la: Tienæ in Brabantia inuentum est simulachrum in quadam caua quercu, inde dictum Sancta Maria de Quercu, ad eam populus turmatim accurrit, Albertus ibi curauit ædificari Capellam, & dicebatur ibi edi magna miracula sanationum. Infanta nudis pedibus per duo milliaria eam adiit, pro prole & victoria contra hæreticos vota faciens.
units.tr: At Tienen in Brabant an image was found in a hollow oak, whence it was called Holy Mary of the Oak; the people ran to it in crowds, Albert had a chapel built there, and great miracles of healing were said to be wrought there. The Infanta went to it barefoot for two miles, making vows for offspring and for victory against the heretics.

units.la: Anno M.DC.IV. cives Buscoduc. mittunt ad Albertum, & petunt vt subleuentur, nihil ibi commerciorum esse, & opifices se sustentare non posse.
units.tr: In the year 1604 the citizens of Bois-le-Duc sent to Albert and asked to be relieved, since there was no trade there and the craftsmen could not support themselves.

units.la: Statenses spoliant Confoyam vini & aliarum rerum.
units.tr: The States plunder Konfoy of wine and other goods.

units.la: Henricus de Berg cogit Erklenses, vt recipiant Hispanos, occupant & arcem Pesch in Ducatu Iuliacensi.
units.tr: Henry of Berg compels the people of Erkelenz to receive the Spaniards, and seizes the fortress of Pesch in the Duchy of Jülich.

units.la: Meutinenses à Connestablio di Castiglia proscribuntur.
units.tr: The Meutenians are proscribed by the Constable of Castile.

units.la: Status in Haga congregati imponunt Prouinciis contributionem, videl. quinquagesimum quenque nummum.
units.tr: The States, assembled at The Hague, impose a contribution on the Provinces, namely every fiftieth penny.

units.la: Meutinenses & Statenses magno numero pergunt versus Erklens, ibi cum Hispani iam egressi essent, Cives multant 20. M. Talerorum, coegerunt & Kerpenses sese dedere.
units.tr: The Meutenians and the States advance in great numbers towards Erkelenz; when the Spaniards had already withdrawn from there, the citizens were fined 20,000 talers, and the people of Kerpen also were forced to surrender.

units.la: Cum vni ex Meutinensibus equus à Coloniense milite esset interfectus, Meutinenses toti vrbi dira minantur. Itaque ex Duitsch in vrbem bombardis fulminant. Sed cum vicissim ex vrbe globis peterentur, discesserunt in Westphaliam, ibi ab Episcopo Padebornensi 13. M. Talerorum extorquent, & impetiti à rusticis eorum circa 500. occidunt.
units.tr: When one of the Meutenians' horses had been killed by a soldier of Cologne, the Meutenians threatened the whole town with dreadful things. Accordingly they bombarded the town from Düsseldorf. But when in turn they were struck by balls from the town, they withdrew into Westphalia, where they extorted 13,000 talers from the Bishop of Paderborn, and when attacked by the peasants, about 500 of them were killed.

units.la: Hispani inuenerunt magnam nouam Insulam in occidentali India.
units.tr: The Spaniards discovered a large new island in the western Indies.

units.la: Hispani ad Ostendam occupant propugnaculum, sed rursus reiiciuntur.
units.tr: The Spaniards seize a outwork at Ostend, but are again driven back.

units.la: Nota descriptionem noui Pontis, quem Hispani magnis sumptibus ædificarunt, cuius admotu propugnaculum mediæ Lunæ fe superare posse sperabant. Traxerunt eum erectum 40 equi, qui yna cum militibus subter eo tuti ab ictibus latitantes processerunt. Sed Oftendani vnam eius pontis rotam tormentis concusserunt & fregerunt, ita vt amplius procedere non possent. Sic cum ea celebri machina nihil effecerunt.
units.tr: Note the description of the new bridge, which the Spaniards built at great expense, by whose approach they hoped to be able to overcome the crescent-shaped outwork. Forty horses drew it erected, and together with the soldiers, sheltered beneath it from blows, they advanced. But the Ostenders shattered and broke one of the wheels of that bridge with artillery, so that it could go no further. Thus they accomplished nothing with that famous machine.

units.la: Mauritius interea sese innumeris nauibus instruxit, & eas circum ea littora adduxit, quæ Slusium spectant, & simul ipsam Ciuitatem Slus circumquaque terra marique arcta obsidione cinxit, & eo vsque coangustauit, vt ad deditionem eam coegerit. Sic igitur satis commodum momentum Statibus accessit. Oftenda Hesperiis donec circumdatur armis, Vrbes Mauritius tres capit interea.
units.tr: Meanwhile Maurice equipped himself with innumerable ships and brought them along the shores that face Sluis, and at the same time surrounded the town of Sluis on all sides by land and sea with a close siege, and narrowed it so far that he forced it to surrender. Thus a fairly considerable advantage came to the States. While Ostend is surrounded by Spanish arms, Maurice meanwhile takes three cities.

units.la: Contra vero Status rudera Oftendæ Alberto tolerabilibus conditionibus dediderunt, sic vt obsessi cum armis & signis discesserint, & Slusium saluo conducto incolumes abiuerint.
units.tr: On the other hand the States surrendered the ruins of Ostend to Albert on tolerable terms, so that the besieged departed with arms and standards, and went safely to Sluis under safe conduct.

units.la: Et hic finis fuit memorabilis illius obsidionis & defensionis huius loci vltra triennium durantis. Quid vero vtrinque specialiter quouis tempore gestum sit, id peculiari volumine diligenter est descriptum, vbi, qui volet, cum admiratione legere poterit.
units.tr: And this was the end of that memorable siege and defence of this place, which lasted more than three years. What was done on either side at any particular time has been described carefully in a separate volume, where anyone who wishes may read it with admiration.

units.la: FINIS.
units.tr: FINIS.

units.la: Tuam Deus custodias Ecclesiam.
units.tr: May God keep your Church.
